<div class="col-sm order-1">
      <h2 class="chapter_title">CHAPTER 144. DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH</h2>
      
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.001"><b>144.001</b> MS 2006 [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/15.001">15.001</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">STATE COMMISSIONER OF HEALTH</h1>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.01"><b>144.01</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.46.0">1977 c 305 s 46</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.011">
        <h1 class="shn">144.011 DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.011.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>The Department of Health shall be under the control and supervision of the commissioner of health who shall be appointed by the governor under the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/15.06">15.06</a>. The State Board of Health is abolished and all powers and duties of the board are transferred to the commissioner of health. The commissioner shall be selected without regard to political affiliation but with regard to ability and experience in matters of public health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.011.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/192/#laws.4.3.0">2014 c 192 art 4 s 3</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.011.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.39.0">1977 c 305 s 39</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/260/#laws.0.30.0">1983 c 260 s 30</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.02"><b>144.02</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.46.0">1977 c 305 s 46</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.03"><b>144.03</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.46.0">1977 c 305 s 46</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.04"><b>144.04</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.46.0">1977 c 305 s 46</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.05">
        <h1 class="shn">144.05 GENERAL DUTIES OF COMMISSIONER; REPORTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.05.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">General duties.</span></h2>
          <p>The state commissioner of health shall have general authority as the state's official health agency and shall be responsible for the development and maintenance of an organized system of programs and services for protecting, maintaining, and improving the health of the citizens. This authority shall include but not be limited to the following:</p>
          <p>(1) conduct studies and investigations, collect and analyze health and vital data, and identify and describe health problems;</p>
          <p>(2) plan, facilitate, coordinate, provide, and support the organization of services for the prevention and control of illness and disease and the limitation of disabilities resulting therefrom;</p>
          <p>(3) establish and enforce health standards for the protection and the promotion of the public's health such as quality of health services, reporting of disease, regulation of health facilities, environmental health hazards and personnel;</p>
          <p>(4) affect the quality of public health and general health care services by providing consultation and technical training for health professionals and paraprofessionals;</p>
          <p>(5) promote personal health by conducting general health education programs and disseminating health information;</p>
          <p>(6) coordinate and integrate local, state and federal programs and services affecting the public's health;</p>
          <p>(7) continually assess and evaluate the effectiveness and efficiency of health service systems and public health programming efforts in the state; and</p>
          <p>(8) advise the governor and legislature on matters relating to the public's health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.05.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Mission; efficiency.</span></h2>
          <p>It is part of the department's mission that within the department's resources the commissioner shall endeavor to:</p>
          <p>(1) prevent the waste or unnecessary spending of public money;</p>
          <p>(2) use innovative fiscal and human resource practices to manage the state's resources and operate the department as efficiently as possible;</p>
          <p>(3) coordinate the department's activities wherever appropriate with the activities of other governmental agencies;</p>
          <p>(4) use technology where appropriate to increase agency productivity, improve customer service, increase public access to information about government, and increase public participation in the business of government;</p>
          <p>(5) utilize constructive and cooperative labor-management practices to the extent otherwise required by chapters 43A and 179A;</p>
          <p>(6) report to the legislature on the performance of agency operations and the accomplishment of agency goals in the agency's biennial budget according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/16A.10#stat.16A.10.1">16A.10, subdivision 1</a>; and</p>
          <p>(7) recommend to the legislature appropriate changes in law necessary to carry out the mission and improve the performance of the department.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.05.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Appropriation transfers to be reported.</span></h2>
          <p>When the commissioner transfers operational money between programs under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/16A.285">16A.285</a>, in addition to the requirements of that section the commissioner must provide the chairs of the legislative committees that have jurisdiction over the agency's budget with sufficient detail to identify the account to which the money was originally appropriated, and the account to which the money is being transferred.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.05.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Identification of deceased individuals.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon receiving notice under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/149A.90#stat.149A.90.1">149A.90, subdivision 1</a>, of the death of an individual who cannot be identified, the commissioner must post on the department's website information regarding the individual for purposes of obtaining information that may aid in identifying the individual and for purposes of notifying relatives who may be seeking the individual. The information must remain on the website continuously until the person's identity is determined.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.05.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Firearms data.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, the commissioner of health is prohibited from collecting data on individuals regarding lawful firearm ownership in the state or data related to an individual's right to carry a weapon under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/624.714">624.714</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.05.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Reports on interagency agreements and intra-agency transfers.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall provide quarterly reports to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over health and human services policy and finance on:</p>
          <p>(1) interagency agreements or service-level agreements and any renewals or extensions of existing interagency or service-level agreements with a state department under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/15.01">15.01</a>, state agency under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/15.012">15.012</a>, or the Department of Information Technology Services, with a value of more than $100,000, or related agreements with the same department or agency with a cumulative value of more than $100,000; and</p>
          <p>(2) transfers of appropriations of more than $100,000 between accounts within or between agencies.</p>
          <p class="bl">The report must include the statutory citation authorizing the agreement, transfer or dollar amount, purpose, and effective date of the agreement, and duration of the agreement.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.05.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Expiration of report mandates.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If the submission of a report by the commissioner of health to the legislature is mandated by statute and the enabling legislation does not include a date for the submission of a final report, the mandate to submit the report shall expire in accordance with this section.</p>
          <p>(b) If the mandate requires the submission of an annual report and the mandate was enacted before January 1, 2021, the mandate shall expire on January 1, 2023. If the mandate requires the submission of a biennial or less frequent report and the mandate was enacted before January 1, 2021, the mandate shall expire on January 1, 2024.</p>
          <p>(c) Any reporting mandate enacted on or after January 1, 2021, shall expire three years after the date of enactment if the mandate requires the submission of an annual report and shall expire five years after the date of enactment if the mandate requires the submission of a biennial or less frequent report, unless the enacting legislation provides for a different expiration date.</p>
          <p>(d) The commissioner shall submit a list to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over health by February 15 of each year, beginning February 15, 2022, of all reports set to expire during the following calendar year in accordance with this section. The mandate to submit a report to the legislature under this paragraph does not expire.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.05.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Grant consultation.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner must consult with the commissioner of management and budget to create, review, and revise grant program performance measures and to evaluate grant programs administered by the commissioner in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/16A.055">16A.055, subdivisions 1a</a> and 1b.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.05.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/29">5339</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1905/cite/29">RL s 2130</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/356/#laws.0.2.0">1973 c 356 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/248/#laws.11.11.0">1995 c 248 art 11 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/366/#laws.0.57.0">1998 c 366 s 57</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/245/#laws.1.14.0">1999 c 245 art 1 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/375/#laws.3.4.0">2002 c 375 art 3 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/1/1/#laws.20.5.0">1Sp2010 c 1 art 20 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/189/#laws.20.7.0">2016 c 189 art 20 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/0/30/#laws.3.10.0">2021 c 30 art 3 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/0/31/#laws.2.16.0">2021 c 31 art 2 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.59.5.0">2024 c 127 art 59 s 5</a>,6; art 66 s 5</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.0505">
        <h1 class="shn">144.0505 COOPERATION WITH COMMISSIONER OF HUMAN SERVICES.</h1>
        <p>The commissioner shall promptly provide to the commissioner of human services upon request information on hospital revenues, nursing home licensure, and health maintenance organization revenues specifically required by the commissioner of human services to operate the provider surcharge program.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.0505.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/513/#laws.7.1.0">1992 c 513 art 7 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.0506"><b>144.0506</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/192/#laws.4.3.0">2014 c 192 art 4 s 3</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.051">
        <h1 class="shn">144.051 DATA RELATING TO LICENSED AND REGISTERED PERSONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.051.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Purpose.</span></h2>
          <p>The legislature finds that accurate information pertaining to the numbers, distribution and characteristics of health-related personnel is required in order that there exist an adequate information resource at the state level for purposes of making decisions pertaining to health personnel.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.051.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Information system.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall establish a system for the collection, analysis and reporting of data on individuals licensed or registered by the commissioner or the health-related licensing boards as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.01#stat.214.01.2">214.01, subdivision 2</a>. Individuals licensed or registered by the commissioner or the health-related licensing boards shall provide information to the commissioner of health that the commissioner may, pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.052">144.052</a>, require. The commissioner shall publish at least biennially, a report which indicates the type of information available and methods for requesting the information.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.051.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Data classification; private data.</span></h2>
          <p>For providers regulated pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.43">144A.43</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.482">144A.482</a> and chapter 144G, the following data collected, created, or maintained by the commissioner are classified as private data on individuals as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02">13.02</a>, subdivision 12:</p>
          <p>(1) data submitted by or on behalf of applicants for licenses prior to issuance of the license;</p>
          <p>(2) the identity of complainants who have made reports concerning licensees or applicants unless the complainant consents to the disclosure;</p>
          <p>(3) the identity of individuals who provide information as part of surveys and investigations;</p>
          <p>(4) Social Security numbers; and</p>
          <p>(5) health record data.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.051.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Data classification; public data.</span></h2>
          <p>For providers regulated pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.43">144A.43</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.482">144A.482</a> and chapter 144G, the following data collected, created, or maintained by the commissioner are classified as public data as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.15">13.02, subdivision 15</a>:</p>
          <p>(1) all application data on licensees, license numbers, and license status;</p>
          <p>(2) licensing information about licenses previously held under this chapter;</p>
          <p>(3) correction orders, including information about compliance with the order and whether the fine was paid;</p>
          <p>(4) final enforcement actions pursuant to chapter 14;</p>
          <p>(5) orders for hearing, findings of fact, and conclusions of law; and</p>
          <p>(6) when the licensee and department agree to resolve the matter without a hearing, the agreement and specific reasons for the agreement are public data.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.051.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Data classification; confidential data.</span></h2>
          <p>For providers regulated pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.43">144A.43</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.482">144A.482</a> and chapter 144G, the following data collected, created, or maintained by the Department of Health are classified as confidential data on individuals as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.3">13.02, subdivision 3</a>: active investigative data relating to the investigation of potential violations of law by a licensee including data from the survey process before the correction order is issued by the department.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.051.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Release of private or confidential data.</span></h2>
          <p>For providers regulated pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.43">144A.43</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.482">144A.482</a> and chapter 144G, the department may release private or confidential data, except Social Security numbers, to the appropriate state, federal, or local agency and law enforcement office to enhance investigative or enforcement efforts or further a public health protective process. Types of offices include Adult Protective Services, Office of the Ombudsman for Long-Term Care and Office of the Ombudsman for Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities, the health licensing boards, Department of Human Services, county or city attorney's offices, police, and local or county public health offices.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.051.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/759/#laws.0.1.0">1978 c 759 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.11.3.0">2013 c 108 art 11 s 3</a>-6; 2019 c 60 art 1 s 47; art 4 s 1-3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/7/1/#laws.6.25.0">7Sp2020 c 1 art 6 s 25</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.052">
        <h1 class="shn">144.052 USE OF DATA.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.052.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Rules.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner, after consultation with the health-related licensing boards as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.01#stat.214.01.2">214.01, subdivision 2</a>, shall promulgate rules in accordance with chapter 14 regarding the types of information collected and the forms used for collection. The types of information collected shall include licensure or registration status, name, address, birth date, sex, professional activity status, and educational background or similar information needed in order to make decisions pertaining to health personnel.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.052.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Coordination with licensure renewal.</span></h2>
          <p>In order that the collection of the information specified in this section not impose an unnecessary burden on the licensed or registered individual or require additional administrative cost to the state, the commissioner of health shall, whenever possible, collect the information at the time of the individual's licensure or registration renewal. The health-related licensing boards shall include the request for the information that the commissioner may require pursuant to subdivision 1 with the licensure renewal application materials, provided, however, that the collection of health personnel data by the commissioner shall not cause the licensing boards to incur additional costs or delays with regard to the license renewal process.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.052.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/759/#laws.0.2.0">1978 c 759 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/424/#laws.0.130.0">1982 c 424 s 130</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.0525">
        <h1 class="shn">144.0525 EPIDEMIOLOGIC STUDIES; HEALTH HAZARDS; HEALTH SURVEILLANCE.</h1>
        <p>All data collected by the commissioner of health under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/176.234">176.234</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/268.19">268.19</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/270B.14#stat.270B.14.11">270B.14, subdivision 11</a>, shall be used only for the purposes of epidemiologic investigations, notification of persons exposed to health hazards as a result of employment, and surveillance of occupational health and safety.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.0525.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/202/#laws.0.5.0">1991 c 202 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/569/#laws.0.7.0">1992 c 569 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/483/#laws.0.1.0">1994 c 483 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/66/#laws.0.79.0">1997 c 66 s 79</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.0526">
        <h1 class="shn">144.0526 MINNESOTA ONE HEALTH ANTIMICROBIAL STEWARDSHIP COLLABORATIVE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.0526.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Establishment.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall establish the Minnesota One Health Antimicrobial Stewardship Collaborative. The commissioner shall hire a director to execute operations, conduct health education, and provide technical assistance.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.0526.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Commissioner's duties.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall oversee a program to:</p>
          <p>(1) maintain the position of director of One Health Antimicrobial Stewardship to lead state antimicrobial stewardship initiatives across human, animal, and environmental health;</p>
          <p>(2) communicate to professionals and the public the interconnectedness of human, animal, and environmental health, especially related to preserving the efficacy of antibiotic medications, which are a shared resource;</p>
          <p>(3) leverage new and existing partnerships. The commissioner of health shall consult and collaborate with academic institutions, industry and community organizations, and organizations and agencies in fields including but not limited to health care, veterinary medicine, and animal agriculture to inform strategies for education, practice improvement, and research in all settings where antimicrobial products are used;</p>
          <p>(4) ensure that veterinary settings have education and strategies needed to practice appropriate antibiotic prescribing, implement clinical antimicrobial stewardship programs, and prevent transmission of antimicrobial-resistant microbes; and</p>
          <p>(5) support collaborative research and programmatic initiatives to improve the understanding of the impact of antimicrobial use and resistance in the natural environment.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.0526.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Biennial report.</span></h2>
          <p>By January 15, 2025, and every two years thereafter, the commissioner of health shall report to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with primary jurisdiction over health policy and finance on the work accomplished by the commissioner under this section and the collaborative research conducted in the previous two years and on program goals for the upcoming two years.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.0526.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.4.14.0">2023 c 70 art 4 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.59.7.0">2024 c 127 art 59 s 7</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.0528">
        <h1 class="shn">144.0528 COMPREHENSIVE DRUG OVERDOSE AND MORBIDITY PREVENTION ACT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.0528.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purpose of this section, "drug overdose and morbidity" means health problems that people experience after inhaling, ingesting, or injecting medicines in quantities that exceed prescription status; medicines taken that are prescribed to a different person; medicines that have been adulterated or adjusted by contaminants intentionally or unintentionally; or nonprescription drugs in amounts that result in morbidity or mortality.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.0528.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Establishment.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall establish a comprehensive drug overdose and morbidity program to conduct comprehensive drug overdose and morbidity prevention activities, epidemiologic investigations and surveillance, and evaluation to monitor, address, and prevent drug overdoses statewide through integrated strategies that include the following:</p>
          <p>(1) advance access to evidence-based nonnarcotic pain management services;</p>
          <p>(2) implement culturally specific interventions and prevention programs with population and community groups in greatest need, including those who are pregnant and their infants;</p>
          <p>(3) enhance overdose prevention and supportive services for people experiencing homelessness. This strategy includes funding for emergency and short-term housing subsidies through the homeless overdose prevention hub and expanding support for syringe services programs serving people experiencing homelessness statewide;</p>
          <p>(4) equip employers to promote health and well-being of employees by addressing substance misuse and drug overdose;</p>
          <p>(5) improve outbreak detection and identification of substances involved in overdoses through the expansion of the Minnesota Drug Overdose and Substance Use Surveillance Activity (MNDOSA);</p>
          <p>(6) implement Tackling Overdose With Networks (TOWN) community prevention programs;</p>
          <p>(7) identify, address, and respond to drug overdose and morbidity in those who are pregnant or have just given birth through multitiered approaches that may:</p>
          <p>(i) promote medication-assisted treatment options;</p>
          <p>(ii) support programs that provide services in accord with evidence-based care models for mental health and substance abuse disorder;</p>
          <p>(iii) collaborate with interdisciplinary and professional organizations that focus on quality improvement initiatives related to substance use disorder; and</p>
          <p>(iv) implement substance use disorder-related recommendations from the maternal mortality review committee, as appropriate; and</p>
          <p>(8) design a system to assess, address, and prevent the impacts of drug overdose and morbidity on those who are pregnant, their infants, and children. Specifically, the commissioner of health may:</p>
          <p>(i) inform health care providers and the public of the prevalence, risks, conditions, and treatments associated with substance use disorders involving or affecting pregnancies, infants, and children; and</p>
          <p>(ii) identify communities, families, infants, and children affected by substance use disorder in order to recommend focused interventions, prevention, and services.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.0528.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Partnerships.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health may consult with sovereign Tribal nations, the Minnesota Departments of Human Services, Corrections, Public Safety, and Education, local public health agencies, care providers and insurers, community organizations that focus on substance abuse risks and recovery, individuals affected by substance use disorders, and any other individuals, entities, and organizations as necessary to carry out the goals of this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.0528.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Grants authorized.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner of health may award grants, as funding allows, to entities and organizations focused on addressing and preventing the negative impacts of drug overdose and morbidity. Examples of activities the commissioner may consider for these grant awards include:</p>
          <p>(1) developing, implementing, or promoting drug overdose and morbidity prevention programs and activities;</p>
          <p>(2) community outreach and other efforts addressing the root causes of drug overdose and morbidity;</p>
          <p>(3) identifying risk and protective factors relating to drug overdose and morbidity that contribute to identification, development, or improvement of prevention strategies and community outreach;</p>
          <p>(4) developing or providing trauma-informed drug overdose and morbidity prevention and services;</p>
          <p>(5) developing or providing culturally and linguistically appropriate drug overdose and morbidity prevention and services, and programs that target and serve historically underserved communities;</p>
          <p>(6) working collaboratively with educational institutions, including school districts, to implement drug overdose and morbidity prevention strategies for students, teachers, and administrators;</p>
          <p>(7) working collaboratively with sovereign Tribal nations, care providers, nonprofit organizations, for-profit organizations, government entities, community-based organizations, and other entities to implement substance misuse and drug overdose prevention strategies within their communities; and</p>
          <p>(8) creating or implementing quality improvement initiatives to improve drug overdose and morbidity treatment and outcomes.</p>
          <p>(b) Any organization or government entity receiving grant money under this section must collect and make available to the commissioner of health aggregate data related to the activity funded by the program under this section. The commissioner of health shall use the information and data from the program evaluation to inform the administration of existing Department of Health programming and the development of Department of Health policies, programs, and procedures.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.0528.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Promotion; administration. </span></h2>
          <p>In fiscal years 2026 and beyond, the commissioner may spend up to 25 percent of the total funding appropriated for the comprehensive drug overdose and morbidity program in each fiscal year to promote, administer, support, and evaluate the programs authorized under this section and to provide technical assistance to program grantees.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.0528.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">External contributions.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may accept contributions from governmental and nongovernmental sources and may apply for grants to supplement state appropriations for the programs authorized under this section. Contributions and grants received from the sources identified in this subdivision to advance the purpose of this section are appropriated to the commissioner for the comprehensive drug overdose and morbidity program.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.0528.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Program evaluation. </span></h2>
          <p>Beginning February 28, 2024, the commissioner of health shall report every even-numbered year to the legislative committees with jurisdiction over health detailing the expenditures of funds authorized under this section. The commissioner shall use the data to evaluate the effectiveness of the program. The commissioner must include in the report:</p>
          <p>(1) the number of organizations receiving grant money under this section;</p>
          <p>(2) the number of individuals served by the grant programs;</p>
          <p>(3) a description and analysis of the practices implemented by program grantees; and</p>
          <p>(4) best practices recommendations to prevent drug overdose and morbidity, including culturally relevant best practices and recommendations focused on historically underserved communities.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.0528.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Measurement.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, the commissioner of health shall assess and evaluate grants and contracts awarded using available data sources, including but not limited to the Minnesota All Payer Claims Database (MN APCD), the Minnesota Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS), the Minnesota Student Survey, vital records, hospitalization data, syndromic surveillance, and the Minnesota Electronic Health Record Consortium.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.0528.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.4.15.0">2023 c 70 art 4 s 15</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.053">
        <h1 class="shn">144.053 RESEARCH STUDIES CONFIDENTIAL.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.053.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Status of data collected by commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>All information, records of interviews, written reports, statements, notes, memoranda, or other data procured by the state commissioner of health, in connection with studies conducted by the state commissioner of health, or carried on by the said commissioner jointly with other persons, agencies or organizations, or procured by such other persons, agencies or organizations, for the purpose of reducing the morbidity or mortality from any cause or condition of health shall be confidential and shall be used solely for the purposes of medical or scientific research.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.053.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Limits on use and disclosure.</span></h2>
          <p>Such information, records, reports, statements, notes, memoranda, or other data shall not be admissible as evidence in any action of any kind in any court or before any other tribunal, board, agency or person. Such information, records, reports, statements, notes, memoranda, or other data shall not be exhibited nor their contents disclosed in any way, in whole or in part, by any representative of the state commissioner of health, nor by any other person, except as may be necessary for the purpose of furthering the research project to which they relate. No person participating in such research project shall disclose, in any manner, the information so obtained except in strict conformity with such research project. No employee of said commissioner shall interview any patient named in any such report, nor a relative of any such patient, unless the consent of the attending physician and surgeon is first obtained.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.053.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">No liability for giving information.</span></h2>
          <p>The furnishing of such information to the state commissioner of health or an authorized representative, or to any other cooperating agency in such research project, shall not subject any person, hospital, sanitarium, nursing home or other person or agency furnishing such information, to any action for damages or other relief.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.053.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Violation a misdemeanor.</span></h2>
          <p>Any disclosure other than is provided for in this section, is hereby declared to be a misdemeanor and punishable as such.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.053.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Personally identifying information.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health or the commissioner's agent is not required to solicit information that personally identifies persons selected to participate in an epidemiologic study if the commissioner determines that:</p>
          <p>(1) the study monitors incidence or prevalence of a serious disease to detect potential health problems and predict risks, provides specific information to develop public health strategies to prevent serious disease, enables the targeting of intervention resources for communities, patients, or groups at risk of the disease, and informs health professionals about risks, early detection, or treatment of the disease;</p>
          <p>(2) the personally identifying information is not necessary to validate the quality, accuracy, or completeness of the study; or</p>
          <p>(3) the collection of personally identifying information may seriously jeopardize the validity of study results, as demonstrated by an epidemiologic study.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.053.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1955/0/769/#laws.0.1.0">1955 c 769 s 1</a>-4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/173/#laws.0.31.0">1976 c 173 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/689/#laws.2.29.0">1988 c 689 art 2 s 29</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.0535">
        <h1 class="shn">144.0535 ENTRY FOR INSPECTION.</h1>
        <p>For the purposes of performing their official duties, all officers and employees of the state Department of Health shall have the right to enter any building, conveyance, or place where contagion, infection, filth, or other source or cause of preventable disease exists or is reasonably suspected.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.0535.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/282/#laws.2.7.0">1989 c 282 art 2 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.054">
        <h1 class="shn">144.054 SUBPOENA POWER.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.054.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Generally.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may, as part of an investigation to determine whether a serious health threat exists or to locate persons who may have been exposed to an agent which can seriously affect their health, issue subpoenas to require the attendance and testimony of witnesses and production of books, records, correspondence, and other information relevant to any matter involved in the investigation. The commissioner or the commissioner's designee may administer oaths to witnesses or take their affirmation. The subpoenas may be served upon any person named therein anywhere in the state by any person authorized to serve subpoenas or other processes in civil actions of the district courts. If a person to whom a subpoena is issued does not comply with the subpoena, the commissioner may apply to the district court in any district and the court shall order the person to comply with the subpoena. Failure to obey the order of the court may be punished by the court as contempt of court. Except as provided in subdivision 2, no person may be compelled to disclose privileged information as described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/595.02#stat.595.02.1">595.02, subdivision 1</a>. All information pertaining to individual medical records obtained under this section shall be considered health data under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.3805#stat.13.3805.1">13.3805, subdivision 1</a>. The fees for the service of a subpoena must be paid in the same manner as prescribed by law for a service of process issued out of a district court. Witnesses must receive the same fees and mileage as in civil actions.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.054.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">HIV; HBV.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may subpoena privileged medical information of patients who may have been exposed by a licensed dental hygienist, dentist, physician, nurse, podiatrist, a registered dental assistant, or a physician assistant who is infected with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) or hepatitis B virus (HBV) when the commissioner has determined that it may be necessary to notify those patients that they may have been exposed to HIV or HBV.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.054.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/579/#laws.0.1.0">1988 c 579 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/559/#laws.1.1.0">1992 c 559 art 1 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/227/#laws.0.22.0">1999 c 227 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.4.58.0">2014 c 291 art 4 s 58</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.055">
        <h1 class="shn">144.055 HOME SAFETY PROGRAMS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.055.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Preventing home accidents; working with local boards.</span></h2>
          <p>The state commissioner of health is authorized to develop and conduct by exhibit, demonstration and by health education or public health engineering activity, or by any other means or methods which the commissioner may determine to be suitable and practicable for the purpose, a program in home safety designed to prevent accidents and fatalities resulting therefrom. The commissioner shall cooperate with community health boards as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145A.02#stat.145A.02.5">145A.02, subdivision 5</a>, the Minnesota Safety Council, and other interested voluntary groups in its conduct of such programs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.055.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Sharing equipment and staff.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purpose of assisting community health boards to develop community home safety programs and to conduct such surveys of safety hazards in municipalities and counties, the commissioner may loan or furnish exhibit, demonstration, and educational materials, and may assign personnel for a limited period to such community health boards.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.055.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1957/0/290/#laws.0.1.0">1957 c 290 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/309/#laws.0.24.0">1987 c 309 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.7.28.0">2014 c 291 art 7 s 28</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.109.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 109</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.056">
        <h1 class="shn">144.056 PLAIN LANGUAGE IN WRITTEN MATERIALS.</h1>
        <p>(a) To the extent reasonable and consistent with the goals of providing easily understandable and readable materials and complying with federal and state laws governing the program, all written materials relating to determinations of eligibility for or amounts of benefits that will be given to applicants for or recipients of assistance under a program administered or supervised by the commissioner of health must be understandable to a person who reads at the seventh-grade level, using the Flesch scale analysis readability score as determined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/72C.09">72C.09</a>.</p>
        <p>(b) All written materials relating to services and determinations of eligibility for or amounts of benefits that will be given to applicants for or recipients of assistance under programs administered or supervised by the commissioner of health must be developed to satisfy the plain language requirements of the Plain Language Contract Act under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325G.29">325G.29</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325G.36">325G.36</a>. Materials may be submitted to the attorney general for review and certification. Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325G.35#stat.325G.35.1">325G.35, subdivision 1</a>, the attorney general shall review submitted materials to determine whether they comply with the requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325G.31">325G.31</a>. The remedies available pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/8.31">8.31</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325G.33">325G.33</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325G.36">325G.36</a> do not apply to these materials. Failure to comply with this section does not provide a basis for suspending the implementation or operation of other laws governing programs administered by the commissioner.</p>
        <p>(c) The requirements of this section apply to all materials modified or developed by the commissioner on or after July 1, 1988. The requirements of this section do not apply to materials that must be submitted to a federal agency for approval to the extent that application of the requirements prevents federal approval.</p>
        <p>(d) Nothing in this section may be construed to prohibit a lawsuit brought to require the commissioner to comply with this section or to affect individual appeal rights under the special supplemental food program for women, infants, and children granted pursuant to federal regulations under the Code of Federal Regulations, chapter 7, section 246.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.056.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/689/#laws.2.30.0">1988 c 689 art 2 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/7/#laws.2.13.0">1997 c 7 art 2 s 13</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.057">
        <h1 class="shn">144.057 BACKGROUND STUDIES ON LICENSEES AND OTHER PERSONNEL.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.057.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Background studies required.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as specified in paragraph (b), the commissioner of health shall contract with the commissioner of human services to conduct background studies of:</p>
          <p>(1) individuals providing services that have direct contact, as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245C.02#stat.245C.02.11">245C.02, subdivision 11</a>, with patients and residents in hospitals, boarding care homes, outpatient surgical centers licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.58">144.58</a>; nursing homes and home care agencies licensed under chapter 144A; assisted living facilities and assisted living facilities with dementia care licensed under chapter 144G; and board and lodging establishments that are registered to provide supportive or health supervision services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/157.17">157.17</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) individuals specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245C.03#stat.245C.03.1">245C.03, subdivision 1</a>, who perform direct contact services in a nursing home or a home care agency licensed under chapter 144A; an assisted living facility or assisted living facility with dementia care licensed under chapter 144G; or a boarding care home licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.58">144.58</a>. If the individual under study resides outside Minnesota, the study must include a check for substantiated findings of maltreatment of adults and children in the individual's state of residence when the information is made available by that state, and must include a check of the National Crime Information Center database;</p>
          <p>(3) all other employees in assisted living facilities or assisted living facilities with dementia care licensed under chapter 144G, nursing homes licensed under chapter 144A, and boarding care homes licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.58">144.58</a>. A disqualification of an individual in this section shall disqualify the individual from positions allowing direct contact or access to patients or residents receiving services. "Access" means physical access to a client or the client's personal property without continuous, direct supervision as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245C.02#stat.245C.02.8">245C.02, subdivision 8</a>, when the employee's employment responsibilities do not include providing direct contact services;</p>
          <p>(4) individuals employed by a supplemental nursing services agency, as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.70">144A.70</a>, who are providing services in health care facilities;</p>
          <p>(5) controlling persons of a supplemental nursing services agency, as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.70">144A.70</a>; and</p>
          <p>(6) license applicants, owners, managerial officials, and controlling individuals who are required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.476#stat.144A.476.1">144A.476, subdivision 1</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144G.13#stat.144G.13.1">144G.13, subdivision 1</a>, to undergo a background study under chapter 245C, regardless of the licensure status of the license applicant, owner, managerial official, or controlling individual.</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioner of human services shall not conduct a background study on any individual identified in paragraph (a), clauses (1) to (5), if the individual has a valid license issued by a health-related licensing board as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.01#stat.214.01.2">214.01, subdivision 2</a>, and has completed the criminal background check as required in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.075">214.075</a>. An entity that is affiliated with individuals who meet the requirements of this paragraph must separate those individuals from the entity's roster for NETStudy 2.0.</p>
          <p>(c) If a facility or program is licensed by the Department of Human Services and subject to the background study provisions of chapter 245C and is also licensed by the Department of Health, the Department of Human Services is solely responsible for the background studies of individuals in the jointly licensed programs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.057.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Responsibilities of Department of Human Services.</span></h2>
          <p>The Department of Human Services shall conduct the background studies required by subdivision 1 in compliance with the provisions of chapter 245C. For the purpose of this section, the term "residential program" shall include all facilities described in subdivision 1. The Department of Human Services shall provide necessary forms and instructions, shall conduct the necessary background studies of individuals, and shall provide notification of the results of the studies to the facilities, supplemental nursing services agencies, individuals, and the commissioner of health. Individuals shall be disqualified under the provisions of chapter 245C. If an individual is disqualified, the Department of Human Services shall notify the facility, the supplemental nursing services agency, and the individual and shall inform the individual of the right to request a reconsideration of the disqualification by submitting the request to the Department of Health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.057.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Reconsiderations.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall review and decide reconsideration requests, including the granting of variances, in accordance with the procedures and criteria contained in chapter 245C. The commissioner must set aside a disqualification for an individual who requests reconsideration and who meets the criteria described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245C.22#stat.245C.22.4">245C.22, subdivision 4</a>, paragraph (d). The commissioner's decision shall be provided to the individual and to the Department of Human Services. The commissioner's decision to grant or deny a reconsideration of disqualification is the final administrative agency action, except for the provisions under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245C.25">245C.25</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245C.27">245C.27</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245C.28#stat.245C.28.3">245C.28, subdivision 3</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.057.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Responsibilities of facilities and agencies.</span></h2>
          <p>Facilities and agencies described in subdivision 1 shall be responsible for cooperating with the departments in implementing the provisions of this section. The responsibilities imposed on applicants and licensees under chapters 245A and 245C shall apply to these facilities and supplemental nursing services agencies. The provision of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245C.09">245C.09</a>, shall apply to applicants, licensees, registrants, or an individual's refusal to cooperate with the completion of the background studies. Supplemental nursing services agencies subject to the registration requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.71">144A.71</a> must maintain records verifying compliance with the background study requirements under this section.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.057.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/229/#laws.3.4.0">1995 c 229 art 3 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/305/#laws.1.35.0">1996 c 305 art 1 s 35</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/408/#laws.10.1.0">1996 c 408 art 10 s 1</a>-3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/248/#laws.0.1.0">1997 c 248 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.7.1.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 7 s 1</a>; art 14 s 2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/379/#laws.1.49.0">2002 c 379 art 1 s 49</a>,113; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/15/#laws.1.33.0">2003 c 15 art 1 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.7.2.0">2015 c 71 art 7 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/60/#laws.1.47.0">2019 c 60 art 1 s 47; art 4 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.2.12.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 2 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/98/#laws.1.1.0">2022 c 98 art 1 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.0571"><b>144.0571</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.10.148.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 10 s 148</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.0572">
        <h1 class="shn">144.0572 CRIMINAL HISTORY BACKGROUND CHECKS ON APPLICANTS, LICENSEES, AND OTHER OCCUPATIONS REGULATED BY COMMISSIONER OF HEALTH.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.0572.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Criminal history background check requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Beginning January 1, 2018, an applicant for initial licensure, temporary licensure, or relicensure after a lapse in licensure as an audiologist or speech-language pathologist, a speech-language pathology assistant, or an applicant for initial certification as a hearing instrument dispenser, must submit to a criminal history records check of state data completed by the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension (BCA) and a national criminal history records check, including a search of the records of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI).</p>
          <p>(b) Beginning January 1, 2020, an applicant for a renewal license or certificate as an audiologist, speech-language pathologist, or hearing instrument dispenser who was licensed or obtained a certificate before January 1, 2018, must submit to a criminal history records check of state data completed by the BCA and a national criminal history records check, including a search of the records of the FBI.</p>
          <p>(c) An applicant must submit to a background study under chapter 245C.</p>
          <p>(d) The criminal history records check must be structured so that any new crimes that an applicant or licensee or certificate holder commits after the initial background check are flagged in the BCA's or FBI's database and reported back to the commissioner of human services.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.0572.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Procedures.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner shall contract with the Department of Human Services to process the criminal history background check requirements through NETStudy 2.0, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245C.02">245C.02</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) The Department of Human Services shall conduct the criminal history background checks according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.057">144.057</a>, except that:</p>
          <p>(1) all applicants must submit to a fingerprint-based criminal history records check of state data completed by the BCA and a national criminal history records check, including a search of the records of the FBI;</p>
          <p>(2) the Department of Human Services shall complete the check and the study and notify the commissioner of health if the applicant, licensee, or certificate holder has a criminal history as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245C.15">245C.15</a>; and</p>
          <p>(3) the Department of Human Services shall simultaneously conduct a background study on each applicant according to chapter 245C.</p>
          <p>(c) When making a determination whether to issue a license, deny a license, or issue a conditional license or other credential to practice an occupation regulated by the Department of Health, the commissioner or the commissioner's designee shall evaluate a criminal conviction, guilty plea, Alford plea, judicial determination, or preponderance of evidence to determine an applicant's risk of harm using the criteria in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/364.03">364.03</a>.</p>
          <p>(d) Before taking disciplinary action against an applicant or a licensee based on a criminal conviction, judicial determination, admission in court, Alford plea, or preponderance of evidence, the commissioner of health shall provide the applicant or licensee an opportunity to complete or challenge the accuracy of the criminal history information. The applicant or licensee shall have 30 calendar days following notice from the commissioner of the intent to deny licensure or take disciplinary action to request an opportunity to correct or complete the record prior to the commissioner taking disciplinary action. The commissioner shall provide the applicant up to 180 days to challenge the accuracy or completeness of the report with the agency responsible for the record. This subdivision does not affect the right of the subject of the data to contest the accuracy or completeness under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.04">13.04, subdivision </a>4.</p>
          <p>(e) The checks and studies must be structured so that any new crimes that an applicant or licensee commits after the initial background check are flagged in the BCA's or FBI's database and reported back to the commissioner of human services.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.0572.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Applicant, licensee, or other regulated individual's responsibilities.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Applicants, licensees, and individuals seeking a credential to practice one of the public health occupations listed in subdivision 1 must submit a complete criminal history records check consent form, a complete background study consent form, and a full set of fingerprints as required by the Department of Human Services in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245C.05">245C.05</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) The applicant or license holder is responsible for paying to the Department of Human Services all fees associated with the preparation of the fingerprints, the criminal records check consent form, and the criminal background check.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.0572.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.10.56.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 10 s 56</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.25.1.0">2024 c 127 art 25 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>The amendment to subdivision 1 by Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 1, is effective July 1, 2025. Laws 2024, chapter 127, article 25, section 1, the effective date.</p>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.058">
        <h1 class="shn">144.058 INTERPRETER SERVICES QUALITY INITIATIVE.</h1>
        <p class="in">(a) The commissioner of health shall establish a voluntary statewide roster and develop a plan for a registry and certification process for interpreters who provide high quality, spoken language health care interpreter services. The roster, registry, and certification process shall be based on the findings and recommendations set forth by the Interpreter Services Work Group required under Laws 2007, chapter 147, article 12, section 13.</p>
        <p class="in">(b) By January 1, 2009, the commissioner shall establish a roster of all available interpreters to address access concerns, particularly in rural areas.</p>
        <p class="in">(c) By January 15, 2010, the commissioner shall:</p>
        <p class="in">(1) develop a plan for a registry of spoken language health care interpreters, including:</p>
        <p class="in">(i) development of standards for registration that set forth educational requirements, training requirements, demonstration of language proficiency and interpreting skills, agreement to abide by a code of ethics, and a criminal background check;</p>
        <p class="in">(ii) recommendations for appropriate alternate requirements in languages for which testing and training programs do not exist;</p>
        <p class="in">(iii) recommendations for appropriate fees; and</p>
        <p class="in">(iv) recommendations for establishing and maintaining the standards for inclusion in the registry; and</p>
        <p class="in">(2) develop a plan for implementing a certification process based on national testing and certification processes for spoken language interpreters 12 months after the establishment of a national certification process.</p>
        <p class="in">(d) The commissioner shall consult with the Interpreter Stakeholder Group of the Upper Midwest Translators and Interpreters Association for advice on the standards required to plan for the development of a registry and certification process.</p>
        <p class="in">(e) The commissioner shall charge an annual fee of $50 to include an interpreter in the roster. Fee revenue shall be deposited in the state government special revenue fund. All fees are nonrefundable.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.058.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/363/#laws.17.2.0">2008 c 363 art 17 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.59.8.0">2024 c 127 art 59 s 8</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.059">
        <h1 class="shn">144.059 PALLIATIVE CARE ADVISORY COUNCIL.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.059.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Membership.</span></h2>
          <p>The Palliative Care Advisory Council shall consist of 18 public members.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.059.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Public members.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner shall appoint, in the manner provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/15.0597">15.0597</a>, 18 public members, including the following:</p>
          <p>(1) two physicians, of which one is certified by the American Board of Hospice and Palliative Medicine;</p>
          <p>(2) two registered nurses or advanced practice registered nurses, of which one is certified by the National Board for Certification of Hospice and Palliative Nurses;</p>
          <p>(3) one care coordinator experienced in working with people with serious or chronic illness and their families;</p>
          <p>(4) one spiritual counselor experienced in working with people with serious or chronic illness and their families;</p>
          <p>(5) three licensed health professionals, such as complementary and alternative health care practitioners, dietitians or nutritionists, pharmacists, or physical therapists, who are neither physicians nor nurses, but who have experience as members of a palliative care interdisciplinary team working with people with serious or chronic illness and their families;</p>
          <p>(6) one licensed social worker experienced in working with people with serious or chronic illness and their families;</p>
          <p>(7) four patients or personal caregivers experienced with serious or chronic illness;</p>
          <p>(8) one representative of a health plan company;</p>
          <p>(9) one physician assistant that is a member of the American Academy of Hospice and Palliative Medicine; and</p>
          <p>(10) two members from any of the categories described in clauses (1) to (9).</p>
          <p>(b) Council membership must include, where possible, representation that is racially, culturally, linguistically, geographically, and economically diverse.</p>
          <p>(c) The council must include at least six members who reside outside Anoka, Carver, Chisago, Dakota, Hennepin, Isanti, Mille Lacs, Ramsey, Scott, Sherburne, Sibley, Stearns, Washington, or Wright Counties.</p>
          <p>(d) To the extent possible, council membership must include persons who have experience in palliative care research, palliative care instruction in a medical or nursing school setting, palliative care services for veterans as a provider or recipient, or pediatric care.</p>
          <p>(e) Council membership must include health professionals who have palliative care work experience or expertise in palliative care delivery models in a variety of inpatient, outpatient, and community settings, including acute care, long-term care, or hospice, with a variety of populations, including pediatric, youth, and adult patients.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.059.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Term.</span></h2>
          <p>Members of the council shall serve for a term of three years and may be reappointed. Members shall serve until their successors have been appointed.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.059.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Administration.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner or the commissioner's designee shall provide meeting space and administrative services for the council.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.059.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Chairs.</span></h2>
          <p>At the council's first meeting, and biannually thereafter, the members shall elect a chair and a vice-chair whose duties shall be established by the council.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.059.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Meeting.</span></h2>
          <p>The council shall meet at least twice yearly.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.059.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">No compensation.</span></h2>
          <p>Public members of the council serve without compensation or reimbursement for expenses.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.059.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Duties.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The council shall consult with and advise the commissioner on matters related to the establishment, maintenance, operation, and outcomes evaluation of palliative care initiatives in the state.</p>
          <p>(b) By February 15 of each year, the council shall submit to the chairs and ranking minority members of the committees of the senate and the house of representatives with primary jurisdiction over health care a report containing:</p>
          <p>(1) the advisory council's assessment of the availability of palliative care in the state;</p>
          <p>(2) the advisory council's analysis of barriers to greater access to palliative care; and</p>
          <p>(3) recommendations for legislative action, with draft legislation to implement the recommendations.</p>
          <p>(c) The Department of Health shall publish the report each year on the department's website.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.059.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Open meetings.</span></h2>
          <p>The council is subject to the requirements of chapter 13D.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.059.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.</h2>
          <p>MS 2022 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.4.113.0">2023 c 70 art 4 s 113</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.059.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.10.57.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 10 s 57</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.06">
        <h1 class="shn">144.06 STATE COMMISSIONER OF HEALTH TO PROVIDE INSTRUCTION.</h1>
        <p>The state commissioner of health, hereinafter referred to as the commissioner, is hereby authorized to provide instruction and advice to expectant mothers and fathers during pregnancy and to mothers, fathers, and their infants after childbirth; and to employ such persons as may be necessary to carry out the requirements of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.06">144.06</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.07">144.07</a>. The instruction, advice, and care shall be given only to applicants residing within the state. No person receiving aid under this section and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.07">144.07</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.09">144.09</a> shall for this reason be affected thereby in any civil or political rights, nor shall the person's identity be disclosed except upon written order of the commissioner.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.06.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/29">5340</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/29">5341</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/29">5342</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1921/0/392/#laws.0.1.0">1921 c 392 s 1</a>-3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/31/#laws.0.2.0">1981 c 31 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.061">
        <h1 class="shn">144.061 EARLY DENTAL PREVENTION INITIATIVE.</h1>
        <p>(a) The commissioner of health, in collaboration with the commissioner of human services, shall implement a statewide initiative to increase awareness among communities of color and recent immigrants on the importance of early preventive dental intervention for infants and toddlers before and after primary teeth appear.</p>
        <p>(b) The commissioner shall develop educational materials and information for expectant and new parents within the targeted communities that include the importance of early dental care to prevent early cavities, including proper cleaning techniques and feeding habits, before and after primary teeth appear.</p>
        <p>(c) The commissioner shall develop a distribution plan to ensure that the materials are distributed to expectant and new parents within the targeted communities, including, but not limited to, making the materials available to health care providers, community clinics, WIC sites, and other relevant sites within the targeted communities.</p>
        <p>(d) In developing these materials and distribution plan, the commissioner shall work collaboratively with members of the targeted communities, dental providers, pediatricians, child care providers, and home visiting nurses.</p>
        <p>(e) The commissioner shall, with input from stakeholders listed in paragraph (d), develop and pilot incentives to encourage early dental care within one year of an infant's teeth erupting.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.061.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.8.23.0">2015 c 71 art 8 s 23</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.062">
        <h1 class="shn">144.062 VACCINE COST REDUCTION PROGRAM.</h1>
        <p>The commissioner of administration, after consulting with the commissioner of health, shall negotiate discounts or rebates on vaccine or may purchase vaccine at reduced prices. Vaccines may be offered for sale to medical care providers at the department's cost plus a fee for administrative costs. As a condition of receiving the vaccine at reduced cost, a medical care provider must agree to pass on the savings to patients. The commissioner of health may transfer money appropriated for other Department of Health programs to the commissioner of administration for the initial cost of purchasing vaccine, provided the money is repaid by the end of each state fiscal year and the commissioner of management and budget approves the transfer. Proceeds from the sale of vaccines to medical care providers, including fees collected for administrative costs, are appropriated to the commissioner of administration. If the commissioner of administration, in consultation with the commissioner of health, determines that a vaccine cost reduction program is not economically feasible or cost-effective, the commissioner may elect not to implement the program.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.062.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/568/#laws.2.5.0">1990 c 568 art 2 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/7/#laws.2.14.0">1997 c 7 art 2 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/101/#laws.2.109.0">2009 c 101 art 2 s 109</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.064">
        <h1 class="shn">144.064 THE VIVIAN ACT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.064.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Short title.</span></h2>
          <p>This section shall be known and may be cited as the "Vivian Act."</p>
        </div>
