              <td style="text-align: right;">$4,715</td>
              <td></td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
              <td>Nonprofit educational institutions</td>
              <td></td>
              <td style="text-align: right;">$345</td>
              <td></td>
            </tr>
          </table>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1205.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Penalty for late payment.</span></h2>
          <p>An annual fee or a license renewal fee submitted to the commissioner after the due date specified by rule must be accompanied by an additional amount equal to 25 percent of the fee due.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1205.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Inspections.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall make periodic safety inspections of the radioactive material and source and special nuclear material of a licensee. The commissioner shall prescribe the frequency of safety inspections by rule.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1205.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Recovery of reinspection cost.</span></h2>
          <p>If the commissioner finds serious violations of public health standards during an inspection under subdivision 6, the licensee must pay all costs associated with subsequent reinspection of the source. The costs shall be the actual costs incurred by the commissioner and include, but are not limited to, labor, transportation, per diem, materials, legal fees, testing, and monitoring costs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1205.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Reciprocity fee.</span></h2>
          <p>A licensee submitting an application for reciprocal recognition of a materials license issued by another agreement state or the United States Nuclear Regulatory Commission for a period of 180 days or less during a calendar year must pay $2,400. For a period of 181 days or more, the licensee must obtain a license under subdivision 4.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1205.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Fees for license amendments.</span></h2>
          <p>A licensee must pay a fee of $600 to amend a license as follows:</p>
          <p>(1) to amend a license requiring review including, but not limited to, addition of isotopes, procedure changes, new authorized users, or a new radiation safety officer; or</p>
          <p>(2) to amend a license requiring review and a site visit including, but not limited to, facility move or addition of processes.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1205.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Fees for general license registrations.</span></h2>
          <p>A person required to register generally licensed devices according to Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4731.3215">4731.3215</a>, must pay an annual registration fee of $450.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.1205.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.1.29.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 1 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/379/#laws.1.113.0">2002 c 379 art 1 s 113</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/236/#laws.0.1.0">2004 c 236 s 1</a>-4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/85/#laws.0.1.0">2007 c 85 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/0/30/#laws.3.11.0">2021 c 30 art 3 s 11</a>-15</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.121">
        <h1 class="shn">144.121 X-RAY MACHINES; OTHER SOURCES OF IONIZING RADIATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Registration; fees.</span></h2>
          <p>The fee for the registration for x-ray equipment and other sources of ionizing radiation required to be registered under rules adopted by the state commissioner of health pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.12">144.12</a>, shall be in an amount as described in subdivision 1a pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.122">144.122</a>. The registration shall expire and be renewed as prescribed by the commissioner pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.122">144.122</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Fees for ionizing radiation-producing equipment.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A facility with ionizing radiation-producing equipment and other sources of ionizing radiation must pay an initial or annual renewal registration fee consisting of a base facility fee of $100 and an additional fee for each x-ray tube, as follows:</p>
          <table>
            <col style="width:7.692307692307693%">
            <col style="width:38.4615384615385%">
            <col style="width:39.2307692307692%">
            <col style="width:6.923076923076923%">
            <col style="width:7.692307692307693%">
            <tr>
              <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: right;">(1)</td>
              <td>medical or veterinary equipment</td>
              <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: right;">$</td>
              <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: right;">100</td>
              <td></td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
              <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: right;">(2)</td>
              <td>dental x-ray equipment</td>
              <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: right;">$</td>
              <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: right;">40</td>
              <td></td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
              <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: right;">(3)</td>
              <td>x-ray equipment not used on humans or animals</td>
              <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: right;">$</td>
              <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: right;">100</td>
              <td></td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
              <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: right;">(4)</td>
              <td>devices with sources of ionizing radiation not used on humans or animals</td>
              <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: right;">$</td>
              <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: right;">100</td>
              <td></td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
              <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: right;">(5)</td>
              <td>security screening system</td>
              <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: right;">$</td>
              <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: right;">100</td>
              <td></td>
            </tr>
          </table>
          <p>(b) A facility with radiation therapy and accelerator equipment must pay an initial or annual registration fee of $500. A facility with an industrial accelerator must pay an initial or annual registration fee of $150.</p>
          <p>(c) Electron microscopy equipment is exempt from the registration fee requirements of this section.</p>
          <p>(d) For purposes of this section, a security screening system means ionizing radiation-producing equipment designed and used for security screening of humans who are in the custody of a correctional or detention facility, and used by the facility to image and identify contraband items concealed within or on all sides of a human body. For purposes of this section, a correctional or detention facility is a facility licensed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/241.021">241.021 </a>and operated by a state agency or political subdivision charged with detection, enforcement, or incarceration in respect to state criminal and traffic laws.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.1b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.<span class="headnote">Penalty fee for late registration.</span></h2>
          <p>Applications for initial or renewal registrations submitted to the commissioner after the time specified by the commissioner shall be accompanied by an amount equal to 25 percent of the fee due in addition to the fees prescribed in subdivision 1a.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.1c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1c.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/85/#laws.0.5.0">2007 c 85 s 5</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.1d">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1d.<span class="headnote">Handheld dental x-ray equipment.</span></h2>
          <p>A facility that uses handheld dental x-ray equipment according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.1215">144.1215</a> must comply with this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Inspections.</span></h2>
          <p>Periodic radiation safety inspections of the x-ray equipment and other sources of ionizing radiation shall be made by the commissioner of health. The frequency of safety inspections shall be prescribed by the commissioner on the basis of the frequency of use of the x-ray equipment and other source of ionizing radiation, provided that each source shall be inspected at least once every four years.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.1.17.0">2020 c 115 art 1 s 17</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/85/#laws.0.5.0">2007 c 85 s 5</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Examination for individual operating x-ray systems.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) An individual in a facility with x-ray systems for use on living humans that is registered under subdivision 1 may not operate, nor may the facility allow the individual to operate, x-ray systems unless the individual has passed a national or state examination.</p>
          <p>(b) Individuals who may operate x-ray systems include:</p>
          <p>(1) an individual who has passed the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists (ARRT) registry for radiography examination;</p>
          <p>(2) an individual who has passed the American Chiropractic Registry of Radiologic Technologists (ACRRT) registry examination and is limited to radiography of spines and extremities;</p>
          <p>(3) a registered limited scope x-ray operator and a registered bone densitometry equipment operator who passed the examination requirements in paragraphs (d) and (e) and practices according to subdivision 5a;</p>
          <p>(4) an x-ray operator who has the original certificate or the original letter of passing the examination that was required before January 1, 2008, under Minnesota Statutes 2008, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.121#stat.144.121.5a">144.121, subdivision 5a</a>, paragraph (b), clause (1);</p>
          <p>(5) an individual who has passed the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists (ARRT) registry for radiation therapy examination according to subdivision 5e;</p>
          <p>(6) a cardiovascular technologist according to subdivision 5c;</p>
          <p>(7) a nuclear medicine technologist according to subdivision 5d;</p>
          <p>(8) an individual who has passed the examination for a dental hygienist under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/150A.06">150A.06</a> and only operates dental x-ray systems;</p>
          <p>(9) an individual who has passed the examination for a dental therapist under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/150A.06">150A.06</a> and only operates dental x-ray systems;</p>
          <p>(10) an individual who has passed the examination for a dental assistant under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/150A.06">150A.06</a> and only operates dental x-ray systems;</p>
          <p>(11) an individual who has passed the examination under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/3100.8500">3100.8500</a>, subpart 3, and only operates dental x-ray systems; and</p>
          <p>(12) a qualified practitioner who is licensed by a health-related licensing board with active practice authority and is working within the practitioner's scope of practice.</p>
          <p>(c) Except for individuals under clauses (3) and (4), an individual who is participating in a training or educational program in any of the occupations listed in paragraph (b) is exempt from the examination requirement within the scope and for the duration of the training or educational program.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) The Minnesota examination for limited scope x-ray operators must include:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) radiation protection, radiation physics and radiobiology, equipment operation and quality assurance, image acquisition and technical evaluation, and patient interactions and management; and</p>
          <p class="in">(2) at least one of the following regions of the human anatomy: chest, extremities, skull and sinus, spine, or podiatry. The examinations must include the anatomy of, and radiographic positions and projections for, the specific regions.</p>
          <p>(e) The examination for bone densitometry equipment operators must include:</p>
          <p>(1) osteoporosis, bone physiology, bone health and patient education, patient preparation, fundamental principals, biological effects of radiation, units of measurements, radiation protection in bone densitometry, fundamentals of x-ray production, quality control, measuring bone mineral testing, determining quality in bone mineral testing, file and database management; and</p>
          <p>(2) dual x-ray absorptiometry scanning of the lumbar spine, proximal femur, and forearm. The examination must include the anatomy, scan acquisition, and scan analysis for these three procedures.</p>
          <p class="in">(f) A limited scope x-ray operator, and a bone densitometry equipment operator, who are required to take an examination under this subdivision must submit to the commissioner a registration application for the examination and a $25 processing fee. The processing fee shall be deposited in the state treasury and credited to the state government special revenue fund.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.5a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5a.<span class="headnote">Limited scope x-ray and bone densitometry equipment operator practice.</span></h2>
          <p class="in"> A registered limited scope x-ray operator and a registered bone densitometry equipment operator may only practice medical radiography on limited regions of the human anatomy for which the operator has successfully passed an examination identified in subdivision 5, paragraphs (d) and (e), and may not operate computed tomography, cone beam computed tomography, the use of contrast media, and the use of fluoroscopic or mammographic x-ray systems.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.5b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5b.</h2>
          <p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.1.17.0">2020 c 115 art 1 s 17</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.5c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5c.<span class="headnote">Cardiovascular technologist practice.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Cardiovascular technologists may assist with the operation of fluoroscopy equipment if they:</p>
          <p>(1) are credentialed by Cardiovascular Credentialing International as a registered cardiovascular invasive specialist or as a registered cardiac electrophysiology specialist, are a graduate of an educational program accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs, which uses the standards and criteria established by the Joint Review Committee on Education in Cardiovascular Technology, or are designated on a variance granted by the commissioner effective July 31, 2019; and</p>
          <p>(2) are under the personal supervision and in the physical presence of a qualified practitioner for diagnosing or treating a disease or condition of the cardiovascular system in fluoroscopically guided interventional procedures. Cardiovascular technologists may not activate the fluoroscopic system or evaluate quality control tests.</p>
          <p>(b) A cardiovascular technologist who is participating in a training or educational program in any of the occupations listed in this subdivision is exempt from the examination requirement within the scope and for the duration of the training or educational program.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.5d">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5d.<span class="headnote">Nuclear medicine technologist practice.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Nuclear medicine technologists who have passed the primary pathway credential in Nuclear Medicine Technology Certification Board (NMTCB) for nuclear medicine or the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists (ARRT) for nuclear medicine technology or the American Society of Clinical Pathologists (NM) (ASCP) may operate a fusion imaging device or a dual imaging device that uses radioactive material as a point source in transmission scanning and attenuation correction.</p>
          <p>(b) A nuclear medicine technologist in paragraph (a) may only operate a stand-alone computed tomography x-ray system if the technologist has passed the Nuclear Medicine Technology Certification Board for computed tomography (CT) or is credentialed in computed tomography (CT) from the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists (ARRT).</p>
          <p>(c) A nuclear medicine technologist who meets the requirements under paragraph (a) and who is participating in a training or educational program to obtain a credential under paragraph (b) is exempt from the examination requirement within the scope and for the duration of the training or educational program.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.5e">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5e.<span class="headnote">Radiation therapy technologist practice.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A radiation therapy technologist who has passed the primary pathway credential in radiation therapy may operate radiation therapy accelerator and simulator x-ray systems.</p>
          <p>(b) A radiation therapy technologist in paragraph (a) may only operate a stand-alone computed tomography x-ray system if the technologist has passed and is credentialed in computed tomography (CT) from the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists (ARRT).</p>
          <p>(c) A radiation therapy technologist who meets the requirements under paragraph (a) and who is participating in a training or educational program to obtain a credential under paragraph (b) is exempt from the examination requirement within the scope and for the duration of the training or educational program.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Inspection.</span></h2>
          <p>At the time a facility with x-ray equipment is inspected by the commissioner of health in accordance with subdivision 2, an individual operating x-ray equipment in the facility must be able to show compliance with the requirements of subdivision 5.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/86/#laws.2.6.0">1999 c 86 art 2 s 6</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Exemption from examination requirements; operators of certain bone densitometers.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) This subdivision applies to a bone densitometer that is used on humans to estimate bone mineral content and bone mineral density in a region of a finger on a person's nondominant hand, gives an x-ray dose equivalent of less than 0.001 microsieverts per scan, and has an x-ray leakage exposure rate of less than two milliroentgens per hour at a distance of one meter, provided that the bone densitometer is operating in accordance with manufacturer specifications.</p>
          <p>(b) An individual who operates a bone densitometer that satisfies the definition in paragraph (a) and the facility in which an individual operates such a bone densitometer are exempt from the requirements of subdivisions 5 and 6.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.121.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Exemption from examination requirements; operators of security screening systems.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An employee of a correctional or detention facility who operates a security screening system and the facility in which the system is being operated are exempt from the requirements of subdivisions 5 and 6.</p>
          <p>(b) An employee of a correctional or detention facility who operates a security screening system and the facility in which the system is being operated must meet the requirements of a variance to Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4732.0305">4732.0305</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4732.0565">4732.0565</a>, issued under Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4717.7000">4717.7000</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4717.7050">4717.7050</a>. This paragraph expires on December 31 of the year that the permanent rules adopted by the commissioner governing security screening systems are published in the State Register.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.121.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/81/#laws.0.1.0">1974 c 81 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/310/#laws.0.35.0">1975 c 310 s 35</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/188/#laws.0.1.0">1993 c 188 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/146/#laws.0.1.0">1995 c 146 s 1</a>-3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/203/#laws.2.7.0">1997 c 203 art 2 s 7</a>-10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/245/#laws.2.20.0">1999 c 245 art 2 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/85/#laws.0.2.0">2007 c 85 s 2</a>,3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/123/#laws.0.1.0">2007 c 123 s 1</a>-3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/277/#laws.1.13.0">2008 c 277 art 1 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.10.2.0">2009 c 79 art 10 s 2</a>,3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/125/#laws.1.108.0">2013 c 125 art 1 s 108</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/119/#laws.0.7.0">2016 c 119 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/17/#laws.0.1.0">2019 c 17 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.11.15.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 11 s 15</a>,16; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.1.1.0">2020 c 115 art 1 s 1</a>-9</p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.1211"><b>144.1211</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/206/#laws.0.25.0">1993 c 206 s 25</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.1212">
        <h1 class="shn">144.1212 NOTICE TO PATIENT; MAMMOGRAM RESULTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1212.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, "facility" has the meaning provided in United States Code, title 42, section 263b(a)(3)(A).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1212.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Required notice.</span></h2>
          <p>A facility at which a mammography examination is performed shall, if a patient is categorized by the facility as having heterogeneously dense breasts or extremely dense breasts based on the Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System established by the American College of Radiology, include in the summary of the written report that is sent to the patient, as required by the federal Mammography Quality Standards Act, United States Code, title 42, section 263b, notice that the patient has dense breast tissue, that this may make it more difficult to detect cancer on a mammogram, and that it may increase her risk of breast cancer. The following language may be used:</p>
          <p>"Your mammogram shows that your breast tissue is dense. Dense breast tissue is relatively common and is found in more than 40 percent of women. However, dense breast tissue may make it more difficult to identify precancerous lesions or cancer through a mammogram and may also be associated with an increased risk of breast cancer. This information about the results of your mammogram is given to you to raise your own awareness and to help inform your conversations with your treating clinician who has received a report of your mammogram results. Together you can decide which screening options are right for you based on your mammogram results, individual risk factors, or physical examination."</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.1212.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.6.2.0">2014 c 291 art 6 s 2</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.1215">
        <h1 class="shn">144.1215 AUTHORIZATION TO USE HANDHELD DENTAL X-RAY EQUIPMENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1215.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition; handheld dental x-ray equipment.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, "handheld dental x-ray equipment" means x-ray equipment that is used to take dental radiographs, is designed to be handheld during operation, and is operated by an individual authorized to take dental radiographs under chapter 150A.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1215.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Use authorized.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Handheld dental x-ray equipment may be used if the equipment:</p>
          <p>(1) has been approved for human use by the United States Food and Drug Administration and is being used in a manner consistent with that approval; and</p>
          <p>(2) utilizes a backscatter shield that:</p>
          <p>(i) is composed of a leaded polymer or a substance with a substantially equivalent protective capacity;</p>
          <p>(ii) has at least 0.25 millimeters of lead or lead-shielding equivalent; and</p>
          <p>(iii) is permanently affixed to the handheld dental x-ray equipment.</p>
          <p>(b) The use of handheld dental x-ray equipment is prohibited if the equipment's backscatter shield is broken or not permanently affixed to the system.</p>
          <p>(c) The use of handheld dental x-ray equipment shall not be limited to situations in which it is impractical to transfer the patient to a stationary x-ray system.</p>
          <p>(d) Handheld dental x-ray equipment must be stored when not in use, by being secured in a restricted, locked area of the facility.</p>
          <p>(e) Handheld dental x-ray equipment must be calibrated initially and at intervals that must not exceed 24 months. Calibration must include the test specified in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4732.1100">4732.1100</a>, subpart 11.</p>
          <p>(f) Notwithstanding Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4732.0880">4732.0880</a>, subpart 2, item C, the tube housing and the position-indicating device of handheld dental x-ray equipment may be handheld during an exposure.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1215.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Exemptions from certain shielding requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>Handheld dental x-ray equipment used according to this section and according to manufacturer instructions is exempt from the following requirements for the equipment:</p>
          <p>(1) shielding requirements in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4732.0365">4732.0365</a>, item B; and</p>
          <p>(2) requirements for the location of the x-ray control console or utilization of a protective barrier in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4732.0800">4732.0800</a>, subpart 2, item B, subitems (2) and (3), provided the equipment utilizes a backscatter shield that satisfies the requirements in subdivision 2, paragraph (a), clause (2).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1215.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Compliance with rules.</span></h2>
          <p>A registrant using handheld dental x-ray equipment shall otherwise comply with Minnesota Rules, chapter 4732.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.1215.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.10.58.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 10 s 58</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">FEES, LICENSES, PERMITS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.122">
        <h1 class="shn">144.122 LICENSE, PERMIT, AND SURVEY FEES.</h1>
        <p class="in">(a) The state commissioner of health, by rule, may prescribe procedures and fees for filing with the commissioner as prescribed by statute and for the issuance of original and renewal permits, licenses, registrations, and certifications issued under authority of the commissioner. The expiration dates of the various licenses, permits, registrations, and certifications as prescribed by the rules shall be plainly marked thereon. Fees may include application and examination fees and a penalty fee for renewal applications submitted after the expiration date of the previously issued permit, license, registration, and certification. The commissioner may also prescribe, by rule, reduced fees for permits, licenses, registrations, and certifications when the application therefor is submitted during the last three months of the permit, license, registration, or certification period. Fees proposed to be prescribed in the rules shall be first approved by the Department of Management and Budget. All fees proposed to be prescribed in rules shall be reasonable. The fees shall be in an amount so that the total fees collected by the commissioner will, where practical, approximate the cost to the commissioner in administering the program. All fees collected shall be deposited in the state treasury and credited to the state government special revenue fund unless otherwise specifically appropriated by law for specific purposes.</p>
        <p class="in">(b) The commissioner may charge a fee for voluntary certification of medical laboratories and environmental laboratories, and for environmental and medical laboratory services provided by the department, without complying with paragraph (a) or chapter 14. Fees charged for environment and medical laboratory services provided by the department must be approximately equal to the costs of providing the services.</p>
        <p class="in">(c) The commissioner may develop a schedule of fees for diagnostic evaluations conducted at clinics held by the services for children with disabilities program. All receipts generated by the program are annually appropriated to the commissioner for use in the maternal and child health program.</p>
        <p class="in">(d) The commissioner shall set license fees for hospitals and nursing homes that are not boarding care homes at the following levels:</p>
        <table class="border_none">
          <col style="width:50%">
          <col style="width:50%">
          <tr>
            <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: left;">Joint Commission on Accreditation of <br>Healthcare Organizations (JCAHO) and American Osteopathic Association (AOA) hospitals</td>
            <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: left;">$7,655 plus $16 per bed</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td style="text-align: left;">Non-JCAHO and non-AOA hospitals</td>
            <td style="text-align: left;">$5,280 plus $250 per bed</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: left;">Nursing home</td>
            <td style="text-align: left;">$183 plus $91 per bed until June 30, 2018. $183 plus $100 per bed between July 1, 2018, and June 30, 2020. $183 plus $105 per bed beginning July 1, 2020.</td>
          </tr>
        </table>
        <p class="in">The commissioner shall set license fees for outpatient surgical centers, boarding care homes, supervised living facilities, assisted living facilities, and assisted living facilities with dementia care at the following levels:</p>
        <table class="border_none">
          <col style="width:50%">
          <col style="width:50%">
          <tr>
            <td style="text-align: left;">Outpatient surgical centers</td>
            <td style="text-align: left;">$3,712</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td style="text-align: left;">Boarding care homes</td>
            <td style="text-align: left;">$183 plus $91 per bed</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td style="text-align: left;">Supervised living facilities</td>
            <td style="text-align: left;">$183 plus $91 per bed.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td>Assisted living facilities with dementia care</td>
            <td>$3,000 plus $100 per resident.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td>Assisted living facilities</td>
            <td>$2,000 plus $75 per resident.</td>
          </tr>
        </table>
        <p class="bl">Fees collected under this paragraph are nonrefundable. The fees are nonrefundable even if received before July 1, 2017, for licenses or registrations being issued effective July 1, 2017, or later.</p>
        <p class="in">(e) Unless prohibited by federal law, the commissioner of health shall charge applicants the following fees to cover the cost of any initial certification surveys required to determine a provider's eligibility to participate in the Medicare or Medicaid program:</p>
        <table class="border_none">
          <col style="width:60%">
          <col style="width:27%">
          <col style="width:13%">
          <tr>
            <td style="text-align: left;">Prospective payment surveys for hospitals</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">$</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">900</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td style="text-align: left;">Swing bed surveys for nursing homes</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">$</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">1,200</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td style="text-align: left;">Psychiatric hospitals</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">$</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">1,400</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td style="text-align: left;">Rural health facilities</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">$</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">1,100</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td style="text-align: left;">Portable x-ray providers</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">$</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">500</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td style="text-align: left;">Home health agencies</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">$</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">1,800</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td style="text-align: left;">Outpatient therapy agencies</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">$</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">800</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td style="text-align: left;">End stage renal dialysis providers</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">$</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">2,100</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td style="text-align: left;">Independent therapists</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">$</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">800</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td style="text-align: left;">Comprehensive rehabilitation outpatient facilities</td>
            <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: right;">$</td>
            <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: right;">1,200</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td style="text-align: left;">Hospice providers</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">$</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">1,700</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td style="text-align: left;">Ambulatory surgical providers</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">$</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">1,800</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td style="text-align: left;">Hospitals</td>
            <td style="text-align: right;">$</td>
            <td class="valign_bottom" style="text-align: right;">4,200</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td class="valign_top" style="text-align: left;">Other provider categories or additional<br>resurveys required to complete initial<br>certification</td>
            <td colspan="2" class="valign_top">Actual surveyor costs: average surveyor cost x number of hours for the survey process.</td>
          </tr>
        </table>
        <p class="in">These fees shall be submitted at the time of the application for federal certification and shall not be refunded. All fees collected after the date that the imposition of fees is not prohibited by federal law shall be deposited in the state treasury and credited to the state government special revenue fund.</p>
        <p class="in">(f) Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/16A.1283">16A.1283</a>, the commissioner may adjust the fees assessed on assisted living facilities and assisted living facilities with dementia care under paragraph (d), in a revenue-neutral manner in accordance with the requirements of this paragraph:</p>
        <p class="in">(1) a facility seeking to renew a license shall pay a renewal fee in an amount that is up to ten percent lower than the applicable fee in paragraph (d) if residents who receive home and community-based waiver services under chapter 256S and section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a> comprise more than 50 percent of the facility's capacity in the calendar year prior to the year in which the renewal application is submitted; and</p>
        <p class="in">(2) a facility seeking to renew a license shall pay a renewal fee in an amount that is up to ten percent higher than the applicable fee in paragraph (d) if residents who receive home and community-based waiver services under chapter 256S and section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.49">256B.49</a> comprise less than 50 percent of the facility's capacity during the calendar year prior to the year in which the renewal application is submitted.</p>
        <p class="bl">The commissioner may annually adjust the percentages in clauses (1) and (2), to ensure this paragraph is implemented in a revenue-neutral manner. The commissioner shall develop a method for determining capacity thresholds in this paragraph in consultation with the commissioner of human services and must coordinate the administration of this paragraph with the commissioner of human services for purposes of verification.</p>
        <p>(g) The commissioner shall charge hospitals an annual licensing base fee of $1,826 per hospital, plus an additional $23 per licensed bed or bassinet fee. Revenue shall be deposited to the state government special revenue fund and credited toward trauma hospital designations under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.605">144.605</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.6071">144.6071</a>.</p>
      </div>

      <h1 class="fgh">POOLS; ENCLOSED SPORTS ARENAS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.1222">
        <h1 class="shn">144.1222 PUBLIC POOLS; ENCLOSED SPORTS ARENAS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1222.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Public pools.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall be responsible for the adoption of rules and enforcement of applicable laws and rules relating to the operation, maintenance, design, installation, and construction of public pools and facilities related to them. The commissioner shall adopt rules governing the collection of fees under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.122">144.122</a> to cover the cost of pool construction plan review, monitoring, and inspections.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1222.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Fees.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">All plans and specifications for public pool and spa construction, installation, or alteration or requests for a variance that are submitted to the commissioner according to Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4717.3975">4717.3975</a>, shall be accompanied by the appropriate fees. All public pool construction plans submitted for review after January 1, 2009, must be certified by a professional engineer registered in the state of Minnesota. If the commissioner determines, upon review of the plans, that inadequate fees were paid, the necessary additional fees shall be paid before plan approval. For purposes of determining fees, a project is defined as a proposal to construct or install a public pool, spa, special purpose pool, or wading pool and all associated water treatment equipment and drains, gutters, decks, water recreation features, spray pads, and those design and safety features that are within five feet of any pool or spa. The commissioner shall charge the following fees for plan review and inspection of public pools and spas and for requests for variance from the public pool and spa rules:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) each pool, $1,500;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) each spa pool, $800;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) each slide, $600;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) projects valued at $250,000 or more, the greater of the sum of the fees in clauses (1), (2), and (3) or 0.5 percent of the documented estimated project cost to a maximum fee of $15,000;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) alterations to an existing pool without changing the size or configuration of the pool, $600;</p>
          <p class="in">(6) removal or replacement of pool disinfection equipment only, $100; and</p>
          <p class="in">(7) request for variance from the public pool and spa rules, $500.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1222.1b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.<span class="headnote">Public pool construction.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">For all public pools constructed after January 1, 2009, without a gravity outlet or drain, each pump must be connected to at least two suction outlets, connected in parallel with suction outlet covers that meet ASME/ANSI standards.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1222.1c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1c.<span class="headnote">Public pools; required equipment.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) Beginning January 1, 2009, all public pools with the deepest water being less than four feet deep must have:</p>
          <p>(1) an unblockable suction outlet or drain;</p>
          <p>(2) at least two suction outlets, connected in parallel with suction outlet covers that meet ASME/ANSI standards; or</p>
          <p class="in">(3) a gravity outlet or drain.</p>
          <p>(b) Beginning January 1, 2011, all other existing public pools must have:</p>
          <p>(1) an unblockable suction outlet or drain;</p>
          <p>(2) at least two suction outlets, connected in parallel with suction outlet covers that meet ASME/ANSI standards;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) a gravity outlet or drain; or</p>
          <p class="in">(4) any other system determined by the commissioner to be equally effective as, or better than, the systems listed in this paragraph at preventing or eliminating the risk of injury or death associated with pool drainage systems.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) By June 1, 2008, all drain covers and grates must be installed with screws that meet the manufacturer's specifications.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) By July 1, 2008, and annually thereafter, all public pool owners must certify to the commissioner on a form prescribed by the commissioner that:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) all outlets except for unblockable drains are equipped with covers that have been stamped by the manufacturer that they are in compliance with ASME/ANSI standards; and</p>
          <p class="in">(2) all covers and grates, including mounting rings, have been inspected to ensure that they have been properly installed and are not broken or loose.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1222.1d">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1d.<span class="headnote">Safety inspections.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) The pool operator is required to conduct a physical inspection of the drain covers and grates on a daily basis. The record required under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4717.0750">4717.0750</a>, must indicate that this inspection was completed every day the pool is open for use.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) If at any time an outlet cover or grate is missing, broken, or loose, the pool must be closed immediately. The pool must not be reopened until the missing or broken cover or grate has been replaced according to the manufacturer's specifications, or the loose cover or grate has been reattached to the manufacturer's specifications.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1222.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Pools used for treatment or therapy.</span></h2>
          <p>A pool used by a medical or rehabilitation facility to facilitate treatment or therapy, to which only authorized access is allowed and which is not open for any other public use, is exempt from the requirements of Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4717.1050">4717.1050</a>, regarding warning signs, and Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4717.1650">4717.1650</a>, subpart 1, regarding placards.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1222.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Portable wading pools at family day care or group family day care homes.</span></h2>
          <p>A portable wading pool that is located at a family day care or group family day care home licensed under Minnesota Rules, chapter 9502, or at a home at which child care services are provided under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/142B.05#stat.142B.05.2">142B.05, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (a), clause (2), shall be defined as a private residential pool and not as a public pool for purposes of public swimming pool regulations under Minnesota Rules, chapter 4717, provided that the portable wading pool has a maximum depth of 24 inches and is capable of being manually emptied and moved.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1222.2b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2b.<span class="headnote">Swimming pools at family day care or group family day care homes.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4717.0250">4717.0250</a>, subpart 8, a swimming pool that is located at a family day care or group family day care home licensed under Minnesota Rules, chapter 9502, shall not be considered a public pool, and is exempt from the requirements for public pools in Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4717.0150">4717.0150</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4717.3975">4717.3975</a>. If the provider chooses to allow children cared for at the family day care or group family day care home to use the swimming pool located at the home, the provider must satisfy the requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/142B.41#stat.142B.41.9">142B.41, subdivision 9</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1222.2c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2c.<span class="headnote">Pools used for adult-only recreation.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4717.1850">4717.1850</a>, a pool with a zero-depth area may be used without a lifeguard present if access to the pool area is prohibited to individuals under the age of 18 years during the time a lifeguard is not present.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1222.2d">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2d.<span class="headnote">Hot tubs on rental houseboats.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A hot water pool intended for seated recreational use, including a hot tub or whirlpool, that is located on a houseboat that is rented to the public is not a public pool and is exempt from the requirements for public pools under Minnesota Rules, chapter 4717.</p>
          <p>(b) A hot water pool under this subdivision must be conspicuously posted with the following notice to renters:</p>
          <p class="ce">"NOTICE</p>
          <p>This spa is exempt from state and local sanitary requirements that prevent disease transmission.</p>
          <p class="ce">USE AT YOUR OWN RISK</p>
          <p>This notice is required under Minnesota Statutes, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.1222#stat.144.1222.2d">144.1222, subdivision 2d</a>."</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1222.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Enclosed sports arenas.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall be responsible for the adoption of rules and enforcement of applicable laws and rules relating to indoor air quality in the operation and maintenance of enclosed sports arenas.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1222.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given them.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) "ASME/ANSI standard" means a safety standard accredited by the American National Standards Institute and published by the American Society of Mechanical Engineers.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) "ASTM standard" means a safety standard issued by ASTM International, formerly known as the American Society for Testing and Materials.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) "Public pool" means any pool other than a private residential pool, that is: (1) open to the public generally, whether for a fee or free of charge; (2) open exclusively to members of an organization and their guests; (3) open to residents of a multiunit apartment building, apartment complex, residential real estate development, or other multifamily residential area; (4) open to patrons of a hotel or lodging or other public accommodation facility; or (5) operated by a person in a park, school, licensed child care facility, group home, motel, camp, resort, club, condominium, manufactured home park, or political subdivision with the exception of swimming pools at family day care homes licensed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/142B.41#stat.142B.41.9">142B.41, subdivision 9</a>, paragraph (a).</p>
          <p class="in">(e) "Unblockable suction outlet or drain" means a drain of any size and shape that a human body cannot sufficiently block to create a suction entrapment hazard and meets ASME/ANSI standards.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1222.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Exemptions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) A public swimming pond in existence before January 1, 2008, is not a public pool for purposes of this section and section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/157.16">157.16</a>, and is exempt from the requirements for public swimming pools under Minnesota Rules, chapter 4717.</p>
          <p>(b) A naturally treated swimming pool located in the city of Minneapolis is not a public pool for purposes of this section and section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/157.16">157.16</a>, and is exempt from the requirements for public swimming pools under Minnesota Rules, chapter 4717.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) Notwithstanding paragraphs (a) and (b), a public swimming pond and a naturally treated swimming pool must meet the requirements for public pools described in subdivisions 1c and 1d.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) For purposes of this subdivision, a "public swimming pond" means an artificial body of water contained within a lined, sand-bottom basin, intended for public swimming, relaxation, or recreational use that includes a water circulation system for maintaining water quality and does not include any portion of a naturally occurring lake or stream.</p>
          <p>(e) For purposes of this subdivision, a "naturally treated swimming pool" means an artificial body of water contained in a basin, intended for public swimming, relaxation, or recreational use that uses a chemical free filtration system for maintaining water quality through natural processes, including the use of plants, beneficial bacteria, and microbes.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.1222.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/165/#laws.0.1.0">1995 c 165 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/279/#laws.0.5.0">2002 c 279 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/333/#laws.0.1.0">2002 c 333 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.7.25.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 7 s 25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/50/#laws.0.1.0">2005 c 50 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/130/#laws.0.1.0">2005 c 130 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/328/#laws.0.2.0">2008 c 328 s 2</a>-7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.10.4.0">2009 c 79 art 10 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/83/#laws.0.1.0">2011 c 83 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/247/#laws.2.2.0">2012 c 247 art 2 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/253/#laws.4.1.0">2012 c 253 art 4 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/158/#laws.1.52.0">2016 c 158 art 1 s 52</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/80/#laws.2.74.0">2024 c 80 art 2 s 74</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/115/#laws.16.41.0">2024 c 115 art 16 s 41</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">DIAGNOSTIC IMAGING</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.1225">
        <h1 class="shn">144.1225 ADVANCED DIAGNOSTIC IMAGING SERVICES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1225.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, "advanced diagnostic imaging services" has the meaning given in United States Code, title 42, section 1395M, except that it does not include x-ray, ultrasound, or fluoroscopy.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1225.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Accreditation required.</span></h2>
          <p>(a)(1) Except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (b) and (c), advanced diagnostic imaging services eligible for reimbursement from any source, including, but not limited to, the individual receiving such services and any individual or group insurance contract, plan, or policy delivered in this state, including, but not limited to, private health insurance plans, workers' compensation insurance, motor vehicle insurance, the State Employee Group Insurance Program (SEGIP), and other state health care programs, shall be reimbursed only if the facility at which the service has been conducted and processed is licensed pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a> or accredited by one of the following entities:</p>
          <p>(i) American College of Radiology (ACR);</p>
          <p>(ii) Intersocietal Accreditation Commission (IAC);</p>
          <p>(iii) the Joint Commission; or</p>
          <p>(iv) other relevant accreditation organization designated by the Secretary of the United States Department of Health and Human Services pursuant to United States Code, title 42, section 1395M.</p>
          <p>(2) All accreditation standards recognized under this section must include, but are not limited to:</p>
          <p>(i) provisions establishing qualifications of the physician;</p>
          <p>(ii) standards for quality control and routine performance monitoring by a medical physicist;</p>
          <p>(iii) qualifications of the technologist, including minimum standards of supervised clinical experience;</p>
          <p>(iv) guidelines for personnel and patient safety; and</p>
          <p>(v) standards for initial and ongoing quality control using clinical image review and quantitative testing.</p>
          <p>(b) Any facility that performs advanced diagnostic imaging services and is eligible to receive reimbursement for such services from any source in paragraph (a), clause (1), must obtain licensure pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a> or accreditation pursuant to paragraph (a) by August 1, 2013. Thereafter, all facilities that provide advanced diagnostic imaging services in the state must obtain licensure or accreditation within six months of commencing operations and must maintain either licensure pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a> or accreditation with an accrediting organization as provided in paragraph (a).</p>
          <p>(c) Dental clinics or offices that perform diagnostic imaging through dental cone beam computerized tomography do not need to meet the accreditation or reporting requirements in this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1225.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Reporting.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Advanced diagnostic imaging facilities and providers of advanced diagnostic imaging services must annually report to the commissioner demonstration of accreditation as required under this section.</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioner may promulgate any rules necessary to administer the reporting required under paragraph (a).</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.1225.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/228/#laws.0.1.0">2012 c 228 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/247/#laws.2.3.0">2012 c 247 art 2 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/8/#laws.0.1.0">2013 c 8 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.6.3.0">2014 c 291 art 6 s 3</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.123">
        <h1 class="shn">144.123 FEES FOR DIAGNOSTIC LABORATORY SERVICES; EXCEPTIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.123.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Who must pay.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Except for the limitation contained in this section, the commissioner of health may enter into a contractual agreement to recover costs incurred for analysis for diagnostic purposes for each specimen submitted to the Department of Health by any hospital, laboratory, clinic, or physician. The commissioner shall not charge for any biological materials submitted to the Department of Health as a requirement of Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4605.7040">4605.7040</a>, or for those biological materials requested by the department to gather information for disease prevention or control purposes. The commissioner of health may establish other exceptions to the handling fee as may be necessary to protect the public's health. Funds generated in a contractual agreement made pursuant to this section shall be deposited in a special account and are appropriated to the commissioner for purposes of providing the services specified in the contracts. All such contractual agreements shall be processed in accordance with the provisions of chapter 16C.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.123.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, 2013 c 108 art 12 s 109]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.123.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/49/#laws.0.1.0">1979 c 49 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/424/#laws.0.130.0">1982 c 424 s 130</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/403/#laws.2.8.0">1987 c 403 art 2 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/513/#laws.6.2.0">1992 c 513 art 6 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/1/1/#laws.9.19.0">1Sp1993 c 1 art 9 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.16.6.0">2007 c 147 art 16 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.12.13.0">2013 c 108 art 12 s 13</a>,109</p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">NEWBORN TESTS FOR MEDICAL CONDITIONS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.125">
        <h1 class="shn">144.125 TESTS OF INFANTS FOR HERITABLE AND CONGENITAL DISORDERS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.125.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Duty to perform testing.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) It is the duty of (1) the administrative officer or other person in charge of each institution caring for infants 28 days or less of age, (2) the person required in pursuance of the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.215">144.215</a>, to register the birth of a child, or (3) the nurse midwife or midwife in attendance at the birth, to arrange to have administered to every infant or child in its care tests for heritable and congenital disorders according to subdivision 2 and rules prescribed by the state commissioner of health.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) Testing, recording of test results, reporting of test results, and follow-up of infants with heritable congenital disorders, including hearing loss detected through the early hearing detection and intervention program in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.966">144.966</a>, shall be performed at the times and in the manner prescribed by the commissioner of health.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) The fee to support the newborn screening program, including tests administered under this section and section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.966">144.966</a>, shall be $177 per specimen. This fee amount shall be deposited in the state treasury and credited to the state government special revenue fund.</p>
          <p>(d) The fee to offset the cost of the support services provided under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.966">144.966</a>, subdivision 3a, shall be $15 per specimen. This fee shall be deposited in the state treasury and credited to the general fund.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.125.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Determination of tests to be administered.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The commissioner shall periodically revise the list of tests to be administered for determining the presence of a heritable or congenital disorder. Revisions to the list shall reflect advances in medical science, new and improved testing methods, or other factors that will improve the public health. In determining whether a test must be administered, the commissioner shall take into consideration the adequacy of analytical methods to detect the heritable or congenital disorder, the ability to treat or prevent medical conditions caused by the heritable or congenital disorder, and the severity of the medical conditions caused by the heritable or congenital disorder. The list of tests to be performed may be revised if the changes are recommended by the advisory committee established under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.1255">144.1255</a>, approved by the commissioner, and published in the State Register. The revision is exempt from the rulemaking requirements in chapter 14, and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.385">14.385</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.386">14.386</a> do not apply.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.125.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Information provided to parents and legal guardians.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) The department shall make information and forms available to childbirth education programs and health care providers who provide prenatal care describing the newborn screening program and the provisions of this section to be used in a discussion with expectant parents and parents of newborns. The department shall promote the materials describing the newborn screening program and encourage providers and education programs to thoroughly discuss the program with expectant parents and parents with newborns. The department shall make information and forms about newborn screening available to the persons with a duty to perform testing under this section and to expectant parents and parents of newborns using electronic and other means.</p>
          <p>(b) Prior to collecting a sample, persons with a duty to perform testing under subdivision 1 must:</p>
          <p>(1) provide parents or legal guardians of infants with a document that provides the following information:</p>
          <p>(i) the benefits of newborn screening;</p>
          <p>(ii) that the blood sample will be used to test for heritable and congenital disorders, as determined under subdivision 2;</p>
          <p>(iii) the data that will be collected as part of the testing;</p>
          <p>(iv) the benefits associated with the department's storage of an infant's blood sample and test results;</p>
          <p>(v) that the Department of Health may store the blood samples and test results unless the parents or legal guardians elect to not have them stored;</p>
          <p>(vi) that blood samples and test results will be used for program operations in accordance with subdivision 5, unless the parents or legal guardians elect not to have the blood samples and test results stored, in which case the blood samples and test results will be destroyed in accordance with subdivision 8, paragraph (b), and until destroyed will only be used for program operations described under subdivision 5, paragraph (a), clauses (1) to (7);</p>
          <p>(vii) that parents or legal guardians have a right to elect not to have newborn screening performed and a right to secure private testing;</p>
          <p>(viii) that parents or legal guardians have a right to elect to have the newborn screening performed, but not have the blood samples and test results stored;</p>
          <p>(ix) that parents or legal guardians have a right to authorize in writing that the blood samples and test results may be used for public health studies or research; and</p>
          <p>(x) the Department of Health's website address where more information and forms may be obtained; and</p>
          <p>(2) upon request, promptly provide parents or legal guardians of infants with forms necessary to request that the infant not have blood collected for testing or to request to have the newborn screening performed, but not have the blood samples and test results stored; and</p>
          <p>(3) record in the infant's medical record that a parent or legal guardian of the infant has received the information provided pursuant to this subdivision and has had an opportunity to ask questions.</p>
          <p>(c) Nothing in this section prohibits a parent or legal guardian of an infant from having newborn screening performed by a private entity.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.125.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Parental options.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The parent or legal guardian of an infant otherwise subject to testing under this section may elect not to have newborn screening performed, or may elect to have newborn screening tests performed, but not to have the blood samples and test results stored.</p>
          <p>(b) If a parent or legal guardian elects not to have newborn screening performed or elects not to allow the blood samples and test results to be stored, then the election must be recorded on a form that is signed by the parent or legal guardian. The signed form must be made part of the infant's medical record and a copy shall be provided to the Department of Health. When a parent or legal guardian elects not to have newborn screening performed, the person with the duty to perform testing under subdivision 1 must follow that election. A written election to decline testing exempts persons with a duty to perform testing and the Department of Health from the requirements of this section and section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.128">144.128</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.125.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Newborn screening program operations.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) "Newborn screening program operations" means actions, testing, and procedures directly related to the operation of the newborn screening program, limited to the following:</p>
          <p>(1) confirmatory testing;</p>
          <p>(2) laboratory quality control assurance and improvement;</p>
          <p>(3) calibration of equipment;</p>
          <p>(4) evaluating and improving the accuracy of newborn screening tests for conditions approved for screening in Minnesota;</p>
          <p>(5) validation of equipment and screening methods;</p>
          <p>(6) continuity of operations to ensure testing can continue as required by Minnesota law in the event of an emergency;</p>
          <p>(7) follow-up services for the cases of heritable and congenital disorders identified by newborn screening; and</p>
          <p>(8) utilization of blood samples and test results for studies related to newborn screening, including studies used to develop new tests.</p>
          <p>(b) No research or public health studies other than those described in paragraph (a) shall be conducted without written consent as described under subdivision 7.</p>
          <p>(c) Any sale of bloodspots, test results, or other data collected in the newborn screening program is strictly prohibited.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.125.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/203/#laws.0.8.0">2014 c 203 s 8</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.125.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Parental options for additional research.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The parent or legal guardian of an infant subject to testing under this section, or an individual who was tested as an infant if the individual is 18 years of age or older may authorize in writing that the infant's blood sample and test results be retained and used by the Department of Health for the purposes described in subdivision 9.</p>
          <p>(b) The Department of Health must provide a consent form, with an attached Tennessen warning pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.04#stat.13.04.2">13.04, subdivision 2</a>. The consent form must provide the following:</p>
          <p>(1) information as to the personal identification and use of samples and test results for public health studies or research not related to newborn screening;</p>
          <p>(2) information that explains that, upon approval by the Department of Health's Institutional Review Board, blood samples and test results may be shared with external parties for public health studies or research; and</p>
          <p>(3) information that explains that blood samples contain various components, including deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.125.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote"> Storage and use of samples and test results.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as limited under paragraph (b), the Department of Health may store blood samples and test results, and may use the blood samples and test results in accordance with subdivision 5. If written informed consent of a parent, legal guardian, or individual is obtained under subdivision 7, the Department of Health may use the blood samples and test results in accordance with subdivision 9.</p>
          <p>(b) If a parent, legal guardian, or individual elects against storage, or revokes prior consent for storage, the blood samples must be destroyed within 30 days after receipt of the request, and test results must be destroyed within 30 days after receipt of the request, or the earliest time allowed under Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) regulations, whichever is later. Until destroyed, the blood samples and test results may be used for program operations described under subdivision 5, paragraph (a), clauses (1) to (7).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.125.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Written, informed consent for other use of samples and test results.</span></h2>
          <p>With the written, informed consent of a parent or legal guardian, the Department of Health may use blood samples and test results for public health studies or research not related to newborn screening, and upon approval by the Department of Health's Institutional Review Board, share samples and test results with external parties for public health studies or research.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.125.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Revoking consent for storage and use.</span></h2>
          <p>A parent or legal guardian, or the individual whose blood was tested as an infant if the individual is 18 years of age or older, may revoke approval for storage or use of blood samples or test results at any time by providing a signed and dated form requesting destruction of the blood samples or test results. Blood samples and test results must be destroyed as specified under subdivision 8, paragraph (b).</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.125.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1965/0/205/#laws.0.1.0">1965 c 205 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/1/4/#laws.1.75.0">1Sp1981 c 4 art 1 s 75</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/689/#laws.2.31.0">1988 c 689 art 2 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.2.2.0">1994 c 636 art 2 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/203/#laws.2.11.0">1997 c 203 art 2 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/205/#laws.0.19.0">1997 c 205 s 19</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.7.26.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 7 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.16.7.0">2007 c 147 art 16 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.10.5.0">2009 c 79 art 10 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/292/#laws.4.3.0">2012 c 292 art 4 s 3</a>-10; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.12.14.0">2013 c 108 art 12 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/125/#laws.1.30.0">2013 c 125 art 1 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/203/#laws.0.1.0">2014 c 203 s 1</a>-7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/7/#laws.3.20.0">1Sp2021 c 7 art 3 s 20</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.1251">
        <h1 class="shn">144.1251 NEWBORN SCREENING FOR CRITICAL CONGENITAL HEART DISEASE (CCHD).</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1251.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Required testing and reporting.</span></h2>
