          <p>(b) "Commissioner" means the commissioner of health.</p>
          <p>(c) "Eligible family medicine residency program" means a program that meets the following criteria:</p>
          <p>(1) is located in Minnesota outside the seven-county metropolitan area, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/473.121#stat.473.121.4">473.121, subdivision 4</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) is accredited as a family medicine residency program or is a candidate for accreditation;</p>
          <p>(3) is focused on the education and training of family medicine physicians to serve communities outside the metropolitan area; and</p>
          <p>(4) demonstrates that over the most recent three years at least 25 percent of its graduates practice in Minnesota communities outside the metropolitan area.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1912.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Program administration.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner shall award family medicine residency grants to existing, eligible, not-for-profit family medicine residency programs to support current and new residency positions. Funds shall be allocated first to proposed new family medicine residency positions, and remaining funds shall be allocated proportionally based on the number of existing residents in eligible programs. The commissioner may fund a new residency position for up to three years.</p>
          <p>(b) Grant funds awarded may only be spent to cover the costs of:</p>
          <p>(1) establishing, maintaining, or expanding training for family medicine residents;</p>
          <p>(2) recruitment, training, and retention of residents and faculty;</p>
          <p>(3) travel and lodging for residents; and</p>
          <p>(4) faculty, resident, and preceptor salaries.</p>
          <p>(c) Grant funds shall not be used to supplant any other government or private funds available for these purposes.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1912.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Applications.</span></h2>
          <p>Eligible family medicine residency programs seeking a grant must apply to the commissioner. The application must include objectives, a related work plan and budget, a description of the number of new and existing residency positions that will be supported using grant funds, and additional information the commissioner determines to be necessary. The commissioner shall determine whether applications are complete and responsive and may require revisions or additional information before awarding a grant.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.1912.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Program oversight.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall require and collect from family medicine residency programs receiving grants, information necessary to administer and evaluate the program. The evaluation shall include the scope of expansion of new residency positions and information describing specific programs to enhance current residency positions, which may include facility improvements. The commissioner shall continue to collect data on greater Minnesota family medicine residency shortages.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.1912.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/189/#laws.20.8.0">2016 c 189 art 20 s 8</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.1913">
        <h1 class="shn">144.1913 CLINICAL DENTAL EDUCATION INNOVATION GRANTS.</h1>
        <p>(a) The commissioner of health shall award clinical dental education innovation grants to teaching institutions and clinical training sites for projects that increase dental access for underserved populations and promote innovative clinical training of dental professionals. In awarding the grants, the commissioner shall consider the following:</p>
        <p>(1) potential to successfully increase access to dental services for an underserved population;</p>
        <p>(2) the long-term viability of the project to improve access to dental services beyond the period of initial funding;</p>
        <p>(3) evidence of collaboration between the applicant and local communities;</p>
        <p>(4) efficiency in the use of grant money; and</p>
        <p>(5) the priority level of the project in relation to state clinical education, access, and workforce goals.</p>
        <p>(b) The commissioner shall periodically evaluate the priorities in awarding innovation grants under this section to ensure that the priorities meet the changing workforce needs of the state.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.1913.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.5.10.0">2023 c 70 art 5 s 10</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">BIOLOGICAL AND HEALTH DATA</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.192">
        <h1 class="shn">144.192 TREATMENT OF BIOLOGICAL SPECIMENS AND HEALTH DATA HELD BY THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HEALTH BOARDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.192.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Biological specimen" means tissue, fluids, excretions, or secretions that contain human DNA originating from an identifiable individual, either living or deceased. Biological specimen does not include infectious agents or chemicals that are isolated from a specimen. Nothing in this section or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.386">13.386</a> is intended to limit the commissioner's ability to collect, use, store, or disseminate such isolated infectious agents or chemicals.</p>
          <p>(c) "Health data" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.3805#stat.13.3805.1">13.3805, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (a), clause (2).</p>
          <p>(d) "Health oversight" means oversight of the health care system for activities authorized by law, limited to the following:</p>
          <p>(1) audits;</p>
          <p>(2) civil, administrative, or criminal investigations;</p>
          <p>(3) inspections;</p>
          <p>(4) licensure or disciplinary actions;</p>
          <p>(5) civil, administrative, or criminal proceedings or actions; and</p>
          <p>(6) other activities necessary for appropriate oversight of the health care system and persons subject to such governmental regulatory programs for which biological specimens or health data are necessary for determining compliance with program standards.</p>
          <p>(e) "Individual" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.8">13.02, subdivision 8</a>. In addition, for a deceased individual, individual also means the representative of the decedent.</p>
          <p>(f) "Person" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.10">13.02, subdivision 10</a>.</p>
          <p>(g) "Program operations" means actions, testing, and procedures directly related to the operation of department programs, limited to the following:</p>
          <p>(1) diagnostic and confirmatory testing;</p>
          <p>(2) laboratory quality control assurance and improvement;</p>
          <p>(3) calibration of equipment;</p>
          <p>(4) evaluation and improvement of test accuracy;</p>
          <p>(5) method development and validation;</p>
          <p>(6) compliance with regulatory requirements; and</p>
          <p>(7) continuity of operations to ensure that testing continues in the event of an emergency.</p>
          <p>(h) "Public health practice" means actions related to disease, conditions, injuries, risk factors, or exposures taken to protect public health, limited to the following:</p>
          <p>(1) monitoring the health status of a population;</p>
          <p>(2) investigating occurrences and outbreaks;</p>
          <p>(3) comparing patterns and trends;</p>
          <p>(4) implementing prevention and control measures;</p>
          <p>(5) conducting program evaluations and making program improvements;</p>
          <p>(6) making recommendations concerning health for a population;</p>
          <p>(7) preventing or controlling known or suspected diseases and injuries; and</p>
          <p>(8) conducting other activities necessary to protect or improve the health of individuals and populations for which biological specimens or health data are necessary.</p>
          <p>(i) "Representative of the decedent" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.10">13.10</a>, subdivision 1, paragraph (c).</p>
          <p>(j) "Research" means activities that are not program operations, public health practice, or health oversight and is otherwise defined in Code of Federal Regulations, title 45, part 46, subpart A, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/46.102">46.102 </a>(d).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.192.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Collection, use, storage, and dissemination.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner may collect, use, store, and disseminate biological specimens and health data, genetic or other, as provided in this section and as authorized under any other provision of applicable law, including any rules adopted on or before June 30, 2013. Any rules adopted after June 30, 2013, must be consistent with the requirements of this section.</p>
          <p>(b) The provisions in this section supplement other provisions of law and do not supersede or repeal other provisions of law applying to the collection, use, storage, or dissemination of biological specimens or health data.</p>
          <p>(c) For purposes of this section, genetic information is limited to biological specimens and health data.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.192.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Biological specimens and health data for program operations, public health practice, and health oversight.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner may collect, use, store, and disseminate biological specimens and health data to conduct program operations activities, public health practice activities, and health oversight activities. Unless required under other applicable law, consent of an individual is not required under this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(b) With the approval of the commissioner, biological specimens may be disseminated to establish a diagnosis, to provide treatment, to identify persons at risk of illness, or to conduct an epidemiologic investigation to control or prevent the spread of serious disease, or to diminish an imminent threat to the public health.</p>
          <p>(c) For purposes of Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments proficiency testing, the commissioner may disseminate de-identified biological specimens to state public health laboratories that agree, pursuant to contract, not to attempt to re-identify the biological specimens.</p>
          <p>(d) Health data may be disseminated as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.3805#stat.13.3805.1">13.3805, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (b).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.192.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Research.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may collect, use, store, and disseminate biological specimens and health data to conduct research in a manner that is consistent with the federal common rule for the protection of human subjects in Code of Federal Regulations, title 45, part 46.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.192.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Storage of biological specimens and health data according to storage schedules.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner shall store health data according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/138.17">138.17</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioner shall store biological specimens according to a specimen storage schedule. The commissioner shall develop the storage schedule by July 1, 2013, and post it on the department's website.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.192.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Secure storage of biological specimens.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall establish appropriate security safeguards for the storage of biological specimens, with regard for the privacy of the individuals from whom the biological specimens originated, and store the biological specimens accordingly. When a biological specimen is disposed of, it must be destroyed in a way that prevents determining the identity of the individual from whom it originated.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.192.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Applicability to health boards.</span></h2>
          <p>The provisions of subdivisions 2; 3, paragraphs (a), (c), and (d); and 4 to 6 pertaining to the commissioner also apply to community health boards organized under chapter 145A. These boards may also disseminate health data pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.3805#stat.13.3805.1">13.3805, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (b), clause (2).</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.192.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/82/#laws.0.11.0">2013 c 82 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.109.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 109</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.193">
        <h1 class="shn">144.193 INVENTORY OF BIOLOGICAL AND HEALTH DATA.</h1>
        <p>By February 1, 2014, and annually after that date, the commissioner shall prepare an inventory of biological specimens, registries, and health data and databases collected or maintained by the commissioner. In addition to the inventory, the commissioner shall provide the schedules for storage of health data and biological specimens. The inventories must be listed in reverse chronological order beginning with the year 2012. The commissioner shall make the inventory and schedules available on the department's website.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.193.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/82/#laws.0.12.0">2013 c 82 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/98/#laws.14.3.0">2022 c 98 art 14 s 3</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.196">
        <h1 class="shn">144.196 CANNABIS DATA COLLECTION AND BIENNIAL REPORTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.196.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">General.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall engage in research and data collection activities to measure the prevalence of cannabis flower use and the use of cannabis products, lower-potency hemp edibles, and hemp-derived consumer products in the state by persons under 21 years of age and by persons 21 years of age or older, and the trends in hospital-treated cannabis poisoning and adverse events. In order to collect data, the commissioner may modify existing data collection tools used by the department or other state agencies or may establish one or more new data collection tools.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.196.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Statewide assessment; baseline data; updates.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner shall conduct a statewide assessment to establish a baseline for the prevalence of cannabis flower use and the use of cannabis products, lower-potency hemp edibles, and hemp-derived consumer products in the state, and the trends in hospital-treated cannabis poisoning and adverse events broken out by:</p>
          <p>(1) the current age of the customer;</p>
          <p>(2) the age at which the customer began consuming cannabis flower, cannabis products, lower-potency hemp edibles, or hemp-derived consumer products;</p>
          <p>(3) whether the customer consumes cannabis flower, cannabis products, lower-potency hemp edibles, or hemp-derived consumer products, and by type of product that the customer consumes, if applicable;</p>
          <p>(4) the amount of cannabis flower, cannabis product, lower-potency hemp edible, or hemp-derived consumer product typically consumed at one time;</p>
          <p>(5) the typical frequency of consumption; and</p>
          <p>(6) other criteria specified by the commissioner.</p>
          <p>(b) The initial assessment must be completed by July 1, 2024. The commissioner shall collect updated data under this subdivision at least every two years thereafter.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.196.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Reports.</span></h2>
          <p>Beginning January 1, 2025, and January 1 every two years thereafter, the commissioner shall issue a public report on the prevalence of cannabis flower use and the use of cannabis products, lower-potency hemp edibles, and hemp-derived consumer products in the state by persons under age 21 and by persons age 21 or older. The report may include recommendations from the commissioner for changes to this chapter that would discourage or prevent personal use of cannabis flower, cannabis products, lower-potency hemp edibles, or hemp-derived consumer products by persons under age 21, that would discourage personal use of cannabis flower, cannabis products, lower-potency hemp edibles, or hemp-derived consumer products by pregnant or breastfeeding individuals, that would prevent access to cannabis flower, cannabis products, lower-potency hemp edibles, or hemp-derived consumer products by young children, or that would otherwise promote public health.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.196.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/63/#laws.6.8.0">2023 c 63 art 6 s 8</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.197">
        <h1 class="shn">144.197 CANNABIS AND SUBSTANCE MISUSE PREVENTION AND EDUCATION PROGRAMS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.197.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Youth prevention and education program.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health, in consultation with the commissioners of human services and education and in collaboration with local health departments and Tribal health departments, shall conduct a long-term, coordinated program to raise public awareness about substance misuse prevention, treatment options, and recovery options. The program must address adverse health effects associated with the use of cannabis flower, cannabis products, lower-potency hemp edibles, or hemp-derived consumer products by persons under age 25. In conducting this education program, the commissioner shall engage and consult with youth around the state on program content and on methods to effectively disseminate program information to youth around the state.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.197.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Prevention and education program for pregnant and breastfeeding individuals and individuals who may become pregnant.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health, in consultation with the commissioners of human services and education, shall conduct a long-term, coordinated prevention program focused on (1) preventing substance use by pregnant individuals, breastfeeding individuals, and individuals who may become pregnant, and (2) raising public awareness of the risks of substance use while pregnant or breastfeeding. The program must include education on the adverse health effects of prenatal exposure to cannabis flower, cannabis products, lower-potency hemp edibles, or hemp-derived consumer products and on the adverse health effects experienced by infants and children who are exposed to cannabis flower, cannabis products, lower-potency hemp edibles, or hemp-derived consumer products in breast milk, from secondhand smoke, or by ingesting cannabinoid products. This prevention and education program must also educate individuals on what constitutes a substance use disorder, signs of a substance use disorder, and treatment options for persons with a substance use disorder. The prevention and education program must also provide resources, including training resources, technical assistance, or educational materials, to local public health home visiting programs, Tribal home visiting programs, and child welfare workers.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.197.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>MS 2023 Supp [Repealed by amendment, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/121/#laws.3.1.0">2024 c 121 art 3 s 1</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.197.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Local and Tribal health departments.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall distribute grants to local health departments and Tribal health departments for the departments to create prevention, education, and recovery programs focusing on substance misuse prevention and treatment options. The programs must include specific cannabis-related initiatives.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.197.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/63/#laws.6.9.0">2023 c 63 art 6 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/121/#laws.3.1.0">2024 c 121 art 3 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.20"><b>144.20</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/512/#laws.0.37.0">1945 c 512 s 37</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.201"><b>144.201</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/699/#laws.0.17.0">1978 c 699 s 17</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.202"><b>144.202</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/699/#laws.0.17.0">1978 c 699 s 17</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.203"><b>144.203</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/699/#laws.0.17.0">1978 c 699 s 17</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.204"><b>144.204</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/699/#laws.0.17.0">1978 c 699 s 17</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.205"><b>144.205</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/699/#laws.0.17.0">1978 c 699 s 17</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.21"><b>144.21</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/512/#laws.0.37.0">1945 c 512 s 37</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">VITAL RECORDS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.211">
        <h1 class="shn">144.211 CITATION.</h1>
        <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.211">144.211</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.227">144.227</a> may be cited as the "Vital Records Act."</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.211.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/699/#laws.0.1.0">1978 c 699 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.109.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 109</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.212">
        <h1 class="shn">144.212 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.211">144.211</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.227">144.227</a>, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Amendment.</span></h2>
          <p>"Amendment" means completion or correction made to certification items on a vital record after a certification has been issued or more than one year after the event, whichever occurs first, that does not result in a sealed or replaced record.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.1b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.<span class="headnote">Authorized representative.</span></h2>
          <p>"Authorized representative" means an agent designated in a written and witnessed statement signed by the subject of the record or other qualified applicant.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.1c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1c.<span class="headnote">Certification item.</span></h2>
          <p>"Certification item" means all individual items appearing on a certificate of birth and the demographic and legal items on a certificate of death.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>"Commissioner" means the commissioner of health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Correction.</span></h2>
          <p>"Correction" means a change made to a noncertification item, including information collected for medical and statistical purposes. A correction also means a change to a certification item within one year of the event provided that no certification, whether paper or electronic, has been issued.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.2b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2b.<span class="headnote">Court of competent jurisdiction.</span></h2>
          <p>"Court of competent jurisdiction" means a court within the United States with jurisdiction over the individual and such other individuals that the court deems necessary.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.2c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2c.<span class="headnote">Delayed registration.</span></h2>
          <p>"Delayed registration" means registration of a record of birth or death filed one or more years after the date of birth or death.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.2d">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2d.<span class="headnote">Disclosure.</span></h2>
          <p>"Disclosure" means to make available or make known personally identifiable information contained in a vital record, by any means of communication.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">File.</span></h2>
          <p>"File" means to present a vital record or report for registration to the Office of Vital Records and to have the vital record or report accepted for registration by the Office of Vital Records.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Final disposition.</span></h2>
          <p>"Final disposition" means the burial, interment, cremation, removal from the state, or other authorized disposition of a dead body or dead fetus.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.4a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4a.<span class="headnote">Institution.</span></h2>
          <p>"Institution" means a public or private establishment that:</p>
          <p>(1) provides inpatient or outpatient medical, surgical, or diagnostic care or treatment; or</p>
          <p>(2) provides nursing, custodial, or domiciliary care, or to which persons are committed by law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.4b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4b.<span class="headnote">Legal representative.</span></h2>
          <p>"Legal representative" means a licensed attorney representing an individual.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.4c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4c.<span class="headnote">Local issuance office.</span></h2>
          <p>"Local issuance office" means a county governmental office authorized by the state registrar to issue certified birth and death records.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.4d">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4d.<span class="headnote">Record.</span></h2>
          <p>"Record" means a report of a vital event that has been registered by the state registrar.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Registration.</span></h2>
          <p>"Registration" means the process by which vital records are completed, filed, and incorporated into the official records of the Office of Vital Records.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.5a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5a.<span class="headnote">Replacement.</span></h2>
          <p>"Replacement" means a completion, addition, removal, or change made to certification items on a vital record after a vital event is registered and a record is established that has no notation of a change on a certificate and seals the prior vital record.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">State registrar.</span></h2>
          <p>"State registrar" means the commissioner of health or a designee.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">System of vital records.</span></h2>
          <p>"System of vital records" includes the registration, collection, preservation, amendment, verification, maintenance of the security and integrity of, and certification of vital records, the collection of other reports required by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.211">144.211</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.227">144.227</a>, and related activities including the tabulation, analysis, publication, and dissemination of vital records.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.7a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7a.<span class="headnote">Verification.</span></h2>
          <p>"Verification" means a confirmation of the information on a vital record based on the facts contained in a certification.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Vital record.</span></h2>
          <p>"Vital record" means a record or report of birth, stillbirth, death, marriage, dissolution and annulment, and data related thereto. The birth record is not a medical record of the mother or the child.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Vital records statistics.</span></h2>
          <p>"Vital records statistics" means the data derived from records and reports of birth, death, fetal death, induced abortion, marriage, dissolution and annulment, and related reports.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.</h2>
          <p> [Repealed by amendment, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.12.16.0">2013 c 108 art 12 s 16</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.</h2>
          <p>MS 2022 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.4.113.0">2023 c 70 art 4 s 113</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.212.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Homeless youth.</span></h2>
          <p>"Homeless youth" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256K.45">256K.45</a>, subdivision 1a.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.212.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/699/#laws.0.2.0">1978 c 699 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/228/#laws.0.3.0">1997 c 228 s 3</a>-5; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.15.1.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 15 s 1</a>-7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/379/#laws.1.113.0">2002 c 379 art 1 s 113</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/60/#laws.0.2.0">2005 c 60 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.12.16.0">2013 c 108 art 12 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.109.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 109</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/7/#laws.3.25.0">1Sp2021 c 7 art 3 s 25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.59.22.0">2024 c 127 art 59 s 22</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.213">
        <h1 class="shn">144.213 OFFICE OF VITAL RECORDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.213.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Creation; state registrar; Office of Vital Records.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall establish an Office of Vital Records under the supervision of the state registrar. The commissioner shall promulgate rules for the collection, filing, and registering of vital records information by the state registrar, physicians, advanced practice registered nurses, physician assistants, morticians, and others. Except as otherwise provided in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.211">144.211</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.227">144.227</a>, rules previously promulgated by the commissioner relating to the collection, filing and registering of vital records shall remain in effect until repealed, modified or superseded by a rule promulgated by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.213.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">General duties.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The state registrar shall maintain a statewide system of vital records. The state registrar is responsible for the administration and enforcement of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.211">144.211</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.227">144.227</a> and shall supervise the enforcement of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.211">144.211</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.227">144.227</a> and the rules promulgated thereunder. Local issuance offices that fail to comply with the statutes or rules or to properly train employees may have their issuance privileges and access to the vital records system revoked.</p>
          <p>(b) To preserve vital records, the state registrar is authorized to prepare typewritten, photographic, electronic, or other reproductions of original records and files in the Office of Vital Records. The reproductions, when certified by the state registrar, shall be accepted as the original records.</p>
          <p>(c) The state registrar shall also:</p>
          <p>(1) establish, designate, and eliminate offices in the state to aid in the efficient issuance of vital records;</p>
          <p>(2) direct the activities of all persons engaged in activities pertaining to the operation of the system of vital records;</p>
          <p>(3) develop and conduct training programs to promote uniformity of policy and procedures throughout the state in matters pertaining to the system of vital records; and</p>
          <p>(4) prescribe, furnish, and distribute all forms required by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.211">144.211</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.227">144.227</a> and any rules adopted under these sections, and prescribe other means for the transmission of data, including electronic submission, that will accomplish the purpose of complete, accurate, and timely reporting and registration.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.213.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p> [Repealed by amendment, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.12.17.0">2013 c 108 art 12 s 17</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.213.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/699/#laws.0.3.0">1978 c 699 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.15.32.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 15 s 32</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.12.17.0">2013 c 108 art 12 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.109.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 109</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/0/59/#laws.0.2.0">2017 c 59 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.2131">
        <h1 class="shn">144.2131 SECURITY OF VITAL RECORDS SYSTEM.</h1>
        <p>The state registrar shall:</p>
        <p>(1) authenticate all users of the system of vital records and document that all users require access based on their official duties;</p>
        <p>(2) authorize authenticated users of the system of vital records to access specific components of the vital records systems necessary for their official roles and duties;</p>
        <p>(3) establish separation of duties between staff roles that may be susceptible to fraud or misuse and routinely perform audits of staff work for the purposes of identifying fraud or misuse within the vital records system;</p>
        <p>(4) require that authenticated and authorized users of the system of vital records maintain a specified level of training related to security and provide written acknowledgment of security procedures and penalties;</p>
        <p>(5) validate data submitted for registration through site visits or with independent sources outside the registration system at a frequency specified by the state registrar to maximize the integrity of the data collected;</p>
        <p>(6) protect personally identifiable information and maintain systems pursuant to applicable state and federal laws;</p>
        <p>(7) accept a report of death if the decedent was born in Minnesota or if the decedent was a resident of Minnesota from the United States Department of Defense or the United States Department of State when the death of a United States citizen occurs outside the United States;</p>
        <p>(8) match death records registered in Minnesota and death records provided from other jurisdictions to live birth records in Minnesota;</p>
        <p>(9) match death records received from the United States Department of Defense or the United States Department of State for deaths of United States citizens occurring outside the United States to live birth records in Minnesota;</p>
        <p>(10) work with law enforcement to initiate and provide evidence for active fraud investigations;</p>
        <p>(11) provide secure workplace, storage, and technology environments that have limited role-based access;</p>
        <p>(12) maintain overt, covert, and forensic security measures for certifications, verifications, and automated systems that are part of the vital records system; and</p>
        <p>(13) comply with applicable state and federal laws and rules associated with information technology systems and related information security requirements.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.2131.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.12.18.0">2013 c 108 art 12 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.109.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 109</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr_by_subd" id="stat.144.214">
        <h1>144.214 </h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.214.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/275/#laws.1.139.0">2014 c 275 art 1 s 139</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.214.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/275/#laws.1.139.0">2014 c 275 art 1 s 139</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.214.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/275/#laws.1.139.0">2014 c 275 art 1 s 139</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.214.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/106/#laws.0.68.0">2005 c 106 s 68</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.215">
        <h1 class="shn">144.215 BIRTH REGISTRATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.215.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">When and where to file.</span></h2>
          <p>A record of birth for each live birth which occurs in this state shall be filed with the state registrar within five days after the birth.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.215.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Rules governing birth registration.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall establish by rule an orderly mechanism for the registration of births including at least a designation for who must file the birth record, a procedure for registering births which occur in moving conveyances, and a provision governing the names of the parent or parents to be entered on the birth record.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.215.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Father's name; child's name.</span></h2>
          <p>In any case in which paternity of a child is determined by a court of competent jurisdiction, or a recognition of parentage is executed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/257.75">257.75</a>, the name of the father shall be entered on the birth record. If the order of the court declares the name of the child, it shall also be entered on the birth record. If the order of the court does not declare the name of the child, or there is no court order, then upon the request of both parents in writing, the surname of the child shall be defined by both parents.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.215.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Social Security number registration.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Parents of a child born within this state shall give the parents' Social Security numbers to the Office of Vital Records at the time of filing the birth record, but the numbers shall not appear on the certified record.</p>
          <p>(b) The Social Security numbers are classified as private data, but the Office of Vital Records shall provide a Social Security number to the public authority responsible for child support services upon request by the public authority for use in the establishment of parentage and the enforcement of child support obligations.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.215.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Births occurring in an institution.</span></h2>
          <p>When a birth occurs in an institution or en route to an institution, the person in charge of the institution or that person's authorized designee shall obtain the personal data required under this section and shall prepare the record of birth. For purposes of this section, "institution" means a hospital or other facility that provides childbirth services.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.215.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Births occurring outside an institution.</span></h2>
          <p>When a birth occurs outside of an institution as defined in subdivision 5, the record of birth shall be filed by one of the following persons, in the indicated order of preference:</p>
          <p>(1) the physician present at the time of the birth or immediately thereafter;</p>
          <p>(2) in the absence of a physician, a person, other than the mother, present at the time of the birth or immediately thereafter;</p>
          <p>(3) the father of the child;</p>
          <p>(4) the mother of the child; or</p>
          <p>(5) in the absence of the father and if the mother is unable, the person with primary responsibility for the premises where the child was born.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.215.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Evidence required to register noninstitution birth within first year of birth.</span></h2>
          <p>When a birth occurs in this state outside of an institution, as defined in subdivision 5, and the birth record is filed before the first birthday, evidence in support of the facts of birth shall be required. Evidence shall be presented by the individual responsible for filing the vital record under subdivision 6. Evidence shall consist of proof that the child was born alive, proof of pregnancy, and evidence of the mother's presence in this state on the date of the birth. If the evidence is not acceptable, the state registrar shall advise the applicant of the reason for not filing a birth record and shall further advise the applicant of the right of appeal to a court of competent jurisdiction.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.215.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/699/#laws.0.5.0">1978 c 699 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/589/#laws.0.28.0">1980 c 589 s 28</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/1/1/#laws.6.1.0">1Sp1993 c 1 art 6 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/205/#laws.0.20.0">1997 c 205 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/228/#laws.0.6.0">1997 c 228 s 6</a>-8; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.15.11.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 15 s 11</a>-15,32; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/379/#laws.1.113.0">2002 c 379 art 1 s 113</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.12.19.0">2013 c 108 art 12 s 19</a>,20</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.2151">
        <h1 class="shn">144.2151 FETAL DEATH RECORD AND CERTIFICATE OF BIRTH RESULTING IN STILLBIRTH.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2151.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Registration.</span></h2>
          <p>A fetal death record must be established for each fetal death reported and registered under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.222#stat.144.222.1">144.222, subdivision 1</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2151.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Information to parents.</span></h2>
          <p>The party responsible for filing a fetal death report under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.222#stat.144.222.1">144.222, subdivision 1</a>, shall advise the parent or parents of a stillbirth:</p>
          <p>(1) that the parent or parents may choose to provide a full name or provide only a last name for the record;</p>
          <p>(2) that the parent or parents may request a certificate of birth resulting in stillbirth after the fetal death record is established;</p>
          <p>(3) that the parent who gave birth may request an informational copy of the fetal death record; and</p>
          <p>(4) that the parent or parents named on the fetal death record and the party responsible for reporting the fetal death may correct or amend the record to protect the integrity and accuracy of vital records.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2151.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Responsibilities of the state registrar.</span></h2>
          <p>The state registrar shall:</p>
          <p>(1) prescribe the process to:</p>
          <p>(i) register a fetal death;</p>
          <p>(ii) request the certificate of birth resulting in stillbirth; and</p>
          <p>(iii) request the informational copy of a fetal death record;</p>
          <p>(2) prescribe a standardized format for the certificate of birth resulting in stillbirth, which shall integrate security features and be as similar as possible to a birth certificate;</p>
          <p>(3) issue a certificate of birth resulting in stillbirth or a statement of no vital record found to the parent or parents named on the fetal death record upon the parent's proper completion of an attestation provided by the commissioner and payment of the required fee;</p>
          <p>(4) correct or amend the fetal death record upon a request from the parent who gave birth, parents, or the person who registered the fetal death or filed the report; and</p>
          <p>(5) refuse to amend or correct the fetal death record when an applicant does not submit the minimum documentation required to amend the record or when the state registrar has cause to question the validity or completeness of the applicant's statements or any documentary evidence and the deficiencies are not corrected. The state registrar shall advise the applicant of the reason for this action and shall further advise the applicant of the right of appeal to a court with competent jurisdiction over the Department of Health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2151.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Delayed registration.</span></h2>
          <p> If a fetal death occurred in this state at any time for which a fetal death report was required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.222#stat.144.222.1">144.222, subdivision 1</a>, but a fetal death was not registered and a record was not established, a person responsible for registering the fetal death, the medical examiner or coroner with jurisdiction, or a parent may submit to the state registrar a written request to register the fetal death and submit the evidence to support the request.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2151.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>MS 2022 [Repealed by amendment, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.3.4.0">2023 c 70 art 3 s 4</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.2151.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/60/#laws.0.1.0">2005 c 60 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.3.4.0">2023 c 70 art 3 s 4</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.216">
        <h1 class="shn">144.216 FOUNDLING REGISTRATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.216.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Reporting foundling.</span></h2>
          <p>Whoever finds a live born infant of unknown parentage shall report within five days to the Office of Vital Records such information as the commissioner may by rule require to identify the foundling.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.216.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Status of foundling reports.</span></h2>
          <p>A report registered under subdivision 1 shall constitute the record of birth for the child. Information about the newborn shall be registered by the state registrar in accordance with Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4601.0600">4601.0600</a>, subpart 4, item C. If the child is identified and a record of birth is found or obtained, the report registered under subdivision 1 shall be confidential pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.3">13.02, subdivision 3</a>, and shall not be disclosed except pursuant to court order.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.216.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Reporting safe place newborns.</span></h2>
          <p>Hospitals that receive a newborn under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145.902">145.902</a> shall report the birth of the newborn to the Office of Vital Records within five days after receiving the newborn. Information about the newborn shall be registered by the state registrar in accordance with Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4601.0600">4601.0600</a>, subpart 4, item C.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.216.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Status of safe place birth reports and registrations.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Information about a safe place newborn registered under subdivision 3 shall constitute the record of birth for the child. The record shall be confidential pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.3">13.02, subdivision 3</a>. Information on the birth record or a birth certificate issued from the birth record shall be disclosed only to the responsible social services agency or pursuant to a court order.</p>
          <p>(b) Information about a safe place newborn registered under subdivision 3 shall constitute the record of birth for the child. If the safe place newborn was born in a hospital and it is known that a record of birth was registered, filed, or amended, the original birth record registered under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.215">144.215</a> shall be replaced pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.218">144.218, subdivision </a>6.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.216.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/699/#laws.0.6.0">1978 c 699 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/311/#laws.0.39.0">1981 c 311 s 39</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/545/#laws.0.24.0">1982 c 545 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.15.32.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 15 s 32</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.12.21.0">2013 c 108 art 12 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.59.23.0">2024 c 127 art 59 s 23</a>-25</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.217">
        <h1 class="shn">144.217 DELAYED RECORDS OF BIRTH.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.217.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Evidence required for filing.</span></h2>
          <p>Before a delayed record of birth is registered, the person presenting the delayed vital record for registration shall offer evidence of the facts contained in the vital record, as required by the rules of the commissioner. In the absence of the evidence required, the delayed vital record shall not be registered. No delayed record of birth shall be registered for a deceased person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.217.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Court petition.</span></h2>
          <p>If a delayed record of birth is rejected under subdivision 1, a person may petition the appropriate court in the county in which the birth allegedly occurred for an order establishing a record of the date and place of the birth and the parentage of the person whose birth is to be registered. The petition shall state:</p>
          <p>(1) that the person for whom a delayed record of birth is sought was born in this state;</p>
          <p>(2) that no record of birth can be found in the Office of Vital Records;</p>
          <p>(3) that diligent efforts by the petitioner have failed to obtain the evidence required in subdivision 1;</p>
          <p>(4) that the state registrar has refused to register a delayed record of birth; and</p>
          <p>(5) other information as may be required by the court.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.217.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Court order.</span></h2>
          <p>The court shall fix a time and place for a hearing on the petition and shall give the state registrar ten days' notice of the hearing. The state registrar may appear and testify in the proceeding. If the court is satisfied from the evidence received at the hearing of the truth of the statements in the petition, the court shall order the registration of the delayed vital record.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.217.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.15.16.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 15 s 16</a>,33]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.217.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/699/#laws.0.7.0">1978 c 699 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.15.16.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 15 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/379/#laws.1.113.0">2002 c 379 art 1 s 113</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.12.22.0">2013 c 108 art 12 s 22</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.218">
        <h1 class="shn">144.218 REPLACEMENT BIRTH RECORDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.218.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Adoption.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon receipt of a certified copy of an order, decree, or certificate of adoption, the state registrar shall register a replacement vital record in the new name of the adopted person. The original record of birth is private data pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.12">13.02, subdivision 12</a>, and shall not be disclosed except pursuant to court order or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2252">144.2252</a>. The information contained on the original birth record, except for the registration number, shall be provided on request to a parent who is named on the original birth record. Upon the receipt of a certified copy of a court order of annulment of adoption the state registrar shall restore the original vital record to its original place in the file.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.218.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Adoption of foreign persons.</span></h2>
          <p>In proceedings for the adoption of a person who was born in a foreign country, the court, upon evidence presented by the commissioner of children, youth, and families from information secured at the port of entry or upon evidence from other reliable sources, may make findings of fact as to the date and place of birth and parentage. Upon receipt of certified copies of the court findings and the order or decree of adoption, a certificate of adoption, or a certified copy of a decree issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/259.60">259.60</a>, the state registrar shall register a birth record in the new name of the adopted person. The certified copies of the court findings and the order or decree of adoption, certificate of adoption, or decree issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/259.60">259.60</a> are private data, pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.12">13.02, subdivision 12</a>, and shall not be disclosed except pursuant to court order or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2252">144.2252</a>. The birth record shall state the place of birth as specifically as possible and that the vital record is not evidence of United States citizenship.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.218.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>MS 2022 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.59.57.0">2024 c 127 art 59 s 57</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.218.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Incomplete, incorrect, and modified vital records.</span></h2>
          <p>If a court finds that a birth record is incomplete, inaccurate, or false or if it is being issued pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/259.10#stat.259.10.2">259.10, subdivision 2</a>, the court may order the registration of a replacement vital record, and, if necessary, set forth the correct information in the order. Upon receipt of the order, the registrar shall register a replacement vital record containing the findings of the court. The prior vital record shall be confidential pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.3">13.02, subdivision 3</a>, and shall not be disclosed except pursuant to court order.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.218.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Replacement of vital records.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon the order of a court of this state, upon the request of a court of another state, or upon the filing of a recognition of parentage with the state registrar, a replacement birth record must be registered consistent with the findings of the court or the recognition of parentage.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.218.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Safe place newborn; birth record.</span></h2>
          <p>If a safe place infant birth is registered pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.216#stat.144.216.4">144.216, subdivision 4</a>, paragraph (b), the state registrar shall issue a replacement birth record free of information that identifies a parent. The prior vital record shall be confidential pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.3">13.02, subdivision 3</a>, and shall not be disclosed except pursuant to a court order.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.218.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/699/#laws.0.8.0">1978 c 699 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/561/#laws.0.1.0">1980 c 561 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/311/#laws.0.24.0">1981 c 311 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/545/#laws.0.24.0">1982 c 545 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/654/#laws.5.58.0">1984 c 654 art 5 s 58</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/465/#laws.1.62.0">1994 c 465 art 1 s 62</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/631/#laws.0.31.0">1994 c 631 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/259/#laws.1.32.0">1995 c 259 art 1 s 32</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/205/#laws.0.21.0">1997 c 205 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/406/#laws.1.1.0">1998 c 406 art 1 s 1</a>,37; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.9.1.0">1998 c 407 art 9 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.15.17.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 15 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/379/#laws.1.113.0">2002 c 379 art 1 s 113</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.12.23.0">2013 c 108 art 12 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.4.28.0">2023 c 70 art 4 s 28</a>,29; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/80/#laws.8.70.0">2024 c 80 art 8 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.59.26.0">2024 c 127 art 59 s 26</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.2181">
        <h1 class="shn">144.2181 AMENDMENT AND CORRECTION OF VITAL RECORDS.</h1>
        <p>(a) A vital record registered under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.212">144.212</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.227">144.227</a> may be amended or corrected only according to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.212">144.212</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.227">144.227</a> and rules adopted by the commissioner of health to protect the integrity and accuracy of vital records.</p>
        <p>(b)(1) A vital record that is amended under this section shall indicate that it has been amended, except as otherwise provided in this section or by rule.</p>
        <p>(2) Electronic documentation shall be maintained by the state registrar that identifies the evidence upon which the amendment or correction was based, the date of the amendment or correction, and the identity of the authorized person making the amendment or correction.</p>
        <p>(c) Upon receipt of a certified copy of an order of a court of competent jurisdiction changing the name of a person whose birth is registered in Minnesota and upon request of such person if 18 years of age or older or having the status of emancipated minor, the state registrar shall amend the birth record to show the new name. If the person is a minor or an incapacitated person then a parent, guardian, or legal representative of the minor or incapacitated person may make the request.</p>
        <p>(d) When an applicant does not submit the minimum documentation required for amending a vital record or when the state registrar has cause to question the validity or completeness of the applicant's statements or the documentary evidence, and the deficiencies are not corrected, the state registrar shall not amend the vital record. The state registrar shall advise the applicant of the reason for this action and shall further advise the applicant of the right of appeal to a court with competent jurisdiction over the Department of Health.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.2181.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.12.24.0">2013 c 108 art 12 s 24</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.219"><b>144.219</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.15.33.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 15 s 33</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.22"><b>144.22</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/512/#laws.0.37.0">1945 c 512 s 37</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.221">
        <h1 class="shn">144.221 DEATH REGISTRATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.221.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">When and where to file.</span></h2>
          <p>A death record for each death which occurs in the state shall be filed with the state registrar within five days after death and prior to final disposition.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.221.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Rules governing death registration.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall establish in rule an orderly mechanism for the registration of deaths including at least a designation for who must file the death record, a procedure for the registration of deaths in moving conveyances, and provision to include cause and certification of death and assurance of registration prior to final disposition.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.221.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">When no body is found.</span></h2>
          <p>When circumstances suggest that a death has occurred although a dead body cannot be produced to confirm the fact of death, a death record shall not be registered until a court has adjudicated the fact of death.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.221.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/699/#laws.0.10.0">1978 c 699 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.15.18.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 15 s 18</a>,19,32; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/379/#laws.1.113.0">2002 c 379 art 1 s 113</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/106/#laws.0.56.0">2005 c 106 s 56</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.2215">
        <h1 class="shn">144.2215 MINNESOTA BIRTH DEFECTS INFORMATION SYSTEM.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2215.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Establishment.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall establish and maintain an information system containing data on the cause, treatment, prevention, and cure of major birth defects. The commissioner shall consult with representatives and experts in epidemiology, medicine, insurance, health maintenance organizations, genetics, consumers, and voluntary organizations in developing the system and may phase in the implementation of the system. Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2215">144.2215</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2219">144.2219</a> apply to birth defects that develop during pregnancy and:</p>
          <p>(1) result in live births; or</p>
          <p>(2) result in fetal deaths, reportable under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.222">144.222</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2215.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Duties of commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall design a system that allows the commissioner to:</p>
          <p>(1) monitor incidence trends of birth defects to detect potential public health problems, predict risks, and assist in responding to birth defects clusters;</p>
          <p>(2) more accurately target intervention, prevention, and services for communities, patients, and their families;</p>
          <p>(3) inform health professionals and citizens of the prevalence of and risks for birth defects;</p>
          <p>(4) conduct scientific investigation and surveys of the causes, mortality, methods of treatment, prevention, and cure for birth defects;</p>
          <p>(5) modify, as necessary, the birth defects information system through demonstration projects;</p>
          <p>(6) remove identifying information about a child whose parent or legal guardian has chosen not to participate in the system as permitted by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2216#stat.144.2216.4">144.2216, subdivision 4</a>;</p>
          <p>(7) protect the individually identifiable information as required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2217">144.2217</a>;</p>
          <p>(8) limit the dissemination of identifying information as required by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2218">144.2218</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2219">144.2219</a>; and</p>
          <p>(9) use the birth defects coding scheme defined by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) of the United States Public Health Service.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.2215.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/451/#laws.4.6.0">1996 c 451 art 4 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/288/#laws.6.11.0">2004 c 288 art 6 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/290/#laws.0.25.0">2004 c 290 s 25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2018/0/152/#laws.0.1.0">2018 c 152 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.2216">
        <h1 class="shn">144.2216 BIRTH DEFECTS RECORDS AND REPORTS REQUIRED.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2216.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Hospitals and similar institutions.</span></h2>
          <p>With the informed consent of a parent or guardian, as provided in subdivision 4, a hospital, medical clinic, medical laboratory, or other institution for the hospitalization, clinical or laboratory diagnosis, or care of human beings shall provide the commissioner of health with access to information on each birth defect case in the manner and at the times that the commissioner designates.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2216.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Other information repositories.</span></h2>
          <p>With the informed consent of a parent or guardian, as provided in subdivision 4, other repositories of information on the diagnosis or care of infants may provide the commissioner with access to information on each case of birth defects in the manner and at the times that the commissioner designates.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2216.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Reporting without liability.</span></h2>
          <p>Furnishing information in good faith in compliance with this section does not subject the person, hospital, medical clinic, medical laboratory, data repository, or other institution furnishing the information to any action for damages or relief.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2216.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Opt out.</span></h2>
          <p>A parent or legal guardian must be informed by the commissioner at the time of the initial data collection that they may request removal at any time of personal identifying information concerning a child from the birth defects information system using a written form prescribed by the commissioner. The commissioner shall advise parents or legal guardians:</p>
          <p>(1) that the information on birth defects may be retained by the Department of Health;</p>
          <p>(2) of the benefit and privacy implications of retaining birth defects records;</p>
          <p>(3) that they may elect to have the birth defects information collected once, within one year of birth or fetal death, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.222">144.222</a>, but to require that all personally identifying information be destroyed immediately upon the commissioner receiving the information. If the parents or legal guardians object in writing to the maintaining of birth defects information, the objection or election shall be recorded on a form that is signed by a parent or legal guardian and submitted to the commissioner of health; and</p>
          <p>(4) that if the parent or legal guardian chooses to opt-out, the commissioner will not be able to inform the parent or legal guardian of information related to the prevention, treatment, or cause of a particular birth defect.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.2216.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/288/#laws.6.12.0">2004 c 288 art 6 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/290/#laws.0.26.0">2004 c 290 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2018/0/152/#laws.0.2.0">2018 c 152 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.2217">
        <h1 class="shn">144.2217 CLASSIFICATION OF BIRTH DEFECTS INFORMATION.</h1>
        <p>Information collected on individuals for the birth defects information system are private data on individuals as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.12">13.02, subdivision 12</a>, and may only be used for the purposes in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2215">144.2215</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2219">144.2219</a>. Any disclosure other than one provided for in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2215">144.2215</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2219">144.2219</a> is a misdemeanor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.2217.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/288/#laws.6.13.0">2004 c 288 art 6 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/290/#laws.0.27.0">2004 c 290 s 27</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.2218">
        <h1 class="shn">144.2218 TRANSFERS OF INFORMATION TO OTHER GOVERNMENT AGENCIES.</h1>
        <p>Information collected by the birth defects information system may be disseminated to a state or local government agency in Minnesota or another state solely for purposes consistent with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2215">144.2215</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2219">144.2219</a>, provided that the state or local government agency agrees to maintain the classification of the information as provided under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2217">144.2217</a>.
