Information collected by other states consistent with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2215">144.2215</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2219">144.2219</a> may be received by the commissioner of health and must be maintained according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2217">144.2217</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.2218.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/288/#laws.6.14.0">2004 c 288 art 6 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/290/#laws.0.28.0">2004 c 290 s 28</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.2219">
        <h1 class="shn">144.2219 TRANSFERS OF INFORMATION TO RESEARCH ENTITIES.</h1>
        <p>Information from the birth defects information system that does not contain identifying information may be shared with research entities upon request for studies approved by the commissioner and appropriate institutional review boards. For studies approved by the commissioner that require identifying information about a child or a parent or legal guardian of the child, the commissioner shall contact the parent or legal guardian to obtain informed consent to share identifying information with the research entity. Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.295">144.295</a>, the parent or legal guardian must provide informed consent before the information may be shared. The commissioner must collect all reasonable costs of locating and obtaining consent from the research entity.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.2219.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/288/#laws.6.15.0">2004 c 288 art 6 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/290/#laws.0.29.0">2004 c 290 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.10.15.0">2007 c 147 art 10 s 15</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.222">
        <h1 class="shn">144.222 FETAL DEATH REPORTS AND REGISTRATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.222.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Fetal death report required.</span></h2>
          <p>A fetal death must be registered or reported within five days of the death of a fetus for whom 20 or more weeks of gestation have elapsed, except for abortions defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145.411">145.411</a>, subdivision 5. A fetal death must be registered or reported in a format prescribed by the state registrar and filed in accordance with Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4601.0100">4601.0100</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4601.2600">4601.2600</a> by:</p>
          <p>(1) a person in charge of an institution or that person's authorized designee if a fetus is delivered in the institution or en route to the institution;</p>
          <p>(2) a physician, certified nurse midwife, or other licensed medical personnel in attendance at or immediately after the delivery if a fetus is delivered outside an institution; or</p>
          <p>(3) a parent or other person in charge of the disposition of the remains if a fetal death occurred without medical attendance at or immediately after the delivery.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.222.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>MS 2022 [Repealed by amendment, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.3.5.0">2023 c 70 art 3 s 5</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.222.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/699/#laws.0.11.0">1978 c 699 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/637/#laws.0.2.0">1984 c 637 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.15.20.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 15 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/379/#laws.1.113.0">2002 c 379 art 1 s 113</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/60/#laws.0.3.0">2005 c 60 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.3.5.0">2023 c 70 art 3 s 5</a>; art 4 s 30</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.223">
        <h1 class="shn">144.223 REPORT OF MARRIAGE.</h1>
        <p>Data relating to certificates of marriage registered shall be reported to the state registrar by the local registrar or designee of the county board in each of the 87 registration districts pursuant to the rules of the commissioner. The information in clause (1) necessary to compile the report shall be furnished by the applicant prior to the issuance of the marriage license. The report shall contain the following:</p>
        <p>(1) personal information on bride and groom:</p>
        <p>(i) name;</p>
        <p>(ii) residence;</p>
        <p>(iii) date and place of birth;</p>
        <p>(iv) if previously married, how terminated; and</p>
        <p>(v) signature of applicant, date signed, and Social Security number; and</p>
        <p>(2) information concerning the marriage:</p>
        <p>(i) date of marriage;</p>
        <p>(ii) place of marriage; and</p>
        <p>(iii) civil or religious ceremony.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.223.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/699/#laws.0.12.0">1978 c 699 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/203/#laws.6.4.0">1997 c 203 art 6 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.15.21.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 15 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/379/#laws.1.113.0">2002 c 379 art 1 s 113</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/0/30/#laws.3.18.0">2021 c 30 art 3 s 18</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.224"><b>144.224</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/372/#laws.0.3.0">2000 c 372 s 3</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.225">
        <h1 class="shn">144.225 DISCLOSURE OF INFORMATION FROM VITAL RECORDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.225.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Public information; access to vital records.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Except as otherwise provided for in this section and section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2252">144.2252</a>, information contained in vital records shall be public information. Physical access to vital records shall be subject to the supervision and regulation of the state registrar and employees pursuant to rules promulgated by the commissioner in order to protect vital records from loss, mutilation or destruction and to prevent improper disclosure of vital records which are confidential or private data on individuals, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02">13.02</a>, subdivisions 3 and 12.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.225.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Data about births.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as otherwise provided in this subdivision, data pertaining to the birth of a child to a woman who was not married to the child's father when the child was conceived nor when the child was born, including the original record of birth and the certified vital record, are confidential data. At the time of the birth of a child to a woman who was not married to the child's father when the child was conceived nor when the child was born, the mother may designate demographic data pertaining to the birth as public. Notwithstanding the designation of the data as confidential, it may be disclosed:</p>
          <p>(1) to a parent or guardian of the child;</p>
          <p>(2) to the child when the child is 16 years of age or older, except as provided in clause (3);</p>
          <p>(3) to the child if the child is a homeless youth;</p>
          <p>(4) under paragraph (b), (e), or (f); or</p>
          <p>(5) pursuant to a court order. For purposes of this section, a subpoena does not constitute a court order.</p>
          <p>(b) Data pertaining to the birth of a child that are not accessible to the public become public data if 100 years have elapsed since the birth of the child who is the subject of the data, or as provided under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.10">13.10</a>, whichever occurs first.</p>
          <p>(c) If a child is adopted, data pertaining to the child's birth are governed by the provisions relating to adoption and birth records, including sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.10#stat.13.10.5">13.10, subdivision 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.218#stat.144.218.1">144.218, subdivision 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2252">and 144.2252</a>.</p>
          <p>(d) The name and address of a mother under paragraph (a) and the child's date of birth may be disclosed to the county social services, Tribal health department, or public health member of a family services collaborative for purposes of providing services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/142D.15">142D.15</a>.</p>
          <p>(e) The commissioner of human services shall have access to birth records for: the purposes of administering medical assistance and the MinnesotaCare program; and other public health purposes as determined by the commissioner of health.</p>
          <p>(f) Tribal child support programs shall have access to birth records for child support enforcement purposes.</p>
          <p>(g) The commissioner of children, youth, and families shall have access to birth records for child support enforcement purposes and other public health purposes as determined by the commissioner of health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.225.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Health data associated with birth registration.</span></h2>
          <p>Information from which an identification of risk for disease, disability, or developmental delay in a mother or child can be made, that is collected in conjunction with birth registration or fetal death reporting, is private data as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.12">13.02, subdivision 12</a>. The commissioner may disclose to a tribal health department or community health board, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145A.02#stat.145A.02.5">145A.02, subdivision 5</a>, health data associated with birth registration which identifies a mother or child at high risk for serious disease, disability, or developmental delay in order to assure access to appropriate health, social, or educational services. Notwithstanding the designation of the private data, the commissioner of human services shall have access to health data associated with birth registration for:</p>
          <p>(1) purposes of administering medical assistance and the MinnesotaCare program; and</p>
          <p>(2) for other public health purposes as determined by the commissioner of health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.225.2b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2b.<span class="headnote">Commissioner of health; duties.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding the designation of certain of this data as confidential under subdivision 2 or private under subdivision 2a, the commissioner shall give the commissioners of human services and children, youth, and families access to birth record data and data contained in recognitions of parentage prepared according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/257.75">257.75 </a>necessary to enable the commissioners of human services and children, youth, and families to identify a child who is subject to threatened injury, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260E.03">260E.03</a>, subdivision 23, by a person responsible for the child's care, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260E.03#stat.260E.03.17">260E.03, subdivision 17</a>. The commissioners shall be given access to all data included on official birth records.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.225.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Laws and rules for preparing vital records.</span></h2>
          <p>No person shall prepare or issue any vital record which purports to be an original, certified copy, or copy of a vital record except as authorized in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.211">144.211</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.227">144.227</a> or the rules of the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.225.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Access to records for research purposes.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The state registrar may permit persons performing medical research access to the information restricted in subdivision 2 or 2a if those persons agree in writing not to disclose private or confidential data on individuals.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.225.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Residents of other states.</span></h2>
          <p>When a resident of another state is born or dies in this state, the state registrar shall send a report of the birth or death to the state of residence.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.225.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Group purchaser identity; nonpublic data; disclosure.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Except as otherwise provided in this subdivision, the named identity of a group purchaser as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62J.03#stat.62J.03.6">62J.03, subdivision 6</a>, collected in association with birth registration is nonpublic data as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02">13.02</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioner may publish, or by other means release to the public, the named identity of a group purchaser as part of an analysis of information collected from the birth registration process. Analysis means the identification of trends in prenatal care and birth outcomes associated with group purchasers. The commissioner may not reveal the named identity of the group purchaser until the group purchaser has had 21 days after receipt of the analysis to review the analysis and comment on it. In releasing data under this subdivision, the commissioner shall include comments received from the group purchaser related to the scientific soundness and statistical validity of the methods used in the analysis. This subdivision does not authorize the commissioner to make public any individual identifying data except as permitted by law.</p>
          <p>(c) A group purchaser may contest whether an analysis made public under paragraph (b) is based on scientifically sound and statistically valid methods in a contested case proceeding under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.57">14.57</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.62">14.62</a>, subject to appeal under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.63">14.63</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.68">14.68</a>. To obtain a contested case hearing, the group purchaser must present a written request to the commissioner before the end of the time period for review and comment. Within ten days of the assignment of an administrative law judge, the group purchaser must demonstrate by clear and convincing evidence the group purchaser's likelihood of succeeding on the merits. If the judge determines that the group purchaser has made this demonstration, the data may not be released during the contested case proceeding and through appeal. If the judge finds that the group purchaser has not made this demonstration, the commissioner may immediately publish, or otherwise make public, the nonpublic group purchaser data, with comments received as set forth in paragraph (b).</p>
          <p>(d) The contested case proceeding and subsequent appeal is not an exclusive remedy and any person may seek a remedy pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.08">13.08</a>, subdivisions 1 to 4, or as otherwise authorized by law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.225.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Certified birth or death record.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) The state registrar or local issuance office shall issue a certified birth or death record or a statement of no vital record found to an individual upon the individual's proper completion of an attestation provided by the commissioner and payment of the required fee:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) to a person who is:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) the subject of the vital record;</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) a child of the subject;</p>
          <p class="in">(iii) the spouse of the subject;</p>
          <p class="in">(iv) a parent of the subject;</p>
          <p class="in">(v) the grandparent or grandchild of the subject;</p>
          <p class="in">(vi) if the requested record is a death record, a sibling of the subject;</p>
          <p class="in">(vii) the legal custodian, guardian or conservator, or health care agent of the subject;</p>
          <p class="in">(viii) a personal representative, by sworn affidavit of the fact that the certified copy is required for administration of the estate;</p>
          <p class="in">(ix) a successor of the subject, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/524.1-201">524.1-201</a>, if the subject is deceased, by sworn affidavit of the fact that the certified copy is required for administration of the estate;</p>
          <p class="in">(x) if the requested record is a death record, a trustee of a trust by sworn affidavit of the fact that the certified copy is needed for the proper administration of the trust;</p>
          <p class="in">(xi) a person or entity who demonstrates that a certified vital record is necessary for the determination or protection of a personal or property right, pursuant to rules adopted by the commissioner; or</p>
          <p class="in">(xii) an adoption agency in order to complete confidential postadoption searches as required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/259.83">259.83</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) to any local, state, tribal, or federal governmental agency upon request if the certified vital record is necessary for the governmental agency to perform its authorized duties;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) to an attorney representing the subject of the vital record or another person listed in clause (1), upon evidence of the attorney's license;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) pursuant to a court order issued by a court of competent jurisdiction. For purposes of this section, a subpoena does not constitute a court order; or</p>
          <p class="in">(5) to a representative authorized by a person under clauses (1) to (4).</p>
          <p class="in">(b) The state registrar or local issuance office shall also issue a certified death record to an individual described in paragraph (a), clause (1), items (ii) to (xi), if, on behalf of the individual, a licensed mortician furnishes the registrar with a properly completed attestation in the form provided by the commissioner within 180 days of the time of death of the subject of the death record. This paragraph is not subject to the requirements specified in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4601.2600">4601.2600</a>, subpart 5, item B.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.225.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Standardized format for certified birth and death records.</span></h2>
          <p class="in"> The commissioner shall maintain a standardized format for certified birth records and death records issued by the state registrar and local issuance offices. The format shall incorporate security features in accordance with this section.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.225.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/699/#laws.0.14.0">1978 c 699 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/509/#laws.0.42.0">1980 c 509 s 42</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/561/#laws.0.2.0">1980 c 561 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/311/#laws.0.39.0">1981 c 311 s 39</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/545/#laws.0.24.0">1982 c 545 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/7/#laws.0.2.0">1983 c 7 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1983/0/243/#laws.0.5.0">1983 c 243 s 5</a> subd 2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/654/#laws.5.58.0">1984 c 654 art 5 s 58</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/203/#laws.0.1.0">1991 c 203 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/631/#laws.0.31.0">1994 c 631 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/259/#laws.1.33.0">1995 c 259 art 1 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/440/#laws.1.34.0">1996 c 440 art 1 s 34</a>,35; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/228/#laws.0.9.0">1997 c 228 s 9</a>-11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/397/#laws.11.3.0">1998 c 397 art 11 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/267/#laws.0.1.0">2000 c 267 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/15/#laws.0.1.0">2001 c 15 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/178/#laws.1.1.0">2001 c 178 art 1 s 1</a>;       </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.2252">
        <h1 class="shn">144.2252 ACCESS TO ORIGINAL BIRTH RECORD AFTER ADOPTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2252.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Person related to the adopted person" means:</p>
          <p>(1) the spouse, child, or grandchild of an adopted person, if the spouse, child, or grandchild is at least 18 years of age; or</p>
          <p>(2) the legal representative of an adopted person.</p>
          <p class="bl">The definition under this paragraph only applies when the adopted person is deceased.</p>
          <p>(c) "Original birth record" means a copy of the original birth record for a person who is born in Minnesota and whose original birth record was sealed and replaced by a replacement birth record after the state registrar received a certified copy of an order, decree, or certificate of adoption.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2252.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Release of original birth record.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The state registrar must provide to an adopted person who is 18 years of age or older or a person related to the adopted person a copy of the adopted person's original birth record and any evidence of the adoption previously filed with the state registrar. To receive a copy of an original birth record under this subdivision, the adopted person or person related to the adopted person must make the request to the state registrar in writing. The copy of the original birth record must clearly indicate that it may not be used for identification purposes. All procedures, fees, and waiting periods applicable to a nonadopted person's request for a copy of a birth record apply in the same manner as requests made under this section.</p>
          <p>(b) If a contact preference form is attached to the original birth record as authorized under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2253">144.2253</a>, the state registrar must provide a copy of the contact preference form along with the copy of the adopted person's original birth record.</p>
          <p>(c) The state registrar shall provide a transcript of an adopted person's original birth record to an authorized representative of a federally recognized American Indian Tribe for the sole purpose of determining the adopted person's eligibility for enrollment or membership. Information contained in the birth record may not be used to provide the adopted person information about the person's birth parents, except as provided in this section or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/259.83">259.83</a>.</p>
          <p>(d) For a replacement birth record issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.218">144.218</a>, the adopted person or a person related to the adopted person may obtain from the state registrar copies of the order or decree of adoption, certificate of adoption, or decree issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/259.60">259.60</a>, as filed with the state registrar.</p>
          <p>(e) The state registrar may request assistance from the commissioner of children, youth, and families if needed to discharge duties under this section, as authorized under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/259.79">259.79</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2252.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Adult adoptions.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.218">144.218</a>, a person adopted as an adult may access the person's birth records that existed before the person's adult adoption. Access to the existing birth records shall be the same access that was permitted prior to the adult adoption.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.2252.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.15.27.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 15 s 27</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/379/#laws.1.113.0">2002 c 379 art 1 s 113</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.4.32.0">2023 c 70 art 4 s 32</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/115/#laws.18.8.0">2024 c 115 art 18 s 8</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.2253">
        <h1 class="shn">144.2253 BIRTH PARENT CONTACT PREFERENCE FORM.</h1>
        <p>(a) The commissioner must make available to the public a contact preference form as described in paragraph (b).</p>
        <p>(b) The contact preference form must provide the following information to be completed at the option of a birth parent:</p>
        <p>(1) "I would like to be contacted."</p>
        <p>(2) "I would prefer to be contacted only through an intermediary."</p>
        <p>(3) "I prefer not to be contacted at this time. If I decide later that I would like to be contacted, I will submit an updated contact preference form to the Minnesota Department of Health."</p>
        <p>(c) A contact preference form must include space where the birth parent may include information that the birth parent feels is important for the adopted person to know.</p>
        <p>(d) If a birth parent of an adopted person submits a completed contact preference form to the commissioner, the commissioner must:</p>
        <p>(1) match the contact preference form to the adopted person's original birth record. The commissioner may request assistance from the commissioner of children, youth, and families if needed to discharge duties under this clause, as authorized under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/259.79">259.79</a>; and</p>
        <p>(2) attach the contact preference form to the original birth record as required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2252">144.2252</a>.</p>
        <p>(e) A contact preference form submitted to the commissioner under this section is private data on an individual as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.12">13.02, subdivision 12</a>, except that the contact preference form may be released as provided under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2252#stat.144.2252.2">144.2252, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.2253.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.4.33.0">2023 c 70 art 4 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/115/#laws.18.9.0">2024 c 115 art 18 s 9</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.2254">
        <h1 class="shn">144.2254 PREVIOUSLY FILED CONSENTS TO DISCLOSURE AND AFFIDAVITS OF NONDISCLOSURE.</h1>
        <p>(a) The commissioner must inform a person applying for an original birth record under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2252">144.2252</a> of the existence of an unrevoked consent to disclosure or an affidavit of nondisclosure on file with the department, including the name of the birth parent who filed the consent or affidavit. If a birth parent authorized the release of the birth parent's address on an unrevoked consent to disclosure, the commissioner shall provide the address to the person who requests the original birth record.</p>
        <p>(b) A birth parent's consent to disclosure or affidavit of nondisclosure filed with the commissioner of health expires and has no force or effect beginning on June 30, 2024.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.2254.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.4.34.0">2023 c 70 art 4 s 34</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.2255">
        <h1 class="shn">144.2255 CERTIFIED BIRTH RECORD FOR HOMELESS YOUTH.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2255.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Application; certified birth record.</span></h2>
          <p>A subject of a birth record who is a homeless youth in Minnesota or another state may apply to the state registrar or a local issuance office for a certified birth record according to this section. The state registrar or local issuance office shall issue a certified birth record or statement of no vital record found to a subject of a birth record who submits:</p>
          <p>(1) a completed application signed by the subject of the birth record;</p>
          <p>(2) a statement that the subject of the birth record is a homeless youth, signed by the subject of the birth record; and</p>
          <p>(3) one of the following:</p>
          <p>(i) a document of identity listed in Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4601.2600">4601.2600</a>, subpart 8, or, at the discretion of the state registrar or local issuance office, Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4601.2600">4601.2600</a>, subpart 9;</p>
          <p>(ii) a statement that complies with Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4601.2600">4601.2600</a>, subparts 6 and 7; or</p>
          <p>(iii) a statement verifying that the subject of the birth record is a homeless youth that complies with the requirements in subdivision 2 and is from an employee of a human services agency that receives public funding to provide services to homeless youth, runaway youth, youth with mental illness, or youth with substance use disorders; a school staff person who provides services to homeless youth; or a school social worker.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2255.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Statement verifying subject is a homeless youth.</span></h2>
          <p>A statement verifying that a subject of a birth record is a homeless youth must include:</p>
          <p>(1) the following information regarding the individual providing the statement: first name, middle name, if any, and last name; home or business address; telephone number, if any; and email address, if any;</p>
          <p>(2) the first name, middle name, if any, and last name of the subject of the birth record; and</p>
          <p>(3) a statement specifying the relationship of the individual providing the statement to the subject of the birth record and verifying that the subject of the birth record is a homeless youth.</p>
          <p class="bl">The individual providing the statement must also provide a copy of the individual's employment identification.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2255.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Expiration; reissuance.</span></h2>
          <p>If a subject of a birth record obtains a certified birth record under this section using the statement specified in subdivision 1, clause (3), item (iii), the certified birth record issued shall expire six months after the date of issuance. Upon expiration of the certified birth record, the subject of the birth record may surrender the expired birth record to the state registrar or a local issuance office and obtain another birth record. Each certified birth record obtained under this subdivision shall expire six months after the date of issuance. If the subject of the birth record does not surrender the expired birth record, the subject may apply for a certified birth record using the process in subdivision 1.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2255.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Data practices.</span></h2>
          <p>Data listed under subdivision 1, clauses (2) and (3), item (iii), are private data on individuals.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.2255.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/7/#laws.3.27.0">1Sp2021 c 7 art 3 s 27</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.226">
        <h1 class="shn">144.226 FEES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.226.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Which services are for fee.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The fees for the following services shall be the following or an amount prescribed by rule of the commissioner:</p>
          <p>(b) The fee for the administrative review and processing of a request for a certified vital record or a certification that the vital record cannot be found is $9. The fee is payable at the time of application and is nonrefundable.</p>
          <p>(c) The fee for processing a request for the replacement of a birth record for all events, except when filing a recognition of parentage pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/257.73#stat.257.73.1">257.73, subdivision 1</a>, is $40. The fee is payable at the time of application and is nonrefundable.</p>
          <p>(d) The fee for administrative review and processing of a request for the filing of a delayed registration of birth, stillbirth, or death is $40. The fee is payable at the time of application and is nonrefundable.</p>
          <p>(e) The fee for administrative review and processing of a request for the amendment of any vital record is $40. The fee is payable at the time of application and is nonrefundable.</p>
          <p>(f) The fee for administrative review and processing of a request for the verification of information from vital records is $9 when the applicant furnishes the specific information to locate the vital record. When the applicant does not furnish specific information, the fee is $20 per hour for staff time expended. Specific information includes the correct date of the event and the correct name of the subject of the record. Fees charged shall approximate the costs incurred in searching and copying the vital records. The fee is payable at the time of application and is nonrefundable.</p>
          <p>(g) The fee for administrative review and processing of a request for the issuance of a copy of any document on file pertaining to a vital record or statement that a related document cannot be found is $9. The fee is payable at the time of application and is nonrefundable.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.226.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Fees to state government special revenue fund.</span></h2>
          <p>Fees collected under this section by the state registrar shall be deposited in the state treasury and credited to the state government special revenue fund.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.226.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Birth record surcharge.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) In addition to any fee prescribed under subdivision 1, there shall be a nonrefundable surcharge of $3 for each certified birth or stillbirth record and for a certification that the vital record cannot be found. The state registrar or local issuance office shall forward this amount to the commissioner of management and budget each month following the collection of the surcharge for deposit into the account for the children's trust fund for the prevention of child abuse established under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/142A.412">142A.412</a>. This surcharge shall not be charged under those circumstances in which no fee for a certified birth or stillbirth record is permitted under subdivision 1, paragraph (b). Upon certification by the commissioner of management and budget that the assets in that fund exceed $20,000,000, this surcharge shall be discontinued.</p>
          <p>(b) In addition to any fee prescribed under subdivision 1, there shall be a nonrefundable surcharge of $10 for each certified birth record. The state registrar or local issuance office shall forward this amount to the commissioner of management and budget each month following the collection of the surcharge for deposit in the general fund.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.226.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Vital records surcharge.</span></h2>
          <p> In addition to any fee prescribed under subdivision 1, there is a nonrefundable surcharge of $4 for each certified and noncertified birth, stillbirth, or death record, and for a certification that the record cannot be found. The local issuance office or state registrar shall forward this amount to the commissioner of management and budget each month following the collection of the surcharge to be deposited into the state government special revenue fund.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.226.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Electronic verification.</span></h2>
          <p>A fee for the electronic verification or electronic certification of a vital event, when the information being verified or certified is obtained from a certified birth or death record, shall be established through contractual or interagency agreements.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.226.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Alternative payment methods.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding subdivision 1, alternative payment methods may be approved and implemented by the state registrar or a local issuance office.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.226.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Transaction fees.</span></h2>
          <p>The state registrar may charge and permit agents to charge a convenience fee and a transaction fee for electronic transactions and transactions by telephone or Internet, as well as the fees established under subdivisions 1 to 4. The convenience fee may not exceed three percent of the cost of the charges for payment. The state registrar may permit agents to charge and retain a transaction fee as payment agreed upon under contract. When an electronic convenience fee or transaction fee is charged, the agent charging the fee is required to post information on their web page informing individuals of the fee. The information must be near the point of payment, clearly visible, include the amount of the fee, and state: "This contracted agent is allowed by state law to charge a convenience fee and transaction fee for this electronic transaction."</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.226.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Birth record fees waived for homeless youth.</span></h2>
          <p>A subject of a birth record who is a homeless youth shall not be charged any of the fees specified in this section for a certified birth record or statement of no vital record found under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2255">144.2255</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.226.history
			">

      <div class="section" id="stat.144.227">
        <h1 class="shn">144.227 PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.227.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">False statements.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who intentionally makes a false statement in a certificate, vital record, or report required to be filed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.211">144.211 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.2131">144.2131</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.216">144.216</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.227">144.227</a>, or in an application for an amendment thereof, or in an application for a certified vital record or who supplies false information intending that the information be used in the preparation of a report, vital record, certificate, or amendment thereof, is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.227.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Fraud.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who, without lawful authority and with the intent to deceive, willfully and knowingly makes, counterfeits, alters, obtains, possesses, uses, or sells a certificate, vital record, or report required to be filed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.211">144.211</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.227">144.227</a> or a certified certificate, vital record, or report, is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.227.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Birth registration.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who intentionally makes a false statement in a registration required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.215">144.215</a> or in an application for an amendment to such a registration or who intentionally supplies false information intending that the information be used in the preparation of a registration under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.215">144.215</a> is guilty of a gross misdemeanor. This offense shall be prosecuted by the county attorney.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.227.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/699/#laws.0.16.0">1978 c 699 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/631/#laws.0.1.0">1994 c 631 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/9/#laws.15.30.0">1Sp2001 c 9 art 15 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/379/#laws.1.113.0">2002 c 379 art 1 s 113</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.27.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 27</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.23"><b>144.23</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/512/#laws.0.37.0">1945 c 512 s 37</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.24"><b>144.24</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/512/#laws.0.37.0">1945 c 512 s 37</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.25"><b>144.25</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/512/#laws.0.37.0">1945 c 512 s 37</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.26"><b>144.26</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/512/#laws.0.37.0">1945 c 512 s 37</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.27"><b>144.27</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/512/#laws.0.37.0">1945 c 512 s 37</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.28"><b>144.28</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/512/#laws.0.37.0">1945 c 512 s 37</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">HEALTH RECORDS AND REPORTS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.29">
        <h1 class="shn">144.29 HEALTH RECORDS; CHILDREN OF SCHOOL AGE.</h1>
        <p>It shall be the duty of every school nurse, school physician, school attendance officer, superintendent of schools, principal, teacher, and of the persons charged with the duty of compiling and keeping the school census records, to cause a health record to be kept for each child of school age. Such record shall be kept in such form that it may be transferred with the child to any school which the child shall attend within the state. It shall contain a record of such student health data as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.32#stat.13.32.2">13.32, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (a), and shall be classified as private data as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.32#stat.13.32.3">13.32, subdivision 3</a>. Nothing in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.29">144.29</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.32">144.32</a> shall be construed to require any child whose parent or guardian objects in writing thereto to undergo a physical or medical examination or treatment. A copy shall be forwarded to the proper department of any state to which the child shall remove. Each district shall assign a teacher, school nurse, or other professional person to review, at the beginning of each school year, the health record of all pupils under the assignee's direction. Growth, results of vision and hearing screening, and findings obtained from health assessments must be entered periodically on the pupil's health record.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.29.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/29">5356-1</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1929/0/277/#laws.0.1.0">1929 c 277 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/224/#laws.12.30.0">1993 c 224 art 12 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/3/#laws.0.23.0">1Sp1997 c 3 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/1/4/#laws.6.16.0">1Sp1997 c 4 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">MINNESOTA HEALTH RECORDS ACT</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.291">
        <h1 class="shn">144.291 MINNESOTA HEALTH RECORDS ACT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.291.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Short title.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291">144.291</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.298">144.298</a> may be cited as the "Minnesota Health Records Act."</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.291.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">For the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291">144.291</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.298">144.298</a>, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p class="in">(a) "Group purchaser" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62J.03">62J.03</a>, subdivision 6.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) "Health information exchange" means a legal arrangement between health care providers and group purchasers to enable and oversee the business and legal issues involved in the electronic exchange of health records between the entities for the delivery of patient care.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) "Health record" means any information, whether oral or recorded in any form or medium, that relates to the past, present, or future physical or mental health or condition of a patient; the provision of health care to a patient; or the past, present, or future payment for the provision of health care to a patient.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) "Identifying information" means the patient's name, address, date of birth, gender, parent's or guardian's name regardless of the age of the patient, and other nonclinical data which can be used to uniquely identify a patient.</p>
          <p class="in">(e) "Individually identifiable form" means a form in which the patient is or can be identified as the subject of the health records.</p>
          <p class="in">(f) "Medical emergency" means medically necessary care which is immediately needed to preserve life, prevent serious impairment to bodily functions, organs, or parts, or prevent placing the physical or mental health of the patient in serious jeopardy.</p>
          <p class="in">(g) "Patient" means a natural person who has received health care services from a provider for treatment or examination of a medical, psychiatric, or mental condition, the surviving spouse and parents of a deceased patient, or a person the patient appoints in writing as a representative, including a health care agent acting according to chapter 145C, unless the authority of the agent has been limited by the principal in the principal's health care directive. Except for minors who have received health care services under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.341">144.341</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.347">144.347</a>, in the case of a minor, patient includes a parent or guardian, or a person acting as a parent or guardian in the absence of a parent or guardian.</p>
          <p>(h) "Patient information service" means a service providing the following query options: a record locator service as defined in paragraph (j) or a master patient index or clinical data repository as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62J.498">62J.498</a>, subdivision 1.</p>
          <p class="in">(i) "Provider" means:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) any person who furnishes health care services and is regulated to furnish the services under chapter 147, 147A, 147B, 147C, 147D, 148, 148B, 148D, 148F, 150A, 151, 153, or 153A;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) a home care provider licensed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.471">144A.471</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) a health care facility licensed under this chapter or chapter 144A;</p>
          <p>(4) an assisted living facility licensed under chapter 144G; and</p>
          <p class="in">(5) a physician assistant registered under chapter 147A.</p>
          <p class="in">(j) "Record locator service" means an electronic index of patient identifying information that directs providers in a health information exchange to the location of patient health records held by providers and group purchasers.</p>
          <p class="in">(k) "Related health care entity" means an affiliate, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.6521#stat.144.6521.3">144.6521, subdivision 3</a>, paragraph (b), of the provider releasing the health records.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.291.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.10.2.0">2007 c 147 art 10 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/187/#laws.1.21.0">2012 c 187 art 1 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/197/#laws.2.44.0">2012 c 197 art 2 s 44</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.8.18.0">2015 c 71 art 8 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/7/1/#laws.6.25.0">7Sp2020 c 1 art 6 s 25</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.292">
        <h1 class="shn">144.292 PATIENT RIGHTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.292.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Patients have the rights specified in this section regarding the treatment the patient receives and the patient's health record.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.292.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Patient access.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Upon request, a provider shall supply to a patient within 30 calendar days of receiving a written request for medical records complete and current information possessed by that provider concerning any diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis of the patient in terms and language the patient can reasonably be expected to understand.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.292.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Additional patient rights.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A patient's right specified in this section and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.293">144.293</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.298">144.298</a> are in addition to the rights specified in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.651">144.651</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.652">144.652</a> and any other provision of law relating to the access of a patient to the patient's health records.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.292.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Notice of rights; information on release.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A provider shall provide to patients, in a clear and conspicuous manner, a written notice concerning practices and rights with respect to access to health records. The notice must include an explanation of:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) disclosures of health records that may be made without the written consent of the patient, including the type of records and to whom the records may be disclosed; and</p>
          <p class="in">(2) the right of the patient to have access to and obtain copies of the patient's health records and other information about the patient that is maintained by the provider.</p>
          <p class="in">The notice requirements of this subdivision are satisfied if the notice is included with the notice and copy of the patient and resident bill of rights under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.652">144.652</a> or if it is displayed prominently in the provider's place of business. The commissioner of health shall develop the notice required in this subdivision and publish it in the State Register.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.292.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Copies of health records to patients.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Except as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.296">144.296</a>, upon a patient's written request, a provider, at a reasonable cost to the patient, shall furnish to the patient within 30 calendar days of receiving a written request for medical records:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) copies of the patient's health record, including but not limited to laboratory reports, x-rays, prescriptions, and other technical information used in assessing the patient's health conditions; or</p>
          <p class="in">(2) the pertinent portion of the record relating to a condition specified by the patient.</p>
          <p class="in">With the consent of the patient, the provider may instead furnish only a summary of the record. The provider may exclude from the health record written speculations about the patient's health condition, except that all information necessary for the patient's informed consent must be provided.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.292.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Cost.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) When a patient requests a copy of the patient's record for purposes of reviewing current medical care, the provider must not charge a fee.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) When a provider or its representative makes copies of patient records upon a patient's request under this section, the provider or its representative may charge the patient or the patient's representative no more than the following amount, unless other law or a rule or contract provide for a lower maximum charge:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) for paper copies, $1 per page, plus $10 for time spent retrieving and copying the records;</p>
          <p>(2) for x-rays, a total of $30 for retrieving and reproducing x-rays; and</p>
          <p class="in">(3) for electronic copies, a total of $20 for retrieving the records.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) For any copies of paper records provided under paragraph (b), clause (1), a provider or the provider's representative may not charge more than a total of:</p>
          <p>(1) $10 if there are no records available;</p>
          <p>(2) $30 for copies of records of up to 25 pages;</p>
          <p>(3) $50 for copies of records of up to 100 pages;</p>
          <p>(4) $50, plus an additional 20 cents per page for pages 101 and above; or</p>
          <p class="in">(5) $500 for any request.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) A provider or its representative may charge a $10 retrieval fee, but must not charge a per page fee or x-ray fee to provide copies of records requested by a patient or the patient's authorized representative if the request for copies of records is for purposes of appealing a denial of Social Security disability income or Social Security disability benefits under title II or title XVI of the Social Security Act. Notwithstanding the foregoing, a provider or its representative must not charge a fee, including a retrieval fee, to provide copies of records requested by a patient or the patient's authorized representative if the request for copies of records is for purposes of appealing a denial of Social Security disability income or Social Security disability benefits under title II or title XVI of the Social Security Act when the patient is receiving public assistance, represented by an attorney on behalf of a civil legal services program, or represented by a volunteer attorney program based on indigency. The patient or the patient's representative must submit one of the following to show that they are entitled to receive records without charge under this paragraph:</p>
          <p>(1) a public assistance statement from the county or state administering assistance;</p>
          <p>(2) a request for records on the letterhead of the civil legal services program or volunteer attorney program based on indigency; or</p>
          <p>(3) a benefits statement from the Social Security Administration.</p>
          <p class="bl">For the purpose of further appeals, a patient may receive no more than two medical record updates without charge, but only for medical record information previously not provided.</p>
          <p class="bl">For purposes of this paragraph, a patient's authorized representative does not include units of state government engaged in the adjudication of Social Security disability claims.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.292.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Withholding health records from patient.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) If a provider, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291#stat.144.291.2">144.291, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (i), clause (1), reasonably determines that the information is detrimental to the physical or mental health of the patient, or is likely to cause the patient to inflict self harm, or to harm another, the provider may withhold the information from the patient and may supply the information to an appropriate third party or to another provider, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291#stat.144.291.2">144.291, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (i), clause (1). The other provider or third party may release the information to the patient.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) A provider, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291#stat.144.291.2">144.291, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (i), clause (3), shall release information upon written request unless, prior to the request, a provider, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291#stat.144.291.2">144.291, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (i), clause (1), has designated and described a specific basis for withholding the information as authorized by paragraph (a).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.292.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Form.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">By January 1, 2008, the Department of Health must develop a form that may be used by a patient to request access to health records under this section. A form developed by the commissioner must be accepted by a provider as a legally enforceable request under this section.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.292.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.10.3.0">2007 c 147 art 10 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/247/#laws.2.4.0">2012 c 247 art 2 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/83/#laws.2.3.0">2020 c 83 art 2 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.1.10.0">2020 c 115 art 1 s 10</a>,11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/98/#laws.1.7.0">2022 c 98 art 1 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.66.6.0">2024 c 127 art 66 s 6</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.2925">
        <h1 class="shn">144.2925 CONSTRUCTION.</h1>
        <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291">144.291</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.298">144.298</a> must be construed to protect the privacy of a patient's health records in a more stringent manner than provided in Code of Federal Regulations, title 45, part 164. For purposes of this section, "more stringent" has the meaning given to that term in Code of Federal Regulations, title 45, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/160.202">160.202</a>, with respect to a use or disclosure or the need for express legal permission from an individual to disclose individually identifiable health information.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.2925.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.66.7.0">2024 c 127 art 66 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.293">
        <h1 class="shn">144.293 RELEASE OR DISCLOSURE OF HEALTH RECORDS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.293.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Release or disclosure of health records.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Health records can be released or disclosed as specified in subdivisions 2 to 9 and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.294">144.294</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.295">144.295</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.293.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Patient consent to release of records.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A provider, or a person who receives health records from a provider, may not release a patient's health records to a person without:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) a signed and dated consent from the patient or the patient's legally authorized representative authorizing the release;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) specific authorization in Minnesota law; or</p>
          <p class="in">(3) a representation from a provider that holds a signed and dated consent from the patient authorizing the release.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.293.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Release from one provider to another.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A patient's health record, including, but not limited to, laboratory reports, x-rays, prescriptions, and other technical information used in assessing the patient's condition, or the pertinent portion of the record relating to a specific condition, or a summary of the record, shall promptly be furnished to another provider upon the written request of the patient. The written request shall specify the name of the provider to whom the health record is to be furnished. The provider who furnishes the health record or summary may retain a copy of the materials furnished. The patient shall be responsible for the reasonable costs of furnishing the information.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.293.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Duration of consent.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Except as provided in this section, a consent is valid for one year or for a period specified in the consent or for a different period provided by Minnesota law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.293.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Exceptions to consent requirement.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) This section does not prohibit the release of health records:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) for a medical emergency when the provider is unable to obtain the patient's consent due to the patient's condition or the nature of the medical emergency;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) to other providers within related health care entities when necessary for the current treatment of the patient; or</p>
          <p class="in">(3) to a health care facility licensed by this chapter, chapter 144A, and chapter 144G, or to the same types of health care facilities licensed by this chapter and chapter 144A that are licensed in another state when a patient:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) is returning to the health care facility and unable to provide consent; or</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) who resides in the health care facility, has services provided by an outside resource under Code of Federal Regulations, title 42, section 483.75(h), and is unable to provide consent.</p>
          <p>(b) A provider may release a deceased patient's health care records to another provider for the purposes of diagnosing or treating the deceased patient's surviving adult child.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.293.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Consent does not expire.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Notwithstanding subdivision 4, if a patient explicitly gives informed consent to the release of health records for the purposes and restrictions in clause (1), (2), or (3), the consent does not expire after one year for:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) the release of health records to a provider who is being advised or consulted with in connection with the releasing provider's current treatment of the patient;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) the release of health records to an accident and health insurer, health service plan corporation, health maintenance organization, or third-party administrator for purposes of payment of claims, fraud investigation, or quality of care review and studies, provided that:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) the use or release of the records complies with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/72A.49">72A.49</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/72A.505">72A.505</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) further use or release of the records in individually identifiable form to a person other than the patient without the patient's consent is prohibited; and</p>
          <p class="in">(iii) the recipient establishes adequate safeguards to protect the records from unauthorized disclosure, including a procedure for removal or destruction of information that identifies the patient; or</p>
          <p class="in">(3) the release of health records to a program in the welfare system, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.46">13.46</a>, to the extent necessary to coordinate services for the patient.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.293.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Exception to consent.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Subdivision 2 does not apply to the release of health records to the commissioner of health or the Health Data Institute under chapter 62J, provided that the commissioner encrypts the patient identifier upon receipt of the data.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.293.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Record locator or patient information service.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) A provider or group purchaser may release patient identifying information and information about the location of the patient's health records to a record locator or patient information service without consent from the patient, unless the patient has elected to be excluded from the service under paragraph (d). The Department of Health may not access the record locator or patient information service or receive data from the service. Only a provider may have access to patient identifying information in a record locator or patient information service. Except in the case of a medical emergency, a provider participating in a health information exchange using a record locator or patient information service does not have access to patient identifying information and information about the location of the patient's health records unless the patient specifically consents to the access. A consent does not expire but may be revoked by the patient at any time by providing written notice of the revocation to the provider.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) A health information exchange maintaining a record locator or patient information service must maintain an audit log of providers accessing information in the service that at least contains information on:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) the identity of the provider accessing the information;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) the identity of the patient whose information was accessed by the provider; and</p>
          <p class="in">(3) the date the information was accessed.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) No group purchaser may in any way require a provider to participate in a record locator or patient information service as a condition of payment or participation.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) A provider or an entity operating a record locator or patient information service must provide a mechanism under which patients may exclude their identifying information and information about the location of their health records from a record locator or patient information service. At a minimum, a consent form that permits a provider to access a record locator or patient information service must include a conspicuous check-box option that allows a patient to exclude all of the patient's information from the service. A provider participating in a health information exchange with a record locator or patient information service who receives a patient's request to exclude all of the patient's information from the service or to have a specific provider contact excluded from the service is responsible for removing that information from the service.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.293.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Documentation of release.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) In cases where a provider releases health records without patient consent as authorized by Minnesota law, the release must be documented in the patient's health record. In the case of a release under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.294#stat.144.294.2">144.294, subdivision 2</a>, the documentation must include the date and circumstances under which the release was made, the person or agency to whom the release was made, and the records that were released.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) When a health record is released using a representation from a provider that holds a consent from the patient, the releasing provider shall document:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) the provider requesting the health records;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) the identity of the patient;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) the health records requested; and</p>
          <p class="in">(4) the date the health records were requested.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.293.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Warranties regarding consents, requests, and disclosures.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) When requesting health records using consent, a person warrants that the consent:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) contains no information known to the person to be false; and</p>
          <p class="in">(2) accurately states the patient's desire to have health records disclosed or that there is specific authorization in Minnesota law.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) When requesting health records using consent, or a representation of holding a consent, a provider warrants that the request:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) contains no information known to the provider to be false;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) accurately states the patient's desire to have health records disclosed or that there is specific authorization in Minnesota law; and</p>
          <p class="in">(3) does not exceed any limits imposed by the patient in the consent.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) When disclosing health records, a person releasing health records warrants that the person:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) has complied with the requirements of this section regarding disclosure of health records;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) knows of no information related to the request that is false; and</p>
          <p class="in">(3) has complied with the limits set by the patient in the consent.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.293.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.10.4.0">2007 c 147 art 10 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/1/1/#laws.20.7.0">1Sp2010 c 1 art 20 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.2.4.0">2015 c 71 art 2 s 4</a>; art 8 s 19,20; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/7/1/#laws.6.25.0">7Sp2020 c 1 art 6 s 25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.66.8.0">2024 c 127 art 66 s 8</a>-11</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.2935">
        <h1 class="shn">144.2935 HEALTH RECORDS; REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH CARE SERVICES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2935.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of this section, "reproductive health care services" means medical, surgical, counseling, or referral services relating to the human reproductive system, including but not limited to services related to pregnancy, contraception, or the termination of a pregnancy.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.2935.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Law or court order of another state.</span></h2>
          <p>Neither a law in another state authorizing a civil or criminal subpoena to obtain a patient's health records relating to the provision of reproductive health care services to the patient, nor an order issued by a court in another state authorizing the investigation or enforcement of another state's law that restricts or punishes the provision, receipt, or attempted provision or receipt of reproductive health care services to a patient, constitutes a specific authorization in law under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.293">144.293</a>, subdivision 2.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.2935.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/31/#laws.0.1.0">2023 c 31 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.294">
        <h1 class="shn">144.294 RECORDS RELATING TO MENTAL HEALTH.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.294.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Provider inquiry.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Upon the written request of a spouse, parent, child, or sibling of a patient being evaluated for or diagnosed with mental illness, a provider shall inquire of a patient whether the patient wishes to authorize a specific individual to receive information regarding the patient's current and proposed course of treatment. If the patient so authorizes, the provider shall communicate to the designated individual the patient's current and proposed course of treatment.
