Section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.293">144.293</a>, subdivisions 2 and 4, apply to consents given under this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.294.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Disclosure to law enforcement agency.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.293">144.293</a>, subdivisions 2 and 4, a provider must disclose health records relating to a patient's mental health to a law enforcement agency if the law enforcement agency provides the name of the patient and communicates that the:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) patient is currently involved in a mental health crisis as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0624#stat.256B.0624.2">256B.0624, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (j), to which the law enforcement agency has responded; and</p>
          <p class="in">(2) disclosure of the records is necessary to protect the health or safety of the patient or of another person.</p>
          <p class="in">The scope of disclosure under this subdivision is limited to the minimum necessary for law enforcement to safely respond to the mental health crisis. The disclosure may include the name and telephone number of the psychiatrist, psychologist, therapist, mental health professional, practitioner, or case manager of the patient, if known; and strategies to address the mental health crisis. A law enforcement agency that obtains health records under this subdivision shall maintain a record of the requestor, the provider of the information, and the patient's name. Health records obtained by a law enforcement agency under this subdivision are private data on individuals as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02">13.02</a>, subdivision 12, and must not be used by law enforcement for any other purpose. A law enforcement agency that obtains health records under this subdivision shall inform the patient that health records were obtained.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.294.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Records release for family and caretaker; mental health care.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.293">144.293</a>, a provider providing mental health care and treatment may disclose health record information described in paragraph (b) about a patient to a family member of the patient or other person who requests the information if:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) the request for information is in writing;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) the family member or other person lives with, provides care for, or is directly involved in monitoring the treatment of the patient;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) the involvement under clause (2) is verified by the patient's mental health care provider, the patient's attending physician, or a person other than the person requesting the information, and is documented in the patient's medical record;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) before the disclosure, the patient is informed in writing of the request, the name of the person requesting the information, the reason for the request, and the specific information being requested;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) the patient agrees to the disclosure, does not object to the disclosure, or is unable to consent or object, and the patient's decision or inability to make a decision is documented in the patient's medical record; and</p>
          <p class="in">(6) the disclosure is necessary to assist in the provision of care or monitoring of the patient's treatment.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) The information disclosed under this paragraph is limited to diagnosis, admission to or discharge from treatment, the name and dosage of the medications prescribed, side effects of the medication, consequences of failure of the patient to take the prescribed medication, and a summary of the discharge plan.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) If a provider reasonably determines that providing information under this subdivision would be detrimental to the physical or mental health of the patient or is likely to cause the patient to inflict self harm or to harm another, the provider must not disclose the information.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) This subdivision does not apply to disclosures for a medical emergency or to family members as authorized or required under subdivision 1 or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.293">144.293</a>, subdivision 5, clause (1).</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.294.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.10.5.0">2007 c 147 art 10 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/98/#laws.6.3.0">2022 c 98 art 6 s 3</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.295">
        <h1 class="shn">144.295 DISCLOSURE OF HEALTH RECORDS FOR EXTERNAL RESEARCH.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.295.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Methods of release.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.293">144.293</a>, subdivisions 2 and 4, health records may be released to an external researcher solely for purposes of medical or scientific research only as follows:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) health records generated before January 1, 1997, may be released if the patient has not objected or does not elect to object after that date;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) for health records generated on or after January 1, 1997, the provider must:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) disclose in writing to patients currently being treated by the provider that health records, regardless of when generated, may be released and that the patient may object, in which case the records will not be released; and</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) use reasonable efforts to obtain the patient's written general authorization that describes the release of records in item (i), which does not expire but may be revoked or limited in writing at any time by the patient or the patient's authorized representative;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) the provider must advise the patient of the rights specified in clause (4); and</p>
          <p class="in">(4) the provider must, at the request of the patient, provide information on how the patient may contact an external researcher to whom the health record was released and the date it was released.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) Authorization may be established if an authorization is mailed at least two times to the patient's last known address with a postage prepaid return envelope and a conspicuous notice that the patient's medical records may be released if the patient does not object, and at least 60 days have expired since the second notice was sent.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.295.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Duties of researcher.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">In making a release for research purposes, the provider shall make a reasonable effort to determine that:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) the use or disclosure does not violate any limitations under which the record was collected;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) the use or disclosure in individually identifiable form is necessary to accomplish the research or statistical purpose for which the use or disclosure is to be made;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) the recipient has established and maintains adequate safeguards to protect the records from unauthorized disclosure, including a procedure for removal or destruction of information that identifies the patient; and</p>
          <p class="in">(4) further use or release of the records in individually identifiable form to a person other than the patient without the patient's consent is prohibited.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.295.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.10.6.0">2007 c 147 art 10 s 6</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.296">
        <h1 class="shn">144.296 COPIES OF VIDEOTAPES.</h1>
        <p class="in">A provider may not release a copy of a videotape of a child victim or alleged victim of physical or sexual abuse without a court order under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.03#stat.13.03.6">13.03, subdivision 6</a>, or as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/611A.90">611A.90</a>. This section does not limit the right of a patient to view the videotape.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.296.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.10.7.0">2007 c 147 art 10 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.297">
        <h1 class="shn">144.297 INDEPENDENT MEDICAL EXAMINATION.</h1>
        <p class="in">Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291">144.291</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.298">144.298</a> apply to the subject and provider of an independent medical examination requested by or paid for by a third party. Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.293">144.293</a>, a provider may release health records created as part of an independent medical examination to the third party who requested or paid for the examination.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.297.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.10.8.0">2007 c 147 art 10 s 8</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.298">
        <h1 class="shn">144.298 PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.298.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Licensing action.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A violation of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291">144.291</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.298">144.298</a> may be grounds for disciplinary action against a provider by the appropriate licensing board or agency.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.298.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Liability of provider or other person.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A person who does any of the following is liable to the patient for compensatory damages caused by an unauthorized release or an intentional, unauthorized access, plus costs and reasonable attorney fees:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) negligently or intentionally requests or releases a health record in violation of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291">144.291</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.297">144.297</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) forges a signature on a consent form or materially alters the consent form of another person without the person's consent;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) obtains a consent form or the health records of another person under false pretenses; or</p>
          <p>(4) intentionally violates sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291">144.291</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.297">144.297</a> by intentionally accessing a record locator or patient information service without authorization.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.298.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Liability for record locator or patient information service.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">A patient is entitled to receive compensatory damages plus costs and reasonable attorney fees if a health information exchange maintaining a record locator or patient information service, or an entity maintaining a record locator or patient information service for a health information exchange, negligently or intentionally violates the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.293#stat.144.293.8">144.293, subdivision 8</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.298.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.10.9.0">2007 c 147 art 10 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2012/0/247/#laws.2.5.0">2012 c 247 art 2 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.8.21.0">2015 c 71 art 8 s 21</a>,22</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.30">
        <h1 class="shn">144.30 COPIES OF RECORDS EVIDENCE IN JUVENILE COURT.</h1>
        <p>When any child shall be brought into juvenile court the court shall request, and the custodian of the record shall furnish, a complete certified copy of such record to the court, which copy shall be received as evidence in the case; and no decision or disposition of the pending matter shall be finally made until such record, if existing, shall be considered.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.30.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/29">5356-2</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1929/0/277/#laws.0.2.0">1929 c 277 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.31"><b>144.31</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/1082/#laws.0.2.0">1969 c 1082 s 2</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.32">
        <h1 class="shn">144.32 FALSE STATEMENTS CAUSE FOR DISCHARGE.</h1>
        <p>Any intentionally false statement in such certificate and any act or omission of a superintendent or superior officer to connive at or permit the same shall be deemed good cause for summary discharge of the person at fault regardless of any contract.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.32.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/29">5356-4</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1929/0/277/#laws.0.4.0">1929 c 277 s 4</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.33"><b>144.33</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1961/0/27/#laws.0.1.0">1961 c 27 s 1</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.334">
        <h1 class="shn">144.334 RIGHT TO REQUEST PATIENT INFORMATION.</h1>
        <p>Upon an oral or written request by a spouse, parent, child, or sibling for information about a patient who is being evaluated for or diagnosed with mental illness, a provider must notify the requesting individual of the right under section 144.294 to have the provider request the patient's authorization to release information about the patient to a designated individual.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.334.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/316/#laws.0.1.0">2000 c 316 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.10.15.0">2007 c 147 art 10 s 15</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.3345">
        <h1 class="shn">144.3345 INTERCONNECTED ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD GRANTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.3345.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) The following definitions are used for the purposes of this section.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) "Eligible community e-health collaborative" means an existing or newly established collaborative to support the adoption and use of interoperable electronic health records. A collaborative must consist of at least two or more eligible health care entities in at least two of the categories listed in paragraph (c) and have a focus on interconnecting the members of the collaborative for secure and interoperable exchange of health care information.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) "Eligible health care entity" means one of the following:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) community clinics, as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145.9268">145.9268</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) hospitals eligible for rural hospital capital improvement grants, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.148">144.148</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant clinics located in a community with a population of less than 50,000 according to United States Census Bureau statistics and outside the seven-county metropolitan area;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) nursing facilities licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.01">144A.01</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.27">144A.27</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) community health boards as established under chapter 145A;</p>
          <p class="in">(6) nonprofit entities with a purpose to provide health information exchange coordination governed by a representative, multi-stakeholder board of directors; and</p>
          <p class="in">(7) other providers of health or health care services approved by the commissioner for which interoperable electronic health record capability would improve quality of care, patient safety, or community health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.3345.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Grants authorized.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The commissioner of health shall award grants to:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) eligible community e-health collaborative projects to improve the implementation and use of interoperable electronic health records including but not limited to the following projects:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) collaborative efforts to host and support fully functional interoperable electronic health records in multiple care settings;</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) electronic medication history and electronic patient medical history information;</p>
          <p class="in">(iii) electronic personal health records for persons with chronic diseases and for prevention services;</p>
          <p class="in">(iv) rural and underserved community models for electronic prescribing;</p>
          <p class="in">(v) modernize local public health information systems to rapidly and electronically exchange information needed to participate in community e-health collaboratives or for public health emergency preparedness and response; and</p>
          <p class="in">(vi) implement regional or community-based health information exchange organizations;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) community clinics, as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145.9268">145.9268</a>, to implement and use interoperable electronic health records, including but not limited to the following projects:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) efforts to plan for and implement fully functional, standards-based interoperable electronic health records; and</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) purchases and implementation of computer hardware, software, and technology to fully implement interoperable electronic health records;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) regional or community-based health information exchange organizations to connect and facilitate the exchange of health information between eligible health care entities, including but not limited to the development, testing, and implementation of:</p>
          <p class="in">(i) data exchange standards, including data, vocabulary, and messaging standards, for the exchange of health information, provided that such standards are consistent with state and national standards;</p>
          <p class="in">(ii) security standards necessary to ensure the confidentiality and integrity of health records;</p>
          <p class="in">(iii) computer interfaces and mechanisms for standardizing health information exchanged between eligible health care entities;</p>
          <p class="in">(iv) a record locator service for identifying the location of patient health records; or</p>
          <p class="in">(v) interfaces and mechanisms for implementing patient consent requirements; and</p>
          <p class="in">(4) community health boards as established under chapter 145A to modernize local public health information systems to be standards-based and interoperable with other electronic health records and information systems, or for enhanced public health emergency preparedness and response.</p>
          <p class="in">Grant funds may not be used for construction of health care or other buildings or facilities.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.3345.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Allocation of grants.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) To receive a grant under this section, an eligible community e-health collaborative, community clinic, regional or community-based health information exchange, or community health board must submit an application to the commissioner of health by the deadline established by the commissioner. A grant may be awarded upon the signing of a grant contract. In awarding grants, the commissioner shall give preference to projects benefiting providers located in rural and underserved areas of Minnesota which the commissioner has determined have an unmet need for the development and funding of electronic health records. Applicants may apply for and the commissioner may award grants for one-year, two-year, or three-year periods.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) An application must be on a form and contain information as specified by the commissioner but at a minimum must contain:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) a description of the purpose or project for which grant funds will be used;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) a description of the problem or problems the grant funds will be used to address, including an assessment of the likelihood of the project occurring absent grant funding;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) a description of achievable objectives, a work plan, budget, budget narrative, a project communications plan, a timeline for implementation and completion of processes or projects enabled by the grant, and an assessment of privacy and security issues and a proposed approach to address these issues;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) a description of the health care entities and other groups participating in the project, including identification of the lead entity responsible for applying for and receiving grant funds;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) a plan for how patients and consumers will be involved in development of policies and procedures related to the access to and interchange of information;</p>
          <p class="in">(6) evidence of consensus and commitment among the health care entities and others who developed the proposal and are responsible for its implementation;</p>
          <p class="in">(7) a plan for documenting and evaluating results of the grant; and</p>
          <p class="in">(8) a plan for use of data exchange standards, including data and vocabulary.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) The commissioner shall review each application to determine whether the application is complete and whether the applicant and the project are eligible for a grant. In evaluating applications, the commissioner shall take into consideration factors, including but not limited to, the following:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) the degree to which the proposal interconnects with other health care entities in the applicant's geographic community;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) the degree to which the project provides for the interoperability of electronic health records or related health information technology;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) the degree to which the project addresses current unmet needs pertaining to interoperable electronic health records in a geographic area of Minnesota and the likelihood that the needs would not be met absent grant funds;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) the applicant's thoroughness and clarity in describing the project, how the project will improve patient safety, quality of care, and consumer empowerment, and the role of the various collaborative members;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) the recommendations of the Health Information and Technology Infrastructure Advisory Committee; and</p>
          <p class="in">(6) other factors that the commissioner deems relevant.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) Grant funds shall be awarded on a three-to-one match basis. Applicants shall be required to provide $1 in the form of cash or in-kind staff or services for each $3 provided under the grant program.</p>
          <p class="in">(e) Grants shall not exceed $900,000 per grant. The commissioner has discretion over the size and number of grants awarded.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.3345.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Evaluation and report.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The commissioner of health shall evaluate the overall effectiveness of the grant program. The commissioner shall collect progress and expenditure reports to evaluate the grant program from the eligible community collaboratives receiving grants.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.3345.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/282/#laws.16.3.0">2006 c 282 art 16 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.10.10.0">2007 c 147 art 10 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.109.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 109</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.4.20.0">2020 c 115 art 4 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/58/#laws.0.25.0">2022 c 58 s 25</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.335"><b>144.335</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.10.16.0">2007 c 147 art 10 s 16</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.3351">
        <h1 class="shn">144.3351 IMMUNIZATION DATA.</h1>
        <p>Providers as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291#stat.144.291.2">144.291, subdivision 2</a>; group purchasers as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62J.03#stat.62J.03.6">62J.03, subdivision 6</a>; elementary or secondary schools or child care facilities as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/121A.15#stat.121A.15.9">121A.15, subdivision 9</a>; public or private postsecondary educational institutions as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/135A.14#stat.135A.14.1">135A.14, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (b); a community health board as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145A.02#stat.145A.02.5">145A.02, subdivision 5</a>; community action agencies as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/142F.301#stat.142F.301.1">142F.301, subdivision 1</a>; and the commissioner of health may exchange immunization data with one another, without the patient's consent, if the person requesting access provides services on behalf of the patient. For purposes of this section immunization data includes:</p>
        <p>(1) patient's name, address, date of birth, gender, parent or guardian's name; and</p>
        <p>(2) date vaccine was received, vaccine type, lot number, and manufacturer of all immunizations received by the patient, and whether there is a contraindication or an adverse reaction indication.</p>
        <p>This section applies to all immunization data, regardless of when the immunization occurred.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.3351.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/569/#laws.0.12.0">1992 c 569 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/259/#laws.1.35.0">1995 c 259 art 1 s 35</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/1/3/#laws.16.13.0">1Sp1995 c 3 art 16 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/397/#laws.11.3.0">1998 c 397 art 11 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/98/#laws.1.24.0">2005 c 98 art 1 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.10.15.0">2007 c 147 art 10 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.7.28.0">2014 c 291 art 7 s 28</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/80/#laws.6.4.0">2024 c 80 art 6 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/115/#laws.16.43.0">2024 c 115 art 16 s 43</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.3352">
        <h1 class="shn">144.3352 HEPATITIS B MATERNAL CARRIER DATA; INFANT IMMUNIZATION.</h1>
        <p>The commissioner of health or a community health board may inform the physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant attending a newborn of the hepatitis B infection status of the biological mother.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.3352.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/618/#laws.1.20.0">1994 c 618 art 1 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.109.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 109</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.4.21.0">2020 c 115 art 4 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/58/#laws.0.26.0">2022 c 58 s 26</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.336">
        <h1 class="shn">144.336 REGISTRY OF PERSONS TYPED FOR HUMAN LEUKOCYTE ANTIGENS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.336.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Release restricted.</span></h2>
          <p>No person, including the state, a state agency, or a political subdivision, that maintains or operates a registry of the names of persons, their human leukocyte antigen types, and their willingness to be a tissue donor shall reveal the identity of the person or the person's human leukocyte antigen type without the person's consent. If the data are maintained by a governmental entity, the data are classified as private data on individuals as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.12">13.02, subdivision 12</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.336.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Duties.</span></h2>
          <p>Persons that maintain or operate a registry described in subdivision 1 have no responsibility for any search beyond their own records to identify potential donors for the benefit of any person seeking a tissue transplant and have no duty to encourage potential donors to assist persons seeking a tissue transplant, and are not liable for their failure to do so.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.336.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/436/#laws.0.33.0">1984 c 436 s 33</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.34">
        <h1 class="shn">144.34 INVESTIGATION AND CONTROL OF OCCUPATIONAL DISEASES.</h1>
        <p>Any physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant having under professional care any person whom the physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant believes to be suffering from poisoning from lead, phosphorus, arsenic, brass, silica dust, carbon monoxide gas, wood alcohol, or mercury, or their compounds, or from anthrax or from compressed-air illness or any other disease contracted as a result of the nature of the employment of such person shall within five days mail to the Department of Health a report stating the name, address, and occupation of such patient, the name, address, and business of the patient's employer, the nature of the disease, and such other information as may reasonably be required by the department. The department shall prepare and furnish the physicians, advanced practice registered nurses, and physician assistants of this state suitable blanks for the reports herein required. No report made pursuant to the provisions of this section shall be admissible as evidence of the facts therein stated in any action at law or in any action under the Workers' Compensation Act against any employer of such diseased person. The Department of Health is authorized to investigate and to make recommendations for the elimination or prevention of occupational diseases which have been reported to it, or which shall be reported to it, in accordance with the provisions of this section. The department is also authorized to study and provide advice in regard to conditions that may be suspected of causing occupational diseases. Information obtained upon investigations made in accordance with the provisions of this section shall not be admissible as evidence in any action at law to recover damages for personal injury or in any action under the Workers' Compensation Act. Nothing herein contained shall be construed to interfere with or limit the powers of the Department of Labor and Industry to make inspections of places of employment or issue orders for the protection of the health of the persons therein employed. When upon investigation the commissioner of health reaches a conclusion that a condition exists which is dangerous to the life and health of the workers in any industry or factory or other industrial institutions the commissioner shall file a report thereon with the Department of Labor and Industry.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.34.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/23">4327-1</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/322/#laws.0.0.0">1939 c 322</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/359/#laws.0.23.0">1975 c 359 s 23</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; 1986 c 444; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.4.22.0">2020 c 115 art 4 s 22</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/58/#laws.0.27.0">2022 c 58 s 27</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CONSENT OF MINORS FOR<br>HEALTH SERVICES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.341">
        <h1 class="shn">144.341 LIVING APART FROM PARENTS AND MANAGING FINANCIAL AFFAIRS.</h1>
        <p>Notwithstanding any other provision of law, any minor who is living separate and apart from parents or legal guardian, whether with or without the consent of a parent or guardian and regardless of the duration of such separate residence, and who is managing personal financial affairs, regardless of the source or extent of the minor's income, may give effective consent to personal medical, dental, mental and other health services, and the consent of no other person is required.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.341.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/544/#laws.0.1.0">1971 c 544 s 1</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.342">
        <h1 class="shn">144.342 MARRIAGE OR GIVING BIRTH, CONSENT FOR HEALTH SERVICE FOR SELF OR CHILD.</h1>
        <p>Any minor who has been married or has borne a child may give effective consent to personal medical, mental, dental and other health services, or to services for the minor's child, and the consent of no other person is required.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.342.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/544/#laws.0.2.0">1971 c 544 s 2</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.343">
        <h1 class="shn">144.343 PREGNANCY, VENEREAL DISEASE, ALCOHOL OR DRUG ABUSE, ABORTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.343.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Minor's consent valid.</span></h2>
          <p>Any minor may give effective consent for medical, mental and other health services to determine the presence of or to treat pregnancy and conditions associated therewith, venereal disease, alcohol and other drug abuse, and the consent of no other person is required.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.343.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Notification concerning abortion.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.8">13.02, subdivision 8</a>, no abortion operation shall be performed upon an unemancipated minor or upon a woman for whom a guardian has been appointed pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/524.5-101">524.5-101</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/524.5-502">524.5-502</a> because of a finding of incapacity, until at least 48 hours after written notice of the pending operation has been delivered in the manner specified in subdivisions 2 to 4.</p>
          <p>(a) The notice shall be addressed to the parent at the usual place of abode of the parent and delivered personally to the parent by the physician or an agent.</p>
          <p>(b) In lieu of the delivery required by paragraph (a), notice shall be made by certified mail addressed to the parent at the usual place of abode of the parent with return receipt requested and restricted delivery to the addressee which means postal employee can only deliver the mail to the authorized addressee. Time of delivery shall be deemed to occur at 12 o'clock noon on the next day on which regular mail delivery takes place, subsequent to mailing.</p>
          <p class="see_note">[See Note.]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.343.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Parent, abortion; definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this section, "parent" means both parents of the pregnant woman if they are both living, one parent of the pregnant woman if only one is living or if the second one cannot be located through reasonably diligent effort, or the guardian or conservator if the pregnant woman has one.</p>
          <p>(b) For purposes of this section, "abortion" means the use of any means to terminate the pregnancy of a woman known to be pregnant with knowledge that the termination with those means will, with reasonable likelihood, cause the death of the fetus and "fetus" means any individual human organism from fertilization until birth.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.343.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Limitations.</span></h2>
          <p>No notice shall be required under this section if:</p>
          <p>(1) the attending physician certifies in the pregnant woman's medical record that the abortion is necessary to prevent the woman's death and there is insufficient time to provide the required notice; or</p>
          <p>(2) the abortion is authorized in writing by the person or persons who are entitled to notice; or</p>
          <p>(3) the pregnant minor woman declares that she is a victim of sexual abuse, neglect, or physical abuse as defined in chapter 260E. Notice of that declaration shall be made to the proper authorities as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260E.06">260E.06</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.343.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>Performance of an abortion in violation of this section shall be a misdemeanor and shall be grounds for a civil action by a person wrongfully denied notification. A person shall not be held liable under this section if the person establishes by written evidence that the person relied upon evidence sufficient to convince a careful and prudent person that the representations of the pregnant woman regarding information necessary to comply with this section are bona fide and true, or if the person has attempted with reasonable diligence to deliver notice, but has been unable to do so.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.343.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Substitute notification provisions.</span></h2>
          <p>If subdivision 2 of this law is ever temporarily or permanently restrained or enjoined by judicial order, subdivision 2 shall be enforced as though the following paragraph were incorporated as paragraph (c) of that subdivision; provided, however, that if such temporary or permanent restraining order or injunction is ever stayed or dissolved, or otherwise ceases to have effect, subdivision 2 shall have full force and effect, without being modified by the addition of the following substitute paragraph which shall have no force or effect until or unless an injunction or restraining order is again in effect.</p>
          <p>(c)(1) If such a pregnant woman elects not to allow the notification of one or both of her parents or guardian or conservator, any judge of a court of competent jurisdiction shall, upon petition, or motion, and after an appropriate hearing, authorize a physician to perform the abortion if said judge determines that the pregnant woman is mature and capable of giving informed consent to the proposed abortion. If said judge determines that the pregnant woman is not mature, or if the pregnant woman does not claim to be mature, the judge shall determine whether the performance of an abortion upon her without notification of her parents, guardian, or conservator would be in her best interests and shall authorize a physician to perform the abortion without such notification if said judge concludes that the pregnant woman's best interests would be served thereby.</p>
          <p>(2) Such a pregnant woman may participate in proceedings in the court on her own behalf, and the court may appoint a guardian ad litem for her. The court shall, however, advise her that she has a right to court appointed counsel, and shall, upon her request, provide her with such counsel.</p>
          <p>(3) Proceedings in the court under this section shall be confidential and shall be given such precedence over other pending matters so that the court may reach a decision promptly and without delay so as to serve the best interests of the pregnant woman. A judge of the court who conducts proceedings under this section shall make in writing specific factual findings and legal conclusions supporting the decision and shall order a record of the evidence to be maintained including the judge's own findings and conclusions.</p>
          <p>(4) An expedited confidential appeal shall be available to any such pregnant woman for whom the court denies an order authorizing an abortion without notification. An order authorizing an abortion without notification shall not be subject to appeal. No filing fees shall be required of any such pregnant woman at either the trial or the appellate level. Access to the trial court for the purposes of such a petition or motion, and access to the appellate courts for purposes of making an appeal from denial of the same, shall be afforded such a pregnant woman 24 hours a day, seven days a week.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.343.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Severability.</span></h2>
          <p>If any provision, word, phrase or clause of this section or the application thereof to any person or circumstance shall be held invalid, such invalidity shall not affect the provisions, words, phrases, clauses or application of this section which can be given effect without the invalid provision, word, phrase, clause, or application, and to this end the provisions, words, phrases, and clauses of this section are declared to be severable.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.343.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/544/#laws.0.3.0">1971 c 544 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/228/#laws.0.1.0">1981 c 228 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/311/#laws.0.39.0">1981 c 311 s 39</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/545/#laws.0.24.0">1982 c 545 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/146/#laws.3.1.0">2004 c 146 art 3 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/1/2/#laws.8.20.0">1Sp2020 c 2 art 8 s 20</a></p>
      </div>
      <p><b>NOTE: </b>The two-parent notification requirement in subdivision 2 was found constitutional by incorporation of paragraph (c) of subdivision 6. <i>Hodgson v. Minnesota</i>, 497 U.S. 417 (1990), but see also <i>Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization</i>, 142 S.Ct. 2228 (2022).</p>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.3431">
        <h1 class="shn">144.3431 NONRESIDENTIAL MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES.</h1>
        <p>(a) A minor who is age 16 or older may give effective consent for nonresidential mental health services, and the consent of no other person is required. For purposes of this section, "nonresidential mental health services" means outpatient services as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245.4871#stat.245.4871.29">245.4871, subdivision 29</a>, provided to a minor who is not residing in a hospital, inpatient unit, or licensed residential treatment facility or program.</p>
        <p>(b) This section does not preclude a minor from providing effective consent for mental health or other health services according to the authority in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.344">144.344</a> or other applicable law.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.3431.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.4.37.0">2023 c 70 art 4 s 37</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.344">
        <h1 class="shn">144.344 EMERGENCY TREATMENT.</h1>
        <p>Medical, dental, mental and other health services may be rendered to minors of any age without the consent of a parent or legal guardian when, in the professional's judgment, the risk to the minor's life or health is of such a nature that treatment should be given without delay and the requirement of consent would result in delay or denial of treatment.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.344.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/544/#laws.0.4.0">1971 c 544 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.3441">
        <h1 class="shn">144.3441 HEPATITIS B VACCINATION.</h1>
        <p>A minor may give effective consent for a hepatitis B vaccination. The consent of no other person is required.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.3441.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/167/#laws.0.1.0">1993 c 167 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.345">
        <h1 class="shn">144.345 REPRESENTATIONS TO PERSONS RENDERING SERVICE.</h1>
        <p>The consent of a minor who claims to be able to give effective consent for the purpose of receiving medical, dental, mental or other health services but who may not in fact do so, shall be deemed effective without the consent of the minor's parent or legal guardian, if the person rendering the service relied in good faith upon the representations of the minor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.345.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/544/#laws.0.5.0">1971 c 544 s 5</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.346">
        <h1 class="shn">144.346 INFORMATION TO PARENTS.</h1>
        <p>The professional may inform the parent or legal guardian of the minor patient of any treatment given or needed where, in the judgment of the professional, failure to inform the parent or guardian would seriously jeopardize the health of the minor patient.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.346.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/544/#laws.0.6.0">1971 c 544 s 6</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.347">
        <h1 class="shn">144.347 FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY.</h1>
        <p>A minor so consenting for such health services shall thereby assume financial responsibility for the cost of said services.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.347.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1971/0/544/#laws.0.7.0">1971 c 544 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">WATER POLLUTION</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.35">
        <h1 class="shn">144.35 POLLUTION OF WATER.</h1>
        <p>No sewage or other matter that will impair the healthfulness of water shall be deposited where it will fall or drain into any pond or stream used as a source of water supply for domestic use. The commissioner shall have general charge of all springs, wells, ponds, and streams so used and take all necessary and proper steps to preserve the same from such pollution as may endanger the public health. In case of violation of any of the provisions of this section, the commissioner may, with or without a hearing, order any person to desist from causing such pollution and to comply with such direction as the commissioner may deem proper and expedient in the premises. Such order shall be served forthwith upon the person found to have violated such provisions.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.35.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/29">5375</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1905/cite/29">RL s 2147</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.36">
        <h1 class="shn">144.36 APPEAL TO DISTRICT COURT.</h1>
        <p>Within five days after service of the order, any person aggrieved thereby may appeal to the district court of the county in which such polluted source of water supply is situated. During the pendency of the appeal the pollution against which the order has been issued shall not be continued and, upon violation of such order, the appeal shall forthwith be dismissed.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.36.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/29">5376</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1905/cite/29">RL s 2148</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/309/#laws.0.16.0">1987 c 309 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.37">
        <h1 class="shn">144.37 OTHER REMEDIES PRESERVED.</h1>
        <p>Nothing in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.36">144.36</a> shall curtail the power of the courts to administer the usual legal and equitable remedies in cases of nuisances or of improper interference with private rights.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.37.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/29">5377</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1905/cite/29">RL s 2149</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/309/#laws.0.17.0">1987 c 309 s 17</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.371"><b>144.371</b> [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/115.01">115.01</a>]
</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.372"><b>144.372</b> [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/115.02">115.02</a>]
</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.373"><b>144.373</b> [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/115.03">115.03</a>]
</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.374"><b>144.374</b> [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/115.04">115.04</a>]
</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.375"><b>144.375</b> [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/115.05">115.05</a>]
</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.376"><b>144.376</b> [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/115.06">115.06</a>]
</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.377"><b>144.377</b> [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/115.07">115.07</a>]
</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.378"><b>144.378</b> [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/115.08">115.08</a>]
</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.379"><b>144.379</b> [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/115.09">115.09</a>]
</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.38"><b>144.38</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/882/#laws.0.11.0">1967 c 882 s 11</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">SAFE DRINKING WATER ACT</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.381">
        <h1 class="shn">144.381 CITATION.</h1>
        <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.381">144.381</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.387">144.387</a> may be cited as the "Safe Drinking Water Act of 1977."</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.381.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/66/#laws.0.1.0">1977 c 66 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.382">
        <h1 class="shn">144.382 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.382.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.381">144.381</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.387">144.387</a>, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.382.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>"Commissioner" means the state commissioner of health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.382.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Connector.</span></h2>
          <p>"Connector" means gooseneck, pigtail, and other service line connectors. A connector is typically a short section of piping not exceeding two feet that can be bent and used for connections between rigid service piping.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.382.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Federal regulations.</span></h2>
          <p>"Federal regulations" means rules promulgated by the federal environmental protection agency, or its successor agencies.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.382.3a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Galvanized requiring replacement.</span></h2>
          <p>"Galvanized requiring replacement" means a galvanized service line that is or was at any time connected to a lead service line or lead status unknown service line, or is currently or was previously affixed to a lead connector. The majority of galvanized service lines fall under this category.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.382.3b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3b.<span class="headnote">Galvanized service line.</span></h2>
          <p>"Galvanized service line" means a service line made of iron or piping that has been dipped in zinc to prevent corrosion and rusting.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.382.3c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3c.<span class="headnote">Lead connector.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead connector" means a connector made of lead.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.382.3d">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3d.<span class="headnote">Lead service line.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead service line" means a portion of pipe that is made of lead, which connects the water main to the building inlet. A lead service line may be owned by the water system, by the property owner, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.382.3e">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3e.<span class="headnote">Lead status unknown service line or unknown service line.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead status unknown service line" or "unknown service line" means a service line that has not been demonstrated to meet or does not meet the definition of lead free in section 1417 of the Safe Drinking Water Act.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.382.3f">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3f.<span class="headnote">Nonlead service line.</span></h2>
          <p>"Nonlead service line" means a service line determined through an evidence-based record, method, or technique not to be a lead service line or galvanized service line requiring replacement. Most nonlead service lines are made of copper or plastic.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.382.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Public water supply.</span></h2>
          <p>"Public water supply" has the meaning given to "public water system" in the federal Safe Drinking Water Act, United States Code, title 42, section 300f, clause (4).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.382.4a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4a.<span class="headnote">Service line.</span></h2>
          <p>"Service line" means a portion of pipe that connects the water main to the building inlet. A service line may be owned by the water system, by the property owner, or both. A service line may be made of many materials, such as lead, copper, galvanized steel, or plastic.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.382.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Supplier.</span></h2>
          <p>"Supplier" means a person who owns, manages or operates a public water supply.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.382.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/66/#laws.0.2.0">1977 c 66 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/18/#laws.0.1.0">1999 c 18 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.3.6.0">2023 c 70 art 3 s 6</a>-13</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.383">
        <h1 class="shn">144.383 AUTHORITY OF COMMISSIONER.</h1>
        <p>In order to ensure safe drinking water in all public water supplies, the commissioner has the following powers:</p>
        <p>(a) To approve the site, design, and construction and alteration of all public water supplies and, for community and nontransient noncommunity water systems as defined in Code of Federal Regulations, title 40, section 141.2, to approve documentation that demonstrates the technical, managerial, and financial capacity of those systems to comply with rules adopted under this section;</p>
        <p>(b) To enter the premises of a public water supply, or part thereof, to inspect the facilities and records kept pursuant to rules promulgated by the commissioner, to conduct sanitary surveys and investigate the standard of operation and service delivered by public water supplies;</p>
        <p>(c) To contract with community health boards as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145A.02#stat.145A.02.5">145A.02, subdivision 5</a>, for routine surveys, inspections, and testing of public water supply quality;</p>
        <p>(d) To develop an emergency plan to protect the public when a decline in water quality or quantity creates a serious health risk, and to issue emergency orders if a health risk is imminent;</p>
        <p>(e) To promulgate rules, pursuant to chapter 14 but no less stringent than federal regulation, which may include the granting of variances and exemptions; and</p>
        <p>(f) To maintain an asset management database of community public water supply systems, provide technical assistance to community systems, and ensure the lead service line inventory data is accessible to the public with relevant educational materials about health risks related to lead and ways to reduce exposure.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.383.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/66/#laws.0.3.0">1977 c 66 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/424/#laws.0.130.0">1982 c 424 s 130</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/309/#laws.0.24.0">1987 c 309 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/209/#laws.2.1.0">1989 c 209 art 2 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/261/#laws.0.1.0">1998 c 261 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.7.28.0">2014 c 291 art 7 s 28,29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/39/#laws.0.1.0">2023 c 39 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.3831">
        <h1 class="shn">144.3831 FEES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.3831.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Fee setting.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health may assess an annual fee of $9.72 for every service connection to a public water supply that is owned or operated by a home rule charter city, a statutory city, a city of the first class, or a town. The commissioner of health may also assess an annual fee for every service connection served by a water user district defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/110A.02">110A.02</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.3831.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Collection and payment of fee.</span></h2>
          <p>The public water supply described in subdivision 1 shall:</p>
          <p>(1) collect the fees assessed on its service connections;</p>
          <p>(2) pay the Department of Health an amount equivalent to the fees based on the total number of service connections. The service connections for each public water supply described in subdivision 1 shall be verified every four years by the Department of Health; and</p>
          <p>(3) pay one-fourth of the total yearly fee to the Department of Health each calendar quarter. In lieu of quarterly payments, a public water supply described in subdivision 1 with fewer than 50 service connections may make a single annual payment by June 30 each year. The fees payable to the Department of Health shall be deposited in the state treasury as nondedicated state government special revenue fund revenues.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.3831.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Late fee.</span></h2>
          <p>The public water supply described in subdivision 1 shall pay a late fee in the amount of five percent of the amount of the fees due from the public water supply if the fees due from the public water supply are not paid within 30 days of the payment dates in subdivision 2, clause (3). The late fee that the public water supply shall pay shall be assessed only on the actual amount collected by the public water supply through fees on service connections.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.3831.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/513/#laws.6.3.0">1992 c 513 art 6 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/1/1/#laws.9.21.0">1Sp1993 c 1 art 9 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/186/#laws.0.42.0">1995 c 186 s 42</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/1/5/#laws.7.3.0">1Sp2001 c 5 art 7 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/4/#laws.6.21.0">1Sp2005 c 4 art 6 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.11.21.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 11 s 21</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.384">
        <h1 class="shn">144.384 NOTICE OF VIOLATION.</h1>
        <p>Upon discovery of a violation of a maximum contaminant level or treatment technique, the commissioner shall promptly notify the supplier of the violation, state the rule violated, and state a date by which the violation must be corrected or by which a request for variance or exemption must be submitted.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.384.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/66/#laws.0.4.0">1977 c 66 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.385">
        <h1 class="shn">144.385 PUBLIC NOTICE.</h1>
        <p>If a public water system has violated a rule of the commissioner, has a variance or exemption granted, or fails to comply with the terms of the variance or exemption, the supplier shall provide public notice of the fact pursuant to the rules of the commissioner.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.385.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/66/#laws.0.5.0">1977 c 66 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.3853">
        <h1 class="shn">144.3853 CLASSIFICATION OF SERVICE LINES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.3853.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Classification of lead status of service line.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A water system may classify the actual material of a service line, such as copper or plastic, as an alternative to classifying the service line as a nonlead service line, for the purpose of the lead service line inventory.</p>
          <p>(b) It is not necessary to physically verify the material composition, such as copper or plastic, of a service line for its lead status to be identified. For example, if records demonstrate the service line was installed after a municipal, state, or federal ban on the installation of lead service lines, the service line may be classified as a nonlead service line.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.3853.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Lead connector.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of the lead service line inventory and lead service line replacement plan, if a service line has a lead connector, the service line shall be classified as a lead service line or a galvanized service line requiring replacement.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.3853.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Galvanized service line.</span></h2>
          <p>A galvanized service line may only be classified as a nonlead service line if there is documentation verifying it was never connected to a lead service line or lead connector. Rarely will a galvanized service line be considered a nonlead service line.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.3853.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.3.14.0">2023 c 70 art 3 s 14</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.3855">
        <h1 class="shn">144.3855 LIMITATION.</h1>
        <p class="in">To meet cross-connection control requirements, as defined in Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4714.0602">4714.0602</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4720.0025">4720.0025</a>, the use of a hose connection backflow preventer and a hose connection vacuum breaker, not rated for continuous use, is permitted at individual water supply connections in recreational camping areas as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/327.14">327.14</a>, subdivision 8.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.3855.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/24/#laws.0.1.0">2007 c 24 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/0/40/#laws.1.121.0">2017 c 40 art 1 s 121</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.386">
        <h1 class="shn">144.386 PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.386.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Basic fine.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who violates a rule of the commissioner, fails to comply with the terms of a variance or exemption, or fails to request a variance or exemption by the date specified in the notice from the commissioner, may be fined up to $1,000 for each day the offense continues, in a civil action brought by the commissioner in district court. All fines shall be deposited in the general fund of the state treasury.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.386.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Gross misdemeanor fine.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who intentionally or repeatedly violates a rule of the commissioner, or fails to comply with an emergency order of the commissioner, is guilty of a gross misdemeanor, and may be fined not more than $10,000, imprisoned not more than 364 days, or both.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.386.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Drinking water notice; fine.</span></h2>
          <p>A supplier who fails to comply with the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.385">144.385</a>, or disseminates false or misleading information relating to the notice required in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.385">144.385</a>, is subject to the penalties described in subdivision 2.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.386.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/206/#laws.0.25.0">1993 c 206 s 25</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.386.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/66/#laws.0.6.0">1977 c 66 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/628/#laws.3.11.0">1984 c 628 art 3 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.6.16.0">2023 c 52 art 6 s 16</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.387">
        <h1 class="shn">144.387 COSTS.</h1>
        <p>If the state prevails in any civil action under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.386">144.386</a>, the court may award reasonable costs and expenses to the state.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.387.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/66/#laws.0.7.0">1977 c 66 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.3871"><b>144.3871</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/418/#laws.0.18.0">1996 c 418 s 18</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">FEMALE GENITAL MUTILATION;<br>EDUCATION AND OUTREACH</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.3872">
        <h1 class="shn">144.3872 FEMALE GENITAL MUTILATION; EDUCATION AND OUTREACH.</h1>
        <p>The commissioner of health shall carry out appropriate education, prevention, and outreach activities in communities that traditionally practice female circumcision, excision, or infibulation to inform people in those communities about the health risks and emotional trauma inflicted by those practices and to inform them and the medical community of the criminal penalties contained in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.2245">609.2245</a>. The commissioner shall work with culturally appropriate groups to obtain private funds to help finance these prevention and outreach activities.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.3872.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/636/#laws.9.9.0">1994 c 636 art 9 s 9</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.388"><b>144.388</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/689/#laws.2.269.0">1988 c 689 art 2 s 269</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.3885">
        <h1 class="shn">144.3885 LABOR TRAFFICKING SERVICES GRANT PROGRAM.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.3885.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Establishment.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health must establish a labor trafficking services grant program to provide comprehensive, trauma-informed, and culturally specific services for victims of labor trafficking or labor exploitation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.3885.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Eligibility; application.</span></h2>
          <p>To be eligible for a grant under this section, applicants must be a nonprofit organization or a nongovernmental organization serving victims of labor trafficking or labor exploitation; a local public health department; a social service agency; a Tribal government; a local unit of government; a school or school district; a health care organization; or another interested agency demonstrating experience or expertise in working with victims of labor trafficking exploitation. An entity seeking a grant under this section must apply to the commissioner at a time and in a manner specified by the commissioner. The commissioner must review each application to determine if the application is complete, the entity is eligible for a grant, and the proposed project is an allowable use of grant funds. The commissioner must determine the grant amount awarded to applicants that the commissioner determines will receive a grant.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.3885.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Reporting.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The grantee must submit a report to the commissioner in a manner and on a timeline specified by the commissioner on how the grant funds were spent and how many individuals were served.</p>
          <p>(b) By January 15 of each year, the commissioner must submit a report to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over health policy and finance. The report must include the names of the grant recipients, how the grant funds were spent, and how many individuals were served.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.3885.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.4.38.0">2023 c 70 art 4 s 38</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.39"><b>144.39</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/882/#laws.0.11.0">1967 c 882 s 11</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">PROMOTION OF NONSMOKING</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.391">
        <h1 class="shn">144.391 PUBLIC POLICY.</h1>
        <p>The legislature finds that:</p>
        <p>(1) smoking causes premature death, disability, and chronic disease, including cancer and heart disease, and lung disease;</p>
        <p>(2) smoking related diseases result in excess medical care costs; and</p>
        <p>(3) smoking initiation occurs primarily in adolescence.</p>
        <p>The legislature desires to prevent young people from starting to smoke, to encourage and assist smokers to quit, and to promote clean indoor air.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.391.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/1/14/#laws.19.13.0">1Sp1985 c 14 art 19 s 13</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.392">
        <h1 class="shn">144.392 DUTIES OF COMMISSIONER.</h1>
        <p>The commissioner of health shall:</p>
        <p>(1) provide assistance to workplaces to develop policies that promote nonsmoking and are consistent with the Minnesota Clean Indoor Air Act;</p>
        <p>(2) provide technical assistance, including design and evaluation methods, materials, and training to local health departments, communities, and other organizations that undertake community programs for the promotion of nonsmoking;</p>
        <p>(3) collect and disseminate information and materials for smoking prevention;</p>
        <p>(4) evaluate new and existing nonsmoking programs on a statewide and regional basis using scientific evaluation methods;</p>
