        <p>(5) conduct surveys in school-based populations regarding the epidemiology of smoking behavior, knowledge, and attitudes related to smoking, and the penetration of statewide smoking control programs; and</p>
        <p>(6) report to the legislature each biennium on activities undertaken, smoking rates in the population and subgroups of the total population, evaluation activities and results of those activities, and recommendations for further action.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.392.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/1/14/#laws.19.14.0">1Sp1985 c 14 art 19 s 14</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.393">
        <h1 class="shn">144.393 PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS PROGRAM.</h1>
        <p>The commissioner may conduct a long-term coordinated public information program that includes public service announcements, public education forums, mass media, and written materials. The program must promote nonsmoking and include background survey research and evaluation. The program must be designed to run over at least five years, subject to the availability of money.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.393.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/1/14/#laws.19.15.0">1Sp1985 c 14 art 19 s 15</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.394">
        <h1 class="shn">144.394 HEALTH PROMOTION AND EDUCATION.</h1>
        <p>The commissioner may sell at market value all health promotion and health education materials. Proceeds from the sale of the materials are appropriated to the Department of Health for the program that developed the material.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.394.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/207/#laws.9.6.0">1995 c 207 art 9 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/203/#laws.2.14.0">1997 c 203 art 2 s 14</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">TOBACCO USE PREVENTION</h1>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.395"><b>144.395</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/282/#laws.14.15.0">2006 c 282 art 14 s 15</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.396">
        <h1 class="shn">144.396 TOBACCO USE PREVENTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.396.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Purpose.</span></h2>
          <p>The legislature finds that it is important to reduce the prevalence of tobacco use among the youth of this state. It is a goal of the state to reduce tobacco use among youth by 25 percent by the year 2005, and to promote statewide and local tobacco use prevention activities to achieve this goal.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.396.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Measurable outcomes.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner, in consultation with other public, private, or nonprofit organizations involved in tobacco use prevention efforts, shall establish measurable outcomes to determine the effectiveness of the grants receiving funds under this section in reducing the use of tobacco among youth.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.396.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Statewide assessment.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall conduct a statewide assessment of tobacco-related behaviors and attitudes among youth to establish a baseline to measure the statewide effect of tobacco use prevention activities. The commissioner of education must provide any information requested by the commissioner of health as part of conducting the assessment. To the extent feasible, the commissioner of health should conduct the assessment so that the results may be compared to nationwide data.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.396.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Process.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner shall develop the criteria and procedures to allocate the grants under this section. In developing the criteria, the commissioner shall establish an administrative cost limit for grant recipients. The outcomes established under subdivision 2 must be specified to the grant recipients receiving grants under this section at the time the grant is awarded.</p>
          <p>(b) A recipient of a grant under this section must coordinate its tobacco use prevention activities with other entities performing tobacco use prevention activities within the recipient's service area.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.396.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Statewide tobacco prevention grants.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) To the extent funds are appropriated for the purposes of this subdivision, the commissioner of health shall award competitive grants to eligible applicants for projects and initiatives directed at the prevention of tobacco use. The project areas for grants include:</p>
          <p>(1) statewide public education and information campaigns which include implementation at the local level; and</p>
          <p>(2) coordinated special projects, including training and technical assistance, a resource clearinghouse, and contracts with ethnic and minority communities.</p>
          <p>(b) Eligible applicants may include, but are not limited to, nonprofit organizations, colleges and universities, professional health associations, community health boards, and other health care organizations. Applicants must submit proposals to the commissioner. The proposals must specify the strategies to be implemented to target tobacco use among youth, and must take into account the need for a coordinated statewide tobacco prevention effort.</p>
          <p>(c) The commissioner must give priority to applicants who demonstrate that the proposed project:</p>
          <p>(1) is research based or based on proven effective strategies;</p>
          <p>(2) is designed to coordinate with other activities and education messages related to other health initiatives;</p>
          <p>(3) utilizes and enhances existing prevention activities and resources; or</p>
          <p>(4) involves innovative approaches preventing tobacco use among youth.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.396.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Local tobacco prevention grants.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner shall award grants to eligible applicants for local and regional projects and initiatives directed at tobacco prevention in coordination with other health areas aimed at reducing high-risk behaviors in youth that lead to adverse health-related problems. The project areas for grants include:</p>
          <p>(1) school-based tobacco prevention programs aimed at youth and parents;</p>
          <p>(2) local public awareness and education projects aimed at tobacco prevention in coordination with locally assessed community public health needs pursuant to chapter 145A; or</p>
          <p>(3) local initiatives aimed at reducing high-risk behavior in youth associated with tobacco use and the health consequences of these behaviors.</p>
          <p>(b) Eligible applicants may include, but are not limited to, community health boards, school districts, community clinics, Indian tribes, nonprofit organizations, and other health care organizations. Applicants must submit proposals to the commissioner. The proposals must specify the strategies to be implemented to target tobacco use among youth, and must be targeted to achieve the outcomes established in subdivision 2.</p>
          <p>(c) The commissioner must give priority to applicants who demonstrate that the proposed project or initiative:</p>
          <p>(1) is supported by the community in which the applicant serves;</p>
          <p>(2) is based on research or on proven effective strategies;</p>
          <p>(3) is designed to coordinate with other community activities related to other health initiatives;</p>
          <p>(4) incorporates an understanding of the role of community in influencing behavioral changes among youth regarding tobacco use and other high-risk health-related behaviors; or</p>
          <p>(5) addresses disparities among populations of color related to tobacco use and other high-risk health-related behaviors.</p>
          <p>(d) The commissioner shall divide the state into specific geographic regions and allocate a percentage of the money available for distribution to projects or initiatives aimed at that geographic region. If the commissioner does not receive a sufficient number of grant proposals from applicants that serve a particular region or the proposals submitted do not meet the criteria developed by the commissioner, the commissioner shall provide technical assistance and expertise to ensure the development of adequate proposals aimed at addressing the public health needs of that region. In awarding the grants, the commissioner shall consider locally assessed community public health needs pursuant to chapter 145A.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.396.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Local public health promotion and protection.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall distribute funds appropriated for the purpose of local health promotion and protection activities to community health boards for local health initiatives other than tobacco prevention aimed at high risk health behaviors among youth. The commissioner shall distribute these funds to the community health boards based on demographics and other need-based factors relating to health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.396.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Coordination.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall coordinate the projects and initiatives funded under this section with the tobacco use prevention efforts of the Minnesota partnership for action against tobacco, community health boards, and other public, private, and nonprofit organizations and the tobacco prevention efforts that are being conducted on the national level.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.396.8a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8a.<span class="headnote">Smoking cessation.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health must prioritize smoking prevention and smoking cessation activities in low-income, indigenous, and minority communities in their collaborations with the organization specifically described in subdivision 8.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.396.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Evaluation.</span></h2>
          <p> Using the outcome measures established in subdivision 2, the commissioner of health shall conduct a biennial evaluation of the statewide and local tobacco use prevention projects and community health board activities funded under this section. The evaluation must include:</p>
          <p>(1) the effect of these activities on the amount of tobacco use by youth and rates at which youth start to use tobacco products; and</p>
          <p>(2) a longitudinal tracking of outcomes for youth.</p>
          <p>Grant recipients and community health boards shall cooperate with the commissioner in the evaluation and provide the commissioner with the information necessary to conduct the evaluation. Beginning January 15, 2003, the results of each evaluation must be submitted to the chairs and members of the house of representatives Health and Human Services Finance Committee and the senate Health and Family Security Budget Division.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.396.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Report.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall submit a biennial report to the chairs and members of the house of representatives Health and Human Services Finance Committee and the senate Health and Family Security Budget Division on the statewide and local projects and community health board prevention activities funded under this section. These reports must include information on grant recipients, activities that were conducted using grant funds, and evaluation data and outcome measures, if available. These reports are due by January 15 of the odd-numbered years, beginning in 2001.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.396.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Audits.</span></h2>
          <p>The legislative auditor may audit tobacco use prevention and local public health expenditures to ensure that the money is spent for tobacco use prevention measures and public health initiatives.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.396.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Funds not to supplant existing funding.</span></h2>
          <p>Funds appropriated to the statewide tobacco prevention grants, local tobacco prevention grants, or the local public health promotion and prevention must not be used as a substitute for traditional sources of funding tobacco use prevention activities or public health initiatives. Any local unit of government receiving money under this section must ensure that existing local financial efforts remain in place.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.396.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/488/#laws.11.12.0">2000 c 488 art 11 s 12</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.396.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/245/#laws.11.5.0">1999 c 245 art 11 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/488/#laws.11.5.0">2000 c 488 art 11 s 5</a>,6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/130/#laws.0.12.0">2003 c 130 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.7.35.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 7 s 35</a>-40; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2008/0/277/#laws.1.14.0">2008 c 277 art 1 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.10.47.0">2009 c 79 art 10 s 47</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.397">
        <h1 class="shn">144.397 STATEWIDE TOBACCO CESSATION SERVICES.</h1>
        <p>(a) The commissioner of health shall administer, or contract for the administration of, statewide tobacco cessation services to assist Minnesotans who are seeking advice or services to help them quit using tobacco products. The commissioner shall establish statewide public awareness activities to inform the public of the availability of the services and encourage the public to utilize the services because of the dangers and harm of tobacco use and dependence.</p>
        <p>(b) Services to be provided may include but are not limited to:</p>
        <p>(1) telephone-based coaching and counseling;</p>
        <p>(2) referrals;</p>
        <p>(3) written materials mailed upon request;</p>
        <p>(4) web-based texting or email services; and</p>
        <p>(5) free United States Food and Drug Administration-approved tobacco cessation medications.</p>
        <p>(c) Services provided must be consistent with evidence-based best practices in tobacco cessation services. Services provided must be coordinated with health plan company tobacco prevention and cessation services that may be available to individuals depending on their health coverage.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.397.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.11.22.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 11 s 22</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.398">
        <h1 class="shn">144.398 TOBACCO USE PREVENTION ACCOUNT; ESTABLISHMENT AND USES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.398.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, the terms in this subdivision have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Electronic delivery device" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.685">609.685, subdivision </a>1, paragraph (c).</p>
          <p>(c) "Nicotine delivery product" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.6855">609.6855, subdivision </a>1, paragraph (c).</p>
          <p>(d) "Tobacco" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.685#stat.609.685.1">609.685, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (a).</p>
          <p>(e) "Tobacco-related devices" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.685#stat.609.685.1">609.685, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (b).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.398.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Account created.</span></h2>
          <p>A tobacco use prevention account is created in the special revenue fund. Pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/16A.151#stat.16A.151.2">16A.151, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (h), the commissioner of management and budget shall deposit into the account any money received by the state resulting from a settlement agreement or an assurance of discontinuance entered into by the attorney general of the state, or a court order in litigation brought by the attorney general of the state on behalf of the state or a state agency related to alleged violations of consumer fraud laws in the marketing, sale, or distribution of electronic nicotine delivery systems in this state or other alleged illegal actions that contributed to the exacerbation of youth nicotine use.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.398.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Appropriations from tobacco use prevention account. </span></h2>
          <p>(a) Each fiscal year, the amount of money in the tobacco use prevention account is appropriated to the commissioner of health for:</p>
          <p>(1) tobacco and electronic delivery device use prevention and cessation projects consistent with the duties specified in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.392">144.392</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) a public information program under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.393">144.393</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) the development of health promotion and health education materials about tobacco and electronic delivery device use prevention and cessation;</p>
          <p>(4) tobacco and electronic delivery device use prevention activities under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.396">144.396</a>; and</p>
          <p>(5) statewide tobacco cessation services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.397">144.397</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) In activities funded under this subdivision, the commissioner of health must:</p>
          <p>(1) prioritize preventing persons under the age of 21 from using commercial tobacco, electronic delivery devices, tobacco-related devices, and nicotine delivery products;</p>
          <p>(2) promote racial and health equity; and</p>
          <p>(3) use strategies that are evidence-based or based on promising practices.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.398.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.4.39.0">2023 c 70 art 4 s 39</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.40"><b>144.40</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/882/#laws.0.11.0">1967 c 882 s 11</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr_by_subd" id="stat.144.401">
        <h1>144.401 </h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.401.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.8.32.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 8 s 32</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.401.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.8.32.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 8 s 32</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.401.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.8.32.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 8 s 32</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.401.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.8.32.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 8 s 32</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.401.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/9/#laws.8.8.0">1Sp2003 c 9 art 8 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.8.32.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 8 s 32</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.41"><b>144.41</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1967/0/882/#laws.0.11.0">1967 c 882 s 11</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CLEAN INDOOR AIR ACT</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.411">
        <h1 class="shn">144.411 CITATION.</h1>
        <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.411">144.411</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a> may be cited as the "Minnesota Clean Indoor Air Act."</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.411.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/211/#laws.0.1.0">1975 c 211 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.412">
        <h1 class="shn">144.412 PUBLIC POLICY.</h1>
        <p class="in">The purpose of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.411">144.411</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a> is to protect employees and the general public from the hazards of secondhand smoke and involuntary exposure to aerosol or vapor from electronic delivery devices by eliminating smoking in public places, places of employment, public transportation, and at public meetings.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.412.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/211/#laws.0.2.0">1975 c 211 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/399/#laws.0.1.0">1987 c 399 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/82/#laws.0.2.0">2007 c 82 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.11.23.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 11 s 23</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.413">
        <h1 class="shn">144.413 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.413.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>As used in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.411">144.411</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a>, the terms defined in this section have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.413.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Indoor area.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">"Indoor area" means all space between a floor and a ceiling that is bounded by walls, doorways, or windows, whether open or closed, covering more than 50 percent of the combined surface area of the vertical planes constituting the perimeter of the area. A wall includes any retractable divider, garage door, or other physical barrier, whether temporary or permanent. A 0.011 gauge window screen with an 18 by 16 mesh count is not a wall.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.413.1b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.<span class="headnote">Place of employment.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">"Place of employment" means any indoor area at which two or more individuals perform any type of a service for consideration of payment under any type of contractual relationship, including, but not limited to, an employment relationship with or for a private corporation, partnership, individual, or government agency. Place of employment includes any indoor area where two or more individuals gratuitously perform services for which individuals are ordinarily paid. A place of employment includes, but is not limited to, public conveyances, factories, warehouses, offices, retail stores, restaurants, bars, banquet facilities, theaters, food stores, banks, financial institutions, employee cafeterias, lounges, auditoriums, gymnasiums, restrooms, elevators, hallways, museums, libraries, bowling establishments, employee medical facilities, and rooms or areas containing photocopying equipment or other office equipment used in common. Vehicles used in whole or in part for work purposes are places of employment during hours of operation if more than one person is present. An area in which work is performed in a private residence is a place of employment during hours of operation if:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) the homeowner uses the area exclusively and regularly as a principal place of business and has one or more on-site employees; or</p>
          <p class="in">(2) the homeowner uses the area exclusively and regularly as a place to meet or deal with patients, clients, or customers in the normal course of the homeowner's trade or business.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.413.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Public place.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">"Public place" means any enclosed, indoor area used by the general public, including, but not limited to, restaurants; bars; any other food or liquor establishment; retail stores and other commercial establishments; educational facilities other than public schools, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/120A.05">120A.05, subdivisions 9, 11, and 13</a>; hospitals; nursing homes; auditoriums; arenas; meeting rooms; and common areas of rental apartment buildings.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.413.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Public meeting.</span></h2>
          <p>"Public meeting" includes all meetings open to the public pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13D.01">13D.01</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.413.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Smoking.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">"Smoking" means inhaling, exhaling, burning, or carrying any lighted or heated cigar, cigarette, pipe, or any other lighted or heated product containing, made, or derived from nicotine, tobacco, marijuana, or other plant, whether natural or synthetic, that is intended for inhalation. Smoking includes carrying or using an activated electronic delivery device, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.685">609.685</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.413.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Public transportation.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">"Public transportation" means public means of transportation, including light and commuter rail transit; buses; enclosed bus and transit stops; taxis, vans, limousines, and other for-hire vehicles other than those being operated by the lessee; and ticketing, boarding, and waiting areas in public transportation terminals.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.413.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/211/#laws.0.3.0">1975 c 211 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/576/#laws.0.1.0">1992 c 576 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/520/#laws.0.1.0">1994 c 520 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/397/#laws.11.3.0">1998 c 397 art 11 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/245/#laws.2.24.0">1999 c 245 art 2 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/82/#laws.0.3.0">2007 c 82 s 3</a>-7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.11.24.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 11 s 24</a>,25</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.414">
        <h1 class="shn">144.414 PROHIBITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.414.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Public places, places of employment, public transportation, and public meetings.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Smoking shall not be permitted in and no person shall smoke in a public place, at a public meeting, in a place of employment, or in public transportation, except as provided in this section or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4167">144.4167</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.414.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Day care premises.</span></h2>
          <p class="in"> Smoking is prohibited in a day care center licensed under Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9503.0005">9503.0005</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9503.0170">9503.0170</a>, or in a family home or in a group family day care provider home licensed under Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9502.0300">9502.0300</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/9502.0445">9502.0445</a>, during its hours of operation. The proprietor of a family home or group family day care provider must disclose to parents or guardians of children cared for on the premises if the proprietor permits smoking outside of its hours of operation. Disclosure must include posting on the premises a conspicuous written notice and orally informing parents or guardians.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.414.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Health care facilities and clinics.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) Smoking is prohibited in any area of a hospital, health care clinic, doctor's office, licensed residential facility for children, or other health care-related facility, except that a patient or resident in a nursing home, boarding care facility, or licensed residential facility for adults may smoke in a designated separate, enclosed room maintained in accordance with applicable state and federal laws.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) Except as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/246.0141">246.0141</a>, smoking by patients in a locked psychiatric unit may be allowed in a separated well-ventilated area in the unit under a policy established by the administrator of the program that allows the treating physician to approve smoking if, in the opinion of the treating physician, the benefits to be gained in obtaining patient cooperation with treatment outweigh the negative impacts of smoking.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.414.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Public transportation vehicles.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Smoking is prohibited in public transportation vehicles except that the driver of a public transportation vehicle may smoke when the vehicle is being used for personal use. For purposes of this subdivision, "personal use" means that the public transportation vehicle is being used by the driver for private purposes and no for-hire passengers are present. If a driver smokes under this subdivision, the driver must post a conspicuous sign inside the vehicle to inform passengers.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.414.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.11.112.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 11 s 112</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.414.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/211/#laws.0.4.0">1975 c 211 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/654/#laws.2.113.0">1984 c 654 art 2 s 113</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/399/#laws.0.2.0">1987 c 399 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/576/#laws.0.2.0">1992 c 576 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/14/#laws.0.1.0">1993 c 14 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/165/#laws.0.2.0">1995 c 165 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/245/#laws.2.25.0">1999 c 245 art 2 s 25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.7.41.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 7 s 41</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/82/#laws.0.8.0">2007 c 82 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.6.4.0">2014 c 291 art 6 s 4</a>-6; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/158/#laws.1.53.0">2016 c 158 art 1 s 53</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.11.26.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 11 s 26</a>,27</p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.415"><b>144.415</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/82/#laws.0.15.0">2007 c 82 s 15</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.416">
        <h1 class="shn">144.416 RESPONSIBILITIES OF PROPRIETORS.</h1>
        <p class="in">(a) The proprietor or other person, firm, limited liability company, corporation, or other entity that owns, leases, manages, operates, or otherwise controls the use of a public place, public transportation, place of employment, or public meeting shall make reasonable efforts to prevent smoking in the public place, public transportation, place of employment, or public meeting by:</p>
        <p class="in">(1) posting appropriate signs or by any other means which may be appropriate; and</p>
        <p class="in">(2) asking any person who smokes in an area where smoking is prohibited to refrain from smoking and, if the person does not refrain from smoking after being asked to do so, asking the person to leave. If the person refuses to leave, the proprietor, person, or entity in charge shall handle the situation consistent with lawful methods for handling other persons acting in a disorderly manner or as a trespasser.</p>
        <p class="in">(b) The proprietor or other person or entity in charge of a public place, public meeting, public transportation, or place of employment must not provide smoking equipment, including ashtrays or matches, in areas where smoking is prohibited. Nothing in this section prohibits the proprietor or other person or entity in charge from taking more stringent measures than those under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.414">144.414</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a> to protect individuals from secondhand smoke or from involuntary exposure to aerosol or vapor from electronic delivery devices. The proprietor or other person or entity in charge of a restaurant or bar may not serve an individual who is in violation of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.411">144.411</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.416.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/211/#laws.0.6.0">1975 c 211 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/82/#laws.0.9.0">2007 c 82 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.11.28.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 11 s 28</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4165">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4165 TOBACCO PRODUCTS PROHIBITED IN PUBLIC SCHOOLS.</h1>
        <p>(a) No person shall at any time smoke, chew, or otherwise ingest tobacco, or carry or use an activated electronic delivery device as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.685#stat.609.685.1">609.685, subdivision 1</a>, in a public school, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/120A.05">120A.05, subdivisions 9, 11, and 13</a>, or in a charter school governed by chapter 124E. This prohibition extends to all facilities, whether owned, rented, or leased, and all vehicles that a school district owns, leases, rents, contracts for, or controls.</p>
        <p>(b) Nothing in this section shall prohibit the lighting of tobacco by an adult as a part of a traditional Indian spiritual or cultural ceremony. An American Indian student may carry a medicine pouch containing loose tobacco intended as observance of traditional spiritual or cultural practices. For purposes of this section, an Indian is a person who is a member of an Indian Tribe as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260.755#stat.260.755.12">260.755, subdivision 12</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4165.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/576/#laws.0.3.0">1992 c 576 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/224/#laws.9.42.0">1993 c 224 art 9 s 42</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/412/#laws.13.30.0">1996 c 412 art 13 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/397/#laws.11.3.0">1998 c 397 art 11 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/139/#laws.4.2.0">1999 c 139 art 4 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/245/#laws.2.26.0">1999 c 245 art 2 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.6.7.0">2014 c 291 art 6 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.11.29.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 11 s 29</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/88/#laws.0.1.0">2020 c 88 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/55/#laws.4.20.0">2023 c 55 art 4 s 20</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4167">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4167 PERMITTED SMOKING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4167.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scientific study participants.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Smoking by participants in peer reviewed scientific studies related to the health effects of smoking may be allowed in a separated room ventilated at a rate of 60 cubic feet per minute per person pursuant to a policy that is approved by the commissioner and is established by the administrator of the program to minimize exposure of nonsmokers to smoke.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4167.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Traditional Native American ceremonies.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.414">144.414</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a> do not prohibit smoking by a Native American as part of a traditional Native American spiritual or cultural ceremony. For purposes of this section, a Native American is a person who is a member of an Indian tribe as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260.755#stat.260.755.12">260.755, subdivision 12</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4167.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Private places.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Except as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.414#stat.144.414.2">144.414, subdivision 2</a>, nothing in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.411">144.411</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a> prohibits smoking in:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) private homes, private residences, or private automobiles when they are not in use as a place of employment, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.413#stat.144.413.1b">144.413, subdivision 1b</a>; or</p>
          <p class="in">(2) a hotel or motel sleeping room rented to one or more guests.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4167.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Tobacco products shop.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.414">144.414</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a> do not prohibit the lighting, heating, or activation of tobacco in a tobacco products shop by a customer or potential customer for the specific purpose of sampling tobacco products. For the purposes of this subdivision, a tobacco products shop is a retail establishment that has an entrance door opening directly to the outside, that cannot be entered at any time by persons younger than 21 years of age, and that derives more than 90 percent of its gross revenue from the sale of tobacco, tobacco-related devices, and electronic delivery devices, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.685">609.685</a>, and in which the sale of other products is merely incidental. "Tobacco products shop" does not include a tobacco department or section of any individual business establishment with any type of liquor, food, or restaurant license.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4167.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Heavy commercial vehicles.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.414">144.414</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a> do not prohibit smoking in the cabs of motor vehicles registered under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.013#stat.168.013.1e">168.013, subdivision 1e</a>, with a total gross weight of 26,001 pounds or greater.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4167.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Farm vehicles and construction equipment.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.414">144.414</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a> do not prohibit smoking in farm trucks, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.002#stat.168.002.8">168.002, subdivision 8</a>; implements of husbandry, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168A.01#stat.168A.01.8">168A.01, subdivision 8</a>; and special mobile equipment, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/168.002#stat.168.002.31">168.002, subdivision 31</a>. This subdivision applies to farm trucks, implements of husbandry, and special mobile equipment, when being used for their intended purposes.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4167.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Family farms.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.414">144.414</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a> do not prohibit smoking in the house, garage, barns, and other buildings on a family farm that meet the following criteria: (1) the family farm is engaged in farming, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/500.24">500.24</a>, subdivision 2, paragraph (a); (2) the family farm meets the definition of family farm under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/500.24#stat.500.24.2">500.24, subdivision 2</a>, paragraph (b), (c), (j), or (l); and (3) the family farm employs two or fewer persons who are not family members.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4167.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Disabled veterans rest camp.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.414">144.414</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a> do not prohibit smoking in the disabled veterans rest camp located in Washington County, established as of January 1, 2007.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4167.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Theatrical productions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.414">144.414</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a> do not prohibit smoking by actors and actresses as part of a theatrical performance conducted in compliance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/366.01">366.01</a>. Notice of smoking in a performance shall be given to theater patrons in advance and shall be included in performance programs.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4167.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/82/#laws.0.10.0">2007 c 82 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.11.30.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 11 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/88/#laws.0.2.0">2020 c 88 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.417">
        <h1 class="shn">144.417 COMMISSIONER OF HEALTH, ENFORCEMENT, PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.417.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Rules.</span></h2>
          <p class="in"> The state commissioner of health shall adopt rules necessary and reasonable to implement the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.411">144.411</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.417.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Violations.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) Any proprietor, person, or entity that owns, leases, manages, operates, or otherwise controls the use of an area in which smoking is prohibited under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.414">144.414</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a>, and that knowingly fails to comply with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.414">144.414</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a>, is guilty of a petty misdemeanor.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) Any person who smokes in an area where smoking is prohibited or restricted under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.414">144.414</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a> is guilty of a petty misdemeanor.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) A proprietor, person, or entity in charge of a public place, public meeting, place of employment, or public transportation must not retaliate or take adverse action against an employee or anyone else who, in good faith, reports a violation of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.414">144.414</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a> to the proprietor or person in charge of the public place, public meeting, place of employment, or public transportation, or to the commissioner of health or other designee responsible for enforcing sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.414">144.414</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a>.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) No person or employer shall discharge, refuse to hire, penalize, discriminate against, or in any manner retaliate against any employee, applicant for employment, or customer because the employee, applicant, or customer exercises any right to a smoke-free environment provided by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.414">144.414</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a> or other law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.417.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Injunction.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The state commissioner of health, a community health board as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145A.02#stat.145A.02.5">145A.02, subdivision 5</a>, or any affected party may institute an action in any court with jurisdiction to enjoin repeated violations of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.414">144.414</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.417.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Local government ordinances.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) Nothing in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.414">144.414</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417 </a>prohibits a statutory or home rule charter city or county from enacting and enforcing more stringent measures to protect individuals from secondhand smoke or from involuntary exposure to aerosol or vapor from electronic delivery devices.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) Except as provided in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.411">144.411</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.417">144.417</a>, smoking is permitted outside of restaurants, bars, and bingo halls unless limited or prohibited by restrictions adopted in accordance with paragraph (a).</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.417.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/211/#laws.0.7.0">1975 c 211 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/309/#laws.0.24.0">1987 c 309 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/576/#laws.0.4.0">1992 c 576 s 4</a>,5; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/165/#laws.0.3.0">1995 c 165 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/375/#laws.3.7.0">2002 c 375 art 3 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/82/#laws.0.11.0">2007 c 82 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.7.28.0">2014 c 291 art 7 s 28</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.11.31.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 11 s 31</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">HEALTH THREAT PROCEDURES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4171">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4171 SCOPE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4171.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Authority.</span></h2>
          <p>Under the powers and duties assigned to the commissioner in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.05">144.05</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.12">144.12</a>, the commissioner shall proceed according to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4171">144.4171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4186">144.4186</a> with respect to persons who pose a health threat to others or who engage in noncompliant behavior.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4171.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Preemption.</span></h2>
          <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4171">144.4171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4186">144.4186</a> preempt and supersede any local ordinance or rule concerning persons who pose a health threat to others or who engage in noncompliant behavior.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4171.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/209/#laws.0.4.0">1987 c 209 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4172">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4172 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4172.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Carrier.</span></h2>
          <p>"Carrier" means a person who serves as a potential source of infection and who harbors or who the commissioner reasonably believes to be harboring a specific infectious agent whether or not there is present discernible clinical disease. In the absence of a medically accepted test, the commissioner may reasonably believe an individual to be a carrier only when a determination based upon specific facts justifies an inference that the individual harbors a specific infectious agent.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4172.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Communicable disease.</span></h2>
          <p>"Communicable disease" means a disease or condition that causes serious illness, serious disability, or death, the infectious agent of which may pass or be carried, directly or indirectly, from the body of one person to the body of another.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4172.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>"Commissioner" means the commissioner of health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4172.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Contact notification program.</span></h2>
          <p>"Contact notification program" means an ongoing program established by the commissioner to encourage carriers of a communicable disease whose primary route of transmission is through an exchange of blood, semen, or vaginal secretions, such as <i>treponema pallidum</i>, <i>neisseria gonorrhea</i>, <i>chlamydia trachomatis</i>, and human immunodeficiency virus, to identify others who may be at risk by virtue of contact with the carrier.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4172.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Directly transmitted.</span></h2>
          <p>"Directly transmitted" means predominately:</p>
          <p>(1) sexually transmitted;</p>
          <p>(2) bloodborne; or</p>
          <p>(3) transmitted through direct or intimate skin contact.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4172.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Health directive.</span></h2>
          <p>"Health directive" means a written statement, or, in urgent circumstances, an oral statement followed by a written statement within three days, from the commissioner, or community health board as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145A.02#stat.145A.02.5">145A.02, subdivision 5</a>, with delegated authority from the commissioner, issued to a carrier who constitutes a health threat to others. A health directive must be individual, specific, and cannot be issued to a class of persons. The directive may require a carrier to cooperate with health authorities in efforts to prevent or control transmission of communicable disease, including participation in education, counseling, or treatment programs, and undergoing medical tests necessary to verify the person's carrier status. The written directive shall be served in the same manner as a summons and complaint under the Minnesota Rules of Civil Procedure.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4172.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Licensed health professional.</span></h2>
          <p>"Licensed health professional" means a person licensed in Minnesota to practice those professions described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.01#stat.214.01.2">214.01, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4172.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Health threat to others.</span></h2>
          <p>"Health threat to others" means that a carrier demonstrates an inability or unwillingness to act in such a manner as to not place others at risk of exposure to infection that causes serious illness, serious disability, or death. It includes one or more of the following:</p>
          <p>(1) With respect to an indirectly transmitted communicable disease:</p>
          <p>(i) behavior by a carrier which has been demonstrated epidemiologically to transmit or which evidences a careless disregard for the transmission of the disease to others; or</p>
          <p>(ii) a substantial likelihood that a carrier will transmit a communicable disease to others as is evidenced by a carrier's past behavior, or by statements of a carrier that are credible indicators of a carrier's intention.</p>
          <p>(2) With respect to a directly transmitted communicable disease:</p>
          <p>(i) repeated behavior by a carrier which has been demonstrated epidemiologically to transmit or which evidences a careless disregard for the transmission of the disease to others;</p>
          <p>(ii) a substantial likelihood that a carrier will repeatedly transmit a communicable disease to others as is evidenced by a carrier's past behavior, or by statements of a carrier that are credible indicators of a carrier's intention;</p>
          <p>(iii) affirmative misrepresentation by a carrier of the carrier's status prior to engaging in any behavior which has been demonstrated epidemiologically to transmit the disease; or</p>
          <p>(iv) the activities referenced in clause (1) if the person whom the carrier places at risk is: (A) a minor; (B) of diminished capacity by reason of mood altering chemicals, including alcohol; (C) has been diagnosed as having significantly subaverage intellectual functioning; (D) has an organic disorder of the brain or a psychiatric disorder of thought, mood, perception, orientation, or memory which substantially impairs judgment, behavior, reasoning, or understanding; (E) adjudicated as an incompetent; or (F) a vulnerable adult as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.5572">626.5572</a>.</p>
          <p>(3) Violation by a carrier of any part of a court order issued pursuant to this chapter.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4172.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Indirectly transmitted.</span></h2>
          <p>"Indirectly transmitted" means any transmission not defined by subdivision 5.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4172.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Noncompliant behavior.</span></h2>
          <p>"Noncompliant behavior" means a failure or refusal by a carrier to comply with a health directive.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4172.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Respondent.</span></h2>
          <p>"Respondent" means any person against whom an action is commenced under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4171">144.4171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4186">144.4186</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4172.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/209/#laws.0.5.0">1987 c 209 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/309/#laws.0.24.0">1987 c 309 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/229/#laws.4.4.0">1995 c 229 art 4 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.7.28.0">2014 c 291 art 7 s 28</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4173">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4173 CAUSE OF ACTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4173.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Compliance with directive.</span></h2>
          <p>Failure or refusal of a carrier to comply with a health directive is grounds for proceeding under subdivision 2.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4173.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Commencement of action.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner, or a community health board as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145A.02#stat.145A.02.5">145A.02, subdivision 5</a>, with express delegated authority from the commissioner, may commence legal action against a carrier who is a health threat to others and, unless a court order is sought under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4182">144.4182</a>, who engages in noncompliant behavior, by filing with the district court in the county in which respondent resides, and serving upon respondent, a petition for relief and notice of hearing.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4173.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/209/#laws.0.6.0">1987 c 209 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/309/#laws.0.24.0">1987 c 309 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.7.28.0">2014 c 291 art 7 s 28</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4174">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4174 STANDING.</h1>
        <p>Only the commissioner, or a community health board as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145A.02#stat.145A.02.5">145A.02, subdivision 5</a>, with express delegated authority from the commissioner, may commence an action under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4171">144.4171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4186">144.4186</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4174.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/209/#laws.0.7.0">1987 c 209 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/309/#laws.0.24.0">1987 c 309 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.7.28.0">2014 c 291 art 7 s 28</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4175">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4175 REPORTING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4175.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Voluntary reporting.</span></h2>
          <p>Any licensed health professional or other human services professional regulated by the state who has knowledge or reasonable cause to believe that a person is a health threat to others or has engaged in noncompliant behavior, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4172">144.4172</a>, may report that information to the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4175.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Liability for reporting.</span></h2>
          <p>A licensed health professional or other human services professional regulated by the state who has knowledge or reasonable cause to believe that a person is a health threat to others or has engaged in noncompliant behavior, and who makes a report in good faith under subdivision 1, is not subject to liability for reporting in any civil, administrative, disciplinary, or criminal action.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4175.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Falsified reports.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person who knowingly or recklessly makes a false report under the provisions of this section shall be liable in a civil suit for any actual damages suffered by the person or persons so reported and for any punitive damages set by the court or jury.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4175.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Waiver of privilege.</span></h2>
          <p>Any privilege otherwise created in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/595.02">595.02</a>, clauses (d), (e), (g), and (j), with respect to persons who make a report under subdivision 1, is waived regarding any information about a carrier as a health threat to others or about a carrier's noncompliant behavior in any investigation or action under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4171">144.4171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4186">144.4186</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4175.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/209/#laws.0.8.0">1987 c 209 s 8</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4176">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4176 PETITION; NOTICE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4176.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Petition.</span></h2>
          <p>The petition must set forth the following:</p>
          <p>(1) the grounds and underlying facts that demonstrate that the respondent is a health threat to others and, unless an emergency court order is sought under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4182">144.4182</a>, has engaged in noncompliant behavior;</p>
          <p>(2) the petitioner's efforts to alleviate the health threat to others prior to the issuance of a health directive, unless an emergency court order is sought under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4182">144.4182</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) the petitioner's efforts to issue the health directive to the respondent in person, unless an emergency court order is sought under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4182">144.4182</a>;</p>
          <p>(4) the type of relief sought; and</p>
          <p>(5) a request for a court hearing on the allegations contained in the petition.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4176.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Hearing notice.</span></h2>
          <p>The notice must contain the following information:</p>
          <p>(1) the time, date, and place of the hearing;</p>
          <p>(2) respondent's right to appear at the hearing;</p>
          <p>(3) respondent's right to present and cross-examine witnesses; and</p>
          <p>(4) respondent's right to counsel, including the right, if indigent, to representation by counsel designated by the court or county of venue.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4176.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/209/#laws.0.9.0">1987 c 209 s 9</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4177">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4177 TIME OF HEARING AND DUTIES OF COUNSEL.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4177.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Time of hearing.</span></h2>
          <p>A hearing on the petition must be held before the district court in the county in which respondent resides as soon as possible, but no later than 14 days from service of the petition and hearing notice.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4177.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Duties of counsel.</span></h2>
          <p>In all proceedings under this section, counsel for the respondent shall (1) consult with the person prior to any hearing; (2) be given adequate time to prepare for all hearings; (3) continue to represent the person throughout any proceedings under this charge unless released as counsel by the court; and (4) be a vigorous advocate on behalf of the client.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4177.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/209/#laws.0.10.0">1987 c 209 s 10</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4178">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4178 CRIMINAL IMMUNITY.</h1>
        <p>In accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.09#stat.609.09.2">609.09, subdivision 2</a>, no person shall be excused in an action under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4171">144.4171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4186">144.4186</a> from giving testimony or producing any documents, books, records, or correspondence, tending to be self-incriminating; but the testimony or evidence, or other testimony or evidence derived from it, must not be used against the person in any criminal case, except for perjury committed in the testimony.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4178.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/209/#laws.0.11.0">1987 c 209 s 11</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4179">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4179 STANDARD OF PROOF; EVIDENCE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4179.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Clear and convincing.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner must prove the allegations in the petition by clear and convincing evidence.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4179.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">All relevant evidence.</span></h2>
          <p>The court shall admit all reliable relevant evidence. Medical and epidemiologic data must be admitted if it otherwise comports with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145.30">145.30</a>, chapter 600, Minnesota Rules of Evidence 803(6), or other statutes or rules that permit reliable evidence to be admitted in civil cases.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4179.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Carrier status.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon a finding by the court that the commissioner's suspicion of carrier status is reasonable as established by presentation of facts justifying an inference that the respondent harbors a specific infectious agent, there shall exist a rebuttable presumption that the respondent is a carrier. This presumption may be rebutted if the respondent demonstrates noncarrier status after undergoing medically accepted tests.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4179.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Failure to appear.</span></h2>
          <p>If a party fails to appear at the hearing without prior court approval, the hearing may proceed without the absent party and the court may make its determination on the basis of all reliable evidence submitted at the hearing.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4179.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Records.</span></h2>
          <p>The court shall take and preserve an accurate stenographic record of the proceedings.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4179.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/209/#laws.0.12.0">1987 c 209 s 12</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4180">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4180 REMEDIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4180.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Remedies available.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon a finding by the court that the commissioner has proven the allegations set forth in the petition, the court may order that the respondent must:</p>
          <p>(1) participate in a designated education program;</p>
          <p>(2) participate in a designated counseling program;</p>
          <p>(3) participate in a designated treatment program;</p>
          <p>(4) undergo medically accepted tests to verify carrier status or for diagnosis, or undergo treatment that is consistent with standard medical practice as necessary to make respondent noninfectious;</p>
          <p>(5) notify or appear before designated health officials for verification of status, testing, or other purposes consistent with monitoring;</p>
          <p>(6) cease and desist the conduct which constitutes a health threat to others;</p>
          <p>(7) live part time or full time in a supervised setting for the period and under the conditions set by the court;</p>
          <p>(8) subject to the provisions of subdivision 2, be committed to an appropriate institutional facility for the period and under the conditions set by the court, but not longer than six months, until the respondent is made noninfectious, or until the respondent completes a course of treatment prescribed by the court, whichever occurs first, unless the commissioner shows good cause for continued commitment; and</p>
          <p>(9) comply with any combination of the remedies in clauses (1) to (8), or other remedies considered just by the court. In no case may a respondent be committed to a correctional facility.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4180.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Commitment review panel.</span></h2>
          <p>The court may not order the remedy specified in subdivision 1, clause (8), unless it first considers the recommendation of a commitment review panel appointed by the commissioner to review the need for commitment of the respondent to an institutional facility.</p>
          <p>The duties of the commitment review panel shall be to:</p>
          <p>(1) review the record of the proceeding;</p>
          <p>(2) interview the respondent. If the respondent is not interviewed, the reasons must be documented; and</p>
          <p>(3) identify, explore, and list the reasons for rejecting or recommending alternatives to commitment.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4180.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Construction.</span></h2>
          <p>This section shall be construed so that the least restrictive alternative is used to achieve the desired purpose of preventing or controlling communicable disease.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4180.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Additional requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>If commitment or supervised living is ordered, the court shall require the head of the institutional facility or the person in charge of supervision to submit: (1) a plan of treatment within ten days of initiation of commitment or supervised living; and (2) a written report, with a copy to both the commissioner and the respondent, at least 60 days, but not more than 90 days, from the start of respondent's commitment or supervised living arrangement, setting forth the following:</p>
          <p>(i) the types of support or therapy groups, if any, respondent is attending and how often respondent attends;</p>
          <p>(ii) the type of care or treatment respondent is receiving, and what future care or treatment is necessary;</p>
          <p>(iii) whether respondent has been cured or made noninfectious, or otherwise no longer poses a threat to public health;</p>
          <p>(iv) whether continued commitment or supervised living is necessary; and</p>
          <p>(v) other information the court considers necessary.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4180.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/209/#laws.0.13.0">1987 c 209 s 13</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4181">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4181 APPEAL.</h1>
        <p>The petitioner or respondent may appeal the decision of the district court. The court of appeals shall hear the appeal within 30 days after service of the notice of appeal. However, respondent's status as determined by the district court remains unchanged, and any remedy ordered by the district court remains in effect while the appeal is pending.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4181.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/209/#laws.0.14.0">1987 c 209 s 14</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4182">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4182 TEMPORARY EMERGENCY HOLD.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4182.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Apprehend and hold.</span></h2>
