        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.445.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Waiver.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may waive any portion of the requirements of subdivisions 1 to 4 if the commissioner of health determines that it is not necessary to protect the public health or if the screening may have a detrimental effect on a person's health status.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.445.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/167/#laws.0.6.0">1993 c 167 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/164/#laws.0.1.0">1997 c 164 s 1</a>,2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.4.2.0">2006 c 260 art 4 s 2</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.45"><b>144.45</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/192/#laws.3.5.0">2014 c 192 art 3 s 5</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.46"><b>144.46</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/357/#laws.0.22.0">1980 c 357 s 22</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.47"><b>144.47</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/357/#laws.0.22.0">1980 c 357 s 22</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.471"><b>144.471</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/209/#laws.0.40.0">1987 c 209 s 40</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.48"><b>144.48</b> [Renumbered <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.427">144.427</a>]
</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">TUBERCULOSIS HEALTH THREAT ACT</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4801">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4801 TITLE.</h1>
        <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4801">144.4801</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4813">144.4813</a> may be cited as the "Tuberculosis Health Threat Act."</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4801.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/164/#laws.0.3.0">1997 c 164 s 3</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4802">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4802 AUTHORITY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4802.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Authority to commit.</span></h2>
          <p>Under the powers and duties assigned to the commissioner in this chapter and chapter 145, the commissioner may proceed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4801">144.4801</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4813">144.4813</a> whenever the commissioner has probable cause to believe that a person who has active tuberculosis or is clinically suspected of having active tuberculosis is an endangerment to the public health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4802.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Preemption.</span></h2>
          <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4801">144.4801</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4813">144.4813</a> preempt and supersede sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4171">144.4171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4186">144.4186</a> with regard to a tuberculosis health threat. Nothing in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4801">144.4801</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4813">144.4813</a> restricts the commissioner's authority to seek injunctive relief pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145.075">145.075</a>, or any other relief under other statutes or at common law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4802.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Reliance on spiritual means in lieu of medical treatment.</span></h2>
          <p>Nothing in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4801">144.4801</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4813">144.4813</a> shall be construed to abridge the right of a carrier to refuse medical treatment for tuberculosis if the carrier opposes medical treatment on the basis of sincere religious beliefs and complies with a monitoring plan developed by the commissioner for the isolation of the carrier as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4803#stat.144.4803.14">144.4803, subdivision 14</a>. A carrier who meets the requirements of this subdivision is not considered an endangerment under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4803#stat.144.4803.10">144.4803, subdivision 10</a>, clauses (2) to (6) and (8). Nothing in this subdivision shall be construed to limit the authority of the commissioner to take necessary actions to protect the public health according to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4801">144.4801</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4813">144.4813</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4802.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/164/#laws.0.4.0">1997 c 164 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/192/#laws.3.4.0">2014 c 192 art 3 s 4</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4803">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4803 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Active tuberculosis.</span></h2>
          <p>"Active tuberculosis" includes infectious and noninfectious tuberculosis and means:</p>
          <p>(1) a condition evidenced by a positive culture for mycobacterium tuberculosis taken from a pulmonary or laryngeal source;</p>
          <p>(2) a condition evidenced by a positive culture for mycobacterium tuberculosis taken from an extrapulmonary source when there is clinical evidence such as a positive skin test for tuberculosis infection, coughing, sputum production, fever, or other symptoms compatible with pulmonary tuberculosis; or</p>
          <p>(3) a condition in which clinical specimens are not available for culture, but there is radiographic evidence of tuberculosis such as an abnormal chest x-ray, and clinical evidence such as a positive skin test for tuberculosis infection, coughing, sputum production, fever, or other symptoms compatible with pulmonary tuberculosis, that lead a physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant to reasonably diagnose active tuberculosis according to currently accepted standards of medical practice and to initiate treatment for tuberculosis.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Advanced practice registered nurse.</span></h2>
          <p>"Advanced practice registered nurse" means a person who is licensed by the Board of Nursing under chapter 148 to practice as an advanced practice registered nurse.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Renumbered subd 5a]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Carrier.</span></h2>
          <p>"Carrier" means a person who has active tuberculosis or is clinically suspected of having active tuberculosis.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Clinically suspected of having active tuberculosis.</span></h2>
          <p>"Clinically suspected of having active tuberculosis" means presenting a reasonable possibility of having active tuberculosis based upon epidemiologic, clinical, or radiographic evidence, laboratory test results, or other reliable evidence as determined by a physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant using currently accepted standards of medical practice.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>"Commissioner" means the commissioner of health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.5a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5a.<span class="headnote">Community health board.</span></h2>
          <p>"Community health board" means an administrative authority established under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145A.03">145A.03</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Contagion precautions for tuberculosis.</span></h2>
          <p>"Contagion precautions for tuberculosis" means those measures under currently accepted standards of medical practice that prevent a carrier from exposing others to tuberculosis.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Department.</span></h2>
          <p>"Department" means the Department of Health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Directly observed therapy.</span></h2>
          <p>"Directly observed therapy" means a method for ensuring compliance with medication directions in which a licensed health professional or designee observes a person ingesting prescribed medications or administers the prescribed medication to the person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Disease prevention officer.</span></h2>
          <p>"Disease prevention officer" means a designated agent of the commissioner, or a designated agent of a community health board that has express delegated authority from the commissioner to proceed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4801">144.4801</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4813">144.4813</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Endangerment to the public health.</span></h2>
          <p>"Endangerment to the public health" means a carrier who may transmit tuberculosis to another person or persons because the carrier has engaged or is engaging in any of the following conduct:</p>
          <p>(1) refuses or fails to submit to a diagnostic tuberculosis examination that is ordered by a physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant and is reasonable according to currently accepted standards of medical practice;</p>
          <p>(2) refuses or fails to initiate or complete treatment for tuberculosis that is prescribed by a physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant and is reasonable according to currently accepted standards of medical practice;</p>
          <p>(3) refuses or fails to keep appointments for treatment of tuberculosis;</p>
          <p>(4) refuses or fails to provide the commissioner, upon request, with evidence showing the completion of a course of treatment for tuberculosis that is prescribed by a physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant and is reasonable according to currently accepted standards of medical practice;</p>
          <p>(5) refuses or fails to initiate or complete a course of directly observed therapy that is prescribed by a physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant and is reasonable according to currently accepted standards of medical practice;</p>
          <p>(6) misses at least 20 percent of scheduled appointments for directly observed therapy, or misses at least two consecutive appointments for directly observed therapy;</p>
          <p>(7) refuses or fails to follow contagion precautions for tuberculosis after being instructed on the precautions by a licensed health professional or by the commissioner;</p>
          <p>(8) based on evidence of the carrier's past or present behavior, may not complete a course of treatment for tuberculosis that is reasonable according to currently accepted standards of medical practice; or</p>
          <p>(9) may expose other persons to tuberculosis based on epidemiological, medical, or other reliable evidence.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Epidemiological data or epidemiological evidence.</span></h2>
          <p>"Epidemiological data" or "epidemiological evidence" means data or evidence relating to the occurrence, distribution, clinical characteristics, and control of disease within a group of people or within a specified population.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Health order.</span></h2>
          <p>"Health order" means an order issued by the commissioner or a community health board with express delegated authority from the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Infectious tuberculosis.</span></h2>
          <p>"Infectious tuberculosis" means the stage of tuberculosis where mycobacterial organisms are capable of being expelled into the air by a person, as determined by laboratory, epidemiological, or clinical findings.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.<span class="headnote">Isolation.</span></h2>
          <p>"Isolation" means placing a carrier who has infectious tuberculosis in:</p>
          <p>(1) a hospital or other treatment facility;</p>
          <p>(2) the carrier's residence or current location; or</p>
          <p>(3) any other place approved by the commissioner, provided that the place of isolation prevents or limits the transmission of the infectious tuberculosis agent to others during the period of infectiousness.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.15">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">Licensed health professional.</span></h2>
          <p>"Licensed health professional" means a person licensed by one of the health-related licensing boards listed in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.01#stat.214.01.2">214.01, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.16">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.<span class="headnote">Peace officer.</span></h2>
          <p>"Peace officer" means an employee or an elected or appointed official of a political subdivision or law enforcement agency who is licensed by the Board of Peace Officer Standards and Training, is charged with the prevention and detection of crime and the enforcement of the general criminal laws of the state, and has the full power of arrest. "Peace officer" includes an officer of the Minnesota State Patrol.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.17">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17.<span class="headnote">Physician.</span></h2>
          <p>"Physician" means a person who is licensed by the Board of Medical Practice under chapter 147 to practice medicine.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.17a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17a.<span class="headnote">Physician assistant.</span></h2>
          <p>"Physician assistant" means a person who is licensed by the Board of Medical Practice under chapter 147A to practice as a physician assistant.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.18">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 18.<span class="headnote">Respondent.</span></h2>
          <p>"Respondent" means a person or group of persons to whom the commissioner has issued a health order, excluding the carrier.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4803.19">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 19.<span class="headnote">Treatment facility.</span></h2>
          <p>"Treatment facility" means a hospital or other treatment provider that is qualified to provide care, treatment, and appropriate contagion precautions for tuberculosis.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4803.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/164/#laws.0.5.0">1997 c 164 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.109.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 109</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.4.26.0">2020 c 115 art 4 s 26</a>-29; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/58/#laws.0.31.0">2022 c 58 s 31</a>-34</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4804">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4804 REPORTING RELATING TO TUBERCULOSIS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4804.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Mandatory reporting.</span></h2>
          <p>A licensed health professional must report to the commissioner or a disease prevention officer within 24 hours of obtaining knowledge of a reportable person as specified in subdivision 3, unless the licensed health professional is aware that the facts causing the person to be a reportable person have previously been reported. Within 72 hours of making a report, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays, the licensed health professional shall submit to the commissioner or to the disease prevention officer a certified copy of the reportable person's medical records relating to the carrier's tuberculosis and status as an endangerment to the public health if the person is reportable under subdivision 3, clause (3), (4), or (5). A reporting facility may designate an infection control practitioner to make reports and to send certified medical records relating to the carrier's tuberculosis and status as an endangerment to the public health under this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4804.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Voluntary reporting.</span></h2>
          <p>A person other than a licensed health professional may report to the commissioner or a disease prevention officer if the person has knowledge of a reportable person as specified in subdivision 3, or has probable cause to believe that a person should be reported under subdivision 3.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4804.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Reportable persons.</span></h2>
          <p>A licensed health professional must report to the commissioner or a disease prevention officer if the licensed health professional has knowledge of:</p>
          <p>(1) a person who has been diagnosed with active tuberculosis;</p>
          <p>(2) a person who is clinically suspected of having active tuberculosis;</p>
          <p>(3) a person who refuses or fails to submit to a diagnostic tuberculosis examination when the person is clinically suspected of having tuberculosis;</p>
          <p>(4) a carrier who has refused or failed to initiate or complete treatment for tuberculosis, including refusal or failure to take medication for tuberculosis or keep appointments for directly observed therapy or other treatment of tuberculosis; or</p>
          <p>(5) a person who refuses or fails to follow contagion precautions for tuberculosis after being instructed on the precautions by a licensed health professional or by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4804.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Reporting information.</span></h2>
          <p>The report by a licensed health professional under subdivision 1 or by a person under subdivision 2 must contain the following information, to the extent known:</p>
          <p>(1) the reportable person's name, birth date, address or last known location, and telephone number;</p>
          <p>(2) the date and specific circumstances that cause the person to be a reportable person;</p>
          <p>(3) the reporting person's name, title, address, and telephone number; and</p>
          <p>(4) any other information relevant to the reportable person's case of tuberculosis.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4804.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Immunity for reporting.</span></h2>
          <p>A licensed health professional who is required to report under subdivision 1 or a person who voluntarily reports in good faith under subdivision 2 is immune from liability in a civil, administrative, disciplinary, or criminal action for reporting under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4804.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Falsified reports.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who knowingly or recklessly makes a false report under this section is liable in a civil suit for actual damages suffered by the person or persons reported and for punitive damages.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4804.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Waiver of privilege.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who is the subject of a report under subdivision 1 is deemed to have waived any privilege created in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/595.02#stat.595.02.1">595.02, subdivision 1</a>, paragraphs (d), (e), (g), (i), (j), and (k), with respect to any information provided under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4804.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Tuberculosis notification.</span></h2>
          <p>If an emergency medical services person, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401#stat.144.7401.4">144.7401, subdivision 4</a>, is exposed to a person with active tuberculosis during the performance of duties, the treatment facility's designated infection control coordinator shall notify the emergency medical services agency's exposure control officer by telephone and by written correspondence. The facility's designated infection control coordinator shall provide the emergency medical services person with information about screening and, if indicated, follow-up.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4804.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/164/#laws.0.6.0">1997 c 164 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/422/#laws.0.4.0">2000 c 422 s 4</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4805">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4805 HEALTH ORDER; RIGHTS OF CARRIER AND RESPONDENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4805.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Authority.</span></h2>
          <p>Only the commissioner, or a community health board with express delegated authority from the commissioner, may issue a health order under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4805.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Grounds for health order.</span></h2>
          <p>Whenever the commissioner has probable cause to believe that a carrier is an endangerment to the public health, the commissioner may issue a health order that the commissioner deems necessary to protect the public health. The commissioner may petition the court for enforcement of the health order. In a court proceeding for enforcement of the health order, the commissioner shall demonstrate the particularized circumstances constituting the necessity for the health order. The health order may be issued to any person, including a carrier, physician, licensed health professional, or treatment facility. The health order may be in the form of a subpoena by the commissioner for certified medical records relating to the carrier's tuberculosis and status as an endangerment to the public health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4805.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Contents of health order.</span></h2>
          <p>A health order must include:</p>
          <p>(1) a citation to this section as the legal authority under which the order is issued;</p>
          <p>(2) a summary of evidence upon which the person is alleged to be a carrier;</p>
          <p>(3) a description of the alleged conduct of the carrier that makes the carrier an endangerment to the public health;</p>
          <p>(4) a description of less restrictive alternatives that the commissioner considered and rejected, together with the reasons for the rejection, or a description of less restrictive alternatives that the commissioner used and that were unsuccessful;</p>
          <p>(5) the preventive measure ordered; and</p>
          <p>(6) a notice advising the carrier or respondent that:</p>
          <p>(i) a hearing will be held if the carrier or respondent petitions the court for a hearing or if the commissioner determines that the carrier has not complied with the health order;</p>
          <p>(ii) the carrier or respondent has the right to appear at the hearing;</p>
          <p>(iii) the carrier or respondent has the right to present and cross-examine witnesses at the hearing;</p>
          <p>(iv) the carrier has the right to court-appointed counsel in a proceeding under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4801">144.4801</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4813">144.4813</a>; and</p>
          <p>(v) the carrier or respondent has the right to the assistance of an interpreter in a proceeding under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4801">144.4801</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4813">144.4813</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4805.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Right to counsel.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The carrier or respondent has the right to counsel in any proceeding under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4801">144.4801</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4813">144.4813</a>. The court shall promptly appoint counsel for a carrier if the carrier does not have counsel:</p>
          <p>(1) at the time the court issues an order under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4807#stat.144.4807.7">144.4807, subdivision 7</a>, authorizing the continued detention of the carrier;</p>
          <p>(2) at the time the court issues an order under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4808#stat.144.4808.2">144.4808, subdivision 2</a>, authorizing the carrier to be apprehended and held; or</p>
          <p>(3) in all other cases, at the time either party files a notice for a preliminary hearing under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4810#stat.144.4810.2">144.4810, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
          <p>The court shall appoint counsel for the carrier. The cost of court-appointed counsel shall be paid by the court.</p>
          <p>(b) Upon being notified of the name and address of counsel for the carrier, the commissioner shall promptly forward to the carrier and the carrier's counsel the following:</p>
          <p>(1) a copy of the health order;</p>
          <p>(2) a certified copy of relevant portions of the carrier's medical records; and</p>
          <p>(3) the name and address of the licensed health professional, including the carrier's attending physician or nurse, or the public health physician or nurse whom the commissioner intends to have testify at the preliminary hearing, and a summary of the witness' testimony, including a copy of the witness' affidavit, if any.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4805.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Duty to communicate.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner's counsel and the carrier's counsel shall make every effort to communicate prior to any hearing and to stipulate as to undisputed facts, witnesses, and exhibits.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4805.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Right to interpreter.</span></h2>
          <p>The carrier or respondent has the right to the assistance of an interpreter in a proceeding under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4801">144.4801</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4813">144.4813</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4805.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Service of order.</span></h2>
          <p>A health order may be served by a disease prevention officer or peace officer.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4805.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/164/#laws.0.7.0">1997 c 164 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.109.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 109</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4806">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4806 PREVENTIVE MEASURES UNDER HEALTH ORDER.</h1>
        <p>A health order may include, but need not be limited to, an order:</p>
        <p>(1) requiring the carrier's attending physician, advanced practice registered nurse, physician assistant, or treatment facility to isolate and detain the carrier for treatment or for a diagnostic examination for tuberculosis, pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4807#stat.144.4807.1">144.4807, subdivision 1</a>, if the carrier is an endangerment to the public health and is in a treatment facility;</p>
        <p>(2) requiring a carrier who is an endangerment to the public health to submit to diagnostic examination for tuberculosis and to remain in the treatment facility until the commissioner receives the results of the examination;</p>
        <p>(3) requiring a carrier who is an endangerment to the public health to remain in or present at a treatment facility until the carrier has completed a course of treatment for tuberculosis that is prescribed by a physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant and is reasonable according to currently accepted standards of medical practice;</p>
        <p>(4) requiring a carrier who is an endangerment to the public health to complete a course of treatment for tuberculosis that is prescribed by a physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant and is reasonable according to currently accepted standards of medical practice and, if necessary, to follow contagion precautions for tuberculosis;</p>
        <p>(5) requiring a carrier who is an endangerment to the public health to follow a course of directly observed therapy that is prescribed by a physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant and is reasonable according to currently accepted standards of medical practice;</p>
        <p>(6) excluding a carrier who is an endangerment to the public health from the carrier's place of work or school, or from other premises if the commissioner determines that exclusion is necessary because contagion precautions for tuberculosis cannot be maintained in a manner adequate to protect others from being exposed to tuberculosis;</p>
        <p>(7) requiring a licensed health professional or treatment facility to provide to the commissioner certified copies of all medical and epidemiological data relevant to the carrier's tuberculosis and status as an endangerment to the public health;</p>
        <p>(8) requiring the diagnostic examination for tuberculosis of other persons in the carrier's household, workplace, or school, or other persons in close contact with the carrier if the commissioner has probable cause to believe that the persons may have active tuberculosis or may have been exposed to tuberculosis based on epidemiological, medical, or other reliable evidence; or</p>
        <p>(9) requiring a carrier or other persons to follow contagion precautions for tuberculosis.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4806.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/164/#laws.0.8.0">1997 c 164 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.4.30.0">2020 c 115 art 4 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/58/#laws.0.35.0">2022 c 58 s 35</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4807">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4807 NOTICE OF OBLIGATION TO ISOLATE OR EXAMINE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4807.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Obligation to isolate.</span></h2>
          <p>If the carrier is in a treatment facility, the commissioner or a carrier's attending physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant, after obtaining approval from the commissioner, may issue a notice of obligation to isolate to a treatment facility if the commissioner or attending physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant has probable cause to believe that a carrier is an endangerment to the public health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4807.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Obligation to examine.</span></h2>
          <p>If the carrier is clinically suspected of having active tuberculosis, the commissioner may issue a notice of obligation to examine to the carrier's attending physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant to conduct a diagnostic examination for tuberculosis on the carrier.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4807.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Precautions to avoid exposure.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon receiving a notice of obligation to isolate or notice of obligation to examine, a treatment facility shall immediately take all reasonable precautions to prevent the carrier from exposing other persons to tuberculosis, including the use of guards or locks, if appropriate.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4807.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Service of health order on carrier.</span></h2>
          <p>When issuing a notice of obligation to isolate or examine to the carrier's physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant or a treatment facility, the commissioner shall simultaneously serve a health order on the carrier ordering the carrier to remain in the treatment facility for treatment or examination.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4807.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Duration of detention.</span></h2>
          <p>No carrier may be detained under subdivision 1 or 2 longer than 72 hours, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays, unless the court issues an order authorizing continued detention of the carrier pursuant to subdivision 7. A carrier may not be released prior to the expiration of the 72-hour hold without the express consent of the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4807.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Application for extension of 72-hour hold.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may seek an order extending the hold under subdivision 5 by filing an ex parte application with the probate division of the district court of the county in which the carrier resides. The application may be filed orally by telephone or by facsimile, provided that a written application is filed within 72 hours, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4807.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Court order extending 72-hour hold.</span></h2>
          <p>The court may extend the hold under subdivision 5 by up to six days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays, if the court finds that there is probable cause to believe that the carrier is an endangerment to the public health. The court may find probable cause to detain, examine, and isolate the carrier based upon a written statement by facsimile or upon an oral statement by telephone from the carrier's attending physician, nurse, or physician assistant; a public health physician, nurse, or physician assistant; other licensed health professional; or disease prevention officer, stating the grounds and facts that demonstrate that the carrier is an endangerment to the public health, provided that an affidavit from such witness is filed with the court within 72 hours, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays. The order may be issued orally by telephone, or by facsimile, provided that a written order is issued within 72 hours, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays. The oral and written order shall contain a notice of the carrier's rights contained in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4805#stat.144.4805.3">144.4805, subdivision 3</a>, clause (6). A carrier may not be released prior to the hold extended under this subdivision without the express consent of the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4807.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Appointment of counsel.</span></h2>
          <p>If the carrier does not have counsel at the time the court issues an order to extend the hold under subdivision 7, the court shall promptly appoint counsel for the carrier.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4807.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Immunity.</span></h2>
          <p>A disease prevention officer, peace officer, physician, licensed health professional, or treatment facility that acts in good faith under this section is immune from liability in any civil, administrative, disciplinary, or criminal action for acting under this section.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4807.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/164/#laws.0.9.0">1997 c 164 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.4.31.0">2020 c 115 art 4 s 31</a>-33; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/58/#laws.0.36.0">2022 c 58 s 36</a>-39</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4808">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4808 APPREHEND AND HOLD ORDER.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4808.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Application for apprehend and hold order.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may make an ex parte application for an order to apprehend and hold a carrier who is not in a treatment facility if the commissioner has probable cause to believe that a carrier is:</p>
          <p>(1) an endangerment to the public health; and</p>
          <p>(2) either in imminent danger of exposing another person or persons to tuberculosis, or may flee or become unlocatable.</p>
          <p>The commissioner shall file the application in the probate division of the district court of the county in which the carrier resides. The application may be filed orally by telephone or by facsimile, provided that a written application is filed within 72 hours, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4808.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Court order to apprehend and hold.</span></h2>
          <p>The court may find probable cause to apprehend and hold the carrier based upon a written statement by facsimile or oral statement by telephone from the carrier's attending physician or nurse, a public health physician or nurse, other licensed health professional, or disease prevention officer, stating the grounds and facts that demonstrate that the carrier is an endangerment to the public health, provided that an affidavit from such witness is filed with the court within 72 hours, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays. The court may issue an order to a peace officer or to a disease prevention officer, or both to:</p>
          <p>(1) apprehend and transport the carrier to a designated treatment facility, and detain the carrier until the carrier is admitted to the treatment facility; or</p>
          <p>(2) apprehend and isolate the carrier.</p>
          <p>The order may be issued orally by telephone, or by facsimile, provided that a written order is issued within 72 hours, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays. The oral and written order shall contain a notice of the carrier's rights contained in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4805#stat.144.4805.3">144.4805, subdivision 3</a>, clause (6).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4808.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Duration of detention.</span></h2>
          <p>A carrier may be detained under this subdivision up to six days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays. A carrier may not be released prior to the expiration of the hold authorized under this section without the express consent of the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4808.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Apprehension of carrier.</span></h2>
          <p>If the carrier flees or forcibly resists the peace officer or disease prevention officer, the officer may use all necessary and lawful means to apprehend, hold, transport, or isolate the carrier. This subdivision is authority for the officer to carry out the duties specified in this section. The commissioner shall provide any information and equipment necessary to protect the officer from becoming exposed to tuberculosis.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4808.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Appointment of counsel.</span></h2>
          <p>If the carrier does not have counsel at the time the court issues an apprehend and hold order under subdivision 2, the court shall promptly appoint counsel for the carrier.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4808.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Immunity.</span></h2>
          <p>A disease prevention officer, peace officer, physician, licensed health professional, or treatment facility that acts in good faith under this section is immune from liability in any civil, administrative, disciplinary, or criminal action for acting under this section.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4808.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/164/#laws.0.10.0">1997 c 164 s 10</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4809">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4809 PRELIMINARY HEARING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4809.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Grounds for hearing.</span></h2>
          <p>A party may petition the court for an order for enforcement of or relief from a health order or judicial order.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4809.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Petition for preliminary hearing.</span></h2>
          <p>The petitioning party shall serve on the commissioner and file in the probate division of the district court of the county in which the carrier or respondent resides a petition and notice of preliminary hearing. The court shall hold a preliminary hearing no later than 15 days from the date of the filing and service of the petition for a preliminary hearing. If a carrier detained under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4807">144.4807</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4808">144.4808</a> files a petition for a preliminary hearing, the hearing must be held no later than five days from the date of the filing and service of the petition, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4809.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Commissioner's notice of hearing.</span></h2>
          <p>If the commissioner petitions the court to enforce the health order, the notice of the preliminary hearing must contain the following information:</p>
          <p>(1) the date, time, and place of the hearing;</p>
          <p>(2) the right of the carrier to be represented by court-appointed counsel during any proceeding under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4801">144.4801</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4813">144.4813</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) the right of the carrier or respondent to the assistance of an interpreter in any proceeding under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4801">144.4801</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4813">144.4813</a>;</p>
          <p>(4) the right of the carrier or respondent to appear at the hearing;</p>
          <p>(5) the right of the carrier or respondent to present and cross-examine witnesses;</p>
          <p>(6) a statement of any disputed facts, or a statement of the nature of any other disputed matter; and</p>
          <p>(7) the name and address of any witness that the petitioning party intends to call to testify at the hearing, and a brief summary of the witness' testimony.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4809.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Carrier's or respondent's notice of hearing.</span></h2>
          <p>If the carrier or respondent petitions the court for relief from the health order or court order, the notice of preliminary hearing must contain the information in subdivision 3, clauses (1), (6), and (7).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4809.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Duty to communicate.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) At least five days before the date of the preliminary hearing, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays, the nonpetitioning party shall respond to the petition for hearing by filing and serving on the petitioning party:</p>
          <p>(1) a statement of any disputed facts, or a statement of the nature of any other disputed matter; and</p>
          <p>(2) the name and address of any witness that the nonpetitioning party intends to call to testify at the hearing, and a brief summary of the witness' testimony.</p>
          <p>If the carrier seeks release from an emergency hold ordered under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4807#stat.144.4807.7">144.4807, subdivision 7</a>, or under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4808#stat.144.4808.2">144.4808, subdivision 2</a>, the commissioner shall file and serve on the carrier's counsel the items in clauses (1) and (2) at least 48 hours prior to the preliminary hearing, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays.</p>
          <p>(b) At the hearing, the parties shall identify the efforts they made to resolve the matter prior to the preliminary hearing.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4809.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Hearing room in treatment facility.</span></h2>
          <p>If the carrier is infectious, the treatment facility in which the carrier is sought to be detained or to which the carrier is sought to be removed shall make reasonable accommodations to provide a room where the hearing may be held that minimizes the risk of exposing persons attending the hearing to tuberculosis. If a room is not available at the treatment facility, the court may designate another location for the hearing.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4809.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Standard of proof.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner must prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the carrier is an endangerment to the public health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4809.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Rules of evidence.</span></h2>
          <p>The court shall admit all reliable relevant evidence. Medical and epidemiological data must be admitted if it conforms with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145.31">145.31</a>, chapter 600, Minnesota Rules of Evidence, rule 803(6), or other statutes or rules that permit reliable evidence to be admitted in civil cases. The court may rely on medical and epidemiological data, including hearsay, if it finds that physicians and other licensed health professionals rely on the data in the regular course of providing health care and treatment.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4809.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Sufficiency of evidence.</span></h2>
          <p>It is a sufficient basis for the court to order continued confinement of the carrier or other preventive measures requested by the commissioner if reliable testimony is provided solely by the carrier's attending physician or nurse, a public health physician or nurse, other licensed health professional, or disease prevention officer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4809.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Failure to appear at hearing.</span></h2>
          <p>If the carrier or respondent fails to appear at the hearing without prior court approval, the hearing may proceed without the carrier or respondent and the court may make its determination on the basis of all reliable evidence submitted at the hearing.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4809.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/164/#laws.0.11.0">1997 c 164 s 11</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4810">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4810 FINAL HEARING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4810.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Grounds for hearing.</span></h2>
          <p>After the preliminary hearing, the commissioner, carrier, or respondent may petition the court for relief from or enforcement of the court order issued pursuant to the preliminary hearing. The commissioner may petition the court for additional preventive measures if the carrier or respondent has not complied with the court order issued pursuant to the preliminary hearing. The petitioning party shall serve and file a petition and notice of hearing with the probate division of the district court. The court shall hold the final hearing no later than 15 days from the date of the filing and service of the petition for a final hearing.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4810.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Notice of hearing.</span></h2>
          <p>The notice of the final hearing must contain the same information as for the preliminary hearing in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4809#stat.144.4809.3">144.4809, subdivision 3</a> or 4.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4810.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Duty to communicate.</span></h2>
          <p>The parties have a duty to communicate and exchange information as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4809#stat.144.4809.5">144.4809, subdivision 5</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4810.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Hearing room in treatment facility.</span></h2>
          <p>The hearing room for the final hearing is governed by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4809#stat.144.4809.6">144.4809, subdivision 6</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4810.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Standard of proof.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner must prove by clear and convincing evidence that the carrier is an endangerment to the public health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4810.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Rules of evidence.</span></h2>
          <p>The rules of evidence are governed by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4809#stat.144.4809.8">144.4809, subdivision 8</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4810.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Sufficiency of evidence.</span></h2>
          <p>The sufficiency of evidence is governed by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4809#stat.144.4809.9">144.4809, subdivision 9</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4810.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Failure to appear at hearing.</span></h2>
          <p>The failure of the carrier or respondent to appear at the hearing is governed by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4809#stat.144.4809.10">144.4809, subdivision 10</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4810.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Right of appeal.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner, carrier, or respondent may appeal the decision of the district court. The court of appeals shall hear the appeal within 60 days after filing and service of the notice of appeal.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4810.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Right of commissioner to issue subsequent order.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding any ruling by the district court, the commissioner may issue a subsequent health order if the commissioner has probable cause to believe that a health order is necessary based on additional facts not known or present at the time of the district court hearing.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4810.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/164/#laws.0.12.0">1997 c 164 s 12</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4811">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4811 PERIODIC REVIEW AND RELEASE FROM DETENTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4811.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Periodic review.</span></h2>
          <p>If the carrier has been detained in a treatment facility or has been isolated pursuant to a court order, the commissioner shall submit a report to the court, the carrier, and the carrier's counsel within 90 days of the date of the court-ordered detention and every 90 days thereafter, until the carrier is released. The report must state the treatment the carrier receives, whether the carrier is cured or noninfectious, and whether the carrier will continue to be detained. If the carrier contests the commissioner's determination for continued detention, the carrier may request a hearing. The hearing on continued detention is governed by the provisions for a final hearing under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4810">144.4810</a>, excluding subdivision 5 of that section. The court shall order continued detention of the carrier if it finds that such detention is reasonable. This subdivision does not apply to consent orders or other confinement that has been voluntarily agreed upon by the parties.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4811.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Carrier's petition for release.</span></h2>
          <p>If the carrier is detained in a treatment facility or isolated pursuant to a court order, the carrier may make a good faith request for release from confinement prior to the 90-day review under subdivision 1 by filing a petition and notice of hearing with the court that ordered the confinement and by serving the petition and notice on the commissioner. The hearing on continued confinement is governed by the provisions for a final hearing under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4810">144.4810</a>, excluding subdivision 5 of that section. The court shall order continued detention of the carrier if it finds that such detention is reasonable.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4811.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Release from detention based on order to compel examination.</span></h2>
          <p>A carrier who has been detained in a treatment facility under a court order to compel the carrier to submit to a diagnostic tuberculosis examination shall be released only after:</p>
          <p>(1) the commissioner determines that the carrier does not have active tuberculosis; or</p>
          <p>(2) the commissioner determines that the carrier is not an endangerment to the public health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4811.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Release from detention based on endangerment.</span></h2>
          <p>A carrier who is detained in a treatment facility or isolated under a court order because the carrier is an endangerment to the public health shall be released only after:</p>
          <p>(1) the commissioner determines that the carrier is cured; or</p>
          <p>(2) the commissioner determines that the carrier is no longer an endangerment to the public health.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4811.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/164/#laws.0.13.0">1997 c 164 s 13</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4812">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4812 COSTS OF CARE.</h1>
        <p>The costs incurred by the treatment facility and other providers of services to diagnose or treat the carrier for tuberculosis must be borne by the carrier, the carrier's health plan, or public programs. During the period of insurance coverage, a health plan may direct the implementation of the care required by the health order or court order and shall pay at the contracted rate of payment, which shall be considered payment in full. Inpatient hospital services required by the health order or court order and covered by medical assistance are not billable to any other governmental entity. If the carrier cannot pay for treatment, and the carrier does not have public or private health insurance coverage, the carrier shall apply for financial assistance with the aid of the county. For persons not otherwise eligible for public assistance, the commissioner of human services shall determine what, if any, costs the carrier shall pay. The commissioner of human services shall make payments at the medical assistance rate, which will be considered payment in full.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4812.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/164/#laws.0.14.0">1997 c 164 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/158/#laws.2.34.0">2016 c 158 art 2 s 34</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4813">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4813 DATA PRIVACY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4813.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Nonpublic data.</span></h2>
          <p>Data on individuals contained in the health order are health data under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.3805#stat.13.3805.1">13.3805, subdivision 1</a>. Other data on individuals collected by the commissioner as part of an investigation of a carrier under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4801">144.4801</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4813">144.4813</a> are investigative data under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.39">13.39</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4813.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Protective order.</span></h2>
          <p>After a judicial action is commenced, a party may seek a protective order to protect the disclosure of portions of the court record identifying individuals or entities.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4813.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Records retention.</span></h2>
          <p>A records retention schedule for records developed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4801">144.4801</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4813">144.4813</a> must be established pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/138.17#stat.138.17.7">138.17, subdivision 7</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4813.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/164/#laws.0.15.0">1997 c 164 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/227/#laws.0.22.0">1999 c 227 s 22</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.49">
        <h1 class="shn">144.49 VIOLATIONS; PENALTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.49.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Violating rules or board directions.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person violating any rule of the commissioner or any lawful direction of a community health board as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145A.02#stat.145A.02.5">145A.02, subdivision 5</a>, or an agent of a community health board as authorized under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145A.04">145A.04</a> is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.49.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/50/#laws.0.14.0">1979 c 50 s 14</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.49.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/50/#laws.0.14.0">1979 c 50 s 14</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.49.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1979/0/50/#laws.0.14.0">1979 c 50 s 14</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.49.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/209/#laws.0.40.0">1987 c 209 s 40</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.49.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Operating without license.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person, partnership, association, or corporation establishing, conducting, managing, or operating any hospital, sanitarium, or other institution in accordance with the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a>, without first obtaining a license therefor is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.49.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Operating outside law or rules.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person, partnership, association, or corporation which establishes, conducts, manages or operates any hospital, sanitarium or other institution required to be licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a>, in violation of any provision of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a> or any rule established thereunder, is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.49.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">False statements in reports.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person lawfully engaged in the practice of healing who willfully makes any false statement in any report required to be made is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.49.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">(<a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/29">5346</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/29">5356</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/29">5367</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1940A/cite/29">5388</a>) <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/1905/cite/29">RL s 2132</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1913/0/434/#laws.0.8.0">1913 c 434 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1913/0/579/#laws.0.0.0">1913 c 579</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1917/0/220/#laws.0.6.0">1917 c 220 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1939/0/89/#laws.0.1.0">1939 c 89 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1941/0/549/#laws.0.10.0">1941 c 549 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1943/0/649/#laws.0.1.0">1943 c 649 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/512/#laws.0.35.0">1945 c 512 s 35</a>,37; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1949/0/471/#laws.0.14.0">1949 c 471 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/173/#laws.0.32.0">1976 c 173 s 32</a>,33; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/357/#laws.0.11.0">1980 c 357 s 11</a>,12; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/309/#laws.0.24.0">1987 c 309 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/384/#laws.2.1.0">1987 c 384 art 2 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/199/#laws.2.15.0">1991 c 199 art 2 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/192/#laws.3.4.0">2014 c 192 art 3 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.7.28.0">2014 c 291 art 7 s 28</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.491"><b>144.491</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.109.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 109</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">STROKE CENTERS AND STROKE HOSPITALS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.492">
        <h1 class="shn">144.492 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.492.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Applicability.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.492">144.492</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.494">144.494</a>, the terms defined in this section have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.492.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>"Commissioner" means the commissioner of health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.492.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Joint commission.</span></h2>
          <p>"Joint commission" means the independent, not-for-profit organization that accredits and certifies health care organizations and programs in the United States.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.492.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Stroke.</span></h2>
          <p>"Stroke" means the sudden death of brain cells in a localized area due to inadequate blood flow.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.492.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.12.30.0">2013 c 108 art 12 s 30</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.493">
        <h1 class="shn">144.493 CRITERIA.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.493.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Comprehensive stroke center.</span></h2>
          <p>A hospital meets the criteria for a comprehensive stroke center if the hospital has been certified as a comprehensive stroke center by the joint commission or another nationally recognized accreditation entity and the hospital participates in the Minnesota stroke registry program.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.493.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Primary stroke center.</span></h2>
          <p>A hospital meets the criteria for a primary stroke center if the hospital has been certified as a primary stroke center by the joint commission or another nationally recognized accreditation entity and the hospital participates in the Minnesota stroke registry program.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.493.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Thrombectomy-capable stroke center.</span></h2>
          <p>A hospital meets the criteria for a thrombectomy-capable stroke center if the hospital has been certified as a thrombectomy-capable stroke center by the joint commission or another nationally recognized accreditation entity, or is a primary stroke center that is not certified as a thrombectomy-based capable stroke center but the hospital has attained a level of stroke care distinction by offering mechanical endovascular therapies and has been certified by a department approved certifying body that is a nationally recognized guidelines-based organization.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.493.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Acute stroke ready hospital.</span></h2>
          <p>A hospital meets the criteria for an acute stroke ready hospital if the hospital has the following elements of an acute stroke ready hospital:</p>
          <p>(1) an acute stroke team available or on call 24 hours a day, seven days a week;</p>
          <p>(2) written stroke protocols, including triage, stabilization of vital functions, initial diagnostic tests, and use of medications;</p>
          <p>(3) a written plan and letter of cooperation with emergency medical services regarding triage and communication that are consistent with regional patient care procedures;</p>
          <p>(4) emergency department personnel who are trained in diagnosing and treating acute stroke;</p>
          <p>(5) the capacity to complete basic laboratory tests, electrocardiograms, and chest x-rays 24 hours a day, seven days a week;</p>
          <p>(6) the capacity to perform and interpret brain injury imaging studies 24 hours a day, seven days a week;</p>
          <p>(7) written protocols that detail available emergent therapies and reflect current treatment guidelines, which include performance measures and are revised at least annually;</p>
          <p>(8) a neurosurgery coverage plan, call schedule, and a triage and transportation plan;</p>
          <p>(9) transfer protocols and agreements for stroke patients; and</p>
          <p>(10) a designated medical director with experience and expertise in acute stroke care.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.493.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.12.31.0">2013 c 108 art 12 s 31</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.6.8.0">2014 c 291 art 6 s 8</a>,9; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.59.27.0">2024 c 127 art 59 s 27</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.494">
        <h1 class="shn">144.494 DESIGNATING STROKE CENTERS AND STROKE HOSPITALS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.494.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Naming privileges.</span></h2>
          <p>Unless it has been designated as a stroke center or stroke hospital pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.493">144.493</a>, no hospital shall use the term "stroke center" or "stroke hospital" in its name or its advertising or shall otherwise indicate it has stroke treatment capabilities.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.494.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Designation.</span></h2>
          <p>A hospital that voluntarily meets the criteria for a comprehensive stroke center, thrombectomy-capable stroke center, primary stroke center, or acute stroke ready hospital may apply to the commissioner for designation, and upon the commissioner's review and approval of the application, shall be designated as a comprehensive stroke center, a thrombectomy-capable stroke center, a primary stroke center, or an acute stroke ready hospital for a three-year period. If a hospital loses its certification as a comprehensive stroke center or primary stroke center from the joint commission or other nationally recognized accreditation entity, or no longer participates in the Minnesota stroke registry program, its Minnesota designation shall be immediately withdrawn. Prior to the expiration of the designation period, a hospital seeking to remain part of the voluntary acute stroke system may reapply to the commissioner for designation.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.494.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.12.32.0">2013 c 108 art 12 s 32</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.6.10.0">2014 c 291 art 6 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.59.28.0">2024 c 127 art 59 s 28</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">HOSPITALS DESIGNATED AS<br>STEMI RECEIVING CENTERS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4941">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4941 ST SEGMENT ELEVATION MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION (STEMI) RECEIVING CENTERS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4941.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Criteria for STEMI receiving center designation.</span></h2>
          <p>A hospital meets the criteria for a STEMI receiving center designation if the hospital has been accredited as a STEMI receiving center by the Society of Cardiovascular Patient Care, the Joint Commission, the American Heart Association, or another nationally recognized accreditation entity that provides STEMI receiving center accreditation for the care of ST segment elevation myocardial infarction. A hospital may apply to the Department of Health for designation as a STEMI receiving center by providing relevant and current documentation of STEMI receiving center accreditation by a nationally recognized accreditation entity.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4941.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Designation of STEMI receiving centers.</span></h2>
          <p>If a hospital voluntarily meeting the criteria for designation as a STEMI receiving center applies to the commissioner for STEMI receiving center designation, then, upon the commissioner's review and approval of its application, the commissioner shall designate the hospital as a STEMI receiving center for a three-year period. If a hospital loses its accreditation as a STEMI receiving center from a nationally recognized accreditation entity, the commissioner shall immediately withdraw the hospital's STEMI designation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4941.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Coordination among hospitals.</span></h2>
          <p>STEMI receiving centers are encouraged to coordinate, through agreement, with STEMI referring hospitals throughout the state to provide appropriate access to care for ST segment elevation myocardial infarction patients.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4941.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/88/#laws.0.1.0">2016 c 88 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">FORMALDEHYDE GASES IN<br>BUILDING MATERIALS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.495">
        <h1 class="shn">144.495 FORMALDEHYDE RULES.</h1>
        <p>The legislature finds that building materials containing urea formaldehyde may emit unsafe levels of formaldehyde in newly constructed housing units.
