The product standards prescribed in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325F.181">325F.181</a> are intended to provide indoor air levels of formaldehyde that do not exceed 0.4 parts per million. If the commissioner of health determines that the standards prescribed in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325F.181">325F.181</a> result in indoor air levels of formaldehyde that exceed 0.4 parts per million, the commissioner may adopt different building materials product standards to ensure that the 0.4 parts per million level is not exceeded. The commissioner may adopt rules under chapter 14 to establish product standards as provided in this section. The rules of the commissioner governing ambient air levels of formaldehyde, Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4620.1600">4620.1600</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4620.2100">4620.2100</a>, are repealed, except that the rule of the commissioner relating to new installations of urea formaldehyde foam insulation in residential housing units remains in effect.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.495.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/594/#laws.0.1.0">1980 c 594 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/424/#laws.0.130.0">1982 c 424 s 130</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/216/#laws.0.1.0">1985 c 216 s 1</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">MINNESOTA RADON AWARENESS ACT</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.496">
        <h1 class="shn">144.496 MINNESOTA RADON AWARENESS ACT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.496.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Citation.</span></h2>
          <p>This section may be cited as the "Minnesota Radon Awareness Act."</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.496.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The following terms used in this section have the meanings given them.</p>
          <p>(b) "Buyer" means a person negotiating or offering to acquire for value, legal or equitable title, or the right to acquire legal or equitable title to residential real property.</p>
          <p>(c) "Mitigation" means measures designed to permanently reduce indoor radon concentrations.</p>
          <p>(d) "Radon test" means a measurement of indoor radon concentrations according to established industry standards for residential real property.</p>
          <p>(e) "Residential real property" means property occupied as, or intended to be occupied as, a single-family residence, including a unit in a common interest community as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/515B.1-103">515B.1-103</a>, clause (10), regardless of whether the unit is in a common interest community not subject to chapter 515B.</p>
          <p>(f) "Seller" means a person who owns legal or equitable title to residential real property.</p>
          <p>(g) "Elevated radon concentration" means a radon concentration at or above the United States Environmental Protection Agency's radon action level.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.496.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Radon disclosure.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Before signing an agreement to sell or transfer residential real property, the seller shall disclose in writing to the buyer any knowledge the seller has of radon concentrations in the dwelling. The disclosure shall include:</p>
          <p>(1) whether a radon test or tests have occurred on the real property;</p>
          <p>(2) the most current records and reports pertaining to radon concentrations within the dwelling;</p>
          <p>(3) a description of any radon concentrations, mitigation, or remediation;</p>
          <p>(4) information regarding the radon mitigation system, including system description and documentation, if such system has been installed in the dwelling; and</p>
          <p>(5) a radon warning statement meeting the requirements of subdivision 4.</p>
          <p>(b) The seller shall provide the buyer with a copy of the Minnesota Department of Health publication entitled "Radon in Real Estate Transactions."</p>
          <p class="in">(c) The seller's radon disclosure requirements in this section apply to the transfer of any interest in residential real estate, whether by sale, exchange, deed, contract for deed, lease with an option to purchase, or any other option.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) The seller's radon disclosure requirements in this section do not apply to any of the following:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) real property that is not residential real property;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) a gratuitous transfer;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) a transfer made pursuant to a court order;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) a transfer to a government or governmental agency;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) a transfer by foreclosure or deed in lieu of foreclosure;</p>
          <p class="in">(6) a transfer to heirs or devisees of a decedent;</p>
          <p class="in">(7) a transfer from a cotenant to one or more other cotenants;</p>
          <p class="in">(8) a transfer made to a spouse, parent, grandparent, child, or grandchild of the seller;</p>
          <p class="in">(9) a transfer between spouses resulting from a decree of marriage dissolution or from a property settlement agreement incidental to that decree;</p>
          <p class="in">(10) an option to purchase a unit in a common interest community, until exercised;</p>
          <p class="in">(11) a transfer to a person who controls or is controlled by the grantor as those terms are defined with respect to a declarant under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/515B.1-103">515B.1-103</a>, clause (2);</p>
          <p class="in">(12) a transfer to a tenant who is in possession of the residential real property; or</p>
          <p class="in">(13) a transfer of special declarant rights under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/515B.3-104">515B.3-104</a>.</p>
          <p>(e) A seller may provide the written disclosure required under this section to a real estate licensee representing or assisting a prospective buyer. The written disclosure provided to the real estate licensee representing or assisting a prospective buyer is considered to have been provided to the prospective buyer. If the written disclosure is provided to the real estate licensee representing or assisting the prospective buyer, the real estate licensee must provide a copy to the prospective buyer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.496.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Radon warning statement.</span></h2>
          <p>The radon warning statement must include the following language:</p>
          <p class="bl">"Radon Warning Statement</p>
          <p>The Minnesota Department of Health strongly recommends that ALL home buyers have an indoor radon test performed prior to purchase or taking occupancy, and recommends having the radon levels mitigated if elevated radon concentrations are found. Elevated radon concentrations can easily be reduced by a qualified, certified, or licensed, if applicable, radon mitigator.</p>
          <p>Every buyer of any interest in residential real property is notified that the property may present exposure to dangerous levels of indoor radon gas that may place the occupants at risk of developing radon-induced lung cancer. Radon, a Class A human carcinogen, is the leading cause of lung cancer in nonsmokers and the second leading cause overall. The seller of any interest in residential real property is required to provide the buyer with any information on radon test results of the dwelling."</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.496.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Liability; transfer not invalidated.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A seller who fails to make a radon disclosure as required by this section, and is aware of material facts pertaining to radon concentrations in the dwelling, is liable to the buyer.</p>
          <p>(b) A buyer who is injured by a violation of this section may bring a civil action and recover damages and receive other equitable relief as determined by the court. An action under this subdivision must be commenced within two years after the date on which the buyer closed the purchase or transfer of the real property.</p>
          <p>(c) This section does not invalidate a transfer solely because of the failure of any person to comply with a provision of this section. This section does not prevent a court from ordering a rescission of the transfer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.496.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Effective date.</span></h2>
          <p>This section is effective January 1, 2014, and applies to agreements to sell or transfer residential real property executed on or after that date.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.496.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/43/#laws.0.4.0">2013 c 43 s 4</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">MINNESOTA RADON LICENSING ACT</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.4961">
        <h1 class="shn">144.4961 MINNESOTA RADON LICENSING ACT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4961.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Citation.</span></h2>
          <p>This section may be cited as the "Minnesota Radon Licensing Act."</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4961.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) As used in this section, the following terms have the meanings given them.</p>
          <p>(b) "Mitigation" means the act of repairing or altering a building or building design for the purpose in whole or in part of reducing the concentration of radon in the indoor atmosphere.</p>
          <p>(c) "Radon" means both the radioactive, gaseous element produced by the disintegration of radium, and the short-lived radionuclides that are decay products of radon.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4961.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Rulemaking.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall adopt rules establishing licensure requirements and work standards relating to indoor radon in dwellings and other buildings, with the exception of newly constructed Minnesota homes according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/326B.106#stat.326B.106.6">326B.106, subdivision 6</a>. The commissioner shall coordinate, oversee, and implement all state functions in matters concerning the presence, effects, measurement, and mitigation of risks of radon in dwellings and other buildings. Rules adopted by the commissioner under this subdivision are effective beginning January 1, 2019.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4961.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">System tag.</span></h2>
          <p>All radon mitigation systems installed in Minnesota on or after January 1, 2019, must have a radon mitigation system tag provided by the commissioner. A radon mitigation professional must attach the tag to the radon mitigation system in a visible location.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4961.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">License required annually.</span></h2>
          <p>Effective January 1, 2019, a license is required annually for every person, firm, or corporation that performs a service for compensation to detect the presence of radon in the indoor atmosphere, performs laboratory analysis, or performs a service to mitigate radon in the indoor atmosphere.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4961.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Exemptions.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not apply to:</p>
          <p>(1) employees of a firm or corporation that installs radon control systems in newly constructed Minnesota homes as specified in subdivision 11;</p>
          <p>(2) a person authorized as a building official under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/1300.0070">1300.0070</a>, or that person's designee; or</p>
          <p>(3) any person, firm, corporation, or entity that distributes radon testing devices or information for general educational purposes.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4961.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">License applications and other reports.</span></h2>
          <p>The professionals, companies, and laboratories listed in subdivision 8 must submit applications for licenses, system tags, and any other reporting required under this section and Minnesota Rules on forms prescribed by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4961.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Licensing fees.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) All radon license applications submitted to the commissioner of health must be accompanied by the required fees. If the commissioner determines that insufficient fees were paid, the necessary additional fees must be paid before the commissioner approves the application. The commissioner shall charge the following fees for each radon license:</p>
          <p>(1) Each measurement professional license, $150 per year. "Measurement professional" means any person who performs a test to determine the presence and concentration of radon in a building the person does not own or lease.</p>
          <p>(2) Each mitigation professional license, $250 per year. "Mitigation professional" means an individual who installs or designs a radon mitigation system in a building the individual does not own or lease, or provides on-site supervision of radon mitigation and mitigation technicians. "On-site supervision" means a review at the property of mitigation work upon completion of the work and attachment of a system tag. Employees or subcontractors who are supervised by a licensed mitigation professional are not required to be licensed under this clause. This license also permits the licensee to perform the activities of a measurement professional described in clause (1).</p>
          <p>(3) Each mitigation company license, $100 per year. "Mitigation company" means any business or government entity that performs or authorizes employees to perform radon mitigation. This fee is waived if the mitigation company employs only one licensed mitigation professional.</p>
          <p>(4) Each radon analysis laboratory license, $500 per year. "Radon analysis laboratory" means a business entity or government entity that analyzes passive radon detection devices to determine the presence and concentration of radon in the devices. This fee is waived if the laboratory is a government entity and is only distributing test kits for the general public to use in Minnesota.</p>
          <p>(5) Each Minnesota Department of Health radon mitigation system tag, $75 per tag. "Minnesota Department of Health radon mitigation system tag" or "system tag" means a unique identifiable radon system label provided by the commissioner of health.</p>
          <p>(b) Fees collected under this section shall be deposited in the state treasury and credited to the state government special revenue fund.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4961.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Enforcement.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall enforce this section under the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.989">144.989</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.993">144.993</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4961.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Local inspections or permits.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not preclude local units of government from requiring additional permits or inspections for radon control systems, and does not supersede any local inspection or permit requirements.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.4961.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Application; newly constructed homes.</span></h2>
          <p>This section does not apply to newly constructed Minnesota homes according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/326B.106#stat.326B.106.6">326B.106, subdivision 6</a>, prior to the issuance of a certificate of occupancy.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.4961.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.8.24.0">2015 c 71 art 8 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/189/#laws.20.9.0">2016 c 189 art 20 s 9</a>-15; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2017/1/6/#laws.10.63.0">1Sp2017 c 6 art 10 s 63</a>-65</p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.497"><b>144.497</b> MS 2022 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.59.57.0">2024 c 127 art 59 s 57</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">HOSPITALS AND OTHER HEALTH CARE INSTITUTIONS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.50">
        <h1 class="shn">144.50 HOSPITALS, LICENSES; DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.50.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">License required.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) No person, partnership, association, or corporation, nor any state, county, or local governmental units, nor any division, department, board, or agency thereof, shall establish, operate, conduct, or maintain in the state any hospital, sanitarium or other institution for the hospitalization or care of human beings without first obtaining a license therefor in the manner provided in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a>. No person or entity shall advertise a facility providing services required to be licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a> without first obtaining a license.</p>
          <p>(b) A violation of this subdivision is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not more than $300. The commissioner may seek an injunction in the district court against the continuing operation of the unlicensed institution. Proceedings for securing an injunction may be brought by the attorney general or by the appropriate county attorney.</p>
          <p>(c) The sanctions in this subdivision do not restrict other available sanctions.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.50.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Hospital, sanitarium, other institution; definition.</span></h2>
          <p>Hospital, sanitarium or other institution for the hospitalization or care of human beings, within the meaning of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a> shall mean any institution, place, building, or agency, in which any accommodation is maintained, furnished, or offered for five or more persons for: the hospitalization of the sick or injured; the provision of care in a swing bed authorized under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.562">144.562</a>; elective outpatient surgery for preexamined, prediagnosed low risk patients; emergency medical services offered 24 hours a day, seven days a week, in an ambulatory or outpatient setting in a facility not a part of a licensed hospital; or the institutional care of human beings. Nothing in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a> shall apply to a clinic; a physician's, advanced practice registered nurse's, or physician assistant's office; or to hotels or other similar places that furnish only board and room, or either, to their guests.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.50.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Hospitalization.</span></h2>
          <p>"Hospitalization" means the reception and care of persons for a continuous period longer than 24 hours, for the purpose of diagnosis or treatment bearing on the physical or mental health of such persons.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.50.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1980/0/357/#laws.0.22.0">1980 c 357 s 22</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.50.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Separate licensing for healing; medicine.</span></h2>
          <p>Nothing in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a> shall authorize any person, partnership, association, or corporation, nor any state, county, or local governmental units, nor any division, department, board, or agency thereof, to engage, in any manner, in the practice of healing, or the practice of medicine, as defined by law.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.50.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Supervised living facility licenses.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner may license as a supervised living facility a facility seeking medical assistance certification as an intermediate care facility for persons with developmental disability for four or more persons as authorized under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/252.291">252.291</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) Class B supervised living facilities shall be classified as follows for purposes of the State Building Code:</p>
          <p>(1) Class B supervised living facilities for six or less persons must meet Group R, Division 3, occupancy requirements; and</p>
          <p>(2) Class B supervised living facilities for seven to 16 persons must meet Group R, Division 1, occupancy requirements.</p>
          <p>(c) Class B facilities classified under paragraph (b), clauses (1) and (2), must meet the fire protection provisions of chapter 21 of the 1985 Life Safety Code, NFPA 101, for facilities housing persons with impractical evacuation capabilities, except that Class B facilities licensed prior to July 1, 1990, need only continue to meet institutional fire safety provisions. Class B supervised living facilities shall provide the necessary physical plant accommodations to meet the needs and functional disabilities of the residents. For Class B supervised living facilities licensed after July 1, 1990, and housing nonambulatory or nonmobile persons, the corridor access to bedrooms, common spaces, and other resident use spaces must be at least five feet in clear width, except that a waiver may be requested in accordance with Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4665.0600">4665.0600</a>.</p>
          <p>(d) The commissioner may license as a Class A supervised living facility a residential program for individuals with substance use disorder that allows children to reside with the parent receiving treatment in the facility. The licensee of the program shall be responsible for the health, safety, and welfare of the children residing in the facility. The facility in which the program is located must be provided with a sprinkler system approved by the state fire marshal. The licensee shall also provide additional space and physical plant accommodations appropriate for the number and age of children residing in the facility. For purposes of license capacity, each child residing in the facility shall be considered to be a resident.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.50.6a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6a.<span class="headnote">Supervised living facility; tuberculosis prevention and control.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A supervised living facility must establish and maintain a comprehensive tuberculosis infection control program according to the most current tuberculosis infection control guidelines issued by the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Division of Tuberculosis Elimination, as published in CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR). This program must include a tuberculosis infection control plan that covers all paid and unpaid employees, contractors, students, and volunteers. The Department of Health shall provide technical assistance regarding implementation of the guidelines.</p>
          <p>(b) Written compliance with this subdivision must be maintained by the supervised living facility.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.50.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Residents with AIDS or hepatitis.</span></h2>
          <p>Boarding care homes and supervised living facilities licensed by the commissioner of health must accept as a resident a person who is infected with the human immunodeficiency virus or the hepatitis B virus unless the facility cannot meet the needs of the person under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4665.0200">4665.0200</a>, subpart 5, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4655.1500">4655.1500</a>, subpart 2, or the person is otherwise not eligible for admission to the facility under state laws or rules.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.50.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1941/0/549/#laws.0.1.0">1941 c 549 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1943/0/649/#laws.0.1.0">1943 c 649 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1951/0/304/#laws.0.1.0">1951 c 304 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1969/0/358/#laws.0.1.0">1969 c 358 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/173/#laws.0.34.0">1976 c 173 s 34</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/218/#laws.0.1.0">1977 c 218 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/95/#laws.0.1.0">1981 c 95 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/1/3/#laws.0.2.0">1Sp1985 c 3 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/209/#laws.0.20.0">1987 c 209 s 20</a>,21; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/689/#laws.2.32.0">1988 c 689 art 2 s 32</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/282/#laws.2.8.0">1989 c 282 art 2 s 8</a>; art 3 s 4; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/568/#laws.3.3.0">1990 c 568 art 3 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/286/#laws.0.3.0">1991 c 286 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1992/0/513/#laws.6.4.0">1992 c 513 art 6 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/56/#laws.0.1.0">2005 c 56 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/43/#laws.0.5.0">2013 c 43 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.4.34.0">2020 c 115 art 4 s 34</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/58/#laws.0.40.0">2022 c 58 s 40</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/98/#laws.4.51.0">2022 c 98 art 4 s 51</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.51">
        <h1 class="shn">144.51 LICENSE APPLICATIONS.</h1>
        <p>Before a license shall be issued under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a>, the person applying shall submit evidence satisfactory to the state commissioner of health that the person is not less than 18 years of age and of reputable and responsible character; in the event the applicant is an association or corporation or governmental unit like evidence shall be submitted as to the members thereof and the persons in charge. All applicants shall, in addition, submit satisfactory evidence of their ability to comply with the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a> and all rules and minimum standards adopted thereunder.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.51.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1941/0/549/#laws.0.2.0">1941 c 549 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1943/0/649/#laws.0.2.0">1943 c 649 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1951/0/304/#laws.0.2.0">1951 c 304 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/725/#laws.0.7.0">1973 c 725 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/173/#laws.0.35.0">1976 c 173 s 35</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.52">
        <h1 class="shn">144.52 APPLICATION.</h1>
        <p>Any person, partnership, association, or corporation, including state, county, or local governmental units, or any division, department, board, or agency thereof, desiring a license under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a> shall file with the state commissioner of health a verified application containing the name of the applicant desiring said license; whether such persons so applying are 18 years of age; the type of institution to be operated; the location thereof; the name of the person in charge thereof, and such other information pertinent thereto as the state commissioner of health by rule may require. Application on behalf of a corporation or association or other governmental unit shall be made by any two officers thereof or by its managing agents.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.52.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1941/0/549/#laws.0.3.0">1941 c 549 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1943/0/649/#laws.0.3.0">1943 c 649 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1951/0/304/#laws.0.3.0">1951 c 304 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/725/#laws.0.8.0">1973 c 725 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.53">
        <h1 class="shn">144.53 FEES.</h1>
        <p>Each application for a license, or renewal thereof, to operate a hospital, sanitarium or other institution for the hospitalization or care of human beings, within the meaning of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a>, except applications by the Minnesota Veterans Home, the commissioner of human services for the licensing of state institutions or by the administrator for the licensing of the University of Minnesota hospitals, shall be accompanied by a fee to be prescribed by the state commissioner of health pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.122">144.122</a>. No fee shall be refunded. Licenses shall expire and shall be renewed as prescribed by the commissioner of health pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.122">144.122</a>.</p>
        <p>No license granted hereunder shall be assignable or transferable.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.53.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1941/0/549/#laws.0.4.0">1941 c 549 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1945/0/192/#laws.0.1.0">1945 c 192 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1951/0/304/#laws.0.4.0">1951 c 304 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/466/#laws.0.1.0">1959 c 466 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/471/#laws.0.3.0">1974 c 471 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/63/#laws.0.1.0">1975 c 63 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1975/0/310/#laws.0.5.0">1975 c 310 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/173/#laws.0.36.0">1976 c 173 s 36</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/239/#laws.0.69.0">1976 c 239 s 69</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/654/#laws.5.58.0">1984 c 654 art 5 s 58</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.54">
        <h1 class="shn">144.54 INSPECTIONS.</h1>
        <p>Every building, institution, or establishment for which a license has been issued shall be periodically inspected by a duly appointed representative of the state commissioner of health under the rules to be established by the state commissioner of health. No institution of any kind licensed pursuant to the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a> shall be required to be licensed or inspected under the laws of this state relating to hotels, restaurants, lodging houses, boarding houses, and places of refreshment.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.54.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1941/0/549/#laws.0.5.0">1941 c 549 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1951/0/304/#laws.0.5.0">1951 c 304 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.55">
        <h1 class="shn">144.55 LICENSES; ISSUANCE, SUSPENSION AND REVOCATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.55.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Issuance.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The state commissioner of health is hereby authorized to issue licenses to operate hospitals, sanitariums, outpatient surgical centers, or other institutions for the hospitalization or care of human beings, which are found to comply with the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a> and any reasonable rules promulgated by the commissioner. The commissioner shall not require an outpatient surgical center licensed as part of a hospital to obtain a separate outpatient surgical center license. All decisions of the commissioner thereunder may be reviewed in the district court in the county in which the institution is located or contemplated.</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioner may issue a conditional license to operate an outpatient surgical center if:</p>
          <p>(1) the applicant is seeking a license to operate an outpatient surgical center that will share a facility with an existing licensed outpatient surgical center that is also federally certified under Medicare as an ambulatory surgical center; and</p>
          <p>(2) the outpatient surgical center otherwise meets the requirements for licensure under this subdivision.</p>
          <p class="bl">A conditional license issued under this paragraph is valid for 120 days and may be renewed once for an additional 120 days. The commissioner shall convert a valid conditional license to a nonconditional license if the licensee can demonstrate to the commissioner that the conditionally licensed outpatient surgical center is federally certified under Medicare as an ambulatory surgical center.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.55.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">License fee.</span></h2>
          <p>The annual license fee for outpatient surgical centers is $1,512.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.55.1b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.<span class="headnote">Standards for nursing care.</span></h2>
          <p>As a condition of licensure, outpatient surgical centers must provide nursing care consistent with nationally accepted nursing clinical standards for perioperative nursing, including, but not limited to Association of Operating Room Nurses and American Nurses Association standards, which are generally accepted in the professional nursing community.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.55.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For the purposes of this section, the terms in this subdivision have the meanings given them.</p>
          <p>(b) "Outpatient surgical center" or "center" means a facility organized for the specific purpose of providing elective outpatient surgery for preexamined, prediagnosed, low-risk patients. An outpatient surgical center is not organized to provide regular emergency medical services and does not include a physician's, advanced practice registered nurse's, physician assistant's, or dentist's office or clinic for the practice of medicine, the practice of dentistry, or the delivery of primary care.</p>
          <p>(c) "Approved accrediting organization" means any organization recognized as an accreditation organization by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.55.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Standards for licensure.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Notwithstanding the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a>, for the purpose of hospital licensure, the commissioner of health shall use as minimum standards the hospital certification regulations promulgated pursuant to title XVIII of the Social Security Act, United States Code, title 42, section 1395, et seq. The commissioner may use as minimum standards changes in the federal hospital certification regulations promulgated after May 7, 1981, if the commissioner finds that such changes are reasonably necessary to protect public health and safety.</p>
          <p>(b) Hospitals must meet the applicable provisions of the 2022 edition of the Facility Guidelines Institute <i>Guidelines for Design and Construction of Hospitals</i>. This minimum design standard must be met for all new licenses, new construction, change of use, or change of occupancy for which plan review packages are received on or after January 1, 2024. For the purposes of this subdivision, "Facility Guidelines Institute <i>Guidelines for Design and Construction of Hospitals </i>" does not include any appendices to the guidelines.</p>
          <p>(c) The commissioner shall review each new edition of the guidelines to determine if they will be updated. If the commissioner decides to update the edition of the guidelines specified in paragraph (b) for purposes of this subdivision, the commissioner must notify the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over health care and public safety of the planned update by January 15 of the year in which the new edition will become effective. Following notice from the commissioner, the new edition shall become effective for hospitals beginning August 1 of that year, unless otherwise provided in law. The commissioner shall, by publication in the State Register, specify a date by which hospitals must comply with the updated edition. The date by which hospitals must comply shall not be sooner than 12 months after publication of the commissioner's notice in the State Register and applies only to plan review submissions received on or after that date.</p>
          <p>(d) Hospitals shall be in compliance with all applicable state and local governing laws, regulations, standards, ordinances, and codes for fire safety, building, and zoning requirements. The commissioner shall develop guidance to outline how the commissioner will resolve conflicts between the guidelines and other applicable state and local governing laws, regulations, standards, ordinances, and codes for fire safety, building, and zoning. Guidance must be made publicly available at the time a new edition of the guidelines becomes effective and shall be periodically updated.</p>
          <p>(e) Each hospital and outpatient surgical center shall establish policies and procedures to prevent the transmission of human immunodeficiency virus and hepatitis B virus to patients and within the health care setting. The policies and procedures shall be developed in conformance with the most recent recommendations issued by the United States Department of Health and Human Services, Public Health Service, Centers for Disease Control. The commissioner of health shall evaluate a hospital's compliance with the policies and procedures according to subdivision 4.</p>
          <p>(f) An outpatient surgical center must establish and maintain a comprehensive tuberculosis infection control program according to the most current tuberculosis infection control guidelines issued by the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Division of Tuberculosis Elimination, as published in CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR). This program must include a tuberculosis infection control plan that covers all paid and unpaid employees, contractors, students, and volunteers. The Department of Health shall provide technical assistance regarding implementation of the guidelines.</p>
          <p>(g) Written compliance with this subdivision must be maintained by the outpatient surgical center.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.55.3a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Standards for admission; outpatient surgical centers.</span></h2>
          <p>Admissions to outpatient surgical centers are limited to procedures that utilize general anesthesia or conscious sedation and that do not require overnight inpatient care.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.55.3b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3b.<span class="headnote">Facility standards for outpatient surgical centers.</span></h2>
          <p>An outpatient surgical center must be a freestanding facility unless:</p>
          <p>(1) the outpatient surgical center is licensed as part of a hospital;</p>
          <p>(2) the licensed outpatient surgical center is federally certified under Medicare as an ambulatory surgical center and shares a facility only with other licensed outpatient surgical centers federally certified under Medicare as ambulatory surgical centers; or</p>
          <p>(3) the outpatient surgical center is conditionally licensed under subdivision 1, paragraph (b), and shares a facility only with other licensed outpatient surgical centers federally certified under Medicare as ambulatory surgical centers.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.55.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Routine inspections; presumption.</span></h2>
          <p>Any hospital surveyed and accredited under the standards of the hospital accreditation program of an approved accrediting organization that submits to the commissioner within a reasonable time copies of (a) its currently valid accreditation certificate and accreditation letter, together with accompanying recommendations and comments and (b) any further recommendations, progress reports and correspondence directly related to the accreditation is presumed to comply with application requirements of subdivision 1 and the standards requirements of subdivision 3 and no further routine inspections or accreditation information shall be required by the commissioner to determine compliance. Notwithstanding the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.54">144.54 </a>and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.653">144.653</a>, subdivisions 2 and 4, hospitals shall be inspected only as provided in this section. The provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.653">144.653</a> relating to the assessment and collection of fines shall not apply to any hospital. The commissioner of health shall annually conduct, with notice, validation inspections of a selected sample of the number of hospitals accredited by an approved accrediting organization, not to exceed ten percent of accredited hospitals, for the purpose of determining compliance with the provisions of subdivision 3. If a validation survey discloses a failure to comply with subdivision 3, the provisions of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.653">144.653 </a>relating to correction orders, reinspections, and notices of noncompliance shall apply. The commissioner shall also conduct any inspection necessary to determine whether hospital construction, addition, or remodeling projects comply with standards for construction promulgated in rules pursuant to subdivision 3. The commissioner may also conduct inspections to determine whether a hospital or hospital corporate system continues to satisfy the conditions on which a hospital construction moratorium exception was granted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.551#stat.144.551.1a">144.551, subdivision 1a</a>. Pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.653">144.653</a>, the commissioner shall inspect any hospital that does not have a currently valid hospital accreditation certificate from an approved accrediting organization. Nothing in this subdivision shall be construed to limit the investigative powers of the Office of Health Facility Complaints as established in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.51">144A.51</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.54">144A.54</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.55.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Coordination of inspections.</span></h2>
          <p>Prior to conducting routine inspections of hospitals and outpatient surgical centers, a state agency shall notify the commissioner of its intention to inspect. The commissioner shall then determine whether the inspection is necessary in light of any previous inspections conducted by the commissioner, any other state agency, or an approved accrediting organization. The commissioner shall notify the agency of the determination and may authorize the agency to conduct the inspection. No state agency may routinely inspect any hospital without the authorization of the commissioner. The commissioner shall coordinate, insofar as is possible, routine inspections conducted by state agencies, so as to minimize the number of inspections to which hospitals are subject.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.55.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Suspension, revocation, and refusal to renew.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner may refuse to grant or renew, or may suspend or revoke, a license on any of the following grounds:</p>
          <p>(1) violation of any of the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a> or the rules or standards issued pursuant thereto, or Minnesota Rules, chapters 4650 and 4675;</p>
          <p>(2) permitting, aiding, or abetting the commission of any illegal act in the institution;</p>
          <p>(3) conduct or practices detrimental to the welfare of the patient; or</p>
          <p>(4) obtaining or attempting to obtain a license by fraud or misrepresentation; or</p>
          <p>(5) with respect to hospitals and outpatient surgical centers, if the commissioner determines that there is a pattern of conduct that one or more physicians, advanced practice registered nurses, or physician assistants who have a "financial or economic interest," as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.6521#stat.144.6521.3">144.6521, subdivision 3</a>, in the hospital or outpatient surgical center, have not provided the notice and disclosure of the financial or economic interest required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.6521">144.6521</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioner shall not renew a license for a boarding care bed in a resident room with more than four beds.</p>
          <p>(c) The commissioner shall not renew licenses for hospital beds issued to a hospital or hospital corporate system pursuant to a hospital construction moratorium exception under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.551#stat.144.551.1a">144.551, subdivision 1a</a>, if the commissioner determines the hospital or hospital corporate system is not satisfying the conditions on which the exception was granted.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.55.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Hearing.</span></h2>
          <p>Prior to any suspension, revocation or refusal to renew a license, the licensee shall be entitled to notice and a hearing as provided by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.57">14.57</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.69">14.69</a>. At each hearing, the commissioner shall have the burden of establishing that a violation described in subdivision 6 has occurred.</p>
          <p>If a license is revoked, suspended, or not renewed, a new application for license may be considered by the commissioner if the conditions upon which revocation, suspension, or refusal to renew was based have been corrected and evidence of this fact has been satisfactorily furnished. A new license may then be granted after proper inspection has been made and all provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a> and any rules promulgated thereunder, or Minnesota Rules, chapters 4650 and 4675, have been complied with and recommendation has been made by the inspector as an agent of the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.55.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Rules.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may promulgate rules necessary to implement the provisions of this section, except that the standards described in subdivision 3 shall constitute the sole minimum quality standards for licensure of hospitals.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.55.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Expiration of licenses.</span></h2>
          <p>All licenses expire on the dates specified on the licenses unless suspended or revoked.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.55.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.</h2>
          <p>MS 2018 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/0/22/#laws.0.6.0">2019 c 22 s 6</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.55.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">State hospitals not affected.</span></h2>
          <p>Subdivisions 3, 4, and 5 do not apply to state hospitals and other facilities operated under the direction of the Direct Care and Treatment executive board.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

			">
