          <p>The commissioner must notify the applicant in writing of the decision. If a variance or waiver is granted, the notification must specify the period of time for which the variance or waiver is effective and the alternative measures or conditions, if any, to be met by the applicant.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.6535.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Effect of alternative measures or conditions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Alternative measures or conditions attached to a variance or waiver have the same force and effect as the requirement under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.55#stat.144.55.3">144.55, subdivision 3</a>, paragraph (b), and are subject to the issuance of correction orders and penalty assessments in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.55">144.55</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) Fines for a violation of this section shall be in the same amount as that specified for the particular requirement for which the variance or waiver was requested.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.6535.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Renewal.</span></h2>
          <p>A request for renewal of a variance or waiver must be submitted in writing at least 45 days before its expiration date. Renewal requests must contain the information specified in subdivision 1. A variance or waiver must be renewed by the commissioner if the applicant continues to satisfy the criteria in subdivision 2 and the alternative measures or conditions, if any, specified under subdivision 3 and demonstrates compliance with the alternative measures or conditions imposed at the time the original variance or waiver was granted.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.6535.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Denial, revocation, or refusal to renew.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner must deny, revoke, or refuse to renew a variance or waiver if it is determined that the criteria in subdivision 2 or the alternative measures or conditions, if any, specified under subdivision 3 are not met. The applicant must be notified in writing of the reasons for the decision and informed of the right to appeal the decision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.6535.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Appeal procedure.</span></h2>
          <p>An applicant may contest the denial, revocation, or refusal to renew a variance or waiver by requesting a contested case hearing under chapter 14. The applicant must submit, within 15 days of the receipt of the commissioner's decision, a written request for a hearing. The request for hearing must set forth in detail the reasons why the applicant contends the decision of the commissioner should be reversed or modified. At the hearing, the applicant has the burden of proving that it satisfied the criteria specified in subdivision 2 or the alternative measures or conditions, if any, specified under subdivision 3, except in a proceeding challenging the revocation of a variance or waiver.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.6535.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/29/#laws.0.1.0">2001 c 29 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.3.16.0">2023 c 70 art 3 s 16</a>-18</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.654">
        <h1 class="shn">144.654 EXPERTS MAY BE EMPLOYED.</h1>
        <p>The state commissioner of health may employ experts in the field of health care to assist the staffs of facilities required to be licensed under the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.58">144.58</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.02">144A.02</a>, in programming and providing adequate care of the patients and residents of the facility. Alternate methods of care for patients and residents of the facilities shall be researched by the state commissioner of health using the knowledge and experience of experts employed therefor.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.654.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/688/#laws.0.4.0">1973 c 688 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/173/#laws.0.43.0">1976 c 173 s 43</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.655">
        <h1 class="shn">144.655 PROGRAM FOR VOLUNTARY MEDICAL AID.</h1>
        <p>Licensed physicians may visit a facility required to be licensed under the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.58">144.58</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.02">144A.02</a>, and examine patients and residents thereof under a program which shall be established by the state commissioner of health and regulated and governed by rules promulgated by the state commissioner of health pursuant to the Administrative Procedure Act. The rules shall protect the privacy of patients and residents of facilities. No patient or resident of any facility shall be required to submit to an examination under the program. The state commissioner of health shall consult with medical schools and other experts for the purpose of establishing the program. The state commissioner of health shall encourage the active participation of all licensed physicians on a voluntary basis in the program.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.655.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/688/#laws.0.5.0">1973 c 688 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/173/#laws.0.44.0">1976 c 173 s 44</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.656">
        <h1 class="shn">144.656 EMPLOYEES TO BE COMPENSATED.</h1>
        <p>All employees of facilities required to be licensed under the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.58">144.58</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.02">144A.02</a>, participating in orientation programs or in in-service training provided by the facility shall be compensated therefor at their regular rate of pay, provided, however, that this section will be effective only to the extent that facilities are reimbursed for the compensation by the commissioner of human services in the proportion of welfare to total residents and patients in the facility.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.656.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/688/#laws.0.6.0">1973 c 688 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/173/#laws.0.45.0">1976 c 173 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/654/#laws.5.58.0">1984 c 654 art 5 s 58</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.657">
        <h1 class="shn">144.657 VOLUNTEER EFFORTS ENCOURAGED.</h1>
        <p>The state commissioner of health, through the dissemination of information to appropriate organizations, shall encourage citizens to promote improved care in facilities required to be licensed under the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.58">144.58</a>, or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144A.02">144A.02</a>, throughout the state.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.657.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/688/#laws.0.7.0">1973 c 688 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/173/#laws.0.46.0">1976 c 173 s 46</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">EPIDEMIOLOGICAL DATA</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.658">
        <h1 class="shn">144.658 EPIDEMIOLOGIC DATA DISCOVERY.</h1>
        <p>Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, health data on an individual collected by public health officials conducting an epidemiologic investigation to reduce morbidity or mortality is not subject to discovery in a legal action.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.658.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/298/#laws.0.41.0">1985 c 298 s 41</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.6581">
        <h1 class="shn">144.6581 DETERMINATION OF WHETHER DATA IDENTIFIES INDIVIDUALS.</h1>
        <p>The commissioner of health may: (1) withhold access to health or epidemiologic data if the commissioner determines the data are data on an individual, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.5">13.02, subdivision 5</a>; or (2) grant access to health or epidemiologic data, if the commissioner determines the data are summary data as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.19">13.02, subdivision 19</a>. In the exercise of this discretion, the commissioner shall consider whether the data requested, alone or in combination, may constitute information from which an individual subject of data may be identified using epidemiologic methods. In making this determination, the commissioner shall consider disease incidence, associated risk factors for illness, and similar factors unique to the data by which it could be linked to a specific subject of the data. This discretion is limited to health or epidemiologic data maintained by the commissioner of health or a community health board, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145A.02">145A.02</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.6581.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/351/#laws.0.26.0">1993 c 351 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.7.28.0">2014 c 291 art 7 s 28</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">HEALTH CARE PROVIDERS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.6585">
        <h1 class="shn">144.6585 IDENTIFICATION OF HEALTH CARE PROVIDERS.</h1>
        <p>Any health care provider who is licensed, credentialed, or registered by a health-related licensing board as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.01#stat.214.01.2">214.01, subdivision 2</a>, must wear a name tag that indicates by words, letters, abbreviations, or insignia the profession or occupation of the individual. The name tag must be worn whenever the health care provider is rendering health services to a patient, unless wearing the name tag would create a safety or health risk to the patient. The failure to wear a name tag is not reportable under chapter 214.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.6585.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/237/#laws.0.15.0">1997 c 237 s 15</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">SEXUAL ASSAULT VICTIMS RIGHTS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.6586">
        <h1 class="shn">144.6586 NOTICE OF RIGHTS TO SEXUAL ASSAULT VICTIM.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.6586.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Notice required.</span></h2>
          <p>A hospital shall give a written notice about victim rights and available resources to a person seeking medical services in the hospital who reports to hospital staff or presents evidence of a sexual assault or other unwanted sexual contact or sexual penetration. The hospital shall make a good faith effort to provide this notice prior to medical treatment or the examination performed for the purpose of gathering evidence, subject to applicable federal and state laws and regulations regarding the provision of medical care, and in a manner that does not interfere with any medical screening examination or initiation of treatment necessary to stabilize a victim's emergency medical condition.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.6586.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Contents of notice.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioners of health and public safety, in consultation with sexual assault victim advocates and health care professionals, shall develop the notice required by subdivision 1. The notice must inform the victim, at a minimum, of:</p>
          <p>(1) the obligation under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/609.35">609.35</a> of the state to pay for the examination performed for the purpose of gathering evidence, that payment is not contingent on the victim reporting the criminal sexual conduct to law enforcement, and that the victim may incur expenses for treatment of injuries;</p>
          <p>(2) the victim's rights if the crime is reported to law enforcement, including the victim's right to apply for reimbursement under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/611A.51">611A.51</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/611A.68">611A.68</a>, information on how to apply for reimbursement, and information on how to obtain an order for protection or a harassment restraining order; and</p>
          <p>(3) the opportunity under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/611A.27">611A.27</a> to obtain status information about an unrestricted sexual assault examination kit, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/299C.106#stat.299C.106.1">299C.106, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (h).</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.6586.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2014/0/291/#laws.6.12.0">2014 c 291 art 6 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2018/0/160/#laws.0.1.0">2018 c 160 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/52/#laws.5.1.0">2023 c 52 art 5 s 1</a>,79</p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.659"><b>144.659</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/419/#laws.0.2.0">1982 c 419 s 2</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.66"><b>144.66</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/403/#laws.2.164.0">1987 c 403 art 2 s 164</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">TRAUMATIC BRAIN AND SPINAL CORD INJURIES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.661">
        <h1 class="shn">144.661 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.661.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.661">144.661</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.665">144.665</a>, the following terms have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.661.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Traumatic brain injury.</span></h2>
          <p>"Traumatic brain injury" means a sudden insult or damage to the brain or its coverings caused by an external physical force which may produce a diminished or altered state of consciousness and which results in the following disabilities:</p>
          <p>(1) impairment of cognitive or mental abilities;</p>
          <p>(2) impairment of physical functioning; or</p>
          <p>(3) disturbance of behavioral or emotional functioning.</p>
          <p class="bl">These disabilities may be temporary or permanent and may result in partial or total loss of function. "Traumatic brain injury" does not include injuries of a degenerative or congenital nature.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.661.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Spinal cord injury.</span></h2>
          <p>"Spinal cord injury" means an injury that occurs as a result of trauma which may involve spinal vertebral fracture and where the injured person suffers an acute, traumatic lesion of neural elements in the spinal canal, resulting in any degree of temporary or permanent sensory deficit, motor deficit, or bladder or bowel dysfunction. "Spinal cord injury" does not include intervertebral disc disease.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.661.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/292/#laws.2.5.0">1991 c 292 art 2 s 5</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.662">
        <h1 class="shn">144.662 TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY AND SPINAL CORD INJURY REGISTRY.</h1>
        <p>The commissioner of health shall establish and maintain a central registry of persons who sustain traumatic brain injury or spinal cord injury. The purpose of the registry is to:</p>
        <p>(1) collect information to facilitate the development of injury prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation programs; and</p>
        <p>(2) ensure the provision to persons with traumatic brain injury or spinal cord injury of information regarding appropriate public or private agencies that provide rehabilitative services so that injured persons may obtain needed services to alleviate injuries and avoid secondary problems, such as mental illness and substance use disorder.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.662.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/292/#laws.2.6.0">1991 c 292 art 2 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/98/#laws.4.51.0">2022 c 98 art 4 s 51</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.663">
        <h1 class="shn">144.663 DUTY TO REPORT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.663.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Establishment of reporting system.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall design and establish a reporting system which designates either the treating hospital, medical facility, or physician to report to the department within a reasonable period of time after the identification of a person with traumatic brain injury or spinal cord injury. The consent of the injured person is not required.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.663.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Information.</span></h2>
          <p>The report must be submitted on forms provided by the department and must include the following information:</p>
          <p>(1) the name, age, and residence of the injured person;</p>
          <p>(2) the date and cause of the injury;</p>
          <p>(3) the initial diagnosis; and</p>
          <p>(4) other information required by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.663.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Reporting without liability.</span></h2>
          <p>The furnishing of information required by the commissioner shall not subject any person or facility required to report to any action for damages or other relief, provided that the person or facility is acting in good faith.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.663.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/292/#laws.2.7.0">1991 c 292 art 2 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.664">
        <h1 class="shn">144.664 DUTIES OF COMMISSIONER.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.664.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Studies.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall collect injury incidence information, analyze the information, and conduct special studies regarding traumatic brain injury and spinal cord injury.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.664.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Provision of data.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall provide summary registry data to public and private entities to conduct studies using data collected by the registry. The commissioner may charge a fee under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.03#stat.13.03.3">13.03, subdivision 3</a>, for all out-of-pocket expenses associated with the provision of data or data analysis.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.664.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Notification.</span></h2>
          <p>Within five days of receiving a report of traumatic brain injury or spinal cord injury, the commissioner shall notify the injured person or the injured person's family of resources and services available in Minnesota, pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.662">144.662</a>, clause (2).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.664.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/86/#laws.2.6.0">1999 c 86 art 2 s 6</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.664.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Rules.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall adopt rules to administer the registry, collect information, and distribute data. The rules must include, but are not limited to, the following:</p>
          <p>(1) the specific ICD-9 procedure codes included in the definitions of "traumatic brain injury" and "spinal cord injury";</p>
          <p>(2) the type of data to be reported;</p>
          <p>(3) standards for reporting specific types of data;</p>
          <p>(4) the persons and facilities required to report and the time period in which reports must be submitted;</p>
          <p>(5) criteria relating to the use of registry data by public and private entities engaged in research; and</p>
          <p>(6) specification of fees to be charged under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.03#stat.13.03.3">13.03, subdivision 3</a>, for out-of-pocket expenses.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.664.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/292/#laws.2.8.0">1991 c 292 art 2 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/483/#laws.0.1.0">1994 c 483 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/205/#laws.0.22.0">1997 c 205 s 22</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.665">
        <h1 class="shn">144.665 TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY AND SPINAL CORD INJURY DATA.</h1>
        <p>Data on individuals collected by the commissioner of health under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.662">144.662</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.664">144.664</a> are private data on individuals as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.12">13.02, subdivision 12</a>, and may be used only for the purposes set forth in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.662">144.662</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.664">144.664</a> in accordance with the rules adopted by the commissioner.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.665.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/292/#laws.2.9.0">1991 c 292 art 2 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/483/#laws.0.1.0">1994 c 483 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/205/#laws.0.23.0">1997 c 205 s 23</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.67"><b>144.67</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/403/#laws.2.164.0">1987 c 403 art 2 s 164</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">CANCER REPORTING SYSTEM</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.671">
        <h1 class="shn">144.671 CANCER REPORTING SYSTEM; PURPOSE.</h1>
        <p>The commissioner of health shall establish a statewide population-based cancer reporting system. The purpose of this system is to:</p>
        <p>(1) monitor incidence trends of cancer to detect potential public health problems, predict risks, and assist in investigating cancer clusters;</p>
        <p>(2) more accurately target intervention resources for communities and patients and their families;</p>
        <p>(3) inform health professionals and citizens about risks, early detection, and treatment of cancers known to be elevated in their communities; and</p>
        <p>(4) promote high quality research to provide better information for cancer control and to address public concerns and questions about cancer.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.671.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/403/#laws.2.9.0">1987 c 403 art 2 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.4.112.0">2023 c 70 art 4 s 112</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.672">
        <h1 class="shn">144.672 DUTIES OF COMMISSIONER; RULES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.672.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Rule authority.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall collect cancer incidence information, analyze the information, and conduct special studies designed to determine the potential public health significance of an increase in cancer incidence.</p>
          <p>The commissioner shall adopt rules to administer the system, collect information, and distribute data. The rules must include, but not be limited to, the following:</p>
          <p>(1) the type of data to be reported;</p>
          <p>(2) standards for reporting specific types of data;</p>
          <p>(3) payments allowed to hospitals, pathologists, and registry systems to defray their costs in providing information to the system;</p>
          <p>(4) criteria relating to contracts made with outside entities to conduct studies using data collected by the system. The criteria may include requirements for a written protocol outlining the purpose and public benefit of the study, the description, methods, and projected results of the study, peer review by other scientists, the methods and facilities to protect the privacy of the data, and the qualifications of the researcher proposing to undertake the study; and</p>
          <p>(5) specification of fees to be charged under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.03#stat.13.03.3">13.03, subdivision 3</a>, for all out-of-pocket expenses for data summaries or specific analyses of data requested by public and private agencies, organizations, and individuals, and which are not otherwise included in the commissioner's annual summary reports. Fees collected are appropriated to the commissioner to offset the cost of providing the data.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.672.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Biennial report required.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall prepare and transmit to the governor and to members of the legislature under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/3.195">3.195</a>, a biennial report on the incidence of cancer in Minnesota and a compilation of summaries and reports from special studies and investigations performed to determine the potential public health significance of an increase in cancer incidence, together with any findings and recommendations. The first report shall be delivered by February 1989, with subsequent reports due in February of each of the following odd-numbered years.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.672.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/403/#laws.2.10.0">1987 c 403 art 2 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/629/#laws.0.37.0">1988 c 629 s 37</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/411/#laws.0.1.0">1994 c 411 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/192/#laws.0.24.0">1997 c 192 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/161/#laws.0.21.0">2001 c 161 s 21</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.68">
        <h1 class="shn">144.68 RECORDS AND REPORTS REQUIRED.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.68.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Person practicing healing arts.</span></h2>
          <p>Every person licensed to practice the healing arts in any form, upon request of the commissioner of health, shall prepare and forward to the commissioner, in the manner and at such times as the commissioner designates, a detailed record of each case of cancer treated or seen by the person professionally.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.68.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Hospitals and similar institutions.</span></h2>
          <p>Every hospital, medical clinic, medical laboratory, or other institution for the hospitalization, clinical or laboratory diagnosis, or care of human beings, upon request of the commissioner of health, shall prepare and forward to the commissioner, in the manner and at the times designated by the commissioner, a detailed record of each case of cancer.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.68.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Reporting without liability.</span></h2>
          <p>The furnishing of the information required under subdivisions 1 and 2 shall not subject the person, hospital, medical clinic, medical laboratory, or other institution furnishing the information, to any action for damages or other relief.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.68.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1949/0/350/#laws.0.3.0">1949 c 350 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/173/#laws.0.47.0">1976 c 173 s 47</a>,48; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/403/#laws.2.11.0">1987 c 403 art 2 s 11</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.69">
        <h1 class="shn">144.69 CLASSIFICATION OF DATA ON INDIVIDUALS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.69.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Data collected by the cancer reporting system.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, including section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.05#stat.13.05.9">13.05, subdivision 9</a>, data collected on individuals by the cancer reporting system, including the names and personal identifiers of persons required in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.68">144.68</a> to report, shall be private and may only be used for the purposes set forth in this section and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.671">144.671</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.672">144.672</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.68">144.68</a>. Any disclosure other than is provided for in this section and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.671">144.671</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.672">144.672</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.68">144.68</a>, is declared to be a misdemeanor and punishable as such. Except as provided by rule, and as part of an epidemiologic investigation, an officer or employee of the commissioner of health may interview patients named in any such report, or relatives of any such patient, only after notifying the attending physician, advanced practice registered nurse, physician assistant, or surgeon. Research protections for patients must be consistent with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.04#stat.13.04.2">13.04, subdivision 2</a>, and Code of Federal Regulations, title 45, part 46.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.69.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Transfers of information to state cancer registries and federal government agencies.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Information containing personal identifiers of a non-Minnesota resident collected by the cancer reporting system may be provided to the statewide cancer registry of the nonresident's home state solely for the purposes consistent with this section and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.671">144.671</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.672">144.672</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.68">144.68</a>, provided that the other state agrees to maintain the classification of the information as provided under subdivision 1.</p>
          <p>(b) Information, excluding direct identifiers such as name, Social Security number, telephone number, and street address, collected by the cancer reporting system may be provided to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's National Program of Cancer Registries and the National Cancer Institute's Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program registry.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.69.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1949/0/350/#laws.0.4.0">1949 c 350 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/403/#laws.2.12.0">1987 c 403 art 2 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.4.47.0">2020 c 115 art 4 s 47</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/58/#laws.0.53.0">2022 c 58 s 53</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.3.19.0">2023 c 70 art 3 s 19</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.6905"><b>144.6905</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/220/#laws.16.3.0">2002 c 220 art 16 s 3</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">GRIEVANCES OR COMPLAINTS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.691">
        <h1 class="shn">144.691 GRIEVANCE PROCEDURES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.691.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Facilities.</span></h2>
          <p>Every hospital licensed as such pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a>, and every outpatient surgery center shall establish a grievance or complaint mechanism designed to process and resolve promptly and effectively grievances by patients or their representatives related to billing, inadequacies of treatment, and other factors which may have an impact on the incidence of malpractice claims and suits.</p>
          <p>For the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.691">144.691</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.693">144.693</a>, "outpatient surgery center" shall mean a free standing facility organized for the specific purpose of providing elective outpatient surgery for preexamined prediagnosed low risk patients. Services provided at an outpatient surgery center shall be limited to surgical procedures which utilize local or general anesthesia and which do not require overnight inpatient care. "Outpatient surgery center" does not mean emergency medical services, or physician or dentist offices.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.691.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Patient notice.</span></h2>
          <p>Each patient receiving treatment at a hospital or an outpatient surgery center shall be notified of the grievance or complaint mechanism which is available to the patient.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.691.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Rules.</span></h2>
          <p>The state commissioner of health shall, by January 1, 1977, establish by rule promulgated pursuant to chapter 15:</p>
          <p>(1) minimum standards and procedural requirements for grievance and complaint mechanism;</p>
          <p>(2) a list of patient complaints which may be processed through a complaint or grievance mechanism;</p>
          <p>(3) the form and manner in which patient notices shall be made; and</p>
          <p>(4) a schedule of fines, not to exceed $200 per offense, for the failure of a hospital or outpatient surgery center to comply with the provisions of this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.691.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/451/#laws.4.71.0">1996 c 451 art 4 s 71</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.691.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/325/#laws.0.8.0">1976 c 325 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/0/311/#laws.0.39.0">1981 c 311 s 39</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/545/#laws.0.24.0">1982 c 545 s 24</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.692"><b>144.692</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/209/#laws.0.40.0">1987 c 209 s 40</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.693"><b>144.693</b> MS 2020 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/7/#laws.3.47.0">1Sp2021 c 7 art 3 s 47</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">HEALTH CARE COST INFORMATION</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.695">
        <h1 class="shn">144.695 CITATION.</h1>
        <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.695">144.695</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.703">144.703</a> may be cited as the "Minnesota Health Care Cost Information Act of 1984."</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.695.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/296/#laws.2.1.0">1976 c 296 art 2 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/534/#laws.0.3.0">1984 c 534 s 3</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.696">
        <h1 class="shn">144.696 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.696.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>Unless the context clearly indicates otherwise, for the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.695">144.695</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.703">144.703</a>, the terms defined in this section have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.696.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Commissioner of health.</span></h2>
          <p>"Commissioner of health" means the state commissioner of health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.696.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Hospital.</span></h2>
          <p>"Hospital" means any acute care institution licensed pursuant to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.58">144.58</a>, but does not include any health care institution conducted for those who rely primarily upon treatment by prayer or spiritual means in accordance with the creed or tenets of any church or denomination.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.696.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Outpatient surgical center.</span></h2>
          <p>"Outpatient surgical center" means a facility other than a hospital offering elective outpatient surgery under a license issued under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.58">144.58</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.696.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/296/#laws.2.2.0">1976 c 296 art 2 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/534/#laws.0.4.0">1984 c 534 s 4</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.697">
        <h1 class="shn">144.697 GENERAL POWERS AND DUTIES OF STATE COMMISSIONER OF HEALTH.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.697.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Contracts.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health may contract with third parties for services necessary to carry out the commissioner's activities where this will promote economy, avoid duplication of effort, and make best use of available expertise.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.697.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Grants; gifts.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health may apply for and receive grants and gifts from any governmental agency, private entity or other person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.697.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Committees.</span></h2>
          <p>To further the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.695">144.695</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.703">144.703</a>, the commissioner of health may create committees from the membership and may appoint ad hoc advisory committees.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.697.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Coordinating rules and inspections.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall coordinate regulation and inspection of hospitals to avoid, to the extent possible, conflicting rules and duplicative inspections.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.697.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/296/#laws.2.3.0">1976 c 296 art 2 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; 1986 c 444</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.698">
        <h1 class="shn">144.698 REPORTING REQUIREMENTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.698.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Yearly reports.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Each hospital and each outpatient surgical center, which has not filed the financial information required by this section with a voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization pursuant to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.702">144.702</a>, shall file annually with the commissioner of health after the close of the fiscal year:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) a balance sheet detailing the assets, liabilities, and net worth of the hospital or outpatient surgical center;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) a detailed statement of income and expenses;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) a copy of its most recent cost report, if any, filed pursuant to requirements of Title XVIII of the United States Social Security Act;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) a copy of all changes to articles of incorporation or bylaws;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) information on services provided to benefit the community, including services provided at no cost or for a reduced fee to patients unable to pay, teaching and research activities, or other community or charitable activities;</p>
          <p class="in">(6) information required on the revenue and expense report form set in effect on July 1, 1989, or as amended by the commissioner in rule;</p>
          <p class="in">(7) information on changes in ownership or control;</p>
          <p class="in">(8) other information required by the commissioner in rule;</p>
          <p class="in">(9) information on the number of available hospital beds that are dedicated to certain specialized services, as designated by the commissioner, and annual occupancy rates for those beds, separately for adult and pediatric care;</p>
          <p class="in">(10) from outpatient surgical centers, the total number of surgeries; and</p>
          <p class="in">(11) a report on health care capital expenditures during the previous year, as required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62J.17">62J.17</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.698.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Separate reports for facilities.</span></h2>
          <p>If more than one licensed hospital or outpatient surgical center is operated by the reporting organization, the commissioner of health may require that the information be reported separately for each hospital and each outpatient surgical center.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.698.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Attestation.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health may require attestation by responsible officials of the hospital or outpatient surgical center that the contents of the reports are true.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.698.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Reports open to public inspection.</span></h2>
          <p>All reports, except privileged medical information, filed pursuant to this section, section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.701">144.701</a> or section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.702#stat.144.702.3">144.702, subdivision 3</a> or 4 shall be open to public inspection.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.698.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Commissioner's right to inspect records.</span></h2>
          <p>If the report is not filed or the commissioner of health has reason to believe the report is incomplete or false, the commissioner shall have the right to inspect hospital and outpatient surgical center books, audits, and records.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.698.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/296/#laws.2.4.0">1976 c 296 art 2 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/534/#laws.0.5.0">1984 c 534 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/282/#laws.2.11.0">1989 c 282 art 2 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/202/#laws.0.7.0">1991 c 202 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/198/#laws.0.13.0">2004 c 198 s 13</a>,14; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.15.13.0">2007 c 147 art 15 s 13</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.6985">
        <h1 class="shn">144.6985 COMMUNITY HEALTH NEEDS ASSESSMENT; COMMUNITY HEALTH IMPROVEMENT SERVICES; IMPLEMENTATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.6985.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Community health needs assessment.</span></h2>
          <p>A nonprofit hospital that is exempt from taxation under section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code must make available to the public and submit to the commissioner of health, by January 15, 2026, the most recent community health needs assessment submitted by the hospital to the Internal Revenue Service. Each time the hospital conducts a subsequent community health needs assessment, the hospital must, within 15 business days after submitting the subsequent community health needs assessment to the Internal Revenue Service, make the subsequent assessment available to the public and submit the subsequent assessment to the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.6985.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Description of community.</span></h2>
          <p>A nonprofit hospital subject to subdivision 1 must make available to the public and submit to the commissioner of health a description of the community served by the hospital. The description must include a geographic description of the area where the hospital is located, a description of the general population served by the hospital, and demographic information about the community served by the hospital, such as leading causes of death, levels of chronic illness, and descriptions of the medically underserved, low-income, minority, or chronically ill populations in the community. A hospital is not required to separately make the information available to the public or separately submit the information to the commissioner if the information is included in the hospital's community health needs assessment made available and submitted under subdivision 1.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.6985.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Addendum; community health improvement services.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A nonprofit hospital subject to subdivision 1 must annually submit to the commissioner an addendum which details information about hospital activities identified as community health improvement services with a cost of $5,000 or more. The addendum must include the type of activity, the method through which the activity was delivered, how the activity relates to an identified community need in the community health needs assessment, the target population for the activity, strategies to reach the target population, identified outcome metrics, the cost to the hospital to provide the activity, the methodology used to calculate the hospital's costs, and the number of people served by the activity. If a community health improvement service is administered by an entity other than the hospital, the administering entity must be identified in the addendum. This paragraph does not apply to hospitals required to submit an addendum under paragraph (b).</p>
          <p>(b) A nonprofit hospital subject to subdivision 1 must annually submit to the commissioner an addendum which details information about the ten highest-cost activities of the hospital identified as community health improvement services if the nonprofit hospital:</p>
          <p>(1) is designated as a critical access hospital under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.1483">144.1483</a>, clause (9), and United States Code, title 42, section 1395i-4;</p>
          <p>(2) meets the definition of sole community hospital in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62Q.19#stat.62Q.19.1">62Q.19, subdivision 1</a>, paragraph (a), clause (5); or</p>
          <p>(3) meets the definition of rural emergency hospital in United States Code, title 42, section 1395x(kkk)(2).</p>
          <p class="bl">The addendum must include the type of activity, the method in which the activity was delivered, how the activity relates to an identified community need in the community health needs assessment, the target population for the activity, strategies to reach the target population, identified outcome metrics, the cost to the hospital to provide the activity, the methodology used to calculate the hospital's costs, and the number of people served by the activity. If a community health improvement service is administered by an entity other than the hospital, the administering entity must be identified in the addendum.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.6985.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Community benefit implementation strategy.</span></h2>
          <p>A nonprofit hospital subject to subdivision 1 must make available to the public, within one year after completing each community health needs assessment, a community benefit implementation strategy. In developing the community benefit implementation strategy, the hospital must consult with community-based organizations, stakeholders, local public health organizations, and others as determined by the hospital. The implementation strategy must include how the hospital shall address the top three community health priorities identified in the community health needs assessment. Implementation strategies must be evidence-based, when available, and development and implementation of innovative programs and strategies may be supported by evaluation measures.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.6985.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Information made available to the public.</span></h2>
          <p>A nonprofit hospital required to make information available to the public under this section may do so by posting the information on the hospital's website in a consolidated location and with clear labeling.</p>
          <p class="bl">This section is effective January 1, 2026.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.6985.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.59.32.0">2024 c 127 art 59 s 32</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.699">
        <h1 class="shn">144.699 CONTINUING ANALYSIS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.699.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Acute care costs.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health may:</p>
          <p>(1) undertake analyses and studies relating to acute care costs and to the financial status of any hospital or outpatient surgical center subject to the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.695">144.695</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.703">144.703</a>; and</p>
          <p>(2) publish and disseminate the information relating to acute care costs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.699.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Fostering price competition.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall:</p>
          <p>(1) encourage hospitals, outpatient surgical centers, home care providers, and professionals regulated by the health-related licensing boards as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.01#stat.214.01.2">214.01, subdivision 2</a>, and by the commissioner of health under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/214.13">214.13</a>, to publish prices for procedures and services that are representative of the diagnoses and conditions for which citizens of this state seek treatment; and</p>
          <p>(2) analyze and disseminate available price information and analyses so as to foster the development of price competition among hospitals, outpatient surgical centers, home care providers, and health professionals.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.699.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Cooperation with attorney general.</span></h2>
          <p>Upon request of the attorney general, the commissioner of health shall make available to the attorney general all requested information provided under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.695">144.695</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.703">144.703</a> in order to assist the attorney general in discharging the responsibilities of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/8.31">8.31</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.699.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Other reports or costs.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall prepare and file summaries and compilations or other supplementary reports based on the information filed with or made available to the commissioner of health, which reports will advance the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.695">144.695</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.703">144.703</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.699.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Annual reports on community benefit, community care amounts, and state program underfunding.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) For each hospital reporting health care cost information under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.698">144.698</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.702">144.702</a>, the commissioner shall report annually on the hospital's community benefit and community care, including detailed information on each component of those costs as defined in this subdivision. The information shall be reported in terms of total dollars and as a percentage of total operating costs for each hospital.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) For purposes of this subdivision, "community benefit" means the costs of community care, underpayment for services provided under state health care programs, research costs, community health services costs, financial and in-kind contributions, costs of community building activities, costs of community benefit operations, education costs, and the cost of operating subsidized services. The cost of bad debts and underpayment for Medicare services are not included in the calculation of community benefit.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) For purposes of this subdivision, "community care" means the costs for medical care that a hospital has determined is charity care as defined under Minnesota Rules, part <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4650.0115">4650.0115</a>, or for which the hospital determines after billing for the services that there is a demonstrated inability to pay. Any costs forgiven under a hospital's community care plan or under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62J.83">62J.83</a> may be counted in the hospital's calculation of community care. Bad debt expenses and discounted charges available to the uninsured shall not be included in the calculation of community care. The amount of community care is the value of costs incurred and not the charges made for services.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) For purposes of this subdivision, "underpayment for services provided under state health care programs" means the difference between hospital costs and public program payments.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.699.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/296/#laws.2.5.0">1976 c 296 art 2 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/534/#laws.0.6.0">1984 c 534 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/378/#laws.0.2.0">1987 c 378 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.9.21.0">2007 c 147 art 9 s 21</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.70">
        <h1 class="shn">144.70 BIENNIAL REPORT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.70.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Content.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall prepare a report every two years concerning the status and operations of the health care markets in Minnesota. The commissioner of health shall transmit the reports to the governor, and to the members of the legislature under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/3.195">3.195</a>. The first report must be submitted on January 15, 1987, and succeeding reports on January 15 every two years. Each report must contain information, analysis, and appropriate recommendations concerning the following issues associated with Minnesota health care markets:</p>
          <p>(1) the overall status of the health care cost problem, including the costs faced by employers and individuals, and prospects for the problem's improving or getting worse;</p>
          <p>(2) the status of competitive forces in the market for health services and the market for health plans, and the effect of the forces on the health care cost problem;</p>
          <p>(3) the feasibility and cost-effectiveness of facilitating development of strengthened competitive forces through state initiatives;</p>
          <p>(4) the feasibility of limiting health care costs by means other than competitive forces, including direct forms of government intervention such as price regulation; the commissioner of health may exclude this issue from the report if the report concludes that the overall status of the health care cost problem is improving, or that competitive forces are contributing significantly to health care cost containment;</p>
          <p>(5) the overall status of access to adequate health services by citizens of Minnesota, the scope of financial and geographic barriers to access, the effect of competitive forces on access, and prospects for access improving or getting worse;</p>
          <p>(6) the feasibility and cost-effectiveness of enhancing access to adequate health services by citizens of Minnesota through state initiatives; and</p>
          <p>(7) the commissioner of health's operations and activities for the preceding two years as they relate to the duties imposed on the commissioner of health by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.695">144.695</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.703">144.703</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.70.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Interagency cooperation.</span></h2>
          <p>In completing the report required by subdivision 1, in fulfilling the requirements of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.695">144.695</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.703">144.703</a>, and in undertaking other initiatives concerning health care costs, access, or quality, the commissioner of health shall cooperate with and consider potential benefits to other state agencies that have a role in the market for health services or the market for health plans. Other agencies include the Department of Management and Budget, as administrator of the state employee health benefits program; the Department of Human Services, as administrator of health services entitlement programs; the Department of Commerce, in its regulation of health plans; the Department of Labor and Industry, in its regulation of health service costs under workers' compensation.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.70.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/296/#laws.2.6.0">1976 c 296 art 2 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/1/9/#laws.2.11.0">1Sp1985 c 9 art 2 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1991/0/345/#laws.2.37.0">1991 c 345 art 2 s 37</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/411/#laws.0.2.0">1994 c 411 s 2; 2008 c 204 s 42</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/101/#laws.2.109.0">2009 c 101 art 2 s 109</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.701">
        <h1 class="shn">144.701 RATE DISCLOSURE.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.701.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Consumer information.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall ensure that the total costs, total revenues, overall utilization, and total services of each hospital and each outpatient surgical center are reported to the public in a form understandable to consumers.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.701.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Data for policy making.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall compile relevant financial and accounting, utilization, and services data concerning hospitals and outpatient surgical centers in order to have statistical information available for legislative policy making.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.701.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Rate schedule.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall obtain from each hospital and outpatient surgical center a current rate schedule. Any subsequent amendments or modifications of that schedule shall be filed with the commissioner of health on or before their effective date.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.701.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Filing fees.</span></h2>
          <p>Each report which is required to be submitted to the commissioner of health under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.695">144.695</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.703">144.703</a> and which is not submitted to a voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization in accordance with section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.702">144.702</a> shall be accompanied by a filing fee in an amount prescribed by rule of the commissioner of health. Upon the withdrawal of approval of a reporting organization, or the decision of the commissioner to not renew a reporting organization, fees collected under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.702">144.702</a> shall be submitted to the commissioner. Fees received under this subdivision shall be deposited in a revolving fund and are appropriated to the commissioner of health for the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.695">144.695</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.703">144.703</a>. The commissioner shall report the termination or nonrenewal of the voluntary reporting organization to the chair of the Health and Human Services Finance Committee of the house of representatives, to the chair of the Health and Human Services Division of the Finance Committee of the senate, and the commissioner of management and budget.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.701.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/296/#laws.2.7.0">1976 c 296 art 2 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/424/#laws.0.130.0">1982 c 424 s 130</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/534/#laws.0.7.0">1984 c 534 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/282/#laws.2.12.0">1989 c 282 art 2 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.27.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 27</a>-29; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/284/#laws.2.15.0">2004 c 284 art 2 s 15</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/101/#laws.2.109.0">2009 c 101 art 2 s 109</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.702">
        <h1 class="shn">144.702 HOSPITAL AND OUTPATIENT SURGICAL CENTER COSTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.702.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Reporting through a reporting organization.</span></h2>
          <p>A hospital or outpatient surgical center may agree to submit its financial, utilization, and services reports to a voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization whose reporting procedures have been approved by the commissioner of health in accordance with this section. Each report submitted to the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization under this section shall be accompanied by a filing fee.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.702.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Approval of organization's reporting procedures.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health may approve voluntary reporting procedures consistent with written operating requirements for the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization which shall be established annually by the commissioner. These written operating requirements shall specify reports, analyses, and other deliverables to be produced by the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization, and the dates on which those deliverables must be submitted to the commissioner. These written operating requirements shall specify deliverable dates sufficient to enable the commissioner of health to process and report health care cost information system data to the commissioner of human services by August 15 of each year. The commissioner of health shall, by rule, prescribe standards for submission of data by hospitals and outpatient surgical centers to the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization or to the commissioner. These standards shall provide for:</p>
          <p>(1) the filing of appropriate financial, utilization, and services information with the reporting organization;</p>
          <p>(2) adequate analysis and verification of that financial, utilization, and services information; and</p>
          <p>(3) timely publication of the costs, revenues, and rates of individual hospitals and outpatient surgical centers prior to the effective date of any proposed rate increase. The commissioner of health shall annually review the procedures approved pursuant to this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.702.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Cost and rate information; time limits on filing.</span></h2>
          <p>Any voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization which collects information on costs, revenues, and rates of a hospital or outpatient surgical center located in this state shall file a copy of the information received for each hospital and outpatient surgical center with the commissioner of health within 30 days of completion of the information collection process, together with a summary of the financial information acquired by the organization during the course of its review.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.702.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Making information available to commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>Any voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization which receives the financial information required by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.695">144.695</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.703">144.703</a> shall make the information and all summaries and analyses of the information available to the commissioner of health in accordance with procedures prescribed by the commissioner of health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.702.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Laws governing restraint of trade.</span></h2>
          <p>If the reporting and procedures of a voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization have been approved by the commissioner of health those reporting activities of the organization shall be exempt from the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325D.49">325D.49</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/325D.66">325D.66</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.702.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Reporting organization; definition.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purposes of this section "reporting organization" means an association or other organization which has as one of its primary functions the collection and dissemination of acute care cost information.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.702.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Staff support.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may require as part of the written operating requirements for the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization that the organization provide sufficient funds to cover the costs of one professional staff position who will directly administer the health care cost information system.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.702.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Termination or nonrenewal of reporting organization.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may withdraw approval of any voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization for failure on the part of the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization to comply with the written operating requirements under subdivision 2. Upon the effective date of the withdrawal, all funds collected by the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization under subdivision 1, but not expended shall be deposited in a revolving fund and are appropriated to the commissioner of health for the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.695">144.695</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.703">144.703</a>.</p>
          <p>The commissioner may choose not to renew approval of a voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization if the organization has failed to perform its obligations satisfactorily under the written operating requirements under subdivision 2.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.702.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/296/#laws.2.8.0">1976 c 296 art 2 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/534/#laws.0.8.0">1984 c 534 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1989/0/282/#laws.2.13.0">1989 c 282 art 2 s 13</a>-15; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/207/#laws.6.3.0">1995 c 207 art 6 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.30.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 30</a>-32</p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.7021"><b>144.7021</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/534/#laws.0.33.0">1984 c 534 s 33</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7022">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7022 REPORTING ORGANIZATIONS; PENALTY ORDERS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7022.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Authorization.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may issue an order to the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization requiring violations to be corrected and administratively assess monetary penalties for violations of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.695">144.695</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.703">144.703</a> or rules, written operating requirements, orders, stipulation agreements, settlements, or compliance agreements adopted, enforced, or issued by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7022.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Contents of order.</span></h2>
          <p>An order assessing an administrative penalty under this section must include:</p>
          <p>(1) a concise statement of the facts alleged to constitute a violation;</p>
          <p>(2) a reference to the section of law, rule, written operating requirement, order, stipulation agreement, settlement, or compliance agreement that has been violated;</p>
          <p>(3) a statement of the amount of the administrative penalty to be imposed and the factors upon which the penalty is based;</p>
          <p>(4) a statement of the corrective actions necessary to correct the violation; and</p>
          <p>(5) a statement of the right to request a hearing according to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.57">14.57</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.62">14.62</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7022.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Concurrent corrective order.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may issue an order assessing an administrative penalty and requiring the violations cited in the order be corrected within 30 calendar days from the date the order is received. Before the 31st day after the order was received, the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization that is subject to the order shall provide the commissioner with information demonstrating that the violation has been corrected or that a corrective plan acceptable to the commissioner has been developed. The commissioner shall determine whether the violation has been corrected and notify the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization of the commissioner's determination.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7022.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Penalty.</span></h2>
