          <p>If the commissioner determines that the violation has been corrected or an acceptable corrective plan has been developed, the penalty may be forgiven, except where there are repeated or serious violations. The commissioner may issue an order with a penalty that will not be forgiven after corrective action is taken. Unless there is a request for review of the order under subdivision 6 before the penalty is due, the penalty is due and payable:</p>
          <p>(1) on the 31st calendar day after the order was received, if the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization fails to provide information to the commissioner showing that the violation has been corrected or that appropriate steps have been taken toward correcting the violation;</p>
          <p>(2) on the 20th day after the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization receives the commissioner's determination that the information provided is not sufficient to show that either the violation has been corrected or that appropriate steps have been taken toward correcting the violation; or</p>
          <p>(3) on the 31st day after the order was received where the penalty is for repeated or serious violations and according to the order issued, the penalty will not be forgiven after corrective action is taken.</p>
          <p>All penalties due under this section are payable to the commissioner of management and budget, state of Minnesota, and shall be deposited in the general fund.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7022.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Amount of penalty; considerations.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The maximum amount of an administrative penalty order is $5,000 for each specific violation identified in an inspection, investigation, or compliance review, up to an annual maximum total for all violations of ten percent of the fees collected by the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.702#stat.144.702.1">144.702, subdivision 1</a>. The annual maximum is based on a reporting year.</p>
          <p>(b) In determining the amount of the administrative penalty, the commissioner shall consider the following:</p>
          <p>(1) the willfulness of the violation;</p>
          <p>(2) the gravity of the violation;</p>
          <p>(3) the history of past violations;</p>
          <p>(4) the number of violations;</p>
          <p>(5) the economic benefit gained by the person allowing or committing the violation; and</p>
          <p>(6) other factors as justice may require, if the commissioner specifically identifies the additional factors in the commissioner's order.</p>
          <p>(c) In determining the amount of a penalty for a violation subsequent to an initial violation under paragraph (a), the commissioner shall also consider:</p>
          <p>(1) the similarity of the most recent previous violation and the violation to be penalized;</p>
          <p>(2) the time elapsed since the last violation; and</p>
          <p>(3) the response of the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization to the most recent previous violation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7022.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Request for hearing; hearing; and final order.</span></h2>
          <p>A request for hearing must be in writing, delivered to the commissioner by certified mail within 20 calendar days after the receipt of the order, and specifically state the reasons for seeking review of the order. The commissioner must initiate a hearing within 30 calendar days from the date of receipt of the written request for hearing. The hearing shall be conducted pursuant to the contested case procedures in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.57">14.57</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.62">14.62</a>. No earlier than ten calendar days after and within 30 calendar days of receipt of the presiding administrative law judge's report, the commissioner shall, based on all relevant facts, issue a final order modifying, vacating, or making the original order permanent. If, within 20 calendar days of receipt of the original order, the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization fails to request a hearing in writing, the order becomes the final order of the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7022.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Review of final order and payment of penalty.</span></h2>
          <p>Once the commissioner issues a final order, any penalty due under that order shall be paid within 30 calendar days after the date of the final order, unless review of the final order is requested. The final order of the commissioner may be appealed in the manner prescribed in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.63">14.63</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.69">14.69</a>. If the final order is reviewed and upheld, the penalty shall be paid 30 calendar days after the date of the decision of the reviewing court. Failure to request an administrative hearing pursuant to subdivision 6 shall constitute a waiver of the right to further agency or judicial review of the final order.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7022.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Reinspections and effect of noncompliance.</span></h2>
          <p>If, upon reinspection, or in the determination of the commissioner, it is found that any deficiency specified in the order has not been corrected or an acceptable corrective plan has not been developed, the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization is in noncompliance. The commissioner shall issue a notice of noncompliance and may impose any additional remedy available under this chapter.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7022.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Enforcement.</span></h2>
          <p>The attorney general may proceed on behalf of the commissioner to enforce penalties that are due and payable under this section in any manner provided by law for the collection of debts.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7022.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Termination or nonrenewal of reporting organization.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may withdraw or not renew approval of any voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization for failure on the part of the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization to pay penalties owed under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7022.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Cumulative remedy.</span></h2>
          <p>The authority of the commissioner to issue an administrative penalty order is in addition to other lawfully available remedies.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7022.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Mediation.</span></h2>
          <p>In addition to review under subdivision 6, the commissioner is authorized to enter into mediation concerning an order issued under this section if the commissioner and the voluntary, nonprofit reporting organization agree to mediation.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7022.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.33.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/112/#laws.2.50.0">2003 c 112 art 2 s 50</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/101/#laws.2.109.0">2009 c 101 art 2 s 109</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.703">
        <h1 class="shn">144.703 ADDITIONAL POWERS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.703.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Rulemaking.</span></h2>
          <p>In addition to the other powers granted to the commissioner of health by law, the commissioner of health may:</p>
          <p>(1) adopt, amend, and repeal rules in accordance with chapter 14;</p>
          <p>(2) adopt in rule a schedule of fines, ranging from $100 to $1,000, for failure of a hospital or an outpatient surgical center to submit, or to make a timely submission of, information called for by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.695">144.695</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.703">144.703</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.703.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Contested cases.</span></h2>
          <p>Any person aggrieved by a final determination of the commissioner of health as to any rule or determination under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.695">144.695</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.703">144.703</a> shall be entitled to an administrative hearing and judicial review in accordance with the contested case provisions of chapter 14.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.703.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/296/#laws.2.9.0">1976 c 296 art 2 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1982/0/424/#laws.0.130.0">1982 c 424 s 130</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/534/#laws.0.9.0">1984 c 534 s 9</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.704"><b>144.704</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/534/#laws.0.33.0">1984 c 534 s 33</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.705"><b>144.705</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1984/0/534/#laws.0.33.0">1984 c 534 s 33</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">STAFFING PLAN REPORTS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7055">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7055 STAFFING PLAN REPORTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7055.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For the purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Core staffing plan" means the projected number of full-time equivalent nonmanagerial care staff that will be assigned in a 24-hour period to an inpatient care unit.</p>
          <p>(c) "Nonmanagerial care staff" means registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, and other health care workers, which may include but is not limited to nursing assistants, nursing aides, patient care technicians, and patient care assistants, who perform nonmanagerial direct patient care functions for more than 50 percent of their scheduled hours on a given patient care unit.</p>
          <p>(d) "Inpatient care unit" means a designated inpatient area for assigning patients and staff for which a distinct staffing plan exists and that operates 24 hours per day, seven days per week in a hospital setting. Inpatient care unit does not include any hospital-based clinic, long-term care facility, or outpatient hospital department.</p>
          <p>(e) "Staffing hours per patient day" means the number of full-time equivalent nonmanagerial care staff who will ordinarily be assigned to provide direct patient care divided by the expected average number of patients upon which such assignments are based.</p>
          <p>(f) "Patient acuity tool" means a system for measuring an individual patient's need for nursing care. This includes utilizing a professional registered nursing assessment of patient condition to assess staffing need.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7055.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Hospital staffing report.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The chief nursing executive or nursing designee of every reporting hospital in Minnesota under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> will develop a core staffing plan for each patient care unit.</p>
          <p>(b) Core staffing plans shall specify the full-time equivalent for each patient care unit for each 24-hour period.</p>
          <p>(c) Prior to submitting the core staffing plan, as required in subdivision 3, hospitals shall consult with representatives of the hospital medical staff, managerial and nonmanagerial care staff, and other relevant hospital personnel about the core staffing plan and the expected average number of patients upon which the staffing plan is based.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7055.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Standard electronic reporting developed.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Hospitals must submit the core staffing plans to the Minnesota Hospital Association by January 1, 2014. The Minnesota Hospital Association shall include each reporting hospital's core staffing plan on the Minnesota Hospital Association's Minnesota Hospital Quality Report website by April 1, 2014. Any substantial changes to the core staffing plan shall be updated within 30 days.</p>
          <p>(b) The Minnesota Hospital Association shall include on its website for each reporting hospital on a quarterly basis the actual direct patient care hours per patient and per unit. Hospitals must submit the direct patient care report to the Minnesota Hospital Association by July 1, 2014, and quarterly thereafter.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7055.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/51/#laws.0.1.0">2013 c 51 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">ADVERSE HEALTH CARE EVENTS REPORTING</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.706">
        <h1 class="shn">144.706 CITATION.</h1>
        <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.706">144.706</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7069">144.7069</a> may be cited as the "Minnesota Adverse Health Care Events Reporting Act of 2003."</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.706.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/99/#laws.0.1.0">2003 c 99 s 1</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7063">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7063 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7063.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>Unless the context clearly indicates otherwise, for the purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.706">144.706</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7069">144.7069</a>, the terms defined in this section have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7063.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>"Commissioner" means the commissioner of health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7063.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Facility.</span></h2>
          <p>"Facility" means a hospital or outpatient surgical center licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.58">144.58</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7063.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Serious disability.</span></h2>
          <p>"Serious disability" means (1) a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more of the major life activities of an individual or a loss of bodily function, if the impairment or loss lasts more than seven days or is still present at the time of discharge from an inpatient health care facility, or (2) loss of a body part.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7063.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Surgery.</span></h2>
          <p>"Surgery" means the treatment of disease, injury, or deformity by manual or operative methods. Surgery includes endoscopies and other invasive procedures.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7063.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/99/#laws.0.2.0">2003 c 99 s 2</a>,7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.7.84.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 7 s 84</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/198/#laws.0.15.0">2004 c 198 s 15</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7065">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7065 FACILITY REQUIREMENTS TO REPORT, ANALYZE, AND CORRECT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7065.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Reports of adverse health care events required.</span></h2>
          <p>Each facility shall report to the commissioner the occurrence of any of the adverse health care events described in subdivisions 2 to 7 as soon as is reasonably and practically possible, but no later than 15 working days after discovery of the event. The report shall be filed in a format specified by the commissioner and shall identify the facility but shall not include any identifying information for any of the health care professionals, facility employees, or patients involved. The commissioner may consult with experts and organizations familiar with patient safety when developing the format for reporting and in further defining events in order to be consistent with industry standards.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7065.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Surgical events.</span></h2>
          <p>Events reportable under this subdivision are:</p>
          <p>(1) surgery or other invasive procedure performed on a wrong body part that is not consistent with the documented informed consent for that patient. Reportable events under this clause do not include situations requiring prompt action that occur in the course of surgery or situations whose urgency precludes obtaining informed consent;</p>
          <p>(2) surgery or other invasive procedure performed on the wrong patient;</p>
          <p>(3) the wrong surgical or other invasive procedure performed on a patient that is not consistent with the documented informed consent for that patient. Reportable events under this clause do not include situations requiring prompt action that occur in the course of surgery or situations whose urgency precludes obtaining informed consent;</p>
          <p>(4) retention of a foreign object in a patient after surgery or other invasive procedure, excluding objects intentionally implanted as part of a planned intervention and objects present prior to surgery that are intentionally retained; and</p>
          <p>(5) death during or immediately after surgery or other invasive procedure of a normal, healthy patient who has no organic, physiologic, biochemical, or psychiatric disturbance and for whom the pathologic processes for which the operation is to be performed are localized and do not entail a systemic disturbance.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7065.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Product or device events.</span></h2>
          <p>Events reportable under this subdivision are:</p>
          <p>(1) patient death or serious injury associated with the use of contaminated drugs, devices, or biologics provided by the facility when the contamination is the result of generally detectable contaminants in drugs, devices, or biologics regardless of the source of the contamination or the product;</p>
          <p>(2) patient death or serious injury associated with the use or function of a device in patient care in which the device is used or functions other than as intended. "Device" includes, but is not limited to, catheters, drains, and other specialized tubes, infusion pumps, and ventilators; and</p>
          <p>(3) patient death or serious injury associated with intravascular air embolism that occurs while being cared for in a facility, excluding deaths associated with neurosurgical procedures known to present a high risk of intravascular air embolism.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7065.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Patient protection events.</span></h2>
          <p>Events reportable under this subdivision are:</p>
          <p>(1) a patient of any age, who does not have decision-making capacity, discharged to the wrong person;</p>
          <p>(2) patient death or serious injury associated with patient disappearance, excluding events involving adults who have decision-making capacity; and</p>
          <p>(3) patient suicide, attempted suicide resulting in serious injury, or self-harm resulting in serious injury or death while being cared for in a facility due to patient actions after admission to the facility, excluding deaths resulting from self-inflicted injuries that were the reason for admission to the facility.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7065.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Care management events.</span></h2>
          <p>Events reportable under this subdivision are:</p>
          <p>(1) patient death or serious injury associated with a medication error, including, but not limited to, errors involving the wrong drug, the wrong dose, the wrong patient, the wrong time, the wrong rate, the wrong preparation, or the wrong route of administration, excluding reasonable differences in clinical judgment on drug selection and dose;</p>
          <p>(2) patient death or serious injury associated with unsafe administration of blood or blood products;</p>
          <p>(3) maternal death or serious injury associated with labor or delivery in a low-risk pregnancy while being cared for in a facility, including events that occur within 42 days postdelivery and excluding deaths from pulmonary or amniotic fluid embolism, acute fatty liver of pregnancy, or cardiomyopathy;</p>
          <p>(4) death or serious injury of a neonate associated with labor or delivery in a low-risk pregnancy;</p>
          <p>(5) stage 3 or 4 or unstageable ulcers acquired after admission to a facility, excluding progression from stage 2 to stage 3 if stage 2 was recognized upon admission;</p>
          <p>(6) artificial insemination with the wrong donor sperm or wrong egg;</p>
          <p>(7) patient death or serious injury associated with a fall while being cared for in a facility;</p>
          <p>(8) the irretrievable loss of an irreplaceable biological specimen; and</p>
          <p>(9) patient death or serious injury resulting from the failure to follow up or communicate laboratory, pathology, or radiology test results.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7065.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Environmental events.</span></h2>
          <p>Events reportable under this subdivision are:</p>
          <p>(1) patient death or serious injury associated with an electric shock while being cared for in a facility, excluding events involving planned treatments such as electric countershock;</p>
          <p>(2) any incident in which a line designated for oxygen or other gas to be delivered to a patient contains the wrong gas or is contaminated by toxic substances;</p>
          <p>(3) patient death or serious injury associated with a burn incurred from any source while being cared for in a facility; and</p>
          <p>(4) patient death or serious injury associated with the use or lack of restraints or bedrails while being cared for in a facility.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7065.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Potential criminal events.</span></h2>
          <p>Events reportable under this subdivision are:</p>
          <p>(1) any instance of care ordered by or provided by someone impersonating a physician, nurse, pharmacist, or other licensed health care provider;</p>
          <p>(2) abduction of a patient of any age;</p>
          <p>(3) sexual assault on a patient within or on the grounds of a facility; and</p>
          <p>(4) death or serious injury of a patient or staff member resulting from a physical assault that occurs within or on the grounds of a facility.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7065.7a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7a.<span class="headnote">Radiologic events.</span></h2>
          <p>Death or serious injury of a patient associated with the introduction of a metallic object into the MRI area are reportable events under this subdivision.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7065.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Root cause analysis; corrective action plan.</span></h2>
          <p>Following the occurrence of an adverse health care event, the facility must conduct a root cause analysis of the event. In conducting the root cause analysis, the facility must consider as one of the factors staffing levels and the impact of staffing levels on the event. Following the analysis, the facility must: (1) implement a corrective action plan to implement the findings of the analysis or (2) report to the commissioner any reasons for not taking corrective action. If the root cause analysis and the implementation of a corrective action plan are complete at the time an event must be reported, the findings of the analysis and the corrective action plan must be included in the report of the event. The findings of the root cause analysis and a copy of the corrective action plan must otherwise be filed with the commissioner within 60 days of the event.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7065.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Electronic reporting.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner must design the reporting system so that a facility may file by electronic means the reports required under this section. The commissioner shall encourage a facility to use the electronic filing option when that option is feasible for the facility.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7065.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Relation to other law; data classification.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Adverse health events described in subdivisions 2 to 6 do not constitute "maltreatment," "neglect," or "a physical injury that is not reasonably explained" under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.557">626.557 </a>or chapter 260E and are excluded from the reporting requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.557">626.557</a> and chapter 260E, provided the facility makes a determination within 24 hours of the discovery of the event that this section is applicable and the facility files the reports required under this section in a timely fashion.</p>
          <p>(b) A facility that has determined that an event described in subdivisions 2 to 6 has occurred must inform persons who are mandated reporters under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260E.06">260E.06</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.5572#stat.626.5572.16">626.5572, subdivision 16</a>, of that determination. A mandated reporter otherwise required to report under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260E.06">260E.06</a> or <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.557#stat.626.557.3">626.557, subdivision 3</a>, paragraph (e), is relieved of the duty to report an event that the facility determines under paragraph (a) to be reportable under subdivisions 2 to 6.</p>
          <p>(c) The protections and immunities applicable to voluntary reports under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.557">626.557</a> and chapter 260E are not affected by this section.</p>
          <p>(d) Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.557">626.557</a>, chapter 260E, or any other provision of Minnesota statute or rule to the contrary, a lead agency under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/260E.14#stat.260E.14.1">260E.14, subdivision 1</a>, paragraphs (a), (b), and (c), a lead investigative agency under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.5572#stat.626.5572.13">626.5572, subdivision 13</a>, the commissioner of health, or the director of the Office of Health Facility Complaints is not required to conduct an investigation of or obtain or create investigative data or reports regarding an event described in subdivisions 2 to 6. If the facility satisfies the requirements described in paragraph (a), the review or investigation shall be conducted and data or reports shall be obtained or created only under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.706">144.706</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7069">144.7069</a>, except as permitted or required under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.564">144.564</a>, or as necessary to carry out the state's certification responsibility under the provisions of sections 1864 and 1867 of the Social Security Act. If a licensed health care provider reports an event to the facility required to be reported under subdivisions 2 to 6 in a timely manner, the provider's licensing board is not required to conduct an investigation of or obtain or create investigative data or reports regarding the individual reporting of the events described in subdivisions 2 to 6.</p>
          <p>(e) Data contained in the following records are nonpublic and, to the extent they contain data on individuals, confidential data on individuals, as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02">13.02</a>:</p>
          <p>(1) reports provided to the commissioner under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/147.155">147.155</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/147A.155">147A.155</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.267">148.267</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/151.301">151.301</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/153.255">153.255</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) event reports, findings of root cause analyses, and corrective action plans filed by a facility under this section; and</p>
          <p>(3) records created or obtained by the commissioner in reviewing or investigating the reports, findings, and plans described in clause (2).</p>
          <p>For purposes of the nonpublic data classification contained in this paragraph, the reporting facility shall be deemed the subject of the data.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7065.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/99/#laws.0.3.0">2003 c 99 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/1/14/#laws.7.85.0">1Sp2003 c 14 art 7 s 85</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/186/#laws.0.1.0">2004 c 186 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/41/#laws.0.1.0">2007 c 41 s 1</a>-3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/159/#laws.0.7.0">2009 c 159 s 7</a>,8; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2011/0/28/#laws.0.1.0">2011 c 28 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/43/#laws.0.8.0">2013 c 43 s 8</a>-14; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/1/2/#laws.8.21.0">1Sp2020 c 2 art 8 s 21</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7067">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7067 COMMISSIONER DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7067.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Establishment of reporting system.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner shall establish an adverse health event reporting system designed to facilitate quality improvement in the health care system. The reporting system shall not be designed to punish errors by health care practitioners or health care facility employees.</p>
          <p>(b) The reporting system shall consist of:</p>
          <p>(1) mandatory reporting by facilities of 27 adverse health care events;</p>
          <p>(2) mandatory completion of a root cause analysis and a corrective action plan by the facility and reporting of the findings of the analysis and the plan to the commissioner or reporting of reasons for not taking corrective action;</p>
          <p>(3) analysis of reported information by the commissioner to determine patterns of systemic failure in the health care system and successful methods to correct these failures;</p>
          <p>(4) sanctions against facilities for failure to comply with reporting system requirements; and</p>
          <p>(5) communication from the commissioner to facilities, health care purchasers, and the public to maximize the use of the reporting system to improve health care quality.</p>
          <p>(c) The commissioner is not authorized to select from or between competing alternate acceptable medical practices.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7067.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Duty to analyze reports; communicate findings.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner shall:</p>
          <p>(1) analyze adverse event reports, corrective action plans, and findings of the root cause analyses to determine patterns of systemic failure in the health care system and successful methods to correct these failures;</p>
          <p>(2) communicate to individual facilities the commissioner's conclusions, if any, regarding an adverse event reported by the facility;</p>
          <p>(3) communicate with relevant health care facilities any recommendations for corrective action resulting from the commissioner's analysis of submissions from facilities; and</p>
          <p>(4) publish an annual report:</p>
          <p>(i) describing, by institution, adverse events reported;</p>
          <p>(ii) outlining, in aggregate, corrective action plans and the findings of root cause analyses; and</p>
          <p>(iii) making recommendations for modifications of state health care operations.</p>
          <p>(b) Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.05#stat.144.05.7">144.05, subdivision 7</a>, the mandate to publish an annual report under this subdivision does not expire.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7067.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Sanctions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner shall take steps necessary to determine if adverse event reports, the findings of the root cause analyses, and corrective action plans are filed in a timely manner. The commissioner may sanction a facility for:</p>
          <p>(1) failure to file a timely adverse event report under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7065#stat.144.7065.1">144.7065, subdivision 1</a>; or</p>
          <p>(2) failure to conduct a root cause analysis, to implement a corrective action plan, or to provide the findings of a root cause analysis or corrective action plan in a timely fashion under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7065#stat.144.7065.8">144.7065, subdivision 8</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) If a facility fails to develop and implement a corrective action plan or report to the commissioner why corrective action is not needed, the commissioner may suspend, revoke, fail to renew, or place conditions on the license under which the facility operates.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7067.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/99/#laws.0.4.0">2003 c 99 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/127/#laws.59.33.0">2024 c 127 art 59 s 33</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7068">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7068 REPORTS FROM LICENSING BOARDS.</h1>
        <p>(a) Effective upon full implementation of the adverse health care events reporting system, the records maintained under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/147.155">147.155</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/147A.155">147A.155</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/148.267">148.267</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/151.301">151.301</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/153.255">153.255</a>, shall be reported to the commissioner on the schedule established in those sections.</p>
        <p>(b) The commissioner shall forward these reports to the facility named in the report.</p>
        <p>(c) The facility shall determine whether the event has been previously reported under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7065">144.7065</a>. The facility shall notify the commissioner whether the event has been reported previously. If the event has not been previously reported, the facility shall make a determination whether the event was reportable under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7065">144.7065</a>. If the facility determines the event was reportable, the date of discovery of the event for the purposes of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7065#stat.144.7065.10">144.7065, subdivision 10</a>, paragraph (d), shall be as follows:</p>
        <p>(1) if the commissioner determines that the facility knew or reasonably should have known about the occurrence of the event, the date the event occurred shall be the date of discovery. The facility shall be considered out of compliance with the reporting act, and the event shall be subject to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.557">626.557</a> and chapter 260E; or</p>
        <p>(2) if the commissioner determines that the facility did not know about the occurrence of the event, the date the facility receives the report from the commissioner shall serve as the date of discovery.</p>
        <p class="bl">If the facility determines that the event was not reportable under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7065">144.7065</a>, the facility shall notify the commissioner of that determination.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7068.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/186/#laws.0.2.0">2004 c 186 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/1/2/#laws.8.22.0">1Sp2020 c 2 art 8 s 22</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7069">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7069 INTERSTATE COORDINATION; REPORTS.</h1>
        <p>The commissioner shall report the definitions and the list of reportable events adopted in this act to the National Quality Forum and, working in coordination with the National Quality Forum, to the other states. The commissioner shall monitor discussions by the National Quality Forum of amendments to the forum's list of reportable events and shall report to the legislature whenever the list is modified. The commissioner shall also monitor implementation efforts in other states to establish a list of reportable events and shall make recommendations to the legislature as necessary for modifications in the Minnesota list or in the other components of the Minnesota reporting system to keep the system as nearly uniform as possible with similar systems in other states.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7069.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/99/#laws.0.5.0">2003 c 99 s 5</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">YOUTH CAMPS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.71">
        <h1 class="shn">144.71 PURPOSE; DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.71.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Health and safety.</span></h2>
          <p>The purpose of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.71">144.71</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.74">144.74</a> is to protect the health and safety of persons in attendance at youth camps.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.71.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Definition.</span></h2>
          <p>For the purpose of such sections, a youth camp is defined as a parcel or parcels of land with permanent buildings, tents or other structures together with appurtenances thereon, established or maintained as living quarters where both food and beverage service and lodging or the facilities therefor are provided for ten or more people, operated continuously for a period of five days or more each year for educational, recreational or vacation purposes, and the use of the camp is offered to minors free of charge or for payment of a fee.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.71.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">What not included in definition.</span></h2>
          <p>This definition does not include cabin and trailer camps, fishing and hunting camps, resorts, penal and correctional camps, industrial and construction camps, nor does it include homes operated for care or treatment of children and for the operation of which a license is required under the provisions of chapter 257.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.71.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1951/0/285/#laws.0.1.0">1951 c 285 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1974/0/406/#laws.0.21.0">1974 c 406 s 21</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/206/#laws.0.6.0">1993 c 206 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/451/#laws.4.8.0">1996 c 451 art 4 s 8</a>,9</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.72">
        <h1 class="shn">144.72 OPERATION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.72.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">License required.</span></h2>
          <p>The state commissioner of health is authorized to issue a license according to chapter 157.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.72.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Application.</span></h2>
          <p>On or before June first annually, every person, partnership, limited liability company or corporation, operating or seeking to operate a youth camp, shall make application in writing to the commissioner for a permit to conduct a youth camp. Such application shall be in such form and shall contain such information as the commissioner may find necessary to determine that the youth camp will be operated and maintained in such a manner as to protect and preserve the health and safety of the persons using the camp. Where a person, partnership, limited liability company or corporation operates or is seeking to operate more than one youth camp, a separate application shall be made for each camp.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.72.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Issuance of license.</span></h2>
          <p>If the commissioner should determine from the application that the health and safety of the persons using the camp will be properly safeguarded, the commissioner may, prior to actual inspection of the camp, issue the license in writing. The license shall be posted in a conspicuous place on the premises occupied by the camp.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.72.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1951/0/285/#laws.0.2.0">1951 c 285 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/451/#laws.4.10.0">1996 c 451 art 4 s 10</a>,11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.10.6.0">2009 c 79 art 10 s 6</a>,7</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.73">
        <h1 class="shn">144.73 STATE COMMISSIONER OF HEALTH, DUTIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.73.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Inspection of camps.</span></h2>
          <p>It shall be the duty of the state commissioner of health to make an annual inspection of each youth camp, and where, upon inspection it is found that there is a failure to protect the health and safety of the persons using the camp, or a failure to comply with the camp rules prescribed by the commissioner, the commissioner shall give notice to the camp operator of such failure, which notice shall set forth the reason or reasons for such failure.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.73.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/206/#laws.0.25.0">1993 c 206 s 25</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.73.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/206/#laws.0.25.0">1993 c 206 s 25</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.73.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/206/#laws.0.25.0">1993 c 206 s 25</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.73.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1951/0/285/#laws.0.3.0">1951 c 285 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1978/0/674/#laws.0.60.0">1978 c 674 s 60</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/286/#laws.0.2.0">1993 c 286 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1994/0/465/#laws.3.68.0">1994 c 465 art 3 s 68</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/451/#laws.4.12.0">1996 c 451 art 4 s 12</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.74">
        <h1 class="shn">144.74 RULES, STANDARDS.</h1>
        <p>The state commissioner of health is authorized to adopt and enforce such reasonable rules and standards as the commissioner determines necessary to protect the health and safety of persons in attendance at youth camps. Such rules and standards may include reasonable restrictions and limitations on the following:</p>
        <p>(1) camp sites and buildings, including location, layout, lighting, ventilation, heating, plumbing, drainage and sleeping quarters;</p>
        <p>(2) sanitary facilities, including water supply, toilet and shower facilities, sewage and excreta disposal, waste and garbage disposal, and the control of insects and rodents; and</p>
        <p>(3) food service, including storage, refrigeration, sanitary preparation and handling of food, the cleanliness of kitchens and the proper functioning of equipment.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.74.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1951/0/285/#laws.0.4.0">1951 c 285 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/0/248/#laws.0.70.0">1985 c 248 s 70</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1986/0/444/#laws.0.0.0">1986 c 444</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/451/#laws.4.13.0">1996 c 451 art 4 s 13</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">BLOOD-BORNE PATHOGENS; EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES PERSON</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7401">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7401 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7401.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope of definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>For purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a>, the following terms have the meanings given them.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7401.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Blood-borne pathogens.</span></h2>
          <p>"Blood-borne pathogens" means pathogenic microorganisms that are present in human blood and can cause disease in humans. These pathogens include, but are not limited to, hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7401.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Emergency medical services agency.</span></h2>
          <p>"Emergency medical services agency" means an agency, entity, or organization that employs or uses emergency medical services persons as employees or volunteers.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7401.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Emergency medical services person.</span></h2>
          <p>"Emergency medical services person" means:</p>
          <p>(1) an individual employed or receiving compensation to provide out-of-hospital emergency medical services such as a firefighter, paramedic, emergency medical technician, licensed nurse, rescue squad person, or other individual who serves as an employee or volunteer of an ambulance service as defined under chapter 144E or a member of an organized first responder squad that is formally recognized by a political subdivision in the state, who provides out-of-hospital emergency medical services during the performance of the individual's duties;</p>
          <p>(2) an individual employed as a licensed peace officer under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.84#stat.626.84.1">626.84, subdivision 1</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) an individual employed as a crime laboratory worker while working outside the laboratory and involved in a criminal investigation;</p>
          <p>(4) any individual who renders emergency care or assistance at the scene of an emergency or while an injured person is being transported to receive medical care and who is acting as a Good Samaritan under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/604A.01">604A.01</a>; and</p>
          <p>(5) any individual who, in the process of executing a citizen's arrest under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/629.30">629.30</a>, may have experienced a significant exposure to a source individual.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7401.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Source individual.</span></h2>
          <p>"Source individual" means an individual, living or dead, whose blood, tissue, or potentially infectious body fluids may be a source of blood-borne pathogen exposure to an emergency medical services person. Examples include, but are not limited to, a victim of an accident, injury, or illness or a deceased person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7401.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Significant exposure.</span></h2>
          <p>"Significant exposure" means contact likely to transmit a blood-borne pathogen, in a manner supported by the most current guidelines and recommendations of the United States Public Health Service at the time an evaluation takes place, that includes:</p>
          <p>(1) percutaneous injury, contact of mucous membrane or nonintact skin, or prolonged contact of intact skin; and</p>
          <p>(2) contact, in a manner that may transmit a blood-borne pathogen, with blood, tissue, or potentially infectious body fluids.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7401.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Facility.</span></h2>
          <p>"Facility" means a hospital licensed under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.50">144.50</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.56">144.56</a> or a freestanding emergency medical care facility licensed under Laws 1988, chapter 467, that receives an emergency medical services person for evaluation for significant exposure or a source individual cared for by an emergency medical services person.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7401.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Peace officer; applicability.</span></h2>
          <p>An individual licensed as a peace officer under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/626.84">626.84</a>, subdivision 1, is considered an emergency medical services person for purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a> regardless of whether the officer is engaged in performing emergency services.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7401.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/422/#laws.0.5.0">2000 c 422 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2006/0/260/#laws.3.4.0">2006 c 260 art 3 s 4</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7402">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7402 CONDITIONS FOR APPLICABILITY OF PROCEDURES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7402.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Request for procedures.</span></h2>
          <p>An emergency medical services person or emergency medical services agency may request that a facility follow the procedures of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a> when an emergency medical services person may have experienced a significant exposure to a source individual.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7402.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Conditions.</span></h2>
          <p>A facility shall follow the procedures outlined in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401 </a>to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a> when all of the following conditions are met:</p>
          <p>(1) the facility determines that significant exposure has occurred, following the protocol under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7414">144.7414</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) the licensed physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant for the emergency medical services person needs the source individual's blood-borne pathogen test results to begin, continue, modify, or discontinue treatment, in accordance with the most current guidelines of the United States Public Health Service, because of possible exposure to a blood-borne pathogen; and</p>
          <p>(3) the emergency medical services person consents to provide a blood sample for testing for a blood-borne pathogen. If the emergency medical services person consents to blood collection, but does not consent at that time to blood-borne pathogen testing, the facility shall preserve the sample for at least 90 days. If the emergency medical services person elects to have the sample tested within 90 days, the testing shall be done as soon as feasible.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7402.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Locating source individual.</span></h2>
          <p>If the source individual is not received by a facility but the facility is providing treatment to the emergency medical services person, the emergency medical services agency shall make reasonable efforts to locate the source individual and inform the facility of the source individual's identity and location. The facility shall make a reasonable effort to contact the source individual in order to follow the procedures in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a>. The emergency medical services agency and facilities may exchange private data about the source individual as necessary to fulfill their responsibilities under this subdivision, notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7402.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/422/#laws.0.6.0">2000 c 422 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.4.48.0">2020 c 115 art 4 s 48</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/58/#laws.0.54.0">2022 c 58 s 54</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7403">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7403 INFORMATION REQUIRED TO BE GIVEN TO INDIVIDUALS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7403.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Information to source individual.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Before seeking any consent required by the procedures under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a>, a facility shall inform the source individual that the source individual's blood-borne pathogen test results, without the individual's name, address, or other uniquely identifying information, shall be reported to the emergency medical services person if requested, and that test results collected under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a> are for medical purposes as set forth in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7409">144.7409</a> and may not be used as evidence in any criminal proceedings or civil proceedings, except for procedures under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4171">144.4171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4186">144.4186</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) The facility shall inform the source individual of the insurance protections in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/72A.20#stat.72A.20.29">72A.20, subdivision 29</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) The facility shall inform the source individual that the individual may refuse to provide a blood sample and that the source individual's refusal may result in a request for a court order to require the source individual to provide a blood sample.</p>
          <p>(d) The facility shall inform the source individual that the facility will advise the emergency medical services person of the confidentiality requirements and penalties before disclosing any test information.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7403.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Information to EMS person.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Before disclosing any information about the source individual, the facility shall inform the emergency medical services person of the confidentiality requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7411">144.7411</a> and that the person may be subject to penalties for unauthorized release of information about the source individual under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7412">144.7412</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) The facility shall inform the emergency medical services person of the insurance protections in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/72A.20#stat.72A.20.29">72A.20, subdivision 29</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7403.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/422/#laws.0.7.0">2000 c 422 s 7</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7404">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7404 DISCLOSURE OF POSITIVE BLOOD-BORNE PATHOGEN TEST RESULTS.</h1>
        <p>If the conditions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7402">144.7402</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7403">144.7403</a> are met, the facility shall ask the source individual and the emergency medical services person if they have ever had a positive test for a blood-borne pathogen. The facility must attempt to get existing test results under this section before taking any steps to obtain a blood sample or to test for blood-borne pathogens. The facility shall disclose the source individual's blood-borne pathogen test results to the emergency medical services person without the source individual's name, address, or other uniquely identifying information.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7404.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/422/#laws.0.8.0">2000 c 422 s 8</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7405">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7405 CONSENT PROCEDURES GENERALLY.</h1>
        <p>(a) For purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a>, whenever the facility is required to seek consent, the facility shall follow its usual procedure for obtaining consent from an individual or an individual's representative consistent with other law applicable to consent.</p>
        <p>(b) Consent from a source individual's representative for blood-borne pathogen testing of an existing blood sample obtained from the source individual is not required if the facility has made reasonable efforts to obtain the representative's consent and consent cannot be obtained within 24 hours of a significant exposure.</p>
        <p>(c) If testing of the source individual's blood occurs without consent because the source individual is unable to provide consent or has left the facility and cannot be located, and the source individual's representative cannot be located, the facility shall provide the information required in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7403">144.7403</a> to the source individual or representative whenever it is possible to do so.</p>
        <p>(d) If a source individual dies before an opportunity to consent to blood collection or testing under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a>, the facility does not need consent of the deceased person's representative for purposes of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7405.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/422/#laws.0.9.0">2000 c 422 s 9</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7406">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7406 TESTING OF AVAILABLE BLOOD.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7406.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Procedures with consent.</span></h2>
          <p>If the source individual is or was under the care or custody of the facility and a sample of the source individual's blood is available with the consent of the source individual, the facility shall test that blood for blood-borne pathogens with the consent of the source individual, provided the conditions in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7402">144.7402</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7403">144.7403</a> are met.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7406.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Procedures without consent.</span></h2>
          <p>If the source individual has provided a blood sample with consent but does not consent to blood-borne pathogen testing, the facility shall test for blood-borne pathogens if the emergency medical services person or emergency medical services agency requests the test, provided all of the following criteria are met:</p>
          <p>(1) the emergency medical services person or emergency medical services agency has documented exposure to blood or body fluids during performance of that person's occupation or while acting as a Good Samaritan under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/604A.01">604A.01</a> or executing a citizen's arrest under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/629.30">629.30</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) the facility has determined that a significant exposure has occurred and a licensed physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant for the emergency medical services person has documented in the emergency medical services person's medical record that blood-borne pathogen test results are needed for beginning, modifying, continuing, or discontinuing medical treatment for the emergency medical services person under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7414#stat.144.7414.2">144.7414, subdivision 2</a>;</p>
          <p>(3) the emergency medical services person provides a blood sample for testing for blood-borne pathogens as soon as feasible;</p>
          <p>(4) the facility asks the source individual to consent to a test for blood-borne pathogens and the source individual does not consent;</p>
          <p>(5) the facility has provided the source individual with all of the information required by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7403">144.7403</a>; and</p>
          <p>(6) the facility has informed the emergency medical services person of the confidentiality requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7411">144.7411</a> and the penalties for unauthorized release of source information under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7412">144.7412</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7406.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Follow-up.</span></h2>
          <p>The facility shall inform the source individual and the emergency medical services person of their own test results. The facility shall inform the emergency medical services person of the source individual's test results without the source individual's name, address, or other uniquely identifying information.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7406.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/422/#laws.0.10.0">2000 c 422 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.4.49.0">2020 c 115 art 4 s 49</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/58/#laws.0.55.0">2022 c 58 s 55</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7407">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7407 BLOOD SAMPLE COLLECTION FOR TESTING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7407.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Procedures with consent.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) If a blood sample is not otherwise available, the facility shall obtain consent from the source individual before collecting a blood sample for testing for blood-borne pathogens. The consent process shall include informing the source individual that the individual may refuse to provide a blood sample and that the source individual's refusal may result in a request for a court order under subdivision 2 to require the source individual to provide a blood sample.</p>
          <p>(b) If the source individual consents to provide a blood sample, the facility shall collect a blood sample and test the sample for blood-borne pathogens.</p>
          <p>(c) The facility shall inform the emergency medical services person about the source individual's test results without the individual's name, address, or other uniquely identifying information. The facility shall inform the source individual of the test results.</p>
          <p>(d) If the source individual refuses to provide a blood sample for testing, the facility shall inform the emergency medical services person of the source individual's refusal.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7407.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Procedures without consent.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An emergency medical services agency, or, if there is no agency, an emergency medical services person, may bring a petition for a court order to require a source individual to provide a blood sample for testing for blood-borne pathogens. The petition shall be filed in the district court in the county where the source individual resides or is hospitalized. The petitioner shall serve the petition on the source individual at least three days before a hearing on the petition. The petition shall include one or more affidavits attesting that:</p>
          <p>(1) the facility followed the procedures in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a> and attempted to obtain blood-borne pathogen test results according to those sections;</p>
          <p>(2) it has been determined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7414#stat.144.7414.2">144.7414, subdivision 2</a>, that a significant exposure has occurred to the emergency medical services person; and</p>
          <p>(3) a physician with specialty training in infectious diseases, including HIV, has documented that the emergency medical services person has provided a blood sample and consented to testing for blood-borne pathogens and blood-borne pathogen test results are needed for beginning, continuing, modifying, or discontinuing medical treatment for the emergency medical services person.</p>
          <p>(b) Facilities shall cooperate with petitioners in providing any necessary affidavits to the extent that facility staff can attest under oath to the facts in the affidavits.</p>
          <p>(c) The court may order the source individual to provide a blood sample for blood-borne pathogen testing if:</p>
          <p>(1) there is probable cause to believe the emergency medical services person has experienced a significant exposure to the source individual;</p>
          <p>(2) the court imposes appropriate safeguards against unauthorized disclosure that must specify the persons who have access to the test results and the purposes for which the test results may be used;</p>
          <p>(3) a licensed physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant for the emergency medical services person needs the test results for beginning, continuing, modifying, or discontinuing medical treatment for the emergency medical services person; and</p>
          <p>(4) the court finds a compelling need for the test results. In assessing compelling need, the court shall weigh the need for the court-ordered blood collection and test results against the interests of the source individual, including, but not limited to, privacy, health, safety, or economic interests. The court shall also consider whether the involuntary blood collection and testing would serve the public interest.</p>
          <p>(d) The court shall conduct the proceeding in camera unless the petitioner or the source individual requests a hearing in open court and the court determines that a public hearing is necessary to the public interest and the proper administration of justice.</p>
          <p>(e) The court shall conduct an ex parte hearing if the source individual does not attend the noticed hearing and the petitioner complied with the notice requirements in paragraph (a).</p>
          <p>(f) The source individual has the right to counsel in any proceeding brought under this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(g) The court may order a source individual taken into custody by a peace officer for purposes of obtaining a blood sample if the source individual does not comply with an order issued by the court pursuant to paragraph (c). The source individual shall be held no longer than is necessary to secure a blood sample. A person may not be held for more than 24 hours without receiving a court hearing.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7407.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/422/#laws.0.11.0">2000 c 422 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/145/#laws.0.1.0">2016 c 145 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.4.50.0">2020 c 115 art 4 s 50</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/58/#laws.0.56.0">2022 c 58 s 56</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7408">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7408 NO DISCRIMINATION.</h1>
        <p>A facility shall not base decisions about admission to a facility or the provision of care or treatment on any requirement that the source individual consent to blood-borne pathogen testing under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7408.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/422/#laws.0.12.0">2000 c 422 s 12</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7409">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7409 USE OF TEST RESULTS.</h1>
        <p>Blood-borne pathogen test results of a source individual obtained under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a> are for diagnostic purposes and to determine the need for treatment or medical care specific to a blood-borne pathogen-related illness of an emergency medical services person. The test results may not be used as evidence in any criminal proceedings or civil proceedings, except for procedures under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4171">144.4171</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.4186">144.4186</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7409.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/422/#laws.0.13.0">2000 c 422 s 13</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7411">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7411 TEST INFORMATION CONFIDENTIALITY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7411.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Private data.</span></h2>
          <p>Information concerning test results obtained under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a> is information protected from disclosure without consent under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.291">144.291</a> to 144.298 with respect to private facilities and private data as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.12">13.02, subdivision 12</a>, with respect to public facilities.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7411.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Consent to release information.</span></h2>
          <p>No facility, individual, or employer shall disclose to an emergency medical services person the name, address, or other uniquely identifying information about a source individual without a written release signed by the source individual or the source individual's legally authorized representative. The facility shall not record the name, address, or other uniquely identifying information about the source individual's test results in the emergency medical services person's medical records.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7411.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/422/#laws.0.14.0">2000 c 422 s 14</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.10.15.0">2007 c 147 art 10 s 15</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7412">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7412 PENALTY FOR UNAUTHORIZED RELEASE OF INFORMATION.</h1>
        <p>Unauthorized release by an individual, facility, or agency of a source individual's name, address, or other uniquely identifying information under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a> is subject to the remedies and penalties under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.08">13.08</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.09">13.09</a>.
