This section does not preclude private causes of action against an individual, state agency, statewide system, political subdivision, or person responsible for releasing private data or information protected from disclosure.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7412.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/422/#laws.0.15.0">2000 c 422 s 15</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7413">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7413 RESPONSIBILITY FOR TESTING AND TREATMENT; COSTS.</h1>
        <p>(a) The facility shall ensure that tests under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a> are performed if requested by the emergency medical services person or emergency medical services agency, provided the conditions set forth in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a> are met.</p>
        <p>(b) The emergency medical services agency that employs the emergency medical services person who requests testing under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a> must pay or arrange payment for the cost of counseling, testing, and treatment of the emergency medical services person and costs associated with the testing of the source individual.</p>
        <p>(c) A facility shall have a protocol that states whether the facility will pay for the cost of counseling, testing, or treatment of a person executing a citizen's arrest under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/629.30">629.30</a> or acting as a Good Samaritan under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/604A.01">604A.01</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7413.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/422/#laws.0.16.0">2000 c 422 s 16</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7414">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7414 PROTOCOLS FOR EXPOSURE TO BLOOD-BORNE PATHOGENS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7414.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">EMS agency requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>The emergency medical services agency shall have procedures for an emergency medical services person to notify a facility that the person may have experienced a significant exposure from a source individual. The emergency medical services agency shall also have a protocol to locate the source individual if the facility has not received the source individual and the emergency medical services agency knows the source individual's identity.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7414.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Facility protocol requirements.</span></h2>
          <p>Every facility shall adopt and follow a postexposure protocol for emergency medical services persons who have experienced a significant exposure. The postexposure protocol must adhere to the most current recommendations of the United States Public Health Service and include, at a minimum, the following:</p>
          <p>(1) a process for emergency medical services persons to report an exposure in a timely fashion;</p>
          <p>(2) a process for an infectious disease specialist, or a licensed physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant who is knowledgeable about the most current recommendations of the United States Public Health Service in consultation with an infectious disease specialist, (i) to determine whether a significant exposure to one or more blood-borne pathogens has occurred and (ii) to provide, under the direction of a licensed physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant, a recommendation or recommendations for follow-up treatment appropriate to the particular blood-borne pathogen or pathogens for which a significant exposure has been determined;</p>
          <p>(3) if there has been a significant exposure, a process to determine whether the source individual has a blood-borne pathogen through disclosure of test results, or through blood collection and testing as required by sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a>;</p>
          <p>(4) a process for providing appropriate counseling prior to and following testing for a blood-borne pathogen regarding the likelihood of blood-borne pathogen transmission and follow-up recommendations according to the most current recommendations of the United States Public Health Service, recommendations for testing, and treatment to the emergency medical services person;</p>
          <p>(5) a process for providing appropriate counseling under clause (4) to the emergency medical services person and the source individual; and</p>
          <p>(6) compliance with applicable state and federal laws relating to data practices, confidentiality, informed consent, and the patient bill of rights.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.7414.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2000/0/422/#laws.0.17.0">2000 c 422 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.4.51.0">2020 c 115 art 4 s 51</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/58/#laws.0.57.0">2022 c 58 s 57</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.7415">
        <h1 class="shn">144.7415 PENALTIES AND IMMUNITY.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7415.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Penalties.</span></h2>
          <p>Any facility or person who willfully violates the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a> is guilty of a misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.7415.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Immunity.</span></h2>
          <p>A facility, licensed physician, advanced practice registered nurse, physician assistant, and designated health care personnel are immune from liability in any civil, administrative, or criminal action relating to the disclosure of test results to an emergency medical services person or emergency medical services agency and the testing of a blood sample from the source individual for blood-borne pathogens if a good faith effort has been made to comply with sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7401">144.7401</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.7415">144.7415</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="section" id="stat.144.84">
        <h1 class="shn">144.84 CIVIL SERVICE CLASSIFICATION.</h1>
        <p>The commissioner of management and budget and the Civil Service Commission shall establish a classification to be known as "counselor on alcoholism" the qualifications of which shall give recognition to the value and desirability of recovered alcoholics in performing the duties of their employment.</p>
      </div>

      <h1 class="fgh">HUMAN GENETICS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.91">
        <h1 class="shn">144.91 POWERS AND DUTIES.</h1>
        <p>The state commissioner of health is authorized to develop and carry on a program in the field of human genetics which shall include the collection and interpretation of data relating to human hereditary diseases and pathologic conditions; the assembly, preparation and dissemination of informational material on the subject for professional counselors and the lay public; the conduct of such research studies as may stimulate reduction in the frequency of manifestation of various deleterious genes, and the provision of counseling services to the public on problems of human genetics. It shall consult and cooperate with the University of Minnesota, the Public Health Service and the Children's Bureau of the Department of Health, Education and Welfare, and with nationally recognized scientific and professional organizations engaged in studying the problems of human genetics.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.91.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/572/#laws.0.1.0">1959 c 572 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1977/0/305/#laws.0.45.0">1977 c 305 s 45</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.92">
        <h1 class="shn">144.92 GRANTS OR GIFTS.</h1>
        <p>The board is authorized to receive and expend in accordance with approved plans such funds as may be granted by the Public Health Service or any other federal agency which may appropriate funds for this purpose, or such funds as may be received as gifts from private organizations and individuals to the state for carrying out the purposes of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.91">144.91</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.92.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1959/0/572/#laws.0.2.0">1959 c 572 s 2</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1981/1/4/#laws.1.78.0">1Sp1981 c 4 art 1 s 78</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.93"><b>144.93</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1973/0/250/#laws.0.2.0">1973 c 250 s 2</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.94"><b>144.94</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/209/#laws.0.40.0">1987 c 209 s 40</a>]</div>
      <h1 class="fgh">MOSQUITO CONTROL</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.945">
        <h1 class="shn">144.945 ZIKA PREPAREDNESS AND RESPONSE.</h1>
        <p>The commissioner of health shall seek additional federal funds for the following statewide planning, coordination, preparation, and response activities related to the Zika virus:</p>
        <p>(1) maintaining state and local public health readiness to address Zika-related public health threats;</p>
        <p>(2) conducting diagnostic tests of patients who meet criteria for Zika testing and maintaining enhanced laboratory surveillance activities related to Zika;</p>
        <p>(3) engaging in Zika surveillance activities, including evaluating patients for testing based on criteria, advising health care providers on Zika virus research, providing recommendations and interpretations of test results, and conducting Zika-related public awareness and prevention activities; and</p>
        <p>(4) conducting mosquito surveillance activities under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.95">144.95</a> to enhance monitoring of areas where mosquitoes carrying the Zika virus may be found in Minnesota, notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.95#stat.144.95.10">144.95, subdivision 10</a>.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.945.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first">
          <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2016/0/179/#laws.0.5.0">2016 c 179 s 5</a>
        </p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.95">
        <h1 class="shn">144.95 MOSQUITO RESEARCH PROGRAM.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.95.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Research program.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall establish and maintain a long-range program of research to study:</p>
          <p>(1) the basic biology, distribution, population ecology, and biosystematics of Minnesota mosquitoes;</p>
          <p>(2) the impact of mosquitoes on human and animal health and the economy, including such areas as recreation, tourism, and livestock production;</p>
          <p>(3) the baseline population and environmental status of organisms other than mosquitoes that may be affected by mosquito management;</p>
          <p>(4) the effects of mosquito management strategies on animals and plants that may result in changes in ecology of specific areas;</p>
          <p>(5) the development of mosquito management strategies that are effective, practical, and environmentally safe; and</p>
          <p>(6) the costs and benefits of development of local and regional management and educational programs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.95.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Research facility and field stations.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner of health shall establish and maintain mosquito management research and development facilities, including but not limited to field research stations in the major mosquito ecologic regions and a center for basic mosquito management research and development. The commissioner shall, to the extent possible, contract with the University of Minnesota in establishing, maintaining, and staffing the research facilities.</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioner of health shall establish and implement a program of contractual research grants with public and private agencies and individuals in order to:</p>
          <p>(1) undertake supplemental research studies on basic mosquito biology, physiology, and life cycle history beyond those described in subdivision 1;</p>
          <p>(2) undertake research into the effects of mosquitoes on human health, including vector-borne diseases, and on animal health, including agricultural and wildlife effects;</p>
          <p>(3) undertake studies of other economic factors including tourism and recreation;</p>
          <p>(4) collect and analyze baseline data on the ecology and distribution of organisms other than mosquitoes that may be affected as a result of mosquito management strategies;</p>
          <p>(5) develop new, effective, practical, and biologically compatible control methods and materials;</p>
          <p>(6) conduct additional monitoring of the environmental effects of mosquito control methods and materials; and</p>
          <p>(7) undertake demonstration, training, and education programs for development of local and regional mosquito management programs.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.95.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Conduct research trials.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health may develop and conduct research trials of mosquito management methods and materials. Trials may be conducted, with the agreement of the public or private landholder, wherever and whenever the commissioner considers necessary to provide accurate data for determining the efficacy of a method or material in controlling mosquitoes.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.95.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Research trials.</span></h2>
          <p>Research trials of mosquito management methods and materials are subject to the following laws and rules unless a specific written exemption, license, or waiver is granted; sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/84.0895">84.0895</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/103G.615">103G.615</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/97A.045#stat.97A.045.1">97A.045, subdivision 1</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/103A.201">103A.201</a>, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/103G.255">103G.255</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/103G.275">103G.275</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/103G.285">103G.285</a>; and Minnesota Rules, chapters 1505, 6115, 6120, 6134, and 6140.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.95.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">General authority.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) To carry out subdivisions 1 to 4, the commissioner of health may:</p>
          <p>(1) accept money, property, or services from any source;</p>
          <p>(2) receive and hold lands;</p>
          <p>(3) accept gifts;</p>
          <p>(4) cooperate with city, state, federal, or private agencies whose research on mosquito control or on other environmental matters may be affected by the commissioner's mosquito management and research activities; and</p>
          <p>(5) enter into contracts with any public or private entity.</p>
          <p>(b) The contracts must specify the duties performed, services provided, and the amount and method of reimbursement for them. Money collected by the commissioner under contracts made under this subdivision is appropriated to the commissioner for the purposes specified in the contracts. Contractual agreements must be processed under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/16C.08">16C.08</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.95.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Authority to enter property.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health, officers, employees, or agents may, with express permission of the owner, enter upon any property at reasonable times to:</p>
          <p>(1) determine whether mosquito breeding exists;</p>
          <p>(2) examine, count, study, or collect laboratory samples to determine the property's geographic, geologic, and biologic characteristics; or</p>
          <p>(3) study and collect laboratory samples to determine the effect on animals and vegetation of an insecticide, herbicide, or other method used to control mosquitoes.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.95.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Research plots.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health may lease and maintain experimental plots of land for mosquito research. The commissioner of health shall determine the locations of the experimental plots and may enter into agreements with any public or private agency or individual to lease the land. The commissioners of agriculture, natural resources, transportation, and iron range resources and rehabilitation shall cooperate with the commissioner of health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.95.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Emergencies.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may suspend or revoke a contract, agreement, or delegated authority granted in this section at any time and without prior notice if an emergency, accident, or hazard threatens the public health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.95.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/7/#laws.2.67.0">1997 c 7 art 2 s 67</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.95.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Contingency.</span></h2>
          <p>This section is effective only if the tax on cigarettes imposed by United States Code, title 26, section 5701, as amended, is reduced after June 1, 1985, or if other public or private funds sufficient to fund the program are made available to the commissioner for the purposes of this program.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.95.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1985/1/14/#laws.19.17.0">1Sp1985 c 14 art 19 s 17</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/149/#laws.2.10.0">1987 c 149 art 2 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1987/0/312/#laws.1.26.0">1987 c 312 art 1 s 26</a> subd 2; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1990/0/391/#laws.8.29.0">1990 c 391 art 8 s 29</a>; art 10 s 3; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1993/0/163/#laws.1.25.0">1993 c 163 art 1 s 25</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/386/#laws.2.57.0">1998 c 386 art 2 s 57</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">LEAD POISONING PREVENTION ACT</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.9501">
        <h1 class="shn">144.9501 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Citation.</span></h2>
          <p>Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9501">144.9501</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9512">144.9512</a> may be cited as the "Lead Poisoning Prevention Act."</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Applicability.</span></h2>
          <p>The definitions in this section apply to sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9501">144.9501</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9512">144.9512</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Abatement.</span></h2>
          <p>"Abatement" means any set of measures intended to eliminate known or presumed lead hazards. Abatement includes:</p>
          <p>(1) the removal of lead-based paint and lead-contaminated dust, the permanent enclosure or encapsulation of lead-based paint, the replacement of lead-painted surfaces or fixtures, and the removal or enclosure of lead-contaminated soil; and</p>
          <p>(2) all preparation, cleanup, disposal, and postabatement clearance testing activities associated with these measures.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Areas at high risk for toxic lead exposure.</span></h2>
          <p>"Areas at high risk for toxic lead exposure" means a census tract in a city of the first class or a county or area within a county outside a city of the first class that has been determined to be at high risk for toxic lead exposure under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9503">144.9503</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.4a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4a.<span class="headnote">Assessing agency.</span></h2>
          <p>"Assessing agency" means the commissioner or a community health board with authority and responsibility to conduct lead risk assessments in response to reports of children or pregnant women with elevated blood lead levels.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Bare soil.</span></h2>
          <p>"Bare soil" means any visible soil that is at least an area of 36 contiguous square inches.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p>[Renumbered subd 7a]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.6a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6a.<span class="headnote">Child.</span></h2>
          <p>"Child" means an individual up to 72 months of age.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.6b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6b.<span class="headnote">Clearance inspection.</span></h2>
          <p>"Clearance inspection" means a visual identification of deteriorated paint and bare soil and a resampling and analysis of interior dust lead concentrations in a residence to ensure that the lead standards established in rules adopted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a> are not exceeded.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.6c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6c.<span class="headnote">Capillary blood sample.</span></h2>
          <p>"Capillary blood sample" means a quantity of blood drawn from a capillary. The sample generally is collected by finger stick.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.6d">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6d.<span class="headnote">Certified lead firm.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">"Certified lead firm" means a person that employs individuals to perform regulated lead work, with the exception of renovation, and is certified by the commissioner under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9505">144.9505</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.6e">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6e.<span class="headnote">Certified renovation firm.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">"Certified renovation firm" means a person that employs individuals to perform renovation and is certified by the commissioner under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9505">144.9505</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>"Commissioner" means the commissioner of the Minnesota Department of Health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.7a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7a.</h2>
          <p>[Renumbered subd 7b]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.7a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7a.<span class="headnote">Community health board.</span></h2>
          <p>"Community health board" means an administrative authority established under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/145A.03">145A.03</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.7b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7b.<span class="headnote">Contracting entity.</span></h2>
          <p>"Contracting entity" means a public or private body, board, individual, corporation, partnership, proprietorship, joint venture, fund, authority, or similar entity that contracts with a person to do regulated lead work.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Deteriorated paint.</span></h2>
          <p>"Deteriorated paint" means paint that is chipped, peeled, or otherwise separated from its substrate or that is attached to damaged substrate.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.8a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8a.<span class="headnote">Disclosure pamphlet.</span></h2>
          <p>"Disclosure pamphlet" means the EPA pamphlet titled "Renovate Right: Important Lead Hazard Information for Families, Child Care Providers and Schools" developed under section 406(a) of the Toxic Substance Control Act.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Elevated blood lead level.</span></h2>
          <p>"Elevated blood lead level" means a diagnostic blood lead test with a result that is equal to or greater than 3.5 micrograms of lead per deciliter of whole blood in any person, unless the commissioner finds that a lower concentration is necessary to protect public health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Encapsulation.</span></h2>
          <p>"Encapsulation" means covering a surface coated with paint that exceeds the standards under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a> with a liquid or solid material that adheres to the surface, rather than mechanically attaches to it; or covering bare soil that exceeds the standards under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a> with a permeable material such as vegetation, mulch, or soil that meets the standards under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.<span class="headnote">Enclosure.</span></h2>
          <p>"Enclosure" means covering a surface coated with paint that exceeds the standards under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a> by mechanically fastening to the surface a durable, solid material; or covering bare soil that exceeds the standards under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a> with an impermeable material, such as asphalt or concrete.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.109.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 109</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.13">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13.<span class="headnote">Intact paint.</span></h2>
          <p>"Intact paint" means paint that is not chipped, peeled, or otherwise separated from its substrate or attached to damaged substrate. Painted surfaces which may generate dust but are not chipped, peeled, or otherwise separated from their substrate or attached to damaged substrate are considered to be intact paint.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.13a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 13a.<span class="headnote">Interim controls.</span></h2>
          <p>"Interim controls" means a set of measures intended to temporarily reduce human exposure or likely exposure to known or presumed lead hazards, including specialized cleaning, repairs, maintenance, painting, temporary encapsulation, or enclosure.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.14">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 14.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.109.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 109</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.15">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 15.<span class="headnote">Lead hazard.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead hazard" means a condition that causes exposure to lead from dust, bare soil, drinking water, or deteriorated paint that exceeds the standards adopted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.16">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 16.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.109.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 109</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.17">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17.<span class="headnote">Lead hazard reduction.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) "Lead hazard reduction" means abatement, swab team services, or interim controls undertaken to make a residence, child care facility, school, playground, or other location where lead hazards are identified lead-safe by complying with the lead standards and methods adopted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a>.</p>
          <p>(b) Lead hazard reduction does not include renovation activity that is primarily intended to remodel, repair, or restore a given structure or dwelling rather than abate or control lead-based paint hazards.</p>
          <p>(c) Lead hazard reduction does not include activities that disturb painted surfaces that total:</p>
          <p>(1) less than 20 square feet (two square meters) on exterior surfaces; or</p>
          <p>(2) less than two square feet (0.2 square meters) in an interior room.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.17a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17a.<span class="headnote">Lead hazard screen.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead hazard screen" means a limited risk assessment activity that involves the visual identification of dust, paint, or bare soil and sampling and analysis of dust.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.17b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 17b.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.10.51.0">2009 c 79 art 10 s 51</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.18">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 18.<span class="headnote">Lead inspection.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead inspection" means a surface by surface investigation to determine the presence of lead content of paint and a visual identification of the existence and location of bare soil.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.19">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 19.<span class="headnote">Lead inspector.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead inspector" means a person who is licensed by the commissioner to perform a lead inspection under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9505">144.9505</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.19a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 19a.<span class="headnote">Lead project design.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead project design" means site-specific written project specifications for a regulated lead work project. Lead project design includes written technical project specifications incorporated into bidding documents.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.20">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 20.<span class="headnote">Lead order.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead order" means a legal instrument to compel a property owner to engage in lead hazard reduction according to the specifications given by the assessing agency.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.20a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 20a.<span class="headnote">Lead project designer.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead project designer" means an individual who is responsible for planning the site-specific performance of regulated lead work and who has been licensed by the commissioner under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9505">144.9505</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.20b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 20b.<span class="headnote">Lead risk assessment.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead risk assessment" means an investigation to determine the existence, nature, severity, and location of lead hazards.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.20c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 20c.<span class="headnote">Lead risk assessor.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead risk assessor" means an individual who performs lead risk assessments or lead inspections and who has been licensed by the commissioner under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9505">144.9505</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.21">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 21.<span class="headnote">Lead-safe.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead-safe" means a condition in which:</p>
          <p>(1) lead is not present;</p>
          <p>(2) lead may be present at the residence, child care facility, school, or playground, if the lead concentration in the dust, paint, soil, and water of a residence does not exceed the standards adopted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a>; or</p>
          <p>(3) if the lead concentrations in the paint or soil do exceed the standards, the paint is intact and the soil is not bare soil.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.22">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 22.<span class="headnote">Lead-safe practices.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead-safe practices" means methods for construction, renovation, remodeling, or maintenance activities that are not regulated lead work and that are performed so that they do not:</p>
          <p>(1) violate the standards under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) create lead dust through the use of prohibited practices;</p>
          <p>(3) leave debris or a lead residue that can form a dust;</p>
          <p>(4) provide a readily accessible source of lead dust, lead paint, lead paint chips, or lead-contaminated soil, after the use of containment methods; and</p>
          <p>(5) result in improper disposal of lead-contaminated debris, dust, or soil.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.22a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 22a.<span class="headnote">Lead supervisor.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead supervisor" means an individual who is responsible for the on-site performance of abatement or interim controls and who has been licensed by the commissioner under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9505">144.9505</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.22b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 22b.<span class="headnote">Lead sampling technician.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead sampling technician" means an individual who performs clearance inspections for renovation sites and lead dust sampling for nonabatement sites.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.23">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 23.<span class="headnote">Lead worker.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead worker" means an individual who performs abatement or interim control work and who has been licensed by the commissioner under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9505">144.9505</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.24">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 24.<span class="headnote">Person.</span></h2>
          <p>"Person" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/326.71#stat.326.71.8">326.71, subdivision 8</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.25">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 25.<span class="headnote">Persons at high risk for elevated blood lead level.</span></h2>
          <p>"Persons at high risk for elevated blood lead level" means:</p>
          <p>(1) a child between six and 72 months of age:</p>
          <p>(i) who lives in or visits, at least weekly, a residence, child care facility, or school built before 1978 which has peeling or chipping paint, ongoing remodeling or renovation, or bare soil; or</p>
          <p>(ii) who has a sibling, housemate, or playmate who has been diagnosed with an elevated blood lead level in the last 12 months; and</p>
          <p>(2) a pregnant female or a child between six and 72 months of age:</p>
          <p>(i) who lives in a census tract found to have a median foundation soil lead value exceeding 100 parts per million of lead;</p>
          <p>(ii) who lives near an industrial point source that emits lead;</p>
          <p>(iii) who lives near a road with an average daily traffic which exceeded 5,000 vehicles per day in 1986 or earlier; or</p>
          <p>(iv) who lives with a person whose occupation or hobby involves exposure to lead.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.25a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 25a.<span class="headnote">Play area.</span></h2>
          <p>"Play area" means any established area where children play, or on residential property, any established area where children play or bare soil is accessible to children.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.26">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 26.<span class="headnote">Primary prevention.</span></h2>
          <p>"Primary prevention" means preventing toxic lead exposure before blood levels become elevated.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.26a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 26a.<span class="headnote">Regulated lead work.</span></h2>
          <p> "Regulated lead work" means:</p>
          <p>(1) abatement;</p>
          <p>(2) interim controls;</p>
          <p>(3) a clearance inspection;</p>
          <p>(4) a lead hazard screen;</p>
          <p>(5) a lead inspection;</p>
          <p>(6) a lead risk assessment;</p>
          <p>(7) lead project designer services;</p>
          <p>(8) lead sampling technician services;</p>
          <p>(9) swab team services;</p>
          <p>(10) renovation activities;</p>
          <p>(11) lead hazard reduction; or</p>
          <p>(12) activities performed to comply with lead orders issued by an assessing agency.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.26b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 26b.<span class="headnote">Renovation.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) "Renovation" means the modification of any pre-1978 affected property for compensation that results in the disturbance of known or presumed lead-containing painted surfaces defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a>, unless that activity is performed as lead hazard reduction. A renovation performed for the purpose of converting a building or part of a building into an affected property is a renovation under this subdivision.</p>
          <p>(b) Renovation does not include minor repair and maintenance activities described in this paragraph. All activities that disturb painted surfaces and are performed within 30 days of other activities that disturb painted surfaces in the same room must be considered a single project when applying the criteria below. Unless the activity involves window replacement or demolition of a painted surface, building component, or portion of a structure, for purposes of this paragraph, "minor repair and maintenance" means activities that disturb painted surfaces totaling:</p>
          <p>(1) less than 20 square feet (two square meters) on exterior surfaces; or</p>
          <p>(2) less than six square feet (0.6 square meters) in an interior room.</p>
          <p>(c) Renovation does not include total demolition of a freestanding structure. For purposes of this paragraph, "total demolition" means demolition and disposal of all interior and exterior painted surfaces, including windows. Unpainted foundation building components remaining after total demolition may be reused.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.26c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 26c.<span class="headnote">Lead renovator.</span></h2>
          <p>"Lead renovator" means an individual who directs individuals who perform renovations. A lead renovator also performs renovation, surface coating testing, and cleaning verification.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.27">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 27.<span class="headnote">Safe housing.</span></h2>
          <p>"Safe housing" means a residence that is lead-safe.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.28">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 28.<span class="headnote">Secondary prevention.</span></h2>
          <p>"Secondary prevention" means intervention to mitigate health effects on people with elevated blood lead levels.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.28a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 28a.<span class="headnote">Standard.</span></h2>
          <p>"Standard" means a quantitative assessment of lead in any environmental media or consumer product.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.29">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 29.<span class="headnote">Swab team services.</span></h2>
          <p>"Swab team services" means activities that provide protection from lead hazards primarily through the use of interim controls, such as:</p>
          <p>(1) removing lead dust by washing, vacuuming with high efficiency particle accumulator (HEPA) or wet vacuum cleaners, and cleaning the interior of residential property;</p>
          <p>(2) removing loose paint and paint chips and repainting or installing guards to protect intact paint;</p>
          <p>(3) covering or replacing bare soil that has a lead concentration of 100 parts per million or more;</p>
          <p>(4) health education;</p>
          <p>(5) advice and assistance to help residents locate and move to a temporary residence while lead hazard reduction is being completed; or</p>
          <p>(6) any other assistance necessary to meet the resident's immediate needs as a result of the relocation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.30">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 30.<span class="headnote">Swab team worker.</span></h2>
          <p>"Swab team worker" means an individual who performs swab team services and who has been licensed by the commissioner as a lead worker under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9505">144.9505</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.31">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 31.<span class="headnote">Venous blood sample.</span></h2>
          <p>"Venous blood sample" means a quantity of blood drawn from a vein.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.32">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 32.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/205/#laws.1.43.0">2001 c 205 art 1 s 43</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.33">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 33.<span class="headnote">Compensation.</span></h2>
          <p>"Compensation" means money or other mutually agreed upon form of payment given or received for regulated lead work, including rental payments, rental income, or salaries derived from rental payments.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9501.34">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 34.<span class="headnote">Individual.</span></h2>
          <p>"Individual" means a natural person.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.9501.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/213/#laws.1.3.0">1995 c 213 art 1 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/205/#laws.0.24.0">1997 c 205 s 24</a>,25; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.34.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 34</a>-49; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/205/#laws.1.1.0">2001 c 205 art 1 s 1</a>-25; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.16.20.0">2007 c 147 art 16 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.10.8.0">2009 c 79 art 10 s 8</a>-11; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.109.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 109</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.8.27.0">2015 c 71 art 8 s 27</a>-31; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/7/#laws.3.32.0">1Sp2021 c 7 art 3 s 32</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.3.20.0">2023 c 70 art 3 s 20</a>-24; art 4 s 45</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.9502">
        <h1 class="shn">144.9502 STATEWIDE LEAD SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9502.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Surveillance.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall establish a statewide lead surveillance system. The purpose of this system is to:</p>
          <p>(1) monitor blood lead levels in children and adults to identify trends and populations at high risk for elevated blood lead levels;</p>
          <p>(2) ensure that screening services are provided to populations at high risk for elevated blood lead levels;</p>
          <p>(3) ensure that medical and environmental follow-up services for children with elevated blood lead levels are provided; and</p>
          <p>(4) provide accurate and complete data for planning and implementing primary prevention programs that focus on the populations at high risk for elevated blood lead levels.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9502.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Studies and surveys.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall collect blood lead level and exposure information, analyze the information, and conduct studies designed to determine the potential for high risk for elevated blood lead levels among children and adults.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9502.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Reports of blood lead analysis required.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Every hospital, medical clinic, medical laboratory, other facility, or individual performing blood lead analysis shall report the results after the analysis of each specimen analyzed, for both capillary and venous specimens, and epidemiologic information required in this section to the commissioner of health, within the time frames set forth in clauses (1) and (2):</p>
          <p>(1) within two working days by telephone, fax, or electronic transmission as prescribed by the commissioner, with written or electronic confirmation within one month as prescribed by the commissioner, for a venous blood lead level equal to or greater than 15 micrograms of lead per deciliter of whole blood; or</p>
          <p>(2) within one month in writing or by electronic transmission as prescribed by the commissioner, for any capillary result or for a venous blood lead level less than 15 micrograms of lead per deciliter of whole blood.</p>
          <p>(b) If a blood lead analysis is performed outside of Minnesota and the facility performing the analysis does not report the blood lead analysis results and epidemiological information required in this section to the commissioner, the provider who collected the blood specimen must satisfy the reporting requirements of this section. For purposes of this section, "provider" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/62D.02#stat.62D.02.9">62D.02, subdivision 9</a>.</p>
          <p>(c) The commissioner shall coordinate with hospitals, medical clinics, medical laboratories, and other facilities performing blood lead analysis to develop a universal reporting form and mechanism.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9502.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Blood lead analyses and epidemiologic information.</span></h2>
          <p>The blood lead analysis reports required in this section must specify:</p>
          <p>(1) whether the specimen was collected as a capillary or venous sample;</p>
          <p>(2) the date the sample was collected;</p>
          <p>(3) the results of the blood lead analysis;</p>
          <p>(4) the date the sample was analyzed;</p>
          <p>(5) the method of analysis used;</p>
          <p>(6) the full name, address, and phone number of the laboratory performing the analysis;</p>
          <p>(7) the full name, address, and phone number of the physician, advanced practice registered nurse, physician assistant, or facility requesting the analysis;</p>
          <p>(8) the full name, address, and phone number of the person with the blood lead level, and the person's birthdate, gender, and race.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9502.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Follow-up epidemiologic information.</span></h2>
          <p>The follow-up epidemiologic information required in this section must specify:</p>
          <p>(1) the name, address, and phone number of the agency or individual contacted to investigate the environment of the person with the elevated blood lead level to determine the sources of lead exposure; and</p>
          <p>(2) the name, address, and phone number of all agencies or individuals to whom the person or the person's guardian was referred for education about the sources, effects, and prevention of lead exposure.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9502.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/205/#laws.1.43.0">2001 c 205 art 1 s 43</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9502.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Reporting without liability.</span></h2>
          <p>The furnishing of the information required under this section shall not subject the person, laboratory, or other facility furnishing the information to any action for damages or relief.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9502.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Laboratory standards.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A laboratory performing blood lead analysis shall use methods that:</p>
          <p>(1) meet or exceed the proficiency standards established in the federal Clinical Laboratory Improvement Regulations, Code of Federal Regulations, title 42, section 493, promulgated in accordance with the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Act amendments of 1988, Public Law 100-578; or</p>
          <p>(2) meet or exceed the Occupational Safety and Health Standards for Lead in General Industries, Code of Federal Regulations, section 1910.1025, and Occupational Safety and Health Standards for Lead in Construction, Code of Federal Regulations, section 1926.62.</p>
          <p>(b) A laboratory performing lead analysis of paint, soil, or dust must be a laboratory recognized by the United States Environmental Protection Agency under the Toxic Substances Control Act, United States Code, title 15, section 2685, paragraph (b). Analysis of samples of drinking water must be performed by a laboratory certified by the commissioner to analyze lead in water.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9502.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Classification of data.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, including section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.05#stat.13.05.9">13.05, subdivision 9</a>, data collected by the commissioner of health about persons with blood lead levels, including analytic results from samples of paint, soil, dust, and drinking water taken from the individual's home and immediate property, shall be private and may only be used by the commissioner of health, the commissioner of labor and industry, authorized agents of Indian tribes, and authorized employees of community health boards for the purposes set forth in this section.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.9502.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/213/#laws.1.4.0">1995 c 213 art 1 s 4</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.50.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 50</a>-52; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/205/#laws.1.26.0">2001 c 205 art 1 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.109.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 109</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.4.53.0">2020 c 115 art 4 s 53</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/7/#laws.3.33.0">1Sp2021 c 7 art 3 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/58/#laws.0.59.0">2022 c 58 s 59</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.9503">
        <h1 class="shn">144.9503 PRIMARY PREVENTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9503.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Primary prevention program.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall develop and maintain a primary prevention program to reduce lead exposure in young children and pregnant women. A community health board serving a city of the first class shall determine areas at high risk for toxic lead exposure before doing primary prevention lead hazard reduction activities. The program shall provide primary prevention lead education materials, promote primary prevention swab team services, provide lead cleanup equipment and material grants as funding allows, monitor regulated lead work, and develop and maintain lead-safe practices in cooperation with the commissioner of administration.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9503.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Priorities for primary prevention.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner of health and community health boards serving cities of the first class shall determine areas at high risk for toxic lead exposure.</p>
          <p>(b) A community health board serving a city of the first class shall rank order census tracts by awarding points as specified in this paragraph. The priority for primary prevention in census tracts at high risk for toxic lead exposure shall be based on the cumulative points awarded to each census tract. A greater number of points means a higher priority.</p>
          <p>(1) One point may be awarded to a census tract for each ten percent of children who were under six years old at the time they were screened for lead in blood and whose blood lead level exceeds ten micrograms of lead per deciliter of whole blood, provided the commissioner has determined that the data used to award the points are comprehensive and representative.</p>
          <p>(2) One point may be awarded for every five percent of housing that is defined as dilapidated or deteriorated by the planning department or similar agency of the city in which the housing is located. Where data is available by neighborhood or section within a city, the percent of dilapidated or deteriorated housing shall apply equally to each census tract within the neighborhood or section.</p>
          <p>(3) One point may be awarded for every 100 parts per million of lead in soil, based on the median soil lead values of foundation soil samples, calculated on 100 parts per million intervals, or fraction thereof. A community health board shall use data from its own soil survey conducted according to rules adopted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a>, except that a community health board serving Minneapolis or St. Paul that has not conducted its own soil survey shall use the June 1988 census tract version of the houseside map titled "Distribution of Houseside Lead Content of Soil-Dust in the Twin Cities," prepared by the Center for Urban and Regional Affairs, Humphrey Institute, University of Minnesota, Publication 1989, Center for Urban and Regional Affairs 89-4. Where the map displays a census tract that is crossed by two or more intervals, the community health board shall make a reasoned determination of the median foundation soil lead value for that census tract.</p>
          <p>(4) A community health board may award one point to each census tract for each of the following factors based on cutoff criteria to be determined by the community health board:</p>
          <p>(i) percent of minority population;</p>
          <p>(ii) number of children less than six years of age;</p>
          <p>(iii) percent of housing built before 1950; and</p>
          <p>(iv) percent of population living in poverty.</p>
          <p>(c) The commissioner may determine areas at high risk for toxic lead exposure at the county level or within a county outside a city of the first class using one or more of the following criteria:</p>
          <p>(1) blood lead levels greater than ten micrograms per deciliter of whole blood in children under six years of age;</p>
          <p>(2) percent of dilapidated or deteriorated housing;</p>
          <p>(3) soil lead levels in excess of 100 parts per million;</p>
          <p>(4) percent of minority population;</p>
          <p>(5) percent of housing built before 1950;</p>
          <p>(6) percent of children living in poverty; or</p>
          <p>(7) other factors appropriate in preventing lead exposure, as determined by a federal agency including the United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the United States Environmental Protection Agency, or the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9503.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Primary prevention lead education strategy.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall develop and maintain a primary prevention lead education strategy to prevent lead exposure. The strategy includes:</p>
          <p>(1) lead education materials that describe the health effects of lead exposure, safety measures, and methods to be used in the lead hazard reduction process;</p>
          <p>(2) providing lead education materials to the general public;</p>
          <p>(3) providing lead education materials to property owners, landlords, and tenants by swab team workers and public health professionals, such as nurses, sanitarians, health educators, nonprofit organizations working on lead issues, and other public health professionals in areas at high risk for toxic lead exposure; and</p>
          <p>(4) promoting awareness of community, legal, and housing resources.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9503.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Swab team services.</span></h2>
          <p>Primary prevention may include the use of swab team services. The swab team services may be provided based on lead hazard screens whenever possible and must at least include lead hazard reduction for deteriorated interior lead-based paint, bare soil, and dust.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9503.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.109.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 109</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9503.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/205/#laws.1.27.0">2001 c 205 art 1 s 27</a>,43]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9503.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Lead-safe practices information.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall develop and maintain in cooperation with the commissioner of administration provisions and procedures to define lead-safe practices information for residential remodeling, renovation, installation, and rehabilitation activities that are not lead hazard reduction, but may disrupt lead-based paint surfaces and guidance documents for the regulated industry.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9503.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.109.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 109</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9503.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.109.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 109</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.9503.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/213/#laws.1.5.0">1995 c 213 art 1 s 5</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/451/#laws.4.14.0">1996 c 451 art 4 s 14</a>-16; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.53.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 53</a>-55; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/205/#laws.1.27.0">2001 c 205 art 1 s 27</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/206/#laws.0.28.0">2004 c 206 s 28</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.109.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 109</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.9504">
        <h1 class="shn">144.9504 SECONDARY PREVENTION.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9504.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Jurisdiction.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) A community health board serving cities of the first class must conduct lead risk assessments for purposes of secondary prevention, according to the provisions of this section. A board of health not serving cities of the first class must conduct lead risk assessments for the purposes of secondary prevention, unless they certified in writing to the commissioner by January 1, 1996, that they desired to relinquish these duties back to the commissioner. At the discretion of the commissioner, a community health board may, upon written request to the commissioner, resume these duties.</p>
          <p>(b) Lead risk assessments must be conducted by a community health board serving a city of the first class. The commissioner must conduct lead risk assessments in any area not including cities of the first class where a community health board has relinquished to the commissioner the responsibility for lead risk assessments. The commissioner shall coordinate with the community health board to ensure that the requirements of this section are met.</p>
          <p>(c) The commissioner may assist community health boards by providing technical expertise, equipment, and personnel to community health boards. The commissioner may provide laboratory or field lead-testing equipment to a community health board or may reimburse a community health board for direct costs associated with lead risk assessments.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9504.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Lead risk assessment.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Notwithstanding section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9501#stat.144.9501.6a">144.9501, subdivision 6a</a>, for purposes of this subdivision, "child" means an individual under 18 years of age.</p>
          <p>(b) An assessing agency shall conduct a lead risk assessment of a residence, residential or commercial child care facility, playground, school, or other location where lead hazards are suspected according to the venous blood lead level and time frame set forth in clauses (1) to (4) for purposes of secondary prevention:</p>
          <p>(1) within 48 hours of a child or pregnant female in the residence, residential or commercial child care facility, playground, school, or other location where lead hazards are suspected being identified to the agency as having a venous blood lead level equal to or greater than 60 micrograms of lead per deciliter of whole blood;</p>
          <p>(2) within five working days of a child or pregnant female in the residence, residential or commercial child care facility, playground, school, or other location where lead hazards are suspected being identified to the agency as having a venous blood lead level equal to or greater than 45 micrograms of lead per deciliter of whole blood;</p>
          <p>(3) within ten working days of a child or pregnant female in the residence, residential or commercial child care facility, playground, school, or other location where lead hazards are suspected being identified to the agency as having a venous blood lead level equal to or greater than ten micrograms of lead per deciliter of whole blood; or</p>
          <p>(4) within 20 working days of a child or pregnant female in the residence, residential or commercial child care facility, playground, school, or other location where lead hazards are suspected being identified to the agency as having a venous blood lead level equal to or greater than five micrograms per deciliter of whole blood.</p>
          <p class="bl">An assessing agency may refer investigations at sites other than the child's or pregnant female's residence to the commissioner.</p>
          <p>(c) Within the limits of available local, state, and federal appropriations, an assessing agency may also conduct a lead risk assessment for children with any elevated blood lead level.</p>
          <p>(d) In a building with two or more dwelling units, an assessing agency shall assess the individual unit in which the conditions of this section are met and shall inspect all common areas accessible to a child. If a child visits one or more other sites such as another residence, or a residential or commercial child care facility, playground, or school, the assessing agency shall also inspect the other sites. The assessing agency shall have one additional day added to the time frame set forth in this subdivision to complete the lead risk assessment for each additional site.</p>
          <p>(e) Within the limits of appropriations, the assessing agency shall identify the known addresses for the previous 12 months of the child or pregnant female with venous blood lead levels of at least 15 micrograms per deciliter for the child or at least ten micrograms per deciliter for the pregnant female; notify the property owners, landlords, and tenants at those addresses that an elevated blood lead level was found in a person who resided at the property; and give them primary prevention information. Within the limits of appropriations, the assessing agency may perform a risk assessment and issue corrective orders in the properties, if it is likely that the previous address contributed to the child's or pregnant female's blood lead level. The assessing agency shall provide the notice required by this subdivision without identifying the child or pregnant female with the elevated blood lead level. The assessing agency is not required to obtain the consent of the child's parent or guardian or the consent of the pregnant female for purposes of this subdivision. This information shall be classified as private data on individuals as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.02#stat.13.02.12">13.02, subdivision 12</a>.</p>
          <p>(f) The assessing agency shall conduct the lead risk assessment according to rules adopted by the commissioner under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a>. An assessing agency shall have lead risk assessments performed by lead risk assessors licensed by the commissioner according to rules adopted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a>. If a property owner refuses to allow a lead risk assessment, the assessing agency shall begin legal proceedings to gain entry to the property and the time frame for conducting a lead risk assessment set forth in this subdivision no longer applies. A lead risk assessor or assessing agency may observe the performance of lead hazard reduction in progress and shall enforce the provisions of this section under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9509">144.9509</a>. Deteriorated painted surfaces, bare soil, and dust must be tested with appropriate analytical equipment to determine the lead content, except that deteriorated painted surfaces or bare soil need not be tested if the property owner agrees to engage in lead hazard reduction on those surfaces. The lead content of drinking water must be measured if another probable source of lead exposure is not identified. Within a standard metropolitan statistical area, an assessing agency may order lead hazard reduction of bare soil without measuring the lead content of the bare soil if the property is in a census tract in which soil sampling has been performed according to rules established by the commissioner and at least 25 percent of the soil samples contain lead concentrations above the standard in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a>.</p>
          <p>(g) Each assessing agency shall establish an administrative appeal procedure which allows a property owner to contest the nature and conditions of any lead order issued by the assessing agency. Assessing agencies must consider appeals that propose lower cost methods that make the residence lead safe. The commissioner shall use the authority and appeal procedure granted under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.989">144.989</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.993">144.993</a>.</p>
          <p>(h) Sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9501">144.9501</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9512">144.9512</a> neither authorize nor prohibit an assessing agency from charging a property owner for the cost of a lead risk assessment.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9504.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Lead education strategy.</span></h2>
          <p>At the time of a lead risk assessment or following a lead order, the assessing agency shall ensure that a family will receive a visit at their residence by a swab team worker or public health professional, such as a nurse, sanitarian, public health educator, or other public health professional. The swab team worker or public health professional shall inform the property owner, landlord, and the tenant of the health-related aspects of lead exposure; nutrition; safety measures to minimize exposure; methods to be followed before, during, and after the lead hazard reduction process; and community, legal, and housing resources. If a family moves to a temporary residence during the lead hazard reduction process, lead education services should be provided at the temporary residence whenever feasible.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9504.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/205/#laws.1.43.0">2001 c 205 art 1 s 43</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9504.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Lead orders.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An assessing agency, after conducting a lead risk assessment, shall order a property owner to perform lead hazard reduction on all lead sources that exceed a standard adopted according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a>. If lead risk assessments and lead orders are conducted at times when weather or soil conditions do not permit the lead risk assessment or lead hazard reduction, external surfaces and soil lead shall be assessed, and lead orders complied with, if necessary, at the first opportunity that weather and soil conditions allow.</p>
          <p>(b) If, after conducting a lead risk assessment, an assessing agency determines that the property owner's lead hazard originated from another source location, the assessing agency may order the responsible person of the source location to:</p>
          <p>(1) perform lead hazard reduction at the site where the assessing agency conducted the lead risk assessment; and</p>
          <p>(2) remediate the conditions at the source location that allowed the lead hazard, pollutant, or contaminant to migrate from the source location.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) For purposes of this subdivision, "pollutant or contaminant" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/115B.02#stat.115B.02.13">115B.02, subdivision 13</a>, and "responsible person" has the meaning given in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/115B.03">115B.03</a>.</p>
          <p>(d) If the paint standard under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a> is violated, but the paint is intact, the assessing agency shall not order the paint to be removed unless the intact paint is a known source of actual lead exposure to a specific person. Before the assessing agency may order the intact paint to be removed, a reasonable effort must be made to protect the child and preserve the intact paint by the use of guards or other protective devices and methods.</p>
          <p>(e) Whenever windows and doors or other components covered with deteriorated lead-based paint have sound substrate or are not rotting, those components should be repaired, sent out for stripping or planed down to remove deteriorated lead-based paint, or covered with protective guards instead of being replaced, provided that such an activity is the least cost method. However, a property owner who has been ordered to perform lead hazard reduction may choose any method to address deteriorated lead-based paint on windows, doors, or other components, provided that the method is approved in rules adopted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a> and that it is appropriate to the specific property.</p>
          <p>(f) Lead orders must require that any source of damage, such as leaking roofs, plumbing, and windows, be repaired or replaced, as needed, to prevent damage to lead-containing interior surfaces.</p>
          <p>(g) The assessing agency is not required to pay for lead hazard reduction. The assessing agency shall enforce the lead orders issued to a property owner under this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9504.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Swab team services.</span></h2>
          <p>After a lead risk assessment or after issuing lead orders, the assessing agency, within the limits of appropriations and availability, shall offer the property owner the services of a swab team free of charge and, if accepted, shall send a swab team within ten working days to the residence to perform swab team services as defined in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9501">144.9501</a>. If the assessing agency provides swab team services after a lead risk assessment, but before the issuance of a lead order, swab team services do not need to be repeated after the issuance of the lead order if the swab team services fulfilled the lead order. Swab team services are not considered completed until the clearance inspection required under this section shows that the property is lead safe.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9504.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Relocation of residents.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Within the limits of appropriations, the assessing agency shall ensure that residents are relocated from rooms or dwellings during a lead hazard reduction process that generates leaded dust, such as removal or disruption of lead-based paint or plaster that contains lead.
