Residents shall not remain in rooms or dwellings where the lead hazard reduction process is occurring. An assessing agency is not required to pay for relocation unless state or federal funding is available for this purpose. The assessing agency shall make an effort to assist the resident in locating resources that will provide assistance with relocation costs. Residents shall be allowed to return to the room or dwelling after completion of the lead hazard reduction process. An assessing agency shall use grant funds under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9507">144.9507</a> if available, in cooperation with local housing agencies, to pay for moving costs and rent for a temporary residence for any low-income resident temporarily relocated during lead hazard reduction. For purposes of this section, "low-income resident" means any resident whose gross household income is at or below 185 percent of federal poverty level.</p>
          <p>(b) A resident of rental property who is notified by an assessing agency to vacate the premises during lead hazard reduction, notwithstanding any rental agreement or lease provisions:</p>
          <p>(1) shall not be required to pay rent due the landlord for the period of time the tenant vacates the premises due to lead hazard reduction;</p>
          <p>(2) may elect to immediately terminate the tenancy effective on the date the tenant vacates the premises due to lead hazard reduction; and</p>
          <p>(3) shall not, if the tenancy is terminated, be liable for any further rent or other charges due under the terms of the tenancy.</p>
          <p>(c) A landlord of rental property whose tenants vacate the premises during lead hazard reduction shall:</p>
          <p>(1) allow a tenant to return to the dwelling unit after lead hazard reduction and clearance inspection, required under this section, is completed, unless the tenant has elected to terminate the tenancy as provided for in paragraph (b); and</p>
          <p>(2) return any security deposit due under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/504B.178">504B.178</a> within five days of the date the tenant vacates the unit, to any tenant who terminates tenancy as provided for in paragraph (b).</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9504.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Property owner notification responsibility.</span></h2>
          <p>If the property owner does not hire a person licensed by the commissioner under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9505">144.9505</a> for compliance with the lead orders, the property owner shall submit a notice as to when regulated lead work will begin, according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9505#stat.144.9505.4">144.9505, subdivision 4</a>, to the assessing agency within 30 days after receiving the orders.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9504.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Clearance inspection.</span></h2>
          <p>After completion of swab team services and compliance with the lead orders by the property owner, including any repairs ordered by a local housing or building inspector, the assessing agency shall conduct a clearance inspection by visual identification of deteriorated paint and bare soil and retest the dust lead concentration in the residence to assure that violations of the lead standards under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a> no longer exist. The assessing agency is not required to test a dwelling unit after lead hazard reduction that was not ordered by the assessing agency.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9504.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Case closure.</span></h2>
          <p>A lead risk assessment is completed and the responsibility of the assessing agency ends when all of the following conditions are met:</p>
          <p>(1) lead orders are written on all known sources of violations of lead standards under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a>;</p>
          <p>(2) compliance with all lead orders has been completed; and</p>
          <p>(3) clearance inspections demonstrate that no deteriorated lead paint, bare soil, or lead dust levels exist that exceed the standards adopted under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9508">144.9508</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9504.11">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 11.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/205/#laws.1.43.0">2001 c 205 art 1 s 43</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9504.12">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 12.<span class="headnote">Blood lead level guidelines.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) By January 1, 2011, the commissioner must revise clinical and case management guidelines to include recommendations for protective health actions and follow-up services when a child's blood lead level exceeds five micrograms of lead per deciliter of blood. The revised guidelines must be implemented to the extent possible using available resources.</p>
          <p>(b) In revising the clinical and case management guidelines for blood lead levels greater than five micrograms of lead per deciliter of blood under this subdivision, the commissioner of health must consult with a statewide organization representing physicians, the public health department of Minneapolis and other public health departments, one representative of the residential construction industry, and a nonprofit organization with expertise in lead abatement.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.9504.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/213/#laws.1.6.0">1995 c 213 art 1 s 6</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/451/#laws.4.17.0">1996 c 451 art 4 s 17</a>-19; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/205/#laws.0.26.0">1997 c 205 s 26</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1997/0/228/#laws.0.12.0">1997 c 228 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.56.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 56</a>-65; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/199/#laws.2.3.0">1999 c 199 art 2 s 3</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/205/#laws.1.28.0">2001 c 205 art 1 s 28</a>-32; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/4/#laws.6.32.0">1Sp2005 c 4 art 6 s 32</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.16.20.0">2007 c 147 art 16 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2010/1/1/#laws.20.16.0">1Sp2010 c 1 art 20 s 16</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.109.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 109</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2021/1/7/#laws.3.34.0">1Sp2021 c 7 art 3 s 34</a>,35</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.9505">
        <h1 class="shn">144.9505 CREDENTIALING OF LEAD FIRMS AND PROFESSIONALS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9505.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Licensing, certification, and permitting.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Fees collected under this section shall be deposited into the state treasury and credited to the state government special revenue fund.</p>
          <p>(b) Persons shall not advertise or otherwise present themselves as lead supervisors, lead workers, lead inspectors, lead risk assessors, lead sampling technicians, lead project designers, renovation firms, or lead firms unless they have licenses or certificates issued by the commissioner under this section.</p>
          <p>(c) The fees required in this section for inspectors, risk assessors, and certified lead firms are waived for state or local government employees performing services for or as an assessing agency.</p>
          <p>(d) Individual residential property owners or an adult individual who is related to the property owner who performs regulated lead work on the residence are exempt from the licensure and firm certification requirements of this section. Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraphs (a) to (c), this exemption does not apply when the regulated lead work is a renovation performed for compensation, when a child with an elevated blood level has been identified in the residence or the building in which the residence is located, or when the residence is occupied by one or more individuals who are not related to the property owner, as defined under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/245A.02#stat.245A.02.13">245A.02, subdivision 13</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9505.1a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1a.<span class="headnote">Lead worker license.</span></h2>
          <p>Before an individual performs regulated lead work as a worker, the individual shall first obtain a license from the commissioner. No license shall be issued unless the individual shows evidence of successfully completing a training course in lead hazard control. The commissioner shall specify the course of training and testing requirements and shall charge a $50 fee annually for the license. License fees are nonrefundable and must be submitted with each application. The license must be carried by the individual and be readily available for review by the commissioner and other public health officials charged with the health, safety, and welfare of the state's citizens.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9505.1b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1b.<span class="headnote">Lead supervisor license.</span></h2>
          <p>Before an individual performs regulated lead work as a supervisor, the individual shall first obtain a license from the commissioner. No license shall be issued unless the individual shows evidence of experience and successful completion of a training course in lead hazard control. The commissioner shall specify the course of training, experience, and testing requirements and shall charge a $50 fee annually for the license. License fees are nonrefundable and must be submitted with each application. The license must be carried by the individual and be readily available for review by the commissioner and other public health officials charged with the health, safety, and welfare of the state's citizens.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9505.1c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1c.<span class="headnote">Lead inspector license.</span></h2>
          <p>Before an individual performs lead inspection services, the individual shall first obtain a license from the commissioner. No license shall be issued unless the individual shows evidence of successfully completing a training course in lead inspection. The commissioner shall specify the course of training and testing requirements and shall charge a $50 fee annually for the license. License fees are nonrefundable and must be submitted with each application. The license must be carried by the individual and be readily available for review by the commissioner and other public health officials charged with the health, safety, and welfare of the state's citizens.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9505.1d">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1d.<span class="headnote">Lead risk assessor license.</span></h2>
          <p>Before an individual performs lead risk assessor services, the individual shall first obtain a license from the commissioner. No license shall be issued unless the individual shows evidence of experience and successful completion of a training course in lead risk assessment. The commissioner shall specify the course of training, experience, and testing requirements and shall charge a $100 fee annually for the license. License fees are nonrefundable and must be submitted with each application. The license must be carried by the individual and be readily available for review by the commissioner and other public health officials charged with the health, safety, and welfare of the state's citizens.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9505.1e">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1e.<span class="headnote">Lead project designer license.</span></h2>
          <p>Before an individual performs lead project designer services, the individual shall first obtain a license from the commissioner. No license shall be issued unless the individual shows evidence of experience and successful completion of a training course in lead project design. The commissioner shall specify the course of training, experience, and testing requirements and shall charge a $100 fee annually for the license. License fees are nonrefundable and must be submitted with each application. The license must be carried by the individual and be readily available for review by the commissioner and other public health officials charged with the health, safety, and welfare of the state's citizens.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9505.1f">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1f.</h2>
          <p> [Repealed by amendment, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.8.32.0">2015 c 71 art 8 s 32</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9505.1g">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1g.<span class="headnote">Certified lead firm.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who performs or employs individuals to perform regulated lead work, with the exception of renovation, must obtain certification as a lead firm. The certificate must be in writing, contain an expiration date, be signed by the commissioner, and give the name and address of the person to whom it is issued. A lead firm certificate is valid for one year. The certification fee is $100, is nonrefundable, and must be submitted with each application. The lead firm certificate or a copy of the certificate must be readily available at the worksite for review by the contracting entity, the commissioner, and other public health officials charged with the health, safety, and welfare of the state's citizens.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9505.1h">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1h.<span class="headnote">Certified renovation firm.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who performs or employs individuals to perform renovation for compensation must obtain certification as a renovation firm. The certificate must be in writing, contain an expiration date, be signed by the commissioner, and give the name and address of the person to whom it is issued. A renovation firm certificate is valid for two years. The certification fee is $100, is nonrefundable, and must be submitted with each application. The renovation firm certificate or a copy of the certificate must be readily available at the worksite for review by the contracting entity, the commissioner, and other public health officials charged with the health, safety, and welfare of the state's citizens.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9505.1i">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 1i.<span class="headnote">Lead training course.</span></h2>
          <p>Before a person provides training to lead workers, lead supervisors, lead inspectors, lead risk assessors, lead project designers, lead sampling technicians, and lead renovators, the person shall first obtain a permit from the commissioner. The permit must be in writing, contain an expiration date, be signed by the commissioner, and give the name and address of the person to whom it is issued. A training course permit is valid for two years. Training course permit fees shall be nonrefundable and must be submitted with each application in the amount of $500 for an initial training course, $250 for renewal of a permit for an initial training course, $250 for a refresher training course, and $125 for renewal of a permit of a refresher training course.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9505.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/205/#laws.1.33.0">2001 c 205 art 1 s 33</a>,43]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9505.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>MS 2022 [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.3.83.0">2023 c 70 art 3 s 83</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9505.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Notice of regulated lead work.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) At least five working days before starting work at each regulated lead worksite, the person performing the regulated lead work shall give written notice to the commissioner and the appropriate community health board.</p>
          <p>(b) This provision does not apply to lead hazard screen, lead inspection, lead risk assessment, lead sampling technician, renovation, or lead project design activities.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9505.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/205/#laws.1.33.0">2001 c 205 art 1 s 33</a>,43]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9505.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Duties of contracting entity.</span></h2>
          <p>A contracting entity intending to have regulated lead work performed for its benefit shall include in the specifications and contracts for the work a requirement that the work be performed by contractors and subcontractors licensed by the commissioner under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9501">144.9501</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9512">144.9512</a> and according to rules adopted by the commissioner related to regulated lead work. No contracting entity shall allow regulated lead work to be performed for its benefit unless the contracting entity has seen that the person has a valid license or certificate. A contracting entity's failure to comply with this subdivision does not relieve a person from any responsibility under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9501">144.9501</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9512">144.9512</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.9505.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/213/#laws.1.7.0">1995 c 213 art 1 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1996/0/451/#laws.4.20.0">1996 c 451 art 4 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.66.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 66</a>-68; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/205/#laws.1.33.0">2001 c 205 art 1 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/140/#laws.8.30.0">2007 c 140 art 8 s 30; art 13 s 4; 2007 c 147 art 16 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.10.12.0">2009 c 79 art 10 s 12</a>,13; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.109.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 109</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.8.32.0">2015 c 71 art 8 s 32</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.3.25.0">2023 c 70 art 3 s 25</a>-27</p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.9506"><b>144.9506</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/205/#laws.1.43.0">2001 c 205 art 1 s 43</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.9507">
        <h1 class="shn">144.9507 LEAD-RELATED FUNDING.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9507.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Lead education strategy contracts.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall, within available federal or state appropriations, contract with:</p>
          <p>(1) community health boards to provide funds for lead education as provided for in sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9503">144.9503</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9504">144.9504</a>; and</p>
          <p>(2) swab team workers and community-based advocacy groups to provide funds for lead education for primary prevention of toxic lead exposure in areas at high risk for toxic lead exposure.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9507.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Lead risk assessment contracts.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall, within available federal or state appropriations, contract with community health boards to conduct lead risk assessments to determine sources of lead contamination and to issue and enforce lead orders according to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9504">144.9504</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9507.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Temporary lead-safe housing contracts.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall, within the limits of available appropriations, contract with community health boards for temporary housing, to be used in meeting relocation requirements in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9504">144.9504</a>, and award grants to community health boards for the purposes of paying housing and relocation costs under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9504">144.9504</a>. The commissioner may use up to 15 percent of the available appropriations to provide temporary lead-safe housing in areas of the state in which the commissioner has the duty under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9504">144.9504</a> to perform secondary prevention.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9507.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/245/#laws.2.45.0">1999 c 245 art 2 s 45</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9507.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Federal lead-related funds.</span></h2>
          <p>To the extent practicable under federal guidelines, the commissioner of health may use federal funding to contract with community health boards for purposes specified in this section, but only to the extent that the federal funds do not replace existing funding for these lead services.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9507.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Medical assistance.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Medical assistance reimbursement for lead risk assessment services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/256B.0625#stat.256B.0625.52">256B.0625, subdivision 52</a>, shall not be used to replace or decrease existing state or local funding for lead services and lead-related activities.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.9507.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/213/#laws.1.9.0">1995 c 213 art 1 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.71.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 71</a>-73; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/205/#laws.1.34.0">2001 c 205 art 1 s 34</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.16.8.0">2007 c 147 art 16 s 8</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.109.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 109</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.9508">
        <h1 class="shn">144.9508 RULES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9508.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Sampling and analysis.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall adopt, by rule, methods for:</p>
          <p>(1) lead inspections, lead hazard screens, lead risk assessments, and clearance inspections;</p>
          <p>(2) environmental surveys of lead in paint, soil, dust, and drinking water to determine areas at high risk for toxic lead exposure;</p>
          <p>(3) soil sampling for soil used as replacement soil;</p>
          <p>(4) drinking water sampling, which shall be done in accordance with lab certification requirements and analytical techniques specified by Code of Federal Regulations, title 40, section 141.89; and</p>
          <p>(5) sampling to determine whether at least 25 percent of the soil samples collected from a census tract within a standard metropolitan statistical area contain lead in concentrations that exceed 100 parts per million.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9508.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Regulated lead work standards and methods.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner shall adopt rules establishing regulated lead work standards and methods in accordance with the provisions of this section, for lead in paint, dust, drinking water, and soil in a manner that protects public health and the environment for all residences, including residences also used for a commercial purpose, child care facilities, playgrounds, and schools.</p>
          <p>(b) In the rules required by this section, the commissioner shall require lead hazard reduction of intact paint only if the commissioner finds that the intact paint is on a chewable or lead-dust producing surface that is a known source of actual lead exposure to a specific individual. The commissioner shall prohibit methods that disperse lead dust into the air that could accumulate to a level that would exceed the lead dust standard specified under this section. The commissioner shall work cooperatively with the commissioner of administration to determine which lead hazard reduction methods adopted under this section may be used for lead-safe practices including prohibited practices, preparation, disposal, and cleanup. The commissioner shall work cooperatively with the commissioner of the Pollution Control Agency to develop disposal procedures. In adopting rules under this section, the commissioner shall require the best available technology for regulated lead work methods, paint stabilization, and repainting.</p>
          <p>(c) The commissioner of health shall adopt regulated lead work standards and methods for lead in bare soil in a manner to protect public health and the environment. The commissioner shall adopt a maximum standard of 100 parts of lead per million in bare soil. The commissioner shall set a soil replacement standard not to exceed 25 parts of lead per million. Soil lead hazard reduction methods shall focus on erosion control and covering of bare soil.</p>
          <p>(d) The commissioner shall adopt regulated lead work standards and methods for lead in dust in a manner to protect the public health and environment. Dust standards shall use a weight of lead per area measure and include dust on the floor, on the window sills, and on window wells. Lead hazard reduction methods for dust shall focus on dust removal and other practices which minimize the formation of lead dust from paint, soil, or other sources.</p>
          <p>(e) The commissioner shall adopt lead hazard reduction standards and methods for lead in drinking water both at the tap and public water supply system or private well in a manner to protect the public health and the environment. The commissioner may adopt the rules for controlling lead in drinking water as contained in Code of Federal Regulations, title 40, part 141. Drinking water lead hazard reduction methods may include an educational approach of minimizing lead exposure from lead in drinking water.</p>
          <p>(f) The commissioner of the Pollution Control Agency shall adopt rules to ensure that removal of exterior lead-based coatings from residences and steel structures by abrasive blasting methods is conducted in a manner that protects health and the environment.</p>
          <p>(g) All regulated lead work standards shall provide reasonable margins of safety that are consistent with more than a summary review of scientific evidence and an emphasis on overprotection rather than underprotection when the scientific evidence is ambiguous.</p>
          <p>(h) No unit of local government shall have an ordinance or regulation governing regulated lead work standards or methods for lead in paint, dust, drinking water, or soil that require a different regulated lead work standard or method than the standards or methods established under this section.</p>
          <p>(i) Notwithstanding paragraph (h), the commissioner may approve the use by a unit of local government of an innovative lead hazard reduction method which is consistent in approach with methods established under this section.</p>
          <p>(j) The commissioner shall adopt rules for issuing lead orders required under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9504">144.9504</a>, rules for notification of abatement or interim control activities requirements, and other rules necessary to implement sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9501">144.9501</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9512">144.9512</a>.</p>
          <p>(k) The commissioner shall adopt rules consistent with section 402(c)(3) of the Toxic Substances Control Act and all regulations adopted thereunder to ensure that renovation in a pre-1978 affected property is conducted in a manner that protects health and the environment. Notwithstanding sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.125">14.125</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.128">14.128</a>, the authority to adopt these rules does not expire.</p>
          <p>(l) The commissioner shall adopt rules consistent with sections 406(a) and 406(b) of the Toxic Substances Control Act. Notwithstanding sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.125">14.125</a> and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/14.128">14.128</a>, the authority to adopt these rules does not expire.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9508.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Lead standards for exterior surfaces and street dust.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may, by rule, establish lead standards for exterior horizontal surfaces, concrete or other impervious surfaces, and street dust on residential property to protect the public health and the environment.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9508.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Licensure and certification.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall adopt rules to license lead supervisors, lead workers, lead project designers, lead inspectors, lead risk assessors, and lead sampling technicians. The commissioner shall also adopt rules requiring certification of firms that perform regulated lead work. The commissioner shall require periodic renewal of licenses and certificates and shall establish the renewal periods.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9508.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Lead training course.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall establish by rule requirements for training course providers and the renewal period for each lead-related training course required for certification or licensure. The commissioner shall establish criteria in rules for the content and presentation of training courses intended to qualify trainees for licensure under subdivision 3. The commissioner shall establish criteria in rules for the content and presentation of training courses for lead renovation and lead sampling technicians.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9508.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Variances.</span></h2>
          <p>In adopting the rules required under this section, the commissioner shall provide variance procedures for any provision in rules adopted under this section, except for the numerical standards for the concentrations of lead in paint, dust, bare soil, and drinking water. A variance shall be considered only according to the procedures and criteria in Minnesota Rules, parts <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4717.7000">4717.7000</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/4717.7050">4717.7050</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9508.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/205/#laws.1.43.0">2001 c 205 art 1 s 43</a>]</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.9508.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/213/#laws.1.10.0">1995 c 213 art 1 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.74.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 74</a>-77; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/205/#laws.1.35.0">2001 c 205 art 1 s 35</a>-39; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.16.20.0">2007 c 147 art 16 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.10.14.0">2009 c 79 art 10 s 14</a>-16; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/71/#laws.8.33.0">2015 c 71 art 8 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2023/0/70/#laws.3.28.0">2023 c 70 art 3 s 28</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.9509">
        <h1 class="shn">144.9509 ENFORCEMENT.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9509.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Enforcement.</span></h2>
          <p>When the commissioner exercises authority for enforcement, the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9501">144.9501</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9512">144.9512</a> shall be enforced under the provisions of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.989">144.989</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.993">144.993</a>. Community health boards shall enforce a lead order issued under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9504">144.9504</a> under a local ordinance or as a public health nuisance under chapter 145A.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9509.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Discrimination.</span></h2>
          <p>A person who discriminates against or otherwise sanctions an employee who complains to or cooperates with the assessing agency in administering sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9501">144.9501</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9512">144.9512</a> is guilty of a petty misdemeanor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9509.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Enforcement and status report.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner shall examine compliance with Minnesota's existing lead standards and rules and report to the legislature biennially, beginning February 15, 1997, including an evaluation of current lead program activities by the state and community health boards, the need for any additional enforcement procedures, recommendations on developing a method to enforce compliance with lead standards, and cost estimates for any proposed enforcement procedure. The report shall also include a summary of lead surveillance data collected by the commissioner.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.9509.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/0/213/#laws.1.11.0">1995 c 213 art 1 s 11</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/407/#laws.2.78.0">1998 c 407 art 2 s 78</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/205/#laws.1.40.0">2001 c 205 art 1 s 40</a>,41; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.16.20.0">2007 c 147 art 16 s 20</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2015/0/21/#laws.1.109.0">2015 c 21 art 1 s 109</a></p>
      </div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.951"><b>144.951</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1976/0/173/#laws.0.64.0">1976 c 173 s 64</a>]</div>
      <div class="sr" id="stat.144.9511"><b>144.9511</b> [Repealed, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/245/#laws.2.45.0">1999 c 245 art 2 s 45</a>]</div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.9512">
        <h1 class="shn">144.9512 LEAD ABATEMENT PROGRAM.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9512.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) The definitions in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9501">144.9501</a> and in this subdivision apply to this section.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) "Commissioner" means the commissioner of health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9512.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Grants; administration.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Within the limits of the available appropriation, the commissioner shall make grants to nonprofit organizations to train workers to provide lead screening, education, outreach, and swab team services for residential property. Projects that provide Americorps funding or positions, or leverage matching funds, as part of the delivery of the services must be given priority for the grant funds.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9512.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed by amendment, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.16.9.0">2007 c 147 art 16 s 9</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9512.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Eligible grant activities.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The nonprofit receiving a grant under this section must ensure that all participating lead supervisors or certified firms are licensed and that all swab team workers are certified by the Department of Health under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9505">144.9505</a>. The nonprofit organization may participate in the program by:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) providing on-the-job training for swab team workers;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) providing swab team services to meet the requirements of sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9503#stat.144.9503.4">144.9503, subdivision 4</a>, and <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9504#stat.144.9504.6">144.9504, subdivision 6</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) providing lead hazard reduction to meet the requirements of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9501">144.9501</a>, subdivision 17;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) providing lead dust cleanup equipment and materials, as described in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9503#stat.144.9503.1">144.9503, subdivision 1</a>, to residents;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) having a swab team worker instruct residents and property owners on appropriate lead control techniques, including the lead-safe directives developed by the commissioner of health;</p>
          <p class="in">(6) conducting blood lead testing events including screening children and pregnant women according to Department of Health screening guidelines;</p>
          <p class="in">(7) performing case management services according to Department of Health case management guidelines; or</p>
          <p class="in">(8) conducting mandated risk assessments under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9504#stat.144.9504.2">144.9504, subdivision 2</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9512.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Swab team workers.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">Each worker engaged in swab team services established under this section must have blood lead concentrations below 15 micrograms of lead per deciliter of whole blood as determined by a baseline blood lead screening. The nonprofit organization receiving a grant under this section is responsible for lead screening and must ensure that all swab team workers meet the standards established in this subdivision. The nonprofit organization must use appropriate workplace procedures including following the lead-safe directives developed by the commissioner of health to reduce risk of elevated blood lead levels. The nonprofit organization and participating contractors must report all employee blood lead levels that exceed 15 micrograms of lead per deciliter of whole blood to the commissioner of health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9512.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed by amendment, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.16.9.0">2007 c 147 art 16 s 9</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9512.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed by amendment, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.16.9.0">2007 c 147 art 16 s 9</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9512.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.</h2>
          <p>[Repealed by amendment, <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.16.9.0">2007 c 147 art 16 s 9</a>]</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9512.9">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 9.<span class="headnote">Program benefits.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">As a condition of providing swab team services under this section, the nonprofit organization may require a property owner to not increase rents on a property solely as a result of a substantial improvement made with public funds under the programs in this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9512.10">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 10.<span class="headnote">Requirements of nonprofit organization.</span></h2>
          <p class="in"> The nonprofit organization that is awarded a grant under this section must prepare and submit a quarterly progress report to the commissioner beginning three months after receipt of the grant.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.9512.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1995/1/3/#laws.16.13.0">1Sp1995 c 3 art 16 s 13</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1998/0/273/#laws.0.10.0">1998 c 273 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1999/0/86/#laws.1.30.0">1999 c 86 art 1 s 30</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2001/0/79/#laws.0.1.0">2001 c 79 s 1</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2002/0/379/#laws.1.41.0">2002 c 379 art 1 s 41</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2003/0/130/#laws.0.12.0">2003 c 130 s 12</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2004/0/206/#laws.0.27.0">2004 c 206 s 27</a>,52; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/0/98/#laws.1.24.0">2005 c 98 art 1 s 24</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2005/1/5/#laws.8.1.0">1Sp2005 c 5 art 8 s 1</a>-4, 7; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.16.9.0">2007 c 147 art 16 s 9</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.10.17.0">2009 c 79 art 10 s 17</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">HEALTHY HOUSING PROGRAMS</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.9513">
        <h1 class="shn">144.9513 HEALTHY HOUSING GRANTS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9513.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) For purposes of this section and sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9501">144.9501</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.9512">144.9512</a>, the following terms have the meanings given.</p>
          <p>(b) "Housing" means a room or group of rooms located within a dwelling forming a single habitable unit with facilities used or intended to be used for living, sleeping, cooking, and eating.</p>
          <p>(c) "Healthy housing" means housing that is sited, designed, built, renovated, and maintained in ways that supports the health of residents.</p>
          <p>(d) "Housing-based health threat" means a chemical, biologic, or physical agent in the immediate housing environment, including toxic lead, mold, radon, and indoor allergens and contaminants in carpets, which constitutes a potential or actual hazard to human health at acute or chronic exposure levels.</p>
          <p>(e) "Primary prevention" means preventing exposure to housing-based health threats before seeing clinical symptoms or a diagnosis.</p>
          <p>(f) "Secondary prevention" means intervention to mitigate health effects on people with housing-based health threats.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9513.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Grants; administration.</span></h2>
          <p>Grant applicants shall submit applications to the commissioner as directed by a request for proposals. Grants must be competitively awarded and recipients of a grant under this section must prepare and submit a quarterly progress report to the commissioner beginning three months after receipt of the grant. The commissioner shall provide technical assistance and program support as needed to ensure that housing-based health threats are effectively identified, mitigated, and evaluated by grantees.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.9513.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Healthy housing and implementation grants; eligible activities.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Within the limits of available appropriations, the commissioner shall make grants to support implementation of healthy housing programs to community health boards, community action agencies under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/142F.301">142F.301</a>, and nonprofit organizations with expertise in providing outreach, education, and training on healthy housing subjects and in providing comprehensive healthy housing assessments and interventions.</p>
          <p>(b) The grantee may conduct the following activities:</p>
          <p>(1) implement and maintain primary prevention programs to reduce housing-based health threats that include the following:</p>
          <p>(i) providing education materials to the general public and to property owners, contractors, code officials, health care providers, public health professionals, health educators, nonprofit organizations, and other persons and organizations engaged in housing and health issues;</p>
          <p>(ii) promoting awareness of community, legal, and housing resources; and</p>
          <p>(iii) promoting the use of hazard reduction measures in new housing construction and housing rehabilitation programs;</p>
          <p>(2) provide training on identifying and addressing housing-based health threats;</p>
          <p>(3) provide technical assistance on the implementation of mitigation measures;</p>
          <p>(4) promote adoption of evidence-based best practices for mitigation of housing-based health threats;</p>
          <p>(5) develop work practices for addressing specific housing-based health threats;</p>
          <p>(6) identify, characterize, and mitigate hazards in housing that contribute to adverse health outcomes;</p>
          <p>(7) ensure screening services and other secondary prevention measures are provided to populations at high risk for housing-related health threats;</p>
          <p>(8) promote compliance with Department of Health guidelines and other best practices, as identified by the commissioner, for preventing or reducing housing-based health threats;</p>
          <p>(9) establish local or regional collaborative groups to ensure that resources for addressing housing-based health threats are coordinated; or</p>
          <p>(10) develop model programs for addressing housing-based health threats.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

			">

      <h1 class="fgh">EARLY HEARING DETECTION AND INTERVENTION PROGRAM</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.966">
        <h1 class="shn">144.966 EARLY HEARING DETECTION AND INTERVENTION PROGRAM.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.966.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Definitions.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) "Child" means a person 18 years of age or younger.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) "False positive rate" means the proportion of infants identified as having a significant hearing loss by the screening process who are ultimately found to not have a significant hearing loss.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) "False negative rate" means the proportion of infants not identified as having a significant hearing loss by the screening process who are ultimately found to have a significant hearing loss.</p>
          <p class="in">(d) "Hearing screening test" means automated auditory brain stem response, otoacoustic emissions, or another appropriate screening test approved by the Department of Health.</p>
          <p class="in">(e) "Hospital" means a birthing health care facility or birthing center licensed in this state that provides obstetrical services.</p>
          <p class="in">(f) "Infant" means a child who is not a newborn and has not attained the age of one year.</p>
          <p class="in">(g) "Newborn" means an infant 28 days of age or younger.</p>
          <p class="in">(h) "Parent" means a natural parent, stepparent, adoptive parent, guardian, or custodian of a newborn or infant.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.966.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Newborn Hearing Screening Advisory Committee.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) The commissioner of health shall establish a Newborn Hearing Screening Advisory Committee to advise and assist the Department of Health; Department of Children, Youth, and Families; and the Department of Education in:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) developing protocols and timelines for screening, rescreening, and diagnostic audiological assessment and early medical, audiological, and educational intervention services for children who are deaf or hard-of-hearing;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) designing protocols for tracking children from birth through age three that may have passed newborn screening but are at risk for delayed or late onset of permanent hearing loss;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) designing a technical assistance program to support facilities implementing the screening program and facilities conducting rescreening and diagnostic audiological assessment;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) designing implementation and evaluation of a system of follow-up and tracking; and</p>
          <p class="in">(5) evaluating program outcomes to increase effectiveness and efficiency and ensure culturally appropriate services for children with a confirmed hearing loss and their families.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) The commissioner of health shall appoint at least one member from each of the following groups with no less than two of the members being deaf or hard-of-hearing:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) a representative from a consumer organization representing culturally deaf persons;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) a parent with a child with hearing loss representing a parent organization;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) a consumer from an organization representing oral communication options;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) a consumer from an organization representing cued speech communication options;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) an audiologist who has experience in evaluation and intervention of infants and young children;</p>
          <p class="in">(6) a speech-language pathologist who has experience in evaluation and intervention of infants and young children;</p>
          <p class="in">(7) two primary care providers who have experience in the care of infants and young children, one of which shall be a pediatrician;</p>
          <p class="in">(8) a representative from the early hearing detection intervention teams;</p>
          <p class="in">(9) a representative from the Department of Education resource center for the deaf and hard-of-hearing or the representative's designee;</p>
          <p class="in">(10) a representative of the Commission of the Deaf, DeafBlind and Hard of Hearing;</p>
          <p class="in">(11) a representative from the Department of Human Services Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing Services Division;</p>
          <p class="in">(12) one or more of the Part C coordinators from the Department of Education; the Department of Health; the Department of Children, Youth, and Families; or the Department of Human Services or the department's designees;</p>
          <p class="in">(13) the Department of Health early hearing detection and intervention coordinators;</p>
          <p class="in">(14) two birth hospital representatives from one rural and one urban hospital;</p>
          <p class="in">(15) a pediatric geneticist;</p>
          <p class="in">(16) an otolaryngologist;</p>
          <p class="in">(17) a representative from the Newborn Screening Advisory Committee under this subdivision;</p>
          <p class="in">(18) a representative of the Department of Education regional low-incidence facilitators;</p>
          <p>(19) a representative from the deaf mentor program; and</p>
          <p>(20) a representative of the Minnesota State Academy for the Deaf from the Minnesota State Academies staff.</p>
          <p class="bl">The commissioner must complete the initial appointments required under this subdivision by September 1, 2007, and the initial appointments under clauses (19) and (20) by September 1, 2019.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) The Department of Health member shall chair the first meeting of the committee. At the first meeting, the committee shall elect a chair from its membership. The committee shall meet at the call of the chair, at least four times a year. The committee shall adopt written bylaws to govern its activities. The Department of Health shall provide technical and administrative support services as required by the committee. These services shall include technical support from individuals qualified to administer infant hearing screening, rescreening, and diagnostic audiological assessments.</p>
          <p class="in">Members of the committee shall receive no compensation for their service, but shall be reimbursed as provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/15.059">15.059</a> for expenses incurred as a result of their duties as members of the committee.</p>
          <p>(d) By February 15, 2015, and by February 15 of the odd-numbered years after that date, the commissioner shall report to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over health and data privacy on the activities of the committee that have occurred during the past two years.</p>
          <p class="in">(e) This subdivision expires June 30, 2025.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.966.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Early hearing detection and intervention programs.</span></h2>
          <p class="in"> All hospitals shall establish an early hearing detection and intervention (EHDI) program. Each EHDI program shall:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) in advance of any hearing screening testing, provide to the newborn's or infant's parents or parent information concerning the nature of the screening procedure, applicable costs of the screening procedure, the potential risks and effects of hearing loss, and the benefits of early detection and intervention;</p>
          <p class="in">(2) comply with parental election as described under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.125#stat.144.125.4">144.125, subdivision 4</a>;</p>
          <p class="in">(3) develop policies and procedures for screening and rescreening based on Department of Health recommendations;</p>
          <p class="in">(4) provide appropriate training and monitoring of individuals responsible for performing hearing screening tests as recommended by the Department of Health;</p>
          <p class="in">(5) test the newborn's hearing prior to discharge, or, if the newborn is expected to remain in the hospital for a prolonged period, testing shall be performed prior to three months of age or when medically feasible;</p>
          <p class="in">(6) develop and implement procedures for documenting the results of all hearing screening tests;</p>
          <p class="in">(7) inform the newborn's or infant's parents or parent; primary care physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant; and the Department of Health according to recommendations of the Department of Health of the results of the hearing screening test or rescreening if conducted, or if the newborn or infant was not successfully tested. The hospital that discharges the newborn or infant to home is responsible for the screening; and</p>
          <p class="in">(8) collect performance data specified by the Department of Health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.966.3a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Support services to families.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) The commissioner shall contract with a nonprofit organization to provide support and assistance to families with children who are deaf or have a hearing loss. The family support provided must include:</p>
          <p class="in">(1) direct hearing loss specific parent-to-parent assistance and unbiased information on communication, educational, and medical options; and</p>
          <p class="in">(2) individualized deaf or hard-of-hearing mentors who provide education, including instruction in American Sign Language as an available option.</p>
          <p class="bl">The commissioner shall give preference to a nonprofit organization that has the ability to provide these services throughout the state.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) Family participation in the support and assistance services is voluntary.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.966.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Notification and information; data retention and destruction.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) Notification to the parents or parent, primary care provider, and the Department of Health shall occur prior to discharge or no later than ten days following the date of testing. Notification shall include information recommended by the Department of Health and information regarding the right of the parent or legal guardian to discontinue storage of the test results and require destruction under paragraph (d).</p>
          <p class="in">(b) A physician, nurse, midwife, or other health professional attending a birth outside a hospital or institution shall provide information, orally and in writing, as established by the Department of Health, to parents regarding places where the parents may have their infant's hearing screened and the importance of the screening.</p>
          <p class="in">(c) The professional conducting the diagnostic procedure to confirm the hearing loss must report the results to the parents, primary care provider, and Department of Health according to the Department of Health recommendations.</p>
          <p>(d) The Department of Health may store hearing screening and rescreening test results for a period of time not to exceed 18 years from the infant's date of birth.</p>
          <p>(e) Notwithstanding paragraph (d), a parent or legal guardian may instruct the Department of Health to discontinue storing hearing screening and rescreening test results by providing a signed and dated form requesting destruction of the test results. The Department of Health shall make necessary forms available on the department's website. If a parent or legal guardian instructs the Department of Health to discontinue storing hearing screening and rescreening test results, the Department of Health shall destroy the test results within one month of receipt of the instruction or within 25 months after it received the last test result, whichever is later.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.966.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Oversight responsibility.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The Department of Health shall exercise oversight responsibility for EHDI programs, including establishing a performance data set and reviewing performance data collected by each hospital.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.966.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Civil and criminal immunity and penalties.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">(a) No physician, advanced practice registered nurse, physician assistant, or hospital shall be civilly or criminally liable for failure to conduct hearing screening testing.</p>
          <p class="in">(b) No physician, midwife, nurse, physician assistant, other health professional, or hospital acting in compliance with this section shall be civilly or criminally liable for any acts conforming with this section, including furnishing information required according to this section.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.966.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Fees.</span></h2>
          <p class="in">The commissioner shall charge a fee so that the total of fees collected will approximate the costs of implementing and maintaining a system to follow up on infants and provide technical assistance, a tracking system, data management, and evaluation. The fee shall be incorporated in the fee charged under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.125">144.125</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.966.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Construction.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, nothing in this section shall be construed as constituting newborn screening activities conducted under sections <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.125">144.125</a> to <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.128">144.128</a>. Data collected by or submitted to the Department of Health pursuant to this section is not genetic information for purposes of section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/13.386">13.386</a>.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.966.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2007/0/147/#laws.16.10.0">2007 c 147 art 16 s 10</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.10.18.0">2009 c 79 art 10 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/86/#laws.1.18.0">2009 c 86 art 1 s 18</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/82/#laws.0.13.0">2013 c 82 s 13</a>-16; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2013/0/108/#laws.12.34.0">2013 c 108 art 12 s 34</a>,35; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2018/0/121/#laws.0.7.0">2018 c 121 s 7</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2019/1/9/#laws.11.36.0">1Sp2019 c 9 art 11 s 36</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2020/0/115/#laws.4.54.0">2020 c 115 art 4 s 54</a>,55; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2022/0/58/#laws.0.60.0">2022 c 58 s 60</a>,61; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2024/0/115/#laws.16.4.0">2024 c 115 art 16 s 4</a></p>
      </div>
      <h1 class="fgh">ACCREDITATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL LABORATORIES</h1>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.97">
        <h1 class="shn">144.97 DEFINITIONS.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.97.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Scope.</span></h2>
          <p>The definitions in this section apply to section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.98">144.98</a>.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.97.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Accreditation.</span></h2>
          <p>"Accreditation" means written acknowledgment that a laboratory has the policies, procedures, equipment, and practices to produce reliable data in the analysis of environmental samples.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.97.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Commissioner.</span></h2>
          <p>"Commissioner" means the commissioner of health.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.97.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Commercial laboratory.</span></h2>
          <p>"Commercial laboratory" means a laboratory that performs tests on samples on a contract or fee-for-service basis.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.97.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">Environmental sample.</span></h2>
          <p>"Environmental sample" means a substance derived from a nonhuman source and collected for the purpose of analysis.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.97.5a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5a.<span class="headnote">Field of testing.</span></h2>
          <p>"Field of testing" means the combination of analyte, method, matrix, and test category for which a laboratory may hold accreditation.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.97.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Laboratory.</span></h2>
          <p>"Laboratory" means the state, a person, corporation, or other entity, including governmental, that examines, analyzes, or tests samples in a specified physical location.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.97.7">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 7.<span class="headnote">Sample.</span></h2>
          <p>"Sample" means a substance derived from a nonhuman source and collected for the purpose of analysis, or a tissue, blood, excretion, or other bodily fluid specimen obtained from a human for the detection of a chemical, etiologic agent, or histologic abnormality.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.97.8">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 8.<span class="headnote">Test category.</span></h2>
          <p>"Test category" means the combination of program and category as provided by section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/144.98">144.98, subdivisions 3</a>, paragraph (b), clauses (1) to (10), and 3a, paragraph (a), clauses (1) to (5).</p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="history" id="stat.144.97.history
			">
        <h2>History: </h2>
        <p class="first"><a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/1988/0/689/#laws.2.33.0">1988 c 689 art 2 s 33</a>; <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/laws/2009/0/79/#laws.10.19.0">2009 c 79 art 10 s 19</a>-23</p>
      </div>
      <div class="section" id="stat.144.98">
        <h1 class="shn">144.98 ACCREDITATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL LABORATORIES.</h1>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.98.1">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subdivision 1.<span class="headnote">Authorization.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health shall accredit environmental laboratories according to national standards developed using a consensus process as established by Circular A-119, published by the United States Office of Management and Budget.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.98.2">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2.<span class="headnote">Rules and standards.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner may adopt rules to carry out the commissioner's responsibilities under the national standards specified in subdivisions 1 and 2a.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.98.2a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 2a.<span class="headnote">Standards.</span></h2>
          <p>Notwithstanding the exemptions in subdivisions 8 and 9, the commissioner shall accredit laboratories according to the most current environmental laboratory accreditation standards under subdivision 1 and as accepted by the accreditation bodies recognized by the National Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (NELAP) of the NELAC Institute.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.98.3">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3.<span class="headnote">Annual fees.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) An application for accreditation under subdivision 6 must be accompanied by the annual fees specified in this subdivision. The annual fees include:</p>
          <p>(1) base accreditation fee, $600;</p>
          <p>(2) sample preparation techniques fee, $200 per technique;</p>
          <p>(3) an administrative fee for laboratories located outside this state, $2,000; and</p>
          <p>(4) test category fees.</p>
          <p>(b) For the programs in subdivision 3a, the commissioner may accredit laboratories for fields of testing under the categories listed in clauses (1) to (10) upon completion of the application requirements provided by subdivision 6 and receipt of the fees for each category under each program that accreditation is requested. The categories offered and related fees include:</p>
          <p>(1) microbiology, $200;</p>
          <p>(2) inorganics, $200;</p>
          <p>(3) metals, $500;</p>
          <p>(4) volatile organics, $1,000;</p>
          <p>(5) other organics, $1,000;</p>
          <p>(6) radiochemistry, $750;</p>
          <p>(7) emerging contaminants, $1,000;</p>
          <p>(8) agricultural contaminants, $1,000;</p>
          <p>(9) toxicity (bioassay), $500; and</p>
          <p>(10) physical characterization, $250.</p>
          <p>(c) The total annual fee includes the base fee, the sample preparation techniques fees, the test category fees per program, and, when applicable, an administrative fee for out-of-state laboratories.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.98.3a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3a.<span class="headnote">Available programs, categories, and analytes.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) The commissioner shall accredit laboratories that test samples under the following programs:</p>
          <p>(1) the clean water program, such as compliance monitoring under the federal Clean Water Act, and ambient monitoring of surface and groundwater, or analysis of biological tissue;</p>
          <p>(2) the safe drinking water program, including compliance monitoring under the federal Safe Drinking Water Act, and the state requirements for monitoring private wells;</p>
          <p>(3) the resource conservation and recovery program, including federal and state requirements for monitoring solid and hazardous wastes, biological tissue, leachates, and groundwater monitoring wells not intended as drinking water sources;</p>
          <p>(4) the underground storage tank program; and</p>
          <p>(5) the clean air program, including air and emissions testing under the federal Clean Air Act, and state and federal requirements for vapor intrusion monitoring.</p>
          <p>(b) The commissioner shall maintain and publish a list of analytes available for accreditation. The list must be reviewed at least once every six months and the changes published in the State Register and posted on the program's website. The commissioner shall publish the notification of changes and review comments on the changes no less than 30 days from the date the list is published.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.98.3b">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3b.<span class="headnote">Additional fees.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Laboratories located outside of this state that require an on-site assessment more frequent than once every two years must pay an additional assessed fee of $3,000 per assessment for each additional on-site assessment conducted. The laboratory must pay the fee within 15 business days of receiving the commissioner's notification that an on-site assessment is required. The commissioner may conduct additional on-site assessments to determine a laboratory's continued compliance with the standards provided in subdivision 2a.</p>
          <p>(b) A late fee of $200 shall be added to the annual fee for accredited laboratories submitting renewal applications to the commissioner after November 1.</p>
          <p>(c) A change fee shall be assessed if a laboratory requests additional fields of testing at any time other than when initially applying for or renewing its accreditation. A change fee does not apply for applications to add fields of testing for new analytes in response to the published notice under subdivision 3a, paragraph (b), if the laboratory holds valid accreditation for the changed test category and applies for additional analytes within the same test category. The change fee is equal to the applicable test category fee for the field of testing requested. An application that requests accreditation of multiple fields of testing within a test category requires a single payment of the applicable test category fee per application submitted.</p>
          <p>(d) A variance fee shall be assessed if a laboratory requests a variance from a standard provided in subdivision 2a. The variance fee is $500 per variance.</p>
          <p>(e) The commissioner shall assess a fee for changes to laboratory information regarding ownership, name, address, or personnel. Laboratories must submit changes through the application process under subdivision 6. The information update fee is $250 per application.</p>
          <p>(f) Fees must be set so that the total fees support the laboratory accreditation program. Direct costs of the accreditation service include program administration, assessments, the agency's general support costs, and attorney general costs attributable to the fee function.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.98.3c">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 3c.<span class="headnote">Refunds and nonpayment.</span></h2>
          <p>Refunds or credits shall not be made for applications received but not approved. Accreditation of a laboratory shall not be awarded until all fees are paid.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.98.4">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 4.<span class="headnote">Fees for laboratory proficiency testing and technical training.</span></h2>
          <p>The commissioner of health may set fees for proficiency testing and technical training services under section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/16A.1285">16A.1285</a>. Fees must be set so that the total fees cover the direct costs of the proficiency testing and technical training services, including salaries, supplies and equipment, travel expenses, and attorney general costs attributable to the fee function.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.98.5">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 5.<span class="headnote">State government special revenue fund.</span></h2>
          <p>Fees collected by the commissioner under this section must be deposited in the state treasury and credited to the state government special revenue fund.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.98.6">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6.<span class="headnote">Application.</span></h2>
          <p>(a) Laboratories seeking accreditation must apply on a form provided by the commissioner, include the laboratory's procedures and quality manual, and pay the applicable fees.</p>
          <p>(b) Laboratories may be fixed-base or mobile. The commissioner shall accredit mobile laboratories individually and require a vehicle identification number, license plate number, or other uniquely identifying information in addition to the application requirements of paragraph (a).</p>
          <p>(c) Laboratories maintained on separate properties, even though operated under the same management or ownership, must apply separately. Laboratories with more than one building on the same or adjoining properties do not need to submit a separate application.</p>
          <p>(d) The commissioner may accredit laboratories located out of state. Accreditation for out-of-state laboratories may be obtained directly from the commissioner following the requirements in paragraph (a), or out-of-state laboratories may be accredited through a reciprocal agreement if the laboratory:</p>
          <p>(1) is accredited by a NELAP-recognized accreditation body for those fields of testing in which the laboratory requests accreditation from the commissioner;</p>
          <p>(2) submits an application and documentation according to this subdivision; and</p>
          <p>(3) submits a current copy of the laboratory's unexpired accreditation from a NELAP-recognized accreditation body showing the fields of accreditation for which the laboratory is currently accredited.</p>
          <p>(e) Under the conflict of interest determinations provided in section <a href="https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/43A.38">43A.38</a>, subdivision 6, clause (1), the commissioner shall not accredit governmental laboratories operated by agencies of the executive branch of the state. If accreditation is required, laboratories operated by agencies of the executive branch of the state must apply for accreditation through any other NELAP-recognized accreditation body.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.98.6a">
          
          <h2 class="subd_no">Subd. 6a.<span class="headnote">Implementation and effective date.</span></h2>
          <p>All laboratories must comply with standards under this section by July 1, 2009. Fees under subdivisions 3 and 3b apply to applications received and accreditations issued after June 30, 2009. Accreditations issued on or before June 30, 2009, shall expire upon their current expiration date.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="subd" id="stat.144.98.7">
